## 379. The shield bash: the left button with the shield raised

Jeff (2026-10-17): "shield bash is a good addition, approved". With the shield
raised (329's right button, held), the left button bashes with it instead of
striking with the right hand (Player._pursue_action routes the attack order to
World.try_bash); lowered, the left button is the right hand's weapon as ever. No
new key, message or replicated value: the server already knows "raised", so the
protocol is unchanged.

World.try_bash(by, target) (and bash_ready(entity), bash_verb(entity), for the
monsters' AI too; whether and when enemy-ai's shield-bearers bash is theirs) is a
shove on the body beside it, queued like a blow and met by no guard: through
_push, so the mass rules hold, its force a blow's push (ATTACK_FORCE_FACTOR)
times the shield's bash_force, moving it only from knockback_min_force (305), and
a pushed body is stunned by _push's own rule as after a hammer. It does no damage
and always staggers the target bash_stagger ticks. A guard up against it
(guarding: a shield raised, a sword ready) is opened: lowered and not raised again
for GUARD_BROKEN_TICKS, without 340's long stun. The bearer's own shield is down
for the bash's moment (GridEntity.bash_moment_until, bash_stagger ticks; guarding
finds none) and back up after it while the button is held. It costs bash_stamina,
then bash_ticks until the next (GridEntity.next_bash_tick, server only); short of
stamina, no bash. The numbers are the block verb's: bash_force 0 (a sword's, no
bash) by default; the round shield 2.0, stagger 4, stamina 3, 20 ticks. A bash on
a creature credits the shield "guarded" (365), so a much-used shield still tends
to steady; not "struck", the right hand's deed. The party log says "X bashes Y's
guard open" or "X shoves Y with a shield" (World.shield_bashed). Rejected: a key
of its own (the hands are the buttons, 329); damage (an interruption, not a
blow); counting it as the right hand's "struck".
## 400. What a companion knows of her town and the world, and her not knowing

Jeff's play log (2026-10-17): Wren, working in the castle's town, said "I
do not know what town you mean"; asked "what is a stag?" she knew nothing,
though lore has it; and her card took "Wren has not seen Pip before" and a
belief "she does not know what a stag is", against lore. The coordinator's
quick fix, with lore's creatures (257 amended) on main first.

Her voice's place line says whether a town is here (a stockpile place of
this zone's Holdings) and whether she stands on its ground ("There is a
town here, and you are in it."); the town has no name of its own yet, so
her home line says "the town here in <zone>" and "You know that town
well." A record saved without "home" gets one at join from her worker
record ("companion:<name>", its town's place and area, its first trade).

Her lore words (Companion.lore_words(who, about)) put first what is in
play: Companion.lore_topics, the kinds of creature she sees, the things
her player asked about, any lore entry id her player's last line names
("stag"), and the zone; Lore.known_by with those as about, by weight,
then the rest by weight, each fact once, within the 600 characters (a
fact too long for what is left is skipped, not the end of the list).

Her not knowing is never a fact or a belief: CompanionFacts.NOT_KNOWING
(does not / has not know, seen, met, heard of, recognise; never met or
heard of; not familiar; wonders who; who that is) drops it when proposed
and when her record loads, for talk entries only (an event's or a merged
history's words are kept), so a saved
record loses only such entries and nothing else of it changes. The
extraction prompt is shown her lore facts as true of the world, and its
rules say beliefs are only what someone else told her, never her own
words, and nothing may go against the world. companion_test and
resident_test cover it. Protocol unchanged.

Rejected: a town name made up here (lore's to give); dropping not-knowing
from event facts or histories (an event's are the game's words; a history
holds more than the not knowing); any "never" ("she will never see home
again" is a fact).
## 401. One shared UI theme and a style guide

Roadmap `ui`, step 1 (Jeff, 2026-10-17: audit and style, "one shared theme all
screens use"; the coordinator approved the design). Every panel had styled
itself: four copies of the pack panel's constants, five text sizes for one
kind of text, two blacks, three corner radii, and the engine's grey defaults
wherever nothing was set (docs/ui_style.md, "Screens today"; before and after
shots in docs/ui/shots/).

- `render/ui_theme.tres` is the project theme (project.godot `gui/theme/custom`),
  so every Control inherits it with no code: the panel, inset, button, slider,
  text-field, menu and tooltip styles, and named variations a panel asks for
  by `theme_type_variation` (Title, Heading, Hud, Caption, Small, Name,
  Outlined, Inset, HandSlot, Deep; LinkButton for a link). Its type `Psykinetic` holds the named colours (every
  one a swatch of art/kit/palette.png), fonts, sizes and spacing constants,
  which `UiTheme` (render/ui_theme.gd, new class_name; static color, font,
  size, constant, style) reads for what is drawn by hand (the compass, the
  maps, the speech bubbles). The .tres is the one source of truth; a panel
  sets no font, size, colour or style of its own, and a new meaning gets a
  named colour in docs/ui_style.md first.
- Fonts: Alegreya (serif: titles, names, speech, map labels) and Alegreya Sans
  (everything else), SIL OFL 1.1, in art/fonts/ with their licences
  (THIRD_PARTY.md). Sizes in canvas units (3840 x 2160): title 56, heading 44,
  the HUD's line 44, body 38, caption 30, small 24, speech 17 then scaled with
  the zoom (the Alegreya faces have a small x-height: body 30 read too small).
- The panels adopt it in place, behaviour unchanged (their owners' decisions
  stand): pack and chest (items), options (sound, pc-character, perf), shop
  and gold (economy), hints, talk log and chat (companions: the clock time is
  the line's tooltip now, not printed; lines[] keeps its shape), compass,
  minimap (maps: frame, water and labels only), builder's box, the HUD line
  and F3 text (outlined), the first-run screen. Sound's UiSounds hooks and
  the TalkPanel and ShopPanel signals (395) are untouched. The level editor
  and the world map view inherit the theme but are not restyled until the
  game's screens are done.
- `--test-show=<panels>` (hints, options, pack, talk, chat, debug, say, shop,
  setup) opens panels once the player is in, for screenshots; `ui 3200` in
  tests/port_offsets.txt.

Client only; protocol unchanged.

## 392. A heavy weapon winds its blow up

Jeff asked for heavy weapons to wind up before they swing. A weapon's verb may
name windup, the ticks a blow is wound up before it is struck (Items.COMMON,
0 for none): the giant axe 8; the hammer (one-handed, quick) and the spear
(reach) none. The attack with such a weapon (Player._pursue_action, the same
click as any blow: no hold-to-swing, which would need a new input message)
starts it, World.try_wind_up(by, target), and it is struck on its own
windup_ticks later (World._tend_wind_ups, before the tick's hits resolve).
Until then a move order or a step (order_move, order_step), a stun, a
knockdown or being moved off its cell gives it up (cancel_wind_up); after it is
struck nothing does. The struck blow is crushing (Hit.crushing): it breaks any
guard it meets at full weight (_meet_guard's crushing) and lands whole, its
knockdown too; if the target has left reach it whiffs at the air
(try_swing). The answer to it is not to be there, or to stun the swinger first
(a shield bash, 379). World.winding(entity) gives {target, lands, direction,
from} or {}; monsters holding such a weapon wind up through the same calls,
when enemy-ai's AI makes them. The brute's bare-handed wind-up (Monster's
HEAVY tactic) stays its own and blockable.

The views: the "winding" signal and RPC (direction, ticks) move from Monster
to GridEntity, so a player's wind-up is drawn as a brute's is (Client3D
_on_winding: the heavy clip timed to land with the sim; a creature's
CreatureView.wind), and 0 ticks now means a wind-up given up: the views stop it
(CreatureView.unwind; a humanoid's clip freed). The brute sends it too when its
wind-up is dropped (Monster._drop_windup, at each place it gave one up).
PROTOCOL_REVISION 13 for the new meaning of 0; the fingerprint changes with
the moved RPC. Rejected: hold to wind and release to strike (a new message,
and clicks walk up and strike today); a wind-up on every weapon (the quick
ones are quick); the brute's blow made unblockable (enemy-ai's and Jeff's).

## 390. One rig plays a model's clips: an AnimationTree each, in layers (combat animation, phase A)

Roadmap step 3. Every model's clips play through an AnimRig
(client3d/anim_rig.gd), the one way to play them (release's ask, agreed
with art-kit; CreatureView moves onto it next): an AnimationTree of each
body's own beside its AnimationPlayer, in layers. The base plays a loop or
a clip held at its end, every change crossfaded over the rig's blend, so a
knockdown hands over to lying and getting up with no frame of standing
between. An upper layer plays a clip over the spine, clavicles, neck, head
and arms with the legs left to the base (left out of a rig made with
upper = false: quadrupeds have no such bones). A posture layer adds a pose
made outside the rig (pc-character's stooped and slouching, coming). An
action layer plays a strike over everything, timed so its contact (seconds
in at speed 1, from the model's table; half the clip if none) lands when
the blow does and fitted after it to the time till the next, each speed
kept within 0.4 to 3.0. Which clip is played stays with the caller: a
humanoid strikes with what it holds (HUMANOID_MOVES' "strikes" by
World.wielded, bare hands' if it has none for that, never the same blow
twice running), its contact landing STRIKE_LANDS_IN (a tick and a half:
remote bodies are drawn that far behind the sim) after the news, the local
player's own at once; the wound-up heavy blow (392) is a strike too, and a
wind-up given up lets it go. A loop asked for again with only its speed
changed goes on at the new speed (gaits change pace every frame).
Cost, measured: 100 goblins walking posed every frame take 2.6 ms of CPU
(26 us each) against 2.0 ms on bare AnimationPlayers, the tree's layers
about a third more. So each body is posed every frame only within 9 m of
the camera's aim, every other frame within 16 m, every third beyond and
every eighth out of the frame (AnimRig.every, Client3D._pose_every), the
rest spread over the frames. tests/anim_rig_test checks each layer moving
the bones, the held clip's hand-over and the strike's timing; view_test
reads models through the rig. Still to come in phase A: the events of a
blow taken played on the display clock like the strike's. Rejected: one
AnimationTree resource shared by all (each body's clips and speeds are its
own); an AnimationNodeStateMachine of every clip (the tables name clips at
run time, and the code picks them); posing everything every frame (over
the 1 ms budget at sixty people and a herd).
Amended (items' bow audit, the coordinator): a shot's hit plays when its
arrow gets there, not when the sim's news does: _on_shot keeps when the
arrow it draws reaches its cell (_arrows_due), and _on_struck holds a
"shot" hit on whoever is there till then; the sim is as it was.
## 415. Kill counts: what a thing has felled, by kind

Jeff: items held and used grow, with kill counts (growth step 1, approved by
the coordinator). ItemBook tallies what each thing has felled by the kind of
body (ItemBook.fell, felled_of; entry "felled" {kind: count}, saved), across
every holder: a monster's dagger counts too, and the tally stays with the thing
when it changes hands, unlike 365's deeds, which are each carrier's. A body is
felled by a blow (_resolve_hits) or a shot (shoot) that kills it; the kind is
World.kind_of: a monster's or an animal's spawn kind, "person" for a player or a
companion. The slot's note (slot_notes, the pack's tooltip) shows it on a line
under the thing's name: "felled 14: 9 imps, 4 wolves, 1 brute", the most first
(World.kills_line; its own plurals until lore has words for kinds). Display
text only: the protocol is unchanged. The tallies are what bane (25 of a kind)
and vengeance's paying (5) count, in growth step 2.

## 417. Bane and vengeance: sidegrades a thing earns against one kind

Jeff: items held and used grow, with bane and vengeance (growth step 2,
approved by the coordinator; its numbers in items.json's "growth", Items.growth,
open to Jeff's answers). Both change how a fight with one kind goes, never
damage, and are counted from 415's tally.

Bane: a thing that has felled bane_after (25) of one kind is that kind's bane
for life (ItemBook.bane_of, set_bane, the history's "bane" event). That kind
dreads its bearer whatever its temper, and notices the bearer bane_notice (1.5)
times further: World.holder_bane(entity, kind) is the hook, read by enemy-ai as
it reads holder_dread (365), the numbers theirs to apply. So fewer stand-up
fights against that kind, and no sneaking among them.

Vengeance: a thing in the hands of a player or a companion felled by a monster
(damage reaching 0, before the fallen are spared, 396) takes a grudge against
that monster's kind, one at a time (ItemBook.grudge_of, set_grudge; World.
_take_grudges). Its blows on that kind stagger them grudge_stagger (4) ticks,
and that kind seeks its bearer first: World.holder_grudge(entity, kind), read by
enemy-ai's target choice. grudge_paid (5) of that kind felled with it, the grudge
lifts (pay_grudge; "avenged" in its history), those kills still counting toward a
bane. Bane makes them flee you; vengeance draws them to you and breaks their
rhythm.

The slot's note names both ("dagger, imp-bane, vengeance on wolves"; World.
item_note), and the party log tells each as it comes (World.item_grew). Saved in
ItemBook; display text only, so the protocol is unchanged. Questions with Jeff:
whether a bane should cost stealth, whether drawing a kind's fire is too harsh a
cost for vengeance.
## 398. Resident cards: who a town's person is, rolled once and grown from events

Every town resident has a card, as a companion has hers (293/294): who they
are, rolled once and never written by hand, growing from what happens to
them. The new class `ResidentCard` (`sim/resident_card.gd`) is the card
itself, pure; `Townsfolk` makes and keeps it; economy's worker record holds
it whole ("card", `Production.set_card`, saved and loaded as it is, {} for a
save from before and for a companion resting in town, whose card is her own).

The roll (`ResidentCard.roll`, by worker id, the same every time, when the
card is first needed): npc's `levels/resident_traits.json`, tables in
townsfolk words checked by lore (no place or person named: the land's and
the town's names are open), pronoun, birthplace, parentage, hobby, food,
temperament, fear, speech; "came", how they came to the town, the table's
words unless the record's origin is a rescue ("rescued:<x>"), when it is
the rescue itself, by whoever did it when known; and a "look" the character
generator reads (agreed with pc-character: seed, the id's hash, for what no
word names; build, stature, posture, hair, hair_colour, beard, shoulders,
age as words; grey hair twice as likely for the old; no beard for a woman).
Kin and a grudge at founding (`Townsfolk.card_of`, chances in the file): the
newcomer may be sister or brother, cousin or child to one neighbour who has
a card already (the elder resident the parent), and may bear a grudge
against one over a table's cause; each is a fact in both cards, so both
voices know it.

What becomes true of them: facts from events only, written from templates,
no model call (residents share one yielding mind): a raid that got in
(`Towns.raided`: the captive "was carried off by the goblins", every
resident at home "saw <name> carried off", or "lived through a raid" when
nobody was taken), a homecoming (`Towns.rescued`: "came home from the
goblins", the others saw; a newcomer rescued elsewhere has it in their
"came" and the others saw them come), a loan (`Production.loan_changed`:
borrowed from the town's coffer, works off a debt, paid it back), and
raiders seen from the walls (`Resident._look`, as it hides). Factions are
named as lore names them (the entry's "name"). `Townsfolk.learn` is the one
way in: the same words once, the oldest dropped past facts_max (16), each
told to the resident's transcript and the mind log (kind "fact"). Economy's
record field and signals: 8e16e60 (378 amended).

One written paragraph: the first time a town's resident is spoken to,
Main asks the resident mind once for their card (`_write_resident_card`:
the "card" channel, off the tick, as 293; the box's own model, never the
Claude API unless 363's switch is on), taken only when it is a paragraph
with no speech in it (`ResidentCard.take_written`), kept on the record
(`card_by` "model"); the plain card stands until then, and for good without
a model (tests have none). The voice (`Resident.card_words`, within 336's
rules): the written paragraph or the plain card, the hidden type's standing
fact (393), then "Also true of <name>:" the newest facts within the
budget, in the order they happened. Hearsay (378) joins the card at step 5.

resident_card_test covers the tables (no modern words), the roll, the
coming, the look, the plain card and the written one, the record, kin and
grudge, every event, the cap and the voice's words. Protocol unchanged.

Rejected: a model call per fact (294's talk-facts call is a companion's;
a dozen residents a zone would drown the box); the card in a store of its
own (the worker record is where a resident's state lives and is saved);
naming birthplaces or a river (lore: nothing stated that Jeff has not);
kin rolled against residents without cards yet (it would make every card in
the town at once); the type in the written paragraph (it stays a separate
standing fact, so the model never dresses it up).
## 405. The hunt into the town: meat, hides, the roast and the tanner

Herds step 2 (367's herds, 397's wildlife in play), the coordinator's
approval of 2026-10-17: what a player hunts and carries home builds the
town.

- Stockpile.RESOURCES gains meat, hide and leather. The meat item yields
  {"meat": 1} (it was food), hide {"hide": 1} (now tagged resource, a
  yield needs it), leather {"leather": 1}. A save from before reads 0 of
  each. Their values (economy.json "value"): 1, 3, 4. None has a comfort
  line, so a town is never short of them.
- The cook's roast (items.json, items' confirmed): from meat 1 and food 1,
  900 steps, mass 15 for 2400 ticks against the ration's 10 for 1800. A
  made field's "first" (Items._made keeps it) puts a recipe before its
  trade's others, so what the hunt brings home is cooked before rations.
- Townsfolk eat the store's meat when it has no food: folk.needs.meal's
  "store" may be a list, the first there is taken (Economy._eat).
- The tanner (Items.TRADES) and the tannery (economy.json buildings: built
  by the carpenter, wood 8, 4000 steps, max level 2), on the forge's and
  kitchen's rails: a rescued tanner waits for one, the town chooses it,
  and his workshop opens once it stands. Leather from two hides, 1200
  steps, into the shop to sell until items gives it a use. A town's wants
  end with rules' always_want (["resource"]) in every tier, so the tanner
  works whatever the tier: no other trade makes a resource. A tannery has
  no map slot yet: it stands in the town's record, as any building a town
  unlocks; a building.tannery slot is buildings' and art-kit's to add.
- Raids take meat as they take food (raids.takes: meat share 0.5); hides,
  leather and gold never.
- Not in this step: a hunter trade, which goes in step 3 beside the camps'
  hunting, designed so it never empties what players hunt.

Protocol unchanged: stock ids ride the fields they did. tests/larder_test;
builder_test's uses take the tannery.

Amended (the coordinator's balance run, 2026-10-17): a made thing with a
yield (the tanner's leather) is banked as that yield in the town's stock,
not put in the shop. In the shop it was gear the town's own work could
not use: the fletcher's mend and the tanner's buckler (items' 413) take
leather from the stock, so a town's leather sat unused, six in the shop at
its cap, while hides piled up uncured. Production._finish now deposits the
yield and ends the thing, "banked".

## 407. Camps and hunters take from the herds, above their reserves; wolves starve

Herds step 3 (367, 397, 405), the coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17.
What eats from the herds off-screen must never empty what a player is
stalking.

- A group's reserve is its species' least size: camps and hunters take
  only its count above that (Herds.spare), and nothing from a group with
  bodies out (a player is near it). Wolves are not bound by it: they are
  the herds' own.
- Each day an area's budget is take_share (0.25) of its spare at the
  day's start; camps and hunters together take no more than that.
- Camps (Holdings.camps: area, cell, size its worth) eat camp_eats (0.5)
  x size a day, of camp_prey in order (deer, boar, rabbit), nearest groups
  first. Nothing is stored: herds thin about camps. Herds.camp_fed(id),
  0..1 over the last whole day (1 before one has passed; saved), is a hook
  for maps (a hungry camp raiding for food); wiring it is maps' call.
  Herds.camps (a Callable) stands in for Holdings.camps in tests.
- The hunter (rules' hunter: trade hunter, every 3000 steps), a rescued
  trade with no building, in town and not away: Production.hunt (Main:
  Herds.hunt_one near the town's store) gives one animal of hunter_prey,
  the species with the most to spare, from its nearest group; its kind's
  drops (the least of each, monsters.json) go to the store, a resource as
  its yield and a trophy (antlers, tusks) banked as a thing.
  Production.hunted -> the town log: what he brought home, or "found no
  game". The worker's hunt_due is saved.
- Wolves that eat less than half their hunger lose starve (0.1) x the
  shortfall x their number a day, from their kept counts; fed, they breed
  as before. An area hunted out loses its wolves too.

Protocol unchanged: all sim. tests/herds_test (reserves, the stalked herd,
the budget, a camp fed and short, wolves starving and fed), tests/larder_test
(the hunter's catch, no game, away).

Amended (the coordinator's 30- and 90-day balance runs, 2026-10-17):
take_share 0.25 -> 0.05 and the wolf's eats 0.2 -> 0.1. At 0.25 a town's
hunter and the wolves emptied the wilds of deer and rabbits within 75 days
(deer 38 -> 0, rabbits 69 -> 0, wolves starving 9 -> 1), against breeding
of 3 to 8 a hundred a day, and an emptied area is never seeded again; at
0.10 the same by day 90. At 0.05 deer and boar held but wolves still ate
the rabbits out (70 -> 11); with wolves eating 0.1 as well, over 90 days:
deer 52 -> 53, rabbits 81 -> 67, boar 21 -> 28, wolves 8 -> 11. The hunter
brings home less meat for it; a farmer (Jeff: "farms and farmers too -
tune with seasons") is to feed the town.

## 409. A hungry camp raids for food

Maps' hungry-camp raids, the coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17: a raid
group sets out with "want": "food" when its camp is hungry (407's
Herds.camp_fed under 0.5), "" otherwise; maps sends it.

- Towns.raid_arrives reads the group's "want" against rules' raids.wants.
  "food": its own takes (food 0.75, meat 0.75, food-tagged things 4, each
  scaled by margin / strength as ever) and no captives ("captives": false):
  it came to eat, not to take people. Damage past damage.margin as ever.
- "" or a want the rules don't know: the raid as before, with no change.
- The report carries "want" (the group's, if the rules know it).

Protocol unchanged: sim only. tests/larder_test (a food raid, a plain one,
an unknown want).
## 418. The core screens: menu, connect, pause, and the options' choices

Roadmap `ui`, step 2 (the coordinator approved the design; maps reviewed
the join path and the controls setter as live-updates' owner, 241). The
game had no menu and no pause: an exported client joined at once, the
join's state was a sentence in the HUD line, controls= was read from
settings.cfg but never written, and the HUD line carried "host" and the
tick in the player's eye line.

- `MainMenu` (render/main_menu.gd, new class_name, a CanvasLayer): an
  exported client (OS.has_feature("template") and mode CLIENT) starts at
  it; `--menu` forces it for anyone (screenshots). Play, Options, Quit, the
  version in a corner; the HUD is hidden under it. A host, a server, a
  project run and every test go straight in as before (Main._play).
- `ConnectScreen` (render/connect_screen.gd, new; net/setup_screen.gd and
  SetupScreen removed): the join flow in one place. Main._connect_status
  routes what was hud.text: "connecting to a:p", "the server at a:p did
  not answer", the join_rejected reasons in words, "updating to the
  server's vX: the game closes and starts again" (SelfUpdate unchanged),
  "the server did not let you in: check the token", "the server is
  restarting; trying again (n)", "the server is gone". A failure offers
  Retry (Net.reconnect, 240) and Change server (the fields, as the first
  run shows them; a change reconnects when the game is already online);
  Back when there is a menu. The screen goes once the local player is in.
  Hosts' rare messages stay on the HUD line. In-game download progress and
  a server status reply are maps' later items; the screen will show them.
- `PausePanel` (render/pause_panel.gd, new): Esc with nothing open shows
  Resume, Options, Leave and Quit and says the world goes on (co-op never
  pauses the sim).
  Amended (Jeff, 2026-10-17, "might wanna tell UI there's no pause for the
  game"): it is the game menu, `GameMenu` (render/game_menu.gd; PausePanel
  gone), titled with the zone's name, with Close, Options, Leave and Quit
  and the plain line that the world goes on while it is open; nothing the
  player sees says pause or resume (decision 453's landing). Esc closes what is open first (Main.escape: the pause,
  the options, an open chest or pack, the big map as before). Leave on an
  exported build starts the game again and quits; a project run quits.
- Options (sound's and perf's sections untouched): Video gains Window
  (Net.set_fullscreen, F11's state) and Resolution (Net.set_window_size,
  the windowed size); a Controls section with Move (Net.set_controls,
  written as controls= at last) and the controls list (Net.set_hints;
  hints_changed tells Main). Choice rows are toggle buttons as perf's
  anti-aliasing row; the panel shows what is set each time it opens.
- The HUD line shows the player's state alone; "host" and the tick are
  F3's first line (perf's, agreed). The HP number stays until Jeff says
  what shows hurt instead (the no-bars rule).

Client only; protocol unchanged. tests/ui_test (base port 17840): the
menu's and pause's signals, the connect screen's states, buttons and
fields, Esc's order, the options' choices writing Net and settings.cfg.
`--test-show` gains pause, menu, setup, connect, failed. Shots in
docs/ui/shots/step2/.

## 413. Leather's uses: bundles mended, the tanner's buckler

The coordinator asked for a use for leather once the tanner makes it (405),
kept to what the sim already does; designed with economy.

Mending: an item may say how the town mends a worn one back to full condition,
"mend" beside "made" ({by, from, steps}, read as made is: Items.mend_of; checked
as a made from things, and only on a thing with a condition, 375). The three
bundles of arrows are mended by the carpenter from a piece of leather and a
bundle of wood in 600 steps: every town has a carpenter from the start, so leather
is of use as soon as a tanner makes some; a fletcher, as 375 had it, is a "by"
change and a trade when there is one. Economy's mend job (414) works it on the same
uid, so its name and history stay: Production holds the uid, sets its condition
full (ItemBook.set_condition) and banks it back. The reforge (later) is that job
with another id.

The buckler: a leather buckler, made by the tanner from 2 leather and 1 wood
(1800 steps, value 6), tagged shield so a town that wants shields may make it. The
block verb's own numbers, no new verb: a sidegrade to the round shield, lighter
(1.5 kg against 4) and cheaper to guard with (6 stamina against 8), its bash
lighter (bash_force 1.0), but it covers only straight ahead (arc 0), takes three
quarters of a blow (absorb 0.75) and breaks sooner (breaks_at 1.5). Art slot
item.buckler. Rejected: a leather jerkin (armour here would only add mass, all
gain but a pack slot); a sling or bag (the slots are fixed; a new rule); a
bandaging kit variant (the kit has no numbers to vary).

Amended by 428 (Jeff: bundles are "repaired by the town fletcher"): the
three bundles' mend is by the fletcher, a trade in Items.TRADES; the
carpenter stands in (rules' stand_in) while his town has no fletcher.

## 414. The mend job: a worn thing in the store made whole on its own uid

Items' 413 gives a thing with a condition a "mend" ({by, from, steps};
the three bundles of arrows: the carpenter, leather 1 and wood 1, 600
steps). Production does the work, agreed with items.

- One job kind, "mend", holding the thing's uid and a to_id (the same id
  for a mend). A reforge later is this job with another to_id, so it needs
  no kind of its own.
- It serves the "repair" want, which the defend tier lists and nothing
  served before. always_want gains "repair" after "resource", so mending
  happens in every tier, last. Production.items_catalog carries an item's
  mend (Items.mend_of) beside its made.
- A shop bids on the first thing banked in its town's store, by uid, worn
  below its most (ItemBook.condition_of < Items.condition_max), whose mend
  is by its trade, when the store has the mend's "from". It takes those
  resources and the thing (held by the job, job:<id>, as a rework's) for
  the mend's full steps. Done: the same uid set to its most
  (ItemBook.set_condition), "mended" in its history, banked back in the
  store, not put up for sale; its name and history stay.
- Saved as any job, with to_id.

Protocol unchanged: sim only. tests/larder_test (waits without leather, a
mend, the same uid whole and banked, the materials used, none for a whole
bundle, nothing left over in a save).
## 421. A thing's story and the words for what it does, for ui's tooltip

Ui's step 3 (the themed item tooltip, ItemTip; approved by the coordinator)
asked for two things items owns.

The story line: a slot's note (World._show_notes, slot_notes; 365, 375, 415,
417) gains a line "story: ...", after the kills line, built on the server from
the thing's history (World.story_line): its longest carrier, when held a day or
more of the world clock ("carried by Wren for 3 days"); its naming ("named for
Wren"), or else how it came to be ("made by Bram at the smithy", "from Osric's
hunt"); a keeping ("kept from Wren"); each vengeance had ("avenged on wolves").
Parts joined by "; " and dropped from the end until the line is at most
STORY_LONGEST (80); no line when there is nothing to tell. The note's layout for
ItemTip: the first line is the head (the title or catalog name, then its marks,
comma separated: condition, bane, vengeance); each further line is found by its
first word, "felled " (415) or "story: ". Display text in a value already
replicated: the protocol is unchanged.

The words: "says", plain words for what a thing does, as catalog data items owns:
on each weapon's verb ("quick; twice the hurt from behind"; Items.verb_from keeps
it), on each naming strength ("its blows make half the fight noise"; read_naming
keeps a strength's row whole) and for bane and vengeance (growth's "says",
Items.growth). The client reads them through Items.def(id)["verb"], Items.naming()
and Items.growth(); without them a tooltip shows the verb's or strength's name.
## 404. Resident routines: where a town's person is, through the day and the year

A resident's day (333: work, home, else the square, two spans a trade) is now
stints, data in `levels/residents.json`: per trade a list of {from, to, at},
`at` one of work, home, square, well, inn, temple, and a default for a trade
not listed; any hour no stint covers is the square, and a place the town
lacks (no inn linked, no temple or well on the map) is the square too, so a
town with a forge and nothing else looks as it did. "work" is where the body
stands, never when the job runs: economy's production ticks on the world
tick wherever the body is, and its timing is untouched. The coordinator's
note, word for word.

`Townsfolk.whereabouts(trade, hour, season, type, worker_id, day)` answers
from the clock alone (perf's 355: bodies only while someone is near, so a
body spawned as a player walks up must start at the right stint;
`Resident.doing_now` gathers the hour, the season and the day from
DayNight and Season): first the temple day (every `every_days`, the day by
the id, an hour of the morning at the temple), then the hidden type's
stints (393: a bard's evening at the inn runs late, a thief is in the
square after dark, a scholar's hour at the temple), then the trade's, their
edges moved by the season (every boundary before noon by `morning` hours,
after by `evening`: winter out later and home earlier, summer the other
way; a boundary's shift is a function of its hour, so adjacent stints keep
their shared edge and no gap opens), on the resident's own clock, ahead of
or behind the town's by at most `offset_hours`, by the id, so the town never
moves in lockstep. `Resident.Doing` gains WELL, INN and TEMPLE; `PLACE_OF`
and `_pick_goal` are as before (a missing place falls to the square).

Places (`Main._resident_places`): the inn when linked and standing, the
temple and the well by their slots (`building.temple`, `building.well`:
buildings' word, they carry no "use" or town yet), the nearest within
HOME_TILES of the store; the well, a 1x1 on water, is stood beside; a
priest's work is the temple. The healer's hut (economy's return, 396: the
medicine man a worker whose town is the hut's Holdings place id, origin
"wilds"; maps' 372: a place of kind `healers_hut` at the hut's front cell):
`_sync_residents` also takes those places, their residents
`Production.worker_ids(place id)`, work and home the hut's rect (the
`building.healers_hut` whose rect touches the place cell, else three by
three round it), the square round the cell, bodies only while someone is
near as a town's. The voice (`facts_now`) says where it is: "You are at
the well." routine_test covers the file (whole days, known places), the
places through a smith's day, the default, the square for a gap, the
offsets' spread and constancy, the type and season rules and that no season
opens a gap, the temple day and `day_of`, and `Resident.doing_at`.
Protocol unchanged.

Rejected: moving residents on the world tick between stints (a body is only
where it is now; its place is a function of the clock, so a spawn and a
standing body agree); a per-resident timetable saved on the record (data
plus the id gives it); the well as a Holdings place (environment counts
rain for the building; a slot match is enough); shifting whole stints by
the season (gaps and overlaps at the seams; edges shift by their hour
instead); the priest or the medicine man as Towns residents (economy seats
them; the sync reads the record's town either way).
## 410. A hungry camp raids sooner, and for food

Jeff's raids are "food and people only" and "real raiders on the world
tick"; economy's herds step (407) makes a camp hunt its area's herds and
says how well it ate (Herds.camp_fed, 0..1 over the last whole day, 1 until
a day has passed). Raid groups (328) read it through WorldRaids.fed, a
Callable Main sets to World.herds.camp_fed (a camp nobody says is fed ate
well).

- Sooner: raids keep no wait, only a chance a world tick (send_chance times
  the town's threat), so a hungry camp's chance is multiplied: by 1 at or
  above hungry_below (0.5), rising in a straight line to hungry_send (3.0)
  for a camp that ate nothing, never above 1 (WorldRaids.send_chance,
  hunger_factor). Its target is chosen as before, the most threatened town.
  Both are raids.groups data in levels/economy.json.
- For food: a camp hungry when its group sets out gives the group "want":
  "food" (WorldRaids.WANT_FOOD; "" is the usual raid). It is kept on the
  group (saved with it, an old save reading ""), and goes with it to
  Towns.raid_arrives, whose take rules read it (economy's 409: food and meat
  and food-tagged things, no captives), and to World.raids.enter, for
  enemy-ai's raiders later. The send is logged "… hungry (fed 0.20), for
  food".
- A fed camp is unchanged: the same chance and a want of "".

In play: a camp that has hunted out the herds near a town eats less, so it
raids more often and carries food home rather than people; the ledger and
the guards' lines can name a hungry camp later. Raids stay off until
switched on. Protocol unchanged.

tests/raid_groups_test.

## 416. The Blood Rot: orcs and kobolds as allied factions

Jeff, through lore (012d57b, levels/lore/factions.json's goblins entry,
agreed): every goblin in the region is of the Blood Rot; brutes are orcs
and sneaks are kobolds, allied peoples of the Blood Rot, not ranks; the
allies don't worship the star, so an alliance can break or be turned.
levels/factions.json had one "goblins" faction holding imp, brute and
sneak.

- "goblins" keeps its key (saves, place holders, raid groups, captives'
  "by" and economy's raids.raiders all use it), shown as "the Blood Rot",
  lore_id "blood_rot" (lore's entry, so its facts can reach the game). New
  "orcs" (brute) and "kobolds" (sneak), each "allied_to": "goblins",
  lore_id "goblins" (their facts are in that entry until lore gives them
  their own, "orcs" and "kobolds"). Colours: the allies are tints of the
  Blood Rot's green.
- A kind's faction is said in one place, factions.json's "monsters" lists
  (Factions.of_kind), not in monsters.json too (enemy-ai agreed).
- Factions: allied_to is one level deep (an allied_to naming no faction,
  itself, or an ally is dropped with a warning); side(id), same_side(a, b),
  allies_of(id), lore_id(id). hostile goes through sides: an ally takes on
  its lead's enemies (the town needs no new hostile_to), and one side is
  never hostile to itself.
- Holdings: an ally's ground does not block (blocked_cells), so allies
  walk each other's ground on their own route layers; ground two of one
  side cover reads as the lead's, not contested.
- Raids._kinds_of (enemy-ai's, agreed): a faction's kinds and its allies',
  sorted, so a Blood Rot group is imps, brutes and sneaks as before (the
  draw, seeded over that list, is unchanged); an ally's group draws on its
  own. Monster._same_side: factions.same_side of the two kinds' factions,
  so brutes and imps stay one side.
- Words: economy's town notes name a faction by display name (295
  amended, Towns.faction_name): "a raid by the Blood Rot". The party log
  is unchanged.
- A save from before reads the same: every stored faction id is still
  "goblins", now shown as the Blood Rot; monsters are not saved by faction,
  so a brute is an orc by its kind.

Not in this step: turned or broken alliances (the hook: an ally without
allied_to is its own side). Protocol unchanged.

## 426. Wells keep a town's water; the carpenter mends storm-broken roofs

On environment's 384 (town weather: rain fills wells, storms break roofs;
Weather.rain_between) and 383 (roof damage: World.damaged_roofs,
World.repair_roof). The coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17.

Wells:
- A town's wells are the building.well entries in its area (no level edit,
  no "use" link). With none, the town keeps no water and nothing here
  applies.
- The town record keeps "water", full (cap x wells) the first time it is
  seen. On the town tick each well adds spring (4) a day and catch (12) x
  the rain that fell on its region (days of full rain), up to cap (30) a
  well; residents draw draw (0.5) a day each. Saved on the record.
- Dry and wet again are each said once in the town log ("the well is
  dry", "the well has water again").
- PROVISIONAL, JEFF'S TO CONFIRM: while dry, the kitchen (water.dry_slows,
  the cook) works at dry_rate (0.5), so meals take twice as long
  (Production.work_rate, set by Towns). Nothing else changes: no thirst,
  no deaths, no change to the dole.
- Tuning: a season of the town lands' rain (about 10 days of full rain in
  90) with 10 residents: the water dips to about 19 of 30 and never runs
  dry; with 4, it stays full. A draw of 1 left a 10-resident town dry 68
  days of 90, hence 0.5. A big town (20 residents) runs dry in a dry spell.

Roofs:
- A damaged roof of a level belongs to the town whose store is in it.
  After any building repair, Towns orders one roof mended at a time: a
  build job ("roof:<index>") by rules' roof.by (the carpenter), costing
  wood_base (1) + one wood per wood_cells (8) of the roof, roof.steps
  (1200), paid as town work. Done: World.repair_roof; if the roof was
  whole already, the wood is still spent and the log says so.
- Load: about 1.2 storms a season each breaking a quarter of the roofs is
  2 to 3 roofs a season for a town of 8, a small fraction of the
  carpenter's time.
- Towns' hooks wells, rain, roofs and mend_roof are set by Main (the
  level's buildings, Weather.rain_between of its region, World's roofs);
  tests stand in for them.

Protocol unchanged: sim only. tests/wells_test (full at first, spring and
draw, dry and wet once each, the kitchen at half speed and the forge not,
cap, saved, no well, a printed season for 10 and 4 residents, a roof
ordered and mended, one at a time, wood by size, whole already).

## 424. Blessed at the temple: a kept thing made its holder's own

Jeff: items held and used grow, and may be blessed at the temple (growth step 3,
approved by the coordinator; with 370's curse, beside 415 and 417's marks).
ItemBook.bless(uid, owner) blesses a thing for an owner (a carrier key): a kept
thing is cleansed (no longer kept from its namer, every carrier's ill gone), and
while it is blessed no ill gathers on it (_ill_now). Noted "blessed"; kept in the
history like a naming. The blessing follows the owner's will: given by its owner
(World._taken, from the owner's hand) it goes with the gift (pass_blessing);
taken from them by anyone else, not given, it is lost ("unblessed"), and a named
thing may then be kept from its namer again, as 370 has it. No combat effect: it
is how a found heirloom becomes its finder's. The note's head says ", blessed"
and the story "blessed at the temple" (421).

Who does it is economy's: the priest's job (one job kind with the mend and the
reforge: {uid, to_id, effect "bless", for the owner}), an offering in gold about
the thing's value to the town's treasury, the thing held for its owner at the
temple until they next open its counter; buildings' counter spot in the temple
prefab and ui's counter screen (step 4) are theirs, amendments to this entry.
Saved; display text only, so the protocol is unchanged. Open with Jeff: whether a
blessing also grows a name faster.

counter is (decision 301). The temple prefab (tools/seed_prefabs.gd,

(the record whose footprint holds it: use "temple", its "town"). Not yet in

would move every later slot on Jeff's saved town; a rule that a level's
later additions take the next free slot comes first, as its own decision,
then the wilds counter. view_test: the stamped temple has the one counter,

## 428. Rescues: a fallen camp's people come home, and strangers bring their trades

Economy's roadmap step 4 ("rescued people unlock their trade"), the
coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17. Until now nothing in play rescued
anyone: raids carried people off (Jeff's rule: raids take food and people
only) and Towns kept them held at a camp, but only tests and the town_state
tool called note_rescue.

- Freeing the held: Towns.free_held(holder) frees every captive held by a
  camp's place id or by a raid group's id (while it carries them), each
  through note_rescue: a resident back to their work, a companion through
  companion_freed, rescue experience each. Main connects
  Holdings.place_taken: a camp taken by the town or by nobody calls
  Towns.camp_taken, which frees its held; one taken by another hostile
  faction frees nobody. Maps' 429 makes a cleared camp fall in play, and
  calls free_held for a raid group that breaks up on the way home.
- Strangers: each hostile camp (Towns.camps: Holdings.camps) holds
  rescue.per_camp (1) strangers for its home town (Towns.home_of: the
  nearest held store by routes), kept on that town's record ("strangers",
  saved). Each one's trade is drawn by the town, the camp and a running
  count, from rescue.trades' weights (hunter, tanner, fletcher 3; smith,
  cook, carpenter 1) times rescue.lacking (3) for a trade the town has
  nobody of; a name from rescue.names. When the camp falls they join the
  town as residents of their trade (note_rescue, origin "camp:<id>"), and
  the log says where they were held. A trade with a building waits for it
  (a tanner for the tannery). The camp gets new strangers once it is
  hostile again and rescue.restock_days (5) have passed.
- The fletcher is a trade (Items.TRADES, with items): the bundles' mend
  (414) goes to him first; rules' stand_in {"fletcher": "carpenter"} lets
  the carpenter do it while the town has no fletcher there.
- Bodies: record-level. The freed appear in town through npc's resident
  bodies; walking home from the camp in play is for npc or companions
  later.

Protocol unchanged: sim only. tests/rescue_test (a stranger held, the same
every run, once, saved; a camp falling to nobody frees the raid's captive
and the stranger, not to another faction; experience and the log; restock
after its days; free_held by a group's id; the draw leaning to lacking
trades; the fletcher mends, the carpenter stands in). items_test's mend
recipe is the fletcher's.
## 422. Gossip: what a town's person believes or saw passes to a neighbour

npc's step 5 (the coordinator's approval 2026-10-17), on companions' hearsay
(378: a resident keeps what is said near it, believed by a seeded roll on
its intellect, and its voice repeats the newest it believes), the cards
(398) and the routines (404). Townsfolk already kept what they heard from a
player or a companion; nothing moved between them. Now it does, and with
no model call.

Every residents.json "gossip.every" steps (1200) in each town, its
residents (not away, not companions) are grouped by where they are now
(Townsfolk.whereabouts, on the clock alone, so it needs no bodies). In each
group of two or more at one of "gossip.places" (the well, the inn, the
square, the temple; never at work or at home) one teller passes one thing
to one hearer (Townsfolk.gossip, _pass), by a roll seeded by the town, the
place and the step, so a save replays the same. What passes: the teller's
newest believed hearsay the hearer does not hold (Hearsay.holds, by the
words alone, from anyone), else the teller's newest card fact the hearer
has not heard, told as its own ("Mara saw raiders at the walls" becomes
"she saw raiders at the walls"), never one that names the hearer. The
hearer keeps it through Hearsay.hear from the teller's name, with 378's
believe roll on its intellect: a passed-on belief as "beyond" (a sharp
hearer doubts it: chance (11 - intellect) / 10), a first-hand fact as the
new fits "witnessed", believed always (a neighbour saying what she saw is
no rumour). The entry gains "where" (the place; "" for a line said to the
resident), and Hearsay.prompt_words tells the voice "At the well, Tam told
you that the mine is cursed." Kin are picked first as hearers, and nobody
gossips with one they hold a grudge against, either way: the cards keep
kin and grudges by id now beside the facts (Townsfolk._found_among writes
"kin" {id: kind} and "grudge" [ids] into both cards; cards from before have
neither and gossip freely). An official (Lore.binding) tells only what it
saw, never a rumour, and what it hears never reaches its voice (378 as it
is). One pass per group per tick; the heard cap (8) as it is, the oldest
unbelieved going first. Each pass goes to the transcript under both names
("[At the well, Tam told Mara: the mine is cursed]") and to mind.log (kind
"gossip", from, where, fits, believed or doubted), so a lie's path through
the town can be read back. A planted lie thus walks: told to Tam at the
inn, Tam tells Mara at the well next morning, Mara repeats it to the
player, naming Tam and the well.

gossip_test (pure sim, no port or scratch): a belief passes between two at
the well and not across places; never at home; a first-hand fact is
witnessed and believed by the sharpest while a passed lie is doubted by
them; never across a grudge; kin first; an official passes on no rumour
but what she saw; the cap; the same state gives the same pass; the voice's
words. Also met: a stint whose "to" is 24 wraps to 0 under the season shift
and vanishes (whereabouts); residents.json has none, the test's day is two
stints. Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

Rejected: a claims ask per pass (a model call for every pair every hour);
residents speaking aloud to each other (336 rejected idle chatter, and
nothing reads lines not said to a player); passing lore (Lore.known_by has
it already); believing a neighbour's sighting by the intellect roll (it is
first-hand; the roll is for rumours).

Amended 2026-10-19 (the soak, 496): a hearer's card keeps what it was told
("told", Townsfolk.TOLD_MAX 64 texts), and gossip never tells them the same
thing twice, even after it fell off their heard cap (the cap evicts the
oldest not believed, and a small town where everyone knows everything then
told one pair the same line 36 times in a month). With nothing new to tell,
the pass is silent and nothing is recorded.

## 430. The in-game update fetches the server's release, showing how far

ui's connect screen (step 2, decision 418) shows the join flow in words; an
out-of-date client (241) quit to update.ps1, which fetched the latest
release with nothing on screen, so a slow download looked like a crash, and
a release published after a deploy could be the wrong one.

- On "client out of date", where SelfUpdate.refusal allows it (an exported
  game, the server newer, not within MIN_GAP_SEC), Main makes a
  SelfUpdate.Download: it asks GitHub for the release tagged
  v<server version> (release_url; the server's own, never "latest"), takes
  its psykinetic-client-*.zip (asset_url), downloads it beside the game
  (update_download.zip) and unpacks it with ZIPReader into update_stage, a
  few files a frame. It reports progress(fraction, text) (fraction -1 while
  it cannot tell), which Main passes to ConnectScreen.set_progress, and
  finished(ok, why). The screen's Cancel (cancel_pressed) stops it. A
  failure (no connection, no such release, no client zip, not a zip, no
  psykinetic.exe, no room) or a cancel removes the zip and the folder, and
  the screen says why with the line to run launch.bat, as before.
- Done, Main starts update.ps1 -Stage <update_stage> (SelfUpdate.start,
  script_args), says it is updating and quits half a second later.
  update.ps1 -Stage waits for the game (30 s at most), checks the folder
  has psykinetic.exe, copies it over the game keeping settings.cfg,
  removes it and starts the game. Without -Stage (launch.bat) it is as
  before. -NoStart leaves the game unstarted, for the test's dry run.
- The marker (update_marker.txt) is written when update.ps1 is started, as
  before, so a release that still does not match cannot loop.

Client and update.ps1 only: it works from the release after it lands (the
first update into it goes the old way). Protocol unchanged.

tests/self_update_test (no network: a local zip; update.ps1 -Stage's dry
run on Windows).
## 432. The reforge: a named thing made another of the smith's

Jeff's heirlooms, the last of them (the curse design's step 4; approved by the
coordinator): a named thing (365) taken to the forge counter may be reforged
into another of the smith's things. Pairs (Items.reforge_cost, reforge_targets):
from any thing with a verb (a weapon or a shield) to any other id with a verb
the smith makes, taking the same hands or fewer; so a one-handed weapon becomes
any other one-handed smith's thing, a giant axe anything the smith makes, and
nothing becomes the tanner's buckler (it may become the smith's things). The
smith's cost: half the target's made "from", each rounded up, at least 1 ore
(the old metal goes into it), and half its steps: a dagger into a sword 2 ore
and 1 wood in 1500 steps.

ItemBook.reforge(uid, to_id), with which economy's job finishes (the general job
of 414, effect "reforge", worked by the smith; its fee and the town's stock are
economy's, amendments to this entry; the counter's screen ui's): the same uid,
its id the new one. Its name stays, rendered with the new thing's word through
Lore.render_name ("Wren's dagger" now "Wren's sword"); its curse (370), its bane
and grudge (417), its tally (415) and its blessing (424) stay, and its carrier
rows. Its strength stays if it fits the new verb (Items.strength_fits: steady a
block verb, quick a bow, set a bracing reach, quiet a verb that strikes, heavy a
knockdown, dread any), else it is lost. Noted "reforged" ("dagger into sword;
quiet lost"), never evicted, and told in the story ("reforged from a dagger";
421). An unnamed thing is not reforged: the town makes a new one. The id lives in
slots, already replicated: the protocol is unchanged.

## 427. In-game panels: item tips, the talk box, the place, the cursor's hint

Roadmap `ui`, step 3 (the coordinator approved the design; items, companions
and maps answered its asks). A slot's note was a plain tooltip, the log and
the chat box were two controls, the compass said nothing of where you were,
and the controls list sat on screen by default.

- `ItemTip` (render/item_tip.gd, new class_name): a themed hover tip over a
  slot, made from the slot's note (World._show_notes, items' 421: line 1 the
  title or catalog name then marks after commas; "felled ..." the tally;
  "story: ..." the history line) and the catalog the client holds: the name
  (brass_bright when named), the catalog name under it, what it does and
  weighs (Items.verb_of(id)["says"], hands, weight), each strength's words
  (naming "says"), the kept warning (370, in rust), the growth marks with
  their words (Items.growth()["says"]), the kills, the story. ItemTip.lines_for
  is the pure part, for tests. PackPanel shows it on a slot's mouse_entered
  and says under the player's row what they carry weighs (the catalog's
  weights; a caption on the inventory screen, never the HUD: the no-bars rule
  holds, the coordinator's call).
- TalkPanel holds Main's chat box (set_box): a new line shows the panel for
  FADE_AFTER (8 s), then it goes unless pinned (Tab, toggle_pin), hovered or
  the box is open; pinned, the list scrolls up to LIST_HEIGHT. The box's
  channel ("say" or "party", from Main.PARTY_PREFIX) is named beside it, and
  Tab inside the box swaps them without leaving the box (Main._swap_chat_channel;
  companions: fading and the label fine, "[party] Wren:" enough, no
  highlighting of a line she answers). lines[]'s shape and line_added stay.
- The place you stand in, left of the compass (HudCompass.place, Main.place_text):
  the level's place whose disc covers the player's cell, the nearest centre of
  several, then the zone's name; the zone alone outside every place (maps'
  rule: level["places"] on the client, never Holdings, no holder shown).
- The controls list (H) in two columns, and off by default (Net.hints false,
  hints= absent or off; a saved hints=on keeps it), because a context hint by
  the cursor says what the keys do on what it points at: "E  open" (a chest,
  a crate, a cart; "the shop" for a counter), "E  open or close" (a door),
  "F  pick up" (a pile), "E  her pack" (your companion), "LMB  attack" (a
  monster you can target), "E hold  bandage" (another player); Main.context_hint_for
  from the thing under the cursor, the door under it, or a prop on the cell.
- The stale net/setup_screen.gd references in docs point at ConnectScreen.

## 391. A companion inside buildings and in doorways

Jeff's play (2026-10-17, through the coordinator): in Pip's house her voice
was told "You are outdoors, under the sky"; "check this hut for loot" got
"I will look inside the hut" and nothing done; "You are blocking the door"
and "Step aside please" got "I will move" and she did not ("she didn't
move when asked to move, even though she verbally said she would"); and
"companions tend to stand in doorways, when i move into building they
should consider, doorway plugging a battle strategy not a routine".

Inside: Companion.building_at(cell) is the building of this zone's Level
"buildings" whose inside holds the cell (those with an inside: hut,
house, shed, temple, healer's hut); her place line says "You are inside a
small hut (Snagfin's home)": what the town uses it for, else its kind by
size, and whose home it is when a resident's body has it as home. The
hour, season and weather come from DayNight.describe (389), said as
outside.

A look round: inside a building, can_do offers "look round inside the
<building> and see what is there", an errand that walks to its middle
and reports each chest and what it holds, each thing on the floor, each
crate and anyone there, a fact when she finds something. "Check this
shed for loot" promises it, not a look off somewhere. VOICE_ASKED gains
the rule: asked something that is neither a stance nor on her list, she
says plainly she cannot, never that she will.

Out of the way: Companion.door_cells (each door's two cells, its inside
and the one outside it) are where she never stops of her own accord: her
heel cell (381) is never one, nor a yield's; and it is on her player's
side of a building's walls, so she follows them in, or waits outside off
the door when there is no room. In a doorway, or on the other side of
the walls from her player, she moves however near she is. Next to her
player or in a doorway, can_do offers "step out of <player>'s way" (make
way), done by the hands at once, as a bump is (step_aside: the nearest
free cell off their way and off any doorway, else she and they change
places); standing as told, she stands there from then on.

Holding a door is a tactic: with her player inside a building and a
hostile outside that she sees or hears, within GUARD_RANGE of one of its
doors or in sight going for either of them, she guarding or pressing
takes that door's inside cell and fights what comes at her there
(Companion._door_to_hold), and can_do offers "hold the door of <the
building> against what is coming" for any stance; once there is no such
hostile she steps off it. resident_test covers it (its town gains a shed
with walls and a door). Protocol unchanged.

Rejected: a door cell barred to her pathing (she must pass through
doors, only not stop in them); asking enemy-ai for "the way in" (a
building's doors are it).

Amended (2026-10-18, perf's two finds): a companion's first turn in a zone
parsed its level.json again (building_at's Level.load_level, 145 ms), and
one with a foe she could not reach pathfound to it every tick (Wren and
Snagfin, seven a second), giving up and picking it again. Main hands her
each level it loads (Companion.know_level from Main._load_level: its

she was not handed is still read once. A target _approach finds out of
reach is skipped by GUARD's and PRESS's picks (her quarry with them) for
UNREACHABLE_TICKS (30, three seconds), or till it or she has moved

foe next to her is fought all the same. companion_test covers both.
Protocol unchanged.

Amended again (2026-10-18, buildings' 488: a building's "rect" is the box
round its blocks): a look round inside an L-shaped building goes to the
free cell of its own (Level.building_cells) nearest the box's middle,
never the box's empty corner, and counts only what is on its own cells.
A one-block building's look is as before. companion_test covers it.

## 423. The needles' floor: a ground.needles texture under the pine stands

The floor under the border's pine stands (369) was the flat NEEDLES colour
(7a4e2c). It becomes real ground: a texture slot `ground.needles` (art-kit:
category ground, type texture, tile_m 4, 512 px, seamless), its image
art-gen's, procedural as its dirt and sand (orange-brown needles averaging
near NEEDLES, a few cones and twigs, patches of bare earth, no baked light).
The coordinator approved the design.

- Read by `PineStands.floor_material` for the two needle planes: the
  ForestFloor plane under the stands (`Client3D._add_forest`, while
  `PineStands.drawn()`) and TerrainBorder's far floor past them (a shade
  darker, 0.85). Each is one material a build, as the planes are.
- Tiled in world metres, not UV: season.gdshaderinc takes `tile_texture`
  and `world_tile` (the slot's tile_m); above 0 the colour is multiplied by
  the texture at the fragment's world xz over it, so planes of any size
  tile the same and the two planes' needles line up where they meet. Its
  own sampler, linear with mipmaps (the palette's albedo_texture is
  nearest).
- In season as the floor was: snow where it faces up, never dried or
  turned (leaf off); the see-through copy (SEASON_NEAR_META) carries the
  texture too.
- While the slot has no image (or isn't in the manifest yet), the flat
  NEEDLES as before: `PineStands.needles_texture` looks once (forget()
  looks again). `PineStands.needles_stand_in` lets view_test check the
  wiring with a texture made in code, so this lands before the art.
- Ring 1, the land's ground (ground.gdshader), keeps its ragged line into
  the forest floor unchanged; wiring ground.grass, dirt, sand and stone into
  that shader is a later step of its own.

Cost: one 512 x 512 texture with mipmaps (about 1.4 MB of video memory)
and one texture read on two planes that already exist. Client only; no
protocol change.

## 433. Level entities known by their marker cell in a snapshot

A save brought a level entity back by its spawn slot, its index in Level's
order (level.json's listed entries, then the markers by scan), with the
saved tile. A level that gains an entity before others moves every later
slot, so a saved goblin could come back as slot k's new spec, a chest, on
the goblin's tile. Found adding the temple's counter (424) to the wilds,
whose save on the box is Jeff's town. Approved by the coordinator; release
sequences it.
- A level entity's identity is its marker cell: Main._key_of(slot), "x,y"
  of its level spec's tile. Main._slot_spec puts it in the spawn spec as
  "spawn_key" beside "spawn"; Snapshot writes and reads it for entities and
  respawns, and a far record (352) keeps it in its entry.
- Each key and its slot are indexed once as the level is read
  (Main._index_keys, swapped with the zone), so a lookup costs nothing on
  a map of thousands of entities (perf's review).
- Loading finds a slot by key (Main._slot_for): an entity
  (_level_spec_for), a dead slot's timer, a record's slot. A key the level
  no longer has: the entity comes back as saved, holding no slot (its
  "spawn" dropped, so it cannot claim another's). Without a key (a save
  from before), by its index, as before, which is right while the level is
  as it was then; a record from before is given its key on loading, so the
  next save keeps it.
- Order: this ships and the box saves once with keys before any real level
  gains or reorders an entity (the wilds counter first). The server says
  so at its first save each run, "[state] saved N level entities, N keyed",
  for release, which may not read the save itself.
- Slots stay indices inside a run: _alive_slots, _dead_since. Names still
  come from Level's count (a gained chest renames the chests after it);
  nothing saved hangs on a name but the pre-slot fallback, and a thing's
  holder is set again from its entity on loading (World.set_slots).
tests/spawn_key_test (a level gains a listed chest before the rest: the
crates and chest back as themselves, the gained one new, Imp1's timer and
Imp2's record on their own slots; the level loses a crate's marker and the
saved crate comes back as saved in no slot; a save without keys by its
slots).
Snapshot only: the protocol is unchanged; old saves load.
Rejected: a free-slot table written into level.json (every editor and tool
would have to keep it); matching by name (names move with the count too).

- One job on a thing: Production's kind "work", {uids: [uid], to_id,

## 431. A server answers a status query before anyone joins

ui's menu and connect screen (418, 427) want to say whether the server is
there, its build and how full it is, before Play. Joining depends on
Net.protocol() (239), and Godot numbers RPCs by each node's methods, which
change between builds: a status RPC on Net would not work across them.

- A UDP exchange of its own (net/server_status.gd, ServerStatus, a new
  class_name): the client sends {"status": 1} padded to 512 bytes
  (ServerStatus.request); the server answers {"status", "version",
  "protocol", "players", "accepting"} and nothing else (no token, no
  names), never more bytes than the request held, and at most once a second
  per address (Responder), so it cannot amplify traffic. A short request,
  another "status" version or junk gets nothing.
- A server answers only when given --status-port (and only in --server
  mode): the box's unit gives 7779 and staging (server/stage.sh) the game
  port + 2, beside the admin console's TCP 7778/7788, which UDP does not
  clash with. Hosts and tests' servers never listen, so none takes a
  neighbour's port (net_test's phases run on ports one apart). ufw is
  inactive on the box: nothing to open.
- A client asks with Net.query_status(address, port) at --status-port or
  settings status_port=, else the game port + 2 (port_for); the answer
  comes once a query through Net.status_received(address, port, result):
  {ok: true, version, protocol, players, accepting, compatible (the same
  protocol, or a newer server it could update to)}, or {ok: false, why},
  "no answer" after 2 s (an old server, a blocked port, or none).

Joining is unchanged, so PROTOCOL_REVISION is too; the exchange is versioned
by its own "status" number. The unit change is not installed by deploy.sh
(its sudo covers install and systemctl restart only): Jeff copies
server/psykinetic.service to /etc/systemd/system and runs daemon-reload by
hand (docs/server.md), and until then the live server does not answer.
Clients cope: no answer within 2 s is "no answer" (ui shows "status
unknown"), and joining never depends on it.

tests/status_test.

Amended (2026-10-21, perf, found while making 450 amended): `--status-port`
was missing from the options `Net._parse_args` reads, so `_set_option`
never saw it and a server given it on the command line answered nothing.
tests/status_test sets the port in code, so it never ran into this. The box
journal had no "answering status on UDP" line in 7 days. The flag is now
read. tests/server_boot_test.sh passes `--status-port` to the exported
server and fails without the "answering status on UDP" line and the port
bound (on 127.0.0.1, beside 450 amended's `--bind`). It failed on the old
`net.gd` and passes now. Status answers on the box need both pieces: this
build, from the next release, and the installed unit with the flag. On
2026-10-21 the unit in /etc/systemd/system still lacked it, until Jeff's
`sudo cp` and daemon-reload (above). Server only; protocol unchanged.
