## 419. People from a tool of our own: one base body each, keyed, with parts, from a look

Jeff wants numerous town characters with different postures, statures, builds
and hair, and the candidate-mesh route (243's c4 bodies) gave a final product
unlike its candidates. So people's bodies are made by our own script,
tools/body_gen.py (Blender, headless): every vertex placed in code on the
Universal Animation Library's skeleton, which every humanoid clip already plays
on. A body is lofted rings (torso and tunic, sleeves, trousers, boots, mitten
hands, neck, a planar head with nose, brows, eyes and ears, belt, collar),
faceted, about 1,500 triangles; a man's and a woman's (her own proportions),
built at 1.75 m and scaled to the height (1.75, 1.66). The same tool makes the
parts a person may wear, each its own mesh on the same skeleton: three hair
styles (cropped, bound up with a bun, long), two beards, a hood, a brimmed
hat and an apron (100 to 250 triangles each). Seven shape keys (lean, heavy,
broad, narrow, hips, old, young) are the body and every part built again at
other proportions (a MORPH table on the stations' sizes): the same rings, so
the same vertices, exact, never pushed along normals; parts follow the keys
because they are built from the body's own rings. tools/body_build.py --parts
colours it by part as 243 amended (one material, the part one-hot in the
vertex colour, palette swatches for belt, boots, hats and the apron) and keeps
the keys. Both bodies live where 243's did (art/models/characters/human_m,
human_f), so nothing else moves.

A person is values, not a mesh: their spawn spec's "look", one string of
space-separated key=value words, each optional (seed, body, build, stature,
age, posture, shoulders, hair, hair_colour, beard, headwear, apron, skin),
agreed with npc (residents' card["look"], Main writes it; the apron from the
trade) and companions (CompanionCard.look_of). A new class_name, PersonLook,
turns it into a body, key values, a stature (the model's scale, its gaits'
paces scaled with it, so taller legs take longer strides), the parts shown,
the colours (an 8-step skin ramp, 8 hair colours, grey likelier when old) and
a posture. Whatever a look leaves out, the seed decides, the same on every
client; a key or value it does not know is passed over, so words can be added
without breaking older clients. Client3D.look_for reads it, else seeds one by
the entity's name; a player's body is their "body" (388) and they wear no
headwear or apron until the Character panel lets them choose. Residents are
drawn as people too (model_for). Posture is an additive pose on the person's
AnimRig (390's posture layer): Posture_Stooped and Posture_Slouch in the clip
library, authored by tools/humanoid_clips.py as the rest pose plus the bend, so
the layer adds the bend alone to whatever plays; a stooped old man walks
stooped.

Protocol: unchanged. "look" is a new spawn spec key older peers ignore and
whose absence means today's behaviour, and it is purely visual: the sim never
reads it. If anything in a look ever touches reach, collision or sight
(stature is the likeliest), that is a protocol revision. Cost: a person draws
their body and one to three parts, each a surface (perf, 2026-10-17: affordable,
rendering is about 2.5 ms of a 20 ms party frame; merging a person's chosen
parts at make time is the first fix if the budget bench says otherwise).
tools/body_sheet.gd draws looks (keys, scale, colours, parts) for sheets.
view_test checks a look's determinism, its words over the seed, the hood over
the hair, a resident drawn as its look, every part in both bodies with the
seven keys, the postures in the clips, and a player's body, parts, skin and
stature. Rejected: a mesh per person (memory grows with the town); TRELLIS
meshes per candidate (unlike their candidates, and narrow); a third-party base
body (Quaternius's: a superhero nude, painted clothes fail); shape keys by
pushing along normals (243's; a belt and an apron would part from the tunic).
Later: an orc base for the brute and a kobold base for the sneak from the same
tool (Jeff, via lore), and the player's Character panel.

Amended (the base pair's "shoulder tips", Jeff on its sheet): a sleeve's top end, its two
rings at the shoulder, now sits flatter and 1.8 cm lower, under the torso's shoulder line,
and the ring past the joint is half on the clavicle (Part.mixes): as high as the arm and
turning wholly with it, it stood above the shoulder as a ridge when the arm came down.
human_m, human_f (and 478's orc and kobold, the same sleeves) built again.
## 438. The counter's work: what can be done, ordered and collected; the reforge

On items' 432 (Items.reforge_cost, reforge_targets, ItemBook.reforge) and
434 (the work job, held things), for ui's counter screen. The
coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17. PROTOCOL_REVISION 14.

- The wire: the "counter" command rides the command RPC ({counter: path,
  do: "look" | "order" | "collect", slot, effect, to_id, uid}); the
  "counter" message answers it (MESSAGE_KINDS): {counter, kind ("temple"
  | "shop"), town, gold, jobs: [{slot, uid, id, effect, to_id, price,
  materials, steps, ok, why}], working: [{uid, id, effect, to_id, left,
  left_seconds}], waiting: [{uid, id, effect}], why}. Sent on every look,
  order and collect, and when a job of theirs finishes while they stand at
  a counter of that town (Production.work_done). Shop goods and offers
  stay in the "shop" message. A thing with nothing to be done has no job
  entry; one that could be but can't now has ok false and its why. The
  client keeps the last in Main.counter_data and emits counter_told.
- A temple counter offers a blessing for each thing carried, at 434's
  offering; ordering it is the same as dragging it on.
- A shop counter offers each allowed reforge of each thing carried
  (Items.reforge_targets): the town's materials (Items.reforge_cost's
  from, half the target's, at least 1 ore) from its stock, a fee from the
  player of reforge.fee (0.5) of the target's value, at least
  reforge.least (1), into the treasury, and the cost's steps by the
  smith at his forge (Towns.kind_for). Refused, with why: an unnamed
  thing ("only a named thing can be reforged"), no smith there, the town
  short of a material, the fee. THE FEE IS A PLACEHOLDER, JEFF'S TO TUNE
  (economy.json "reforge").
- The work: Production.open_work(..., to_id, materials, steps, fee,
  payer), effect "reforge"; at the finish ItemBook.reforge(uid, to_id) on
  the same uid (its name, curse, bane, grudge, blessing and tally kept,
  items'). If it refuses then, the materials go back to the town and Main
  gives the fee back from the treasury; the thing is held for its owner
  either way.
- Collecting: "collect" puts a thing held for them into their first free
  slot that their hands allow (World.counter_collect), at either counter
  of the town; the temple counter still shows them in its slots too.

Protocol changed: the client goes first. tests/blessing_test (the temple
counter's view; at a shop counter an unnamed dagger refused with why, the
fee refused, a target it can't become refused, the order taken and paid,
being worked on with seconds left, reforged on the same uid with its name,
waiting, collected, nothing waiting); protocol_test.
## 429. A cleared camp falls

Nothing in play called Holdings.take, so a camp never changed hands and
economy's rescues (428, Towns.camp_taken on place_taken) never fired.

- Main looks at its zone's camps every CAMP_CHECK_TICKS (10): a camp with
  no living monster of its holder's side (Factions.same_side of the kind's
  faction, decision 416: orcs and kobolds defend the Blood Rot's) within
  its radius + CAMP_DEFEND_MARGIN (2), and a player within its radius, for
  CAMP_FALL_TICKS (100, 10 s), falls: Holdings.take(id, "nobody"), so
  place_taken fires and economy frees who it held. The party log: "The
  Blood Rot's camp falls." (display name; " at <name>" when the place has
  one of its own). Leaving, or a defender coming, starts the clock again;
  it is not saved. A sleeping zone's camp never falls.
- A cleared camp stays cleared: _check_respawns (382) skips a dead slot
  whose spawn tile is in a camp of its zone its kind's side no longer
  holds. Retaken (economy's restock, Holdings.take back), its slots come
  due again, staggered as any.
- A fallen camp sends no raids and counts for no hunting (Holdings.camps
  skips nobody's). A raid group coming home to a camp its side no longer
  holds breaks up (WorldRaids._arrive): Towns.free_held(group id) frees its
  captives (428), and what it took is left at the camp (_stow).
- The town does not take a camp (it goes to nobody): the town's claim on
  ground is economy's, later. Protocol unchanged.

tests/camp_fall_test (the test room with a camp laid round its imp),
raid_groups_test's home to a fallen camp.
Amended (2026-10-18, the coordinator): the voice is told "Tam told you at the
well that the mine is cursed." (Hearsay.prompt_words), not "At the well, Tam
told you that": the first transcript had Mara answer "You heard from Tam at
the well ...", the sentence's opening "You have heard" pulling her into the
second person.

## 437. The ground's kinds drawn with their own textures

The ground (ground.gdshader) drew each kind, grass, dirt, stone and sand,
from its palette colour and noise; the slots ground.grass, dirt, stone and
sand (art-kit: textures, tile_m 4, 512 px) had no reader. Art-gen's
candidates for them wait on Jeff's picks; this lands first, so each kind
switches over by itself when its picture is in. The coordinator approved
the design.

- `Client3D._ground_material` sets, for each kind (`GROUND_KINDS`, the
  kinds texture's r, g, b, a), `<kind>_tex` and `<kind>_own` from
  `Client3D.ground_texture` (ArtKit.texture("ground.<kind>")), and
  `kind_tiles` from the slots' tile_m. The floors' textures (floor.<set>,
  285) were already read this way.
- With art, a kind's look is its texture at world xz over its tile, under
  a slow swell (fbm at 0.18 a metre, 0.86 to 1.14) so the 4 m repeat
  doesn't read as a grid from the game camera. Read with textureGrad from
  the pixel's derivatives worked out before the kinds' branches, so the
  mipmap is right where kinds meet. Without art, its procedural look as
  before, untouched.
- Everything over the kinds is the same either way: the ragged borders and
  blend between kinds, grass's yellow patches, drying and autumn, wet by
  water, the forest's edge, light and heat, snow, and the floor sets.
- The forest's edge (the land running into the forest floor along a
  ragged line) blends to the forest floor's own look: past pine stands
  (369) their NEEDLES, and 423's ground.needles texture once it has art,
  so the land's edge meets the ForestFloor plane beyond it with no step;
  without stands the dark forest colour as before. The edge's needles are
  EDGE_NEEDLES_DARK (0.3) darker: the edge lies in the sun, the floor
  beyond in the canopy's shade, and at full strength the edge read as a
  bright clay path along the trees (wilds shots).
- Held back until real art shows a repeat: a second read of each texture
  turned about 37 degrees at another scale, blended by noise (twice the
  reads where that kind shows).
- `Client3D.ground_stand_ins` lets view_test check the wiring with
  textures made in code.

Cost: five samplers more (13 of 16); one texture read a kind where it
shows (two where kinds meet), only once that kind has art; about 1.4 MB of
video memory a 512 x 512 texture. Client only; no protocol change.
Amended (economy, 2026-10-17): 428's restock only gives a camp new
strangers once it is hostile again; nothing took a fallen camp back. Maps
does: Holdings remembers who held a fallen camp (fell_from, saved in the
snapshot, forgotten once anyone holds it; fallen_camps()), and on the world
tick Main._retake_camps gives it back to them once economy.json's
rescue.restock_days (5) have passed since it fell, with no player standing
in it, so it is retaken as economy restocks it, and its slots come back.
Amended (2026-10-18, companions' 442: a companion's beliefs as hearsay):
a companion resting in town (her worker record "companion:<name>" in the
town and not away, with her heard, intellect and superstition copied onto
it by companions) stands in gossip groups like anyone (Townsfolk.gossip no
longer skips her id; _pass takes an empty card): as teller she passes only
what she believes, having no card facts; as hearer there is no kin-first
and no grudge check, which read the card; she hears a scholar's lore pass

## 435. Conversation offers: what a town's person has for you, from records only

The data side of ui's step 4 (the conversation panel: who speaks, what
they offer, the exchange), the coordinator's approval 2026-10-18, shapes
agreed with ui. A resident spoken to has at most three things to offer
(Offers.of, sim/offers.gd; residents.json "offers"), each from a record
and never invented, in this order and one of each kind: a shop line (a
thing in the town's shop that this resident's trade makes, economy's
price: "I have a knife at the counter for 12 gold"); one true commission
(the first that holds: kin on the card held captive (Towns.captives) to
be brought home from the camp that holds them; a camp of a faction hostile
to the town (Holdings.camps) to be cleared, from one whose card says they
saw raiders; a thing the town is short of (Production.signals_of) to be
fetched to the store, six of it); a rumour (the newest believed hearsay as
told, "Tam told me at the well that the mine is cursed"; an official
offers the weightiest lore fact it knows instead, never hearsay, 378); and
a plea (help with a loan, through economy's pay_loan, else a word carried
to a neighbour the resident holds a grudge against). Each offer is {id
("<worker>|<kind>|<key>"), kind, title (three or four words for the
panel's button), words (the resident's sentence), what (the record),
accept ("buy", "take", "lend", "carry", ""), cost}.

Accepting: "buy" sells the thing at the town's counter when the player
stands at one (World.try_buy, answered as the shop is); "take" and "carry"
put an ask on the resident's card ("asks", saved with the worker record,
398) and on the player's record ("commissions", PlayerRecord), at most one
open per resident and offers.per_player (3) per player, as a fact on the
card ("Jeff promised Mara: to bring Bram home"); "lend" pays the loan down
through economy. A commission is met from the world's own signals, with
no model call (Offers.watch): a rescue when Towns.rescued names the
captive, a camp when Holdings.place_taken moves it off its faction, in
both the player standing in the camp's area (else it closes unpaid, "kept
by another", said honestly); a fetch when economy's Stockpile.deposited
counts the player's own banking to the number. Met, economy pays the
player from the town's treasury (pay_commission, economy.json
"commissions": rescue 10, camp 20, fetch 1 a unit; economy's 60aaf7b),
the card gains the fact, the party log says. An errand is met when the
player next speaks to the one it is for: the grudge is dropped from both
cards and both gain the fact, which gossip (422) may pass on. An ask not
met in offers.days (7) lapses with a fact told once. The voice is told the
offers as facts, never lines ("What you can offer Jeff, if it comes up:
..."; "Jeff promised to bring Bram home and has not yet."), in
Resident.facts_now while the ask is being made.

Wire: a server message kind "offers" {entity, speaker, offers}, sent to
the player with each answer that resident gives them, when the panel opens
on a resident within earshot (the client's "offers" command {entity}) and
after every accept; accepting is the "offer" command {id} or {id, gold}
(commands ride the existing request RPC, which protocol() cannot see, so
the two new verbs take PROTOCOL_REVISION 15, after economy's 14; the new
MESSAGE_KINDS entry changes the fingerprint too). ui draws the panel; npc
owns the data, the two commands, the accept handling and the voice facts.

offers_test (pure sim: a context of callables stands in for the world;
no port, no scratch): nothing from nothing; the shop line for the trade's
own making; each commission from its record and their order; the rumour
and the official's lore fact; the plea and economy's lend; the cap and the
order; a commission taken, listed as open, refused twice and by the
per-player cap, met with the player there and paid, met by another and
not; a fetch counted from the player's own deposits; an errand met by
speaking, the grudge dropped both ways; the lapse; the voice's facts.
resident_test's round trip is covered by the existing voice cases (the
offers ride with the answer). Protocol changed (revision 15); new class_name
Offers.

Rejected: free-text commissions from the model (invented); offers from
residents with no body (the panel is for one you stand before); more than
three (the panel stays small and the card true); a quest log of its own
(the commission lives on the card and the player's record, and shows in
the panel and the party log); crediting a rescue or a camp to a player
who was elsewhere.

Amended (art's credits, art-kit, release's ask): ArtKit.credits is the second
provider ("Art: Kenney, Quaternius"). Its entries:
- each source in slots.json's "sources" that a slot is filled from now;
- then slots.json's new "credits", third-party parts inside our own art that
  no fill names. One is listed while a slot it names draws its own art, or
  always when it names none: the Quaternius Pig's rig and clips in
  creature.boar, and for now the Universal Animation Library, the humans'
  and the goblin's clips, until the animations have a provider of their own.
Our own and generated art have no line. art_kit_test checks the list;
view_test counts the links across every provider.
Amended (2026-10-18, Jeff, through the coordinator): "try to minimize quests
that are just 'go get object A from location B'", and "if those types of
quests exist, make them so they are auto completed, no need to talk to the
NPC first. Just give player a notice that it was completed and the reward,
and the NPC will remember they completed it." So: the fetch commission is
no longer offered; what the town is short of stays talk (the voice has
signals_of), and a player who banks it is paid then and there (economy's
pay_commission, the fetch rate a unit) with the party-log notice ("The store
was short of wood; Mara's thanks. The town pays 4 gold.") and a point of
standing on every resident's card (443). And no commission needs accepting:
the event that would complete one completes it whether or not it was taken
on, with the notice and the pay: kin home with the player in the camp's area
(Offers.rescued pays the rescuers once and the kin's cards remember), a camp
falling with the player there (Offers.camp_taken pays from every town the
camp's faction threatened whose people saw raiders), a word carried (the
errand, which is the ask itself). "Take it on" in the panel only records
interest and keeps the ask open on the card; an open ask still closes as
before. Commissions come from people and what is between them (kin, a camp,
a word, a loan; later a dispute for the lawspeaker, sick kin to the healer,
someone walked home); the rule is in Offers' header and residents.json
"offers", so no future kind is a fetch. offers_test and standing_test follow.

Amended 2026-10-19 (the soak, 496): the promise in words (Offers._promise,
in the party log's lapse and taking lines) has its own words for an escort
("to walk Tam home", 487) and a quarrel ("to lay the quarrel with Bram
before the lawspeaker", 486), so a name keeps its case; before, a title was
lower-cased whole ("walk tam home").

## 440. The scholar and the merchant: what the last two hidden types do on the side

Step 2's last two (393: a hidden type per resident, what it does beyond
speech designed one at a time), the coordinator's approval 2026-10-18.
Neither had ever been rolled: lore's roles.json held scholar and merchant
as drafts and Townsfolk.roll_type draws only Lore.types() (the agreed),
though townsfolk.json weighted them. Lore marks the two ids agreed on
Jeff's own words ("same for scholar, merchant etc."); their profile values
stay draft until Jeff confirms the table, so under lore's rule a scholar or
merchant still speaks with townsfolk's profile, while these side-doings run
on the type alone.

The scholar knows more: the voice's lore budget is doubled (residents.json
"lore_chars": {"scholar": 1200}, Resident.world_facts; others keep
LORE_CHARS 600), so they tell more of what lore knows; their offer (435)
is a lore fact ("What Odo knows"), as an official's is, never hearsay,
though as townsfolk they may still believe and repeat rumours when asked;
and in gossip (422) a scholar passes a lore fact the hearer has not heard
before any belief, as "witnessed" (true, believed), one per pass, so what
the scholar knows walks through the town over the days. The temple hour
(404) stays.

The merchant trades sharper: economy's Economy.folk_factor(worker_id,
side) (economy's d573a97, economy.json "merchant" buy 0.85, sell 1.15) on
their own meals, store food, inn bed and paid services, and on their own
making sold folk to folk; the difference is the seller's, never the
treasury's tax; nothing for players' prices (shops are the town's, 353).
In offers (435) a merchant's shop line covers any good at the counter, the
dearest first, since they deal in everything, and their rumour prefers
hearsay of goods and prices (a word test on the believed text: price,
gold, sell, short, coin, cost), else the newest.

townsfolk_test: the roll draws scholars and merchants once agreed, with
the file's weights, and a weighted type lore does not know is never
rolled. gossip_test: the scholar's lore pass, witnessed and believed by
the sharpest, before a belief. offers_test: the scholar's lore offer; the
merchant's any-good line, dearest first, and price-first rumour. Protocol
unchanged; no new class_name.

Rejected: a merchant who trades with players at private prices; a scholar
who knows draft lore (lore's status rules stand); a scholar who repeats
no rumours at all (they are townsfolk, not officials).
## 425. A frame's walks over every entity cut: a no-copy read, far puppets looked at every fourth frame, door marks kept

Measured on map_bench's 256 x 256 dungeon (about 2,900 entities) with
players standing together: the median frame 29.5 ms with 8 players and
24.4 ms with 2, rendering under 2 ms of it; Godot's script profiler (a
stand-in for the editor's, on the remote debugger) put most of the rest in
walks over every entity each frame. World.get_entities() copies the zone's
list; Client3D._sync_puppets walked such a copy every frame, each
_local_player (Main's and Client3D's, several calls a frame) and the
minimap's marks walked another. World.entities() now reads the list itself
(not a copy: for code that neither spawns nor despawns while going
through it; get_entities() is as it was for the rest), _sync_puppets uses
it, and _local_player and the marks go through the roster (World.sought(),
the players and companions). A puppet left far off (outside the view's
reach, decision 312's) is looked at again every FAR_EVERY (4) frames,
staggered by its id, not every frame, its body checked only near, and the
mouse's pick (monster_near_ray) skips far ones. The minimap's door marks
(about 1,900 on that map) are made again every DOOR_MARKS_FRAMES (30)
frames and at every level's rebuild, not every frame, and Minimap._draw
skips marks off the part it shows before placing them. After: 11.3 ms with
8 players, about 14 with 2. Rejected: caching _local_player for a frame (a
player spawned or gone in that frame would be missed); events for doors
coming and going (more wiring for what half a second late does not show).
## 408. The raid handover is tested on the real pieces, before any real camp

No real level has a camp yet, so WorldRaids (328) has never handed a group to
World.raids (313) outside a stand-in. raid_groups_test's two strips (a goblin
camp, the town's store) now also run in play for real: the town strip loaded
into World, real Holdings, Towns and WorldRaids hooked to the real World.raids,
the town's area live. A group sent walks the world map into the town area and
becomes real raiders about the cell the world tick had it at (it is already
some steps in, not at the edge), as strong as the group; they march on the
store and raid it (Towns.raid_arrives: food, and Dag carried off); WorldRaids
hears raid_done; they march back to where they came in, leave play
(raid_left) and the group walks home on the world map without coming back
into play, its captive held at the camp. A second group, every raider struck
down, is beaten (raid_beaten) and gone from the world map too.

- A test, no game change: the same scene, port and scratch name. The check
  through a real area (a held camp in a real level, a headless host with
  --raids and the console's raids send) waits for Jeff or maps to place one.
- Seen while writing it: Towns carries a resident off by the numbers here
  because Towns.in_play is unset here; in a real game Main sets it, and
  raiders' blows take people instead (331).

tests/raid_groups_test.

## 411. Monsters bash with their shields (the AI side of 379)

Items' shield bash (379: World.try_bash, bash_ready, a shove and a stagger,
no damage, a guard up against it opened) is the player's and any monster's;
when a monster uses it is enemy-ai's. Approved by the coordinator with the
design.

- Fighting (Monster._bash_guard): a shield-bearer whose bash is ready, its
  target beside it with a guard up against it (World.guarding: a raised
  shield turned to it, or a sword ready), bashes instead of its blow; the
  guard is opened and its next blows land. It never bashes an open foe: a
  bash does no damage, and against one with no guard a blow is better. In
  the plain fight and the tactics' alike, before the flanker's walk round a
  guard (a bash beats going round).
- Fleeing (Monster._bash_free): cornered (no step away), a shield-bearer
  with its bash ready bashes a foe beside it, to shove it off and stagger it,
  then runs on; without a shield it waits a moment, as before. Any fleer,
  not only cowards: only the unbold flee, and a cornered cautious one would
  do the same. A light monster cannot shove a heavy foe (the force falls
  under knockback_min_force), so then the bash only staggers it: a few ticks
  free of its blows, not a way out.
- Its own raised shield goes down for the bash's moment (379's
  bash_moment_until), as a player's does.

tests/monster_test (_test_monster_bash).

## 412. Monsters wind up heavy weapons and meet a foe's wind-up (the AI side of 392)

Items' wind-up (392: World.try_wind_up, winding, windup_ticks, a crushing
blow that breaks any guard, struck by World when due) is the player's and
any monster's; when a monster uses it, and what it does about one aimed at
it, is enemy-ai's. Approved by the coordinator with items' design.

- A monster holding a weapon that winds up (World.windup_ticks over 0: the
  giant axe) winds its blow up with World.try_wind_up wherever it would
  strike (Monster._strike, _blow), and stands while World.winding says it
  is winding: no step, no other blow, till World strikes it. A HEAVY
  monster (the brute) with one uses only that, not its own bare-handed
  wind-up (Monster._windup), which is unchanged and still blockable.
- Its target winding up at it (Monster._meet_wind_up): in that blow's
  reach, a shield-bearer with its bash ready bashes (379, 411; the stagger
  gives the wind-up up); else one not bold steps out of reach (_step_back)
  and keeps out till the blow has fallen, then closes again; a bold one,
  or one with nowhere to step, fights on and takes it. The bash comes
  before temper: even a bold shield-bearer stops a blow it can.
- Nothing new on the wire: the views already wind up from GridEntity.winding.

tests/monster_test (_test_monster_wind_up, _test_meets_wind_up).

## 420. Monsters dread their kind's bane and seek its grudge-bearers (the AI side of 415 and 417)

Items keeps each thing's tally of kinds felled (415) and makes a thing the
bane of a kind it has felled enough of, or gives it a grudge against the kind
its holder fell to (417: World.holder_bane, holder_grudge, kind_of). How a
kind takes them is enemy-ai's, as items and the coordinator meant it.

- Its kind's bane in its target's hands, a monster dreads it whatever its
  temper, a beast too (Monster._dreads_target): the dread of 371 (the
  cautious wait for two and break sooner, a coward counts it as two) and the
  hold-back of any below HOLD_BACK_BELOW or dreading, so even a bold one
  waits for its side before it closes. 371's dread weapons stay for the
  unbold and unbeastly only; a bane is one kind's own fear.
- It notices that bearer Items.growth's bane_notice (1.5) times farther: by
  sight (Monster._nearest_visible_target, through Senses.sees' new farther
  times its range), and by hearing (World.noise: a noise its bearer makes
  is heard that much farther by monsters of that kind alone, World.banes_held).
  The look's early end (nobody within its sight) is skipped while any bearer
  of its kind's bane is in the zone.
- One bearing a grudge against its kind it goes for first when it sees them,
  near or far, over the nearest and the one it kept.
- The bearers are looked up once a tick a kind (Monster._marks), not each
  look. A kindless monster (no spawn kind) has no bane and no grudge, guarded
  here as well as in holder_bane and holder_grudge (items' fix to 417: an
  empty kind once matched every thing with none).
- The numbers are items' (bane_after, bane_notice in levels/items.json
  "growth"): Jeff has yet to say whether a bane should cost stealth or a
  grudge draw too much fire, so nothing here is fixed in code.

tests/monster_test (_test_bane_and_grudge).
## 442. A companion's own beliefs are hearsay, weighed as a resident's

Phase 2 of 378 (the coordinator's design, approved 2026-10-17). A player's
lie to a companion was kept as her belief, on her card, from the
extraction's say-so; a resident weighed the same lie by its intellect
(378) and passed it on at the well (422). Now she hears as they do.

Her card rolls "leanings" {intellect, superstition}, 1..10, by a seed of
their own, so the rest of her traits roll as before;
CompanionCard.leaning(traits, seed, key) gives a card from before them
from her seed, with nothing saved. Wren, Nix and Pip have fixed ones
(companion_traits.json, drafts for Jeff: Wren 7 and 4, Nix 8 and 3, Pip 4
and 8, young and eager to believe). Her card is written without them.

A line said near her (within HEARING_RANGE: her player's, another
player's, a companion's, a resident's) waits for one claims ask, at most
one per claims_ticks, keyed "pet:<player id>" in Main's _claims_asks
queue on the resident mind (its facts channel; her own voice's Claude, if
any, sends voice asks only). The ask is Hearsay.claims_ask with her as
one "who travels with <player>" (a new optional who_is), shown what lore
says she knows and what is true of her. Each claim goes through
Hearsay.hear on her leanings into her player record's "heard" (the same
shape, cap and curves as a resident's), on her too (Companion.heard); her
voice is told Hearsay.prompt_words: "Jeff told you that the mine is
cursed", never as fact. The extraction (CompanionFacts) no longer takes
beliefs: what is said of the world is left out of it; beliefs saved
before stay as they are and are still told.

Staying in town she is a resident ("companion:<name>"): what she heard
and her leanings go onto that worker record (set_heard, and
Production.set_mind, new), so npc's gossip (422 amended: Townsfolk.gossip
takes a resting companion as teller and hearer; she has no card, so she
passes hearsay only, kin and grudges aside) reaches her; when she leaves
with her player again, what her worker record heard comes back to her
record. resident_test covers it: intellect 1 believes and says it as
hearsay, intellect 10 keeps it unbelieved and says nothing, neither is a
belief or a fact on her card, her leanings reach her worker record in
town and what she heard at the well comes back with her. Protocol
unchanged.

Rejected: a claims ask on her own facts mind (the same local model; one
queue keeps the asks apart in time); keeping her extracted beliefs beside
the hearsay (two stores of the same thing, and the extracted one took a
lie whole).

Fixed (2026-10-17, release): PlayerRecord.from_dict rebuilt her record
from a list of keys and made every trait a word, so a load dropped her
"heard" and her "home" (381) and turned her look (293 amended) and
leanings into text. It keeps them now (PlayerRecord.TABLE_TRAITS), and
reads back as tables a look or leanings already saved as text; text that
is no table is dropped and her seed gives them. to_dict always wrote them
as they were, so nothing was lost before a load. companion_test's round
trip covers a record as v0.1.150 saves it, one with the tables as text,
and one from before them.
## 436. The conversation panel: who speaks, the exchange, their offers

Roadmap `ui`, step 4's first landing (the coordinator approved the design
merged with npc's offers, 435; residents speak when spoken to, 336). Talking
to a town's person was typed lines and bubbles: nothing showed who you were
talking to, what had been said, or what they had to offer.

- `ConversePanel` (render/converse_panel.gd, new class_name): a narrow box
  at the left, the world and the bubbles untouched. Who speaks (the
  resident's person and trade, never the hidden type; the label over their
  head when the body has no person yet), "thinking" with moving dots while
  their answer is out (from the line sent until their speech comes, or
  THINKING_FOR 15 s, 336's wait: the ask queue is not sent), the exchange
  with them alone (the player's lines and theirs, the last MAX_LINES 8), and
  three quick asks that are ordinary chat lines their voice answers ("What
  do you sell?", "Any work for me?", "What's the news?"), with Close.
- Opened by Main.open_converse: E tapped on a resident within HEARING_RANGE
  (the same key that opens things), or a line said to one (336's rule,
  Main._resident_addressed read on the client too: the nearest in earshot or
  the one named, never the player's companion); Esc closes it first of all.
- The offers: npc's "offers" message (435) {entity, speaker, offers:
  [{id, kind shop|commission|rumour|plea, title, words, what, accept, cost,
  open}]}, sent when the panel opens (the client's "offers" command naming
  the body), with each answer to the player, and after an accept. Drawn one
  flat list in the order sent: the kind as a small word, the title in the
  serif, the words under it, the cost in brass, and the accept's button
  ("Buy", "Take it on", "Lend" with a slider up to the loan, "Carry it";
  none for a rumour), which sends npc's "offer" {id} ({id, gold} for lend).
  Offers marked open (an accepted commission) are listed as what the player
  owes them. Both commands go only when "offers" is in Net.MESSAGE_KINDS, so
  the panel works before and after 435 lands; the resident's speech fills
  the exchange either way.
- Maps' status caption: {ok: false, why: "no answer"} reads "status unknown"
  (older servers never answer; the join never depends on it).

Client only; nothing on the wire from ui (the message kinds are npc's).
tests/ui_test: the panel's name, exchange, thinking, offers, the accept
signals, the asks, Esc; the status words. `--test-show=converse` opens the
panel on the nearest resident with sample offers (a test's words). The
counter screen (economy's job, decision 434) is step 4's second landing.

## 439. A player chooses their look: the Character section, sent with the join

A player picks how they look in the options panel's Character section, which
replaces 388's Body drop-down: their body (Man, Woman), then build, height,
hair, beard (a man's) as rows of toggle buttons, hair colour and skin as rows of
swatches, a "Surprise me" (a new seed, everything else left to it), and a live
preview: their body as their look makes it (419's PersonLook on the human
bodies), idling and turning slowly in a SubViewport of its own world, framed as
a slot box (CharacterPreview, 440 x 640 HUD units, drawn only while the panel
shows). Layout agreed with ui (its _choice_row, its swatch style); sound, which
owns the panel, agreed. A pick is written at once, with the seed it was seen
with, so what was shown is what others see: settings.cfg "look", beside
"body" (Net.player_look); it is sent with the next join as a new hello field,
"look", as 388's "body" is, and the server keeps it on the PlayerRecord (saved;
an older record has none and is seeded by name, as 419 has it) and puts it in
the player's spawn spec as "look", where Client3D.look_for reads it (seeded by
the name where it names no seed; a player wears no headwear or apron).

A look comes from any client and goes to every other, so the server cleans it
before keeping it (Net.tidy_look, release's requirement): only the words a
player may choose (PersonLook.PLAYER_CHOICES: seed, build, stature, hair,
hair_colour, beard, skin), each once, each with a value it knows (a seed a whole
number from 0 under 10 digits), at most MAX_LOOK_LENGTH (160) characters; the
rest is dropped. respawn_test checks the look asked for, kept, saved, spawned,
drawn, and junk, repeats and huge text cleaned; view_test drives the section
(the body, a build, a skin, the preview following, Surprise me).

Protocol: unchanged (release's ruling): an optional hello field older servers
ignore, whose absence means 419's seeded look, as "body"; and a spawn spec key,
purely visual (419). Rejected: replicating the look as a property (a protocol
change, and the look, like the body, shows from the next join); letting the
client's words through as they are (a hand-edited settings.cfg would send junk
or huge text to everyone).
## 443. Standing: what each of the town's people thinks of each player

The coordinator's approval 2026-10-18, on the cards (398), gossip (422)
and the offers (435); companions' bond with her player takes the same
shape through the same class (444, after this). A per-player score on the
card, moved only by the world's own events, never by a model: card
["standing"] = {player_id: {score, met (the step of their first words),
since (the last change), why (the last three reasons, plain clauses
without the player's name: "brought Bram home"), own (whether any reason
is their own event, not hearsay)}}; saved with the worker record; a card
from before has none. New class Standing (sim/standing.gd), all static,
on any Dictionary that holds "standing" (a resident's card, a companion's
record): met, first_words, bump, heard, score, words, fact, decay;
numbers in residents.json "standing".

The words come from the score through a ladder: Standing.RESIDENT
(stranger: no entry, they have never spoken; wronged: -3 and down; known:
-2..2, from the first words; trusted: 3 and up) or Standing.COMPANION
(fond to start, wary, close from 3, devoted from 6), each word with its
sentence frame. The voice is told one fact (Resident.facts_now, 336's rule:
a fact, never a line): "You trust Jeff: they brought Bram home." / "Jeff
wronged you: they let a promise lapse, to bring Bram home." / "You have
met Jeff before." / for a stranger nothing, and on their first words "This
is the first time Jeff has spoken to you." (Main._ask_resident makes the
entry), so the greeting falls out of the facts. A companion's bond fact
goes in her prompt the same way (444).

What moves it, each through a hook 435 and 422 already had, the amounts
data: a commission met +3 (a rescue +4), lapsed -2 (an errand -1); kin
brought home with the player in a camp's area +4 even with no commission
(Offers.rescued, the kin on the card, the players in a camp's area by
Main's players_in); a loan paid down +1 per quarter of what was owed and
+2 when it is cleared (the lend accept); a word carried +2 on both cards
(Offers.spoke_to); a gift +1, +2 for their favourite food or a tool: a
thing a player puts into a resident's hands by the transfer that exists
(World.try_transfer with a Resident as "to"; World.handed, Main._on_handed:
the thing goes to the town's store in the resident's name, so nothing is
lost, and Offers.gift moves the card); a raid fought off with the player
in the town's area +1 on every resident's card (Townsfolk._raided, the
repelled report; once per raid); being caught taking from the store: the
sim has no verb for a player taking from a store (only the shop and the
thief's lift), so the hook is named here (a Stockpile take with a player's
by_id, -4) and left for when such a verb exists. The score is held within
-10..10. Hearsay (Standing.heard) moves it by 1 only for one with no
dealings of their own with that player, and never past 2 either way.

Gossip (422): after a scholar's lore and before beliefs, a teller's view
of a player that is strong (trusted or wronged) and their own passes as
"Jeff brought Bram home" (the newest reason, with the player's name), kept
by the hearer as witnessed hearsay from the teller, and the hearer's
standing leans the teller's way by one (heard), so the town's view of a
player spreads from those who dealt with them. Decay: on Townsfolk's
gossip tick, every residents' card entry older than decay_days (10) since
its last change moves one step toward 0, so trust fades and wrongs are
slowly forgiven; a companion's record is swept only by companions, while
she is apart from her player (444).

Offers (435) scaled by the word: wronged, nothing but a plea (and the
open asks); known, as before; trusted, the commission before the shop line
and a second open commission allowed from that resident. Nothing on the
wire: the "offers" message is unchanged (the panel sees the order; the
words reach the player through the voice).

standing_test (pure sim, a context of callables; no port, no scratch):
the words by score and by both ladders, the facts, the first words, each
event's move (a rescue by them and by another, a lapse, a fetch, a word on
both cards, a loan by quarters and cleared, gifts plain and favourite, kin
home with no commission, a raid with and without the player), hearsay's
small move and its stop at their own dealings, the gossip pass, decay and
Townsfolk's sweep, the offers' three orders. Protocol unchanged; new
class_name Standing.

Rejected: a model judging what a player deserves (events only); a town-wide
reputation number (it is each person's, and spreads only by gossip);
standing on the wire; scripted greetings (a fact, and the model greets);
crediting a rescue or a camp to a player who was elsewhere.
## 449. Farms: a field, a farmer, and a crop through the seasons

Jeff (2026-10-17): "i wanted to add farms and farmers too - tune with
seasons". The coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17. On 362 (seasons:
Season.name_at, season_days 7, so a year of 28 days), 384 (town weather:
Weather.rain_between, storms_between) and 428 (rescues).

- The field: economy.json buildings.field (trade farmer, built by the
  carpenter, wood 6, 3000 steps, max level 3), a town building like the
  kitchen. Its slot building.field (a fenced 4x4, open air), prefab and art
  are buildings' and art-kit's.
- The crop, on the town record ("crop", saved), moved on the town tick:
  spring, sown by the farmer's crop.sow_steps (3000) of work at the field
  (Production.manned "<town>:field"); summer, growth a day clamp(base 0.7
  + rain 3.0 x the day's rain, least 0.4, most 1.3) / season_days, and each
  storm over the town (Towns.storms; Main: storms_between, strength at its
  climate's storm_min, by storm id) flattens half the growth so far with
  chance crop.flatten (0.5), its step kept ("flattened") for the field's
  look later; autumn, brought in by crop.harvest_steps (3000) of work as
  crop.harvest x the field's level x growth food into the store; not by
  winter, it rots; winter, crop.roots x level food dug once. A season with
  no farmer leaves the crop as it is. All the numbers are in economy.json
  "crop" for Jeff to tune the year.
- The farmer: a trade (rescue.trades, weight 3, by 428), or by growth: a
  town whose field has stood growth_days (5) with no farmer gets a newcomer
  (origin "growth", named from crop.names). His day at the field is npc's.
- The field's look (sown, growing, ripe, flattened, bare: art-kit's state
  nodes) is not sent to clients yet: record-only now, a protocol step with
  buildings later.

The year, from the 90-day balance run of the wilds town (nine residents
with one farmer and one hunter, no players; tables in
C:/dev/review/balance30): at harvest 150 and roots 20 (the first numbers)
the town went hungry about half the time even in normal years, a year's
harvest eaten in two weeks against the 252 food nine people eat in 28
days. At harvest 260 and roots 30: a normal year (growth about 0.87) feeds
the town from the harvest to the next summer; a year whose crop storms
flattened (0.25), and every bad year (no rain and a storm: growth 0.40),
goes hungry before the next harvest. Every run starts hungry for its first
two weeks, before any harvest: a town's starting food (start_food, like
start_gold) is Jeff's to choose.

Protocol unchanged. tests/farm_test (a normal year, a drought, a summer
storm, level 2 twice, saved and loaded, unsown with the farmer away in
spring, rotted with him away in autumn, a farmer coming by growth).
## 446. The "world" message: what each player's world map knows

ui's world map (its step 5; 445 reads this) draws areas, ways and places
from WorldMap.build on the client, but who holds what, what the player has
seen and where the party is in other zones are the server's.

- Known: a PlayerRecord keeps known_areas and known_places (sorted, saved;
  an old record knows nothing yet), so it follows the player between
  machines. An area is known once they stand in it; a place once they come
  within 7 cells of its cell (Senses' sight range). Main looks at every
  player every 10 ticks (WorldNews.observe), once a tick for all zones.
- The message, Net kind "world", to one player (net/world_news.gd,
  WorldNews, a new class_name): {"full": bool, "holdings": {place_id:
  [faction, strength]}, "known": {"areas", "places"}, "party": [{name,
  area, kind: player|companion}]}. Full once they are in; then only what
  changed: newly known areas and places with the holdings of the places
  just learned; a known place taken or its strength changed
  (Holdings.strength_changed, which take emits too), to the players who
  know it only; the party again when it differs from the last sent. Never
  on a timer otherwise.
- Fog: holdings go only for places the player knows.
- Party: every player in the game and each companion, without the receiver
  and without anyone in the receiver's zone (those bodies are replicated).
- Client: Main.world_state ({holdings, known_areas, known_places, party},
  WorldNews.merge; a full message starts it again) and signal
  world_changed. A host's own map is told directly.

A new MESSAGE_KINDS entry: Net.protocol() changes and the server needs the
next release; PROTOCOL_REVISION stays (release: nothing existing changes
meaning, and no client request is added).

tests/world_news_test.

## 451. Attach points: what a hand holds is drawn in it

Roadmap #244: people and goblins hold what is in their hands. Each humanoid
model has sockets on its skeleton (Client3D._sockets, a "sockets" size table
on HUMAN, HUMAN_F and the goblin's MODELS): hand_r and hand_l on RightHand and
LeftHand, back on UpperChest, belt_l on Hips, each a BoneAttachment3D with the
socket a node under it at a place in the bone's frame, scaled back by the
model's scale so what it holds keeps its own size. The bones are the
retargeted SkeletonProfileHumanoid's, so every humanoid model has them in the
same frames (419's bodies and the goblin alike): a hand's +Y along the
fingers, +X toward the right hand's index (the left's little finger), +Z out
of the palm. A held piece's origin is its grip and its length +Y (art_style);
the hand socket puts it inside the closed fist, between the first knuckles
and the palm (HAND_GRIP, HAND_PALM), its length along the fist's axis, out of
the thumb's side. tools/grip_sockets.gd measured that from the bodies' finger
bones (the knuckles at 0.109 and 0.103 m along the hand, the axis little to
index); the goblin, without finger bones, takes the human hand's frame
scaled to its hand's length (0.69).

What is in a carrier's hand slots (Items.RIGHT_HAND, LEFT_HAND, already
replicated) is drawn at the hand sockets from its art slot
(ArtKit.instance(Items.def(id).art): its own art once there is some, a grey
box sized as the slot until then), swapped when the slot changes and gone
when the hand empties (Client3D._sync_held, each frame against what it
drew). It moves with every clip AnimRig plays (390), so a strike's contact
(399) lands with the blade. A two-hander rides in the right hand; its grip_2
waits for a left-hand IK. A shield sits at the left hand by its slot's own
grip, which its art sets on the strap. The carried lantern hangs at belt_l (a
small iron frame round a glow); its light stays above the head, where it lights
the body from outside (decision 388's reason). back is ready for a stowed
two-hander; nothing goes there yet.

Client only: protocol unchanged, no new class_name. view_test: the sockets on
their bones, a sword in the right fist (its grip within 6 cm of the knuckles,
its length along the fist's axis, at its own size whatever the stature), a
shield in the left, an emptied hand drawing nothing, the lantern at the belt,
a goblin's dagger in its hand. Rejected: items as their own puppets placed by

## 447. The town memory log: what the town's people say of its small life, kept with its source

Phase 1 of Jeff's lawspeaker proposal (docs/lore/lawspeaker.md, 2026-10-17:
"its like the story gets written as it goes"; the coordinator's approval
2026-10-18), on hearsay (378), gossip (422) and the cards (398). The
proposal's test, "would this have happened if no player were watching",
holds: beliefs are born in talk the residents already have, spread on the
world tick, and are kept whether or not anyone listens.

One log per town (economy's Towns.memory and set_memory, saved with the
town record; until that hook lands Main keeps the logs in hand, unsaved),
an Array of entries: {id "tm.<n>", tier belief | candidate | memory | left
| reconciled, text (one sentence as first said), said_by (the worker id;
"companion:<name>"; "player:<id>" for a player's words), to, first_said,
last_said, holders (who believes it now), spread (how many have held it),
tags (the names in it), world (whether it touches the world), ruling ({}
until phase 2)}. New class TownMemory (sim/town_memory.gd), all static:
note, hold, drop, told, candidates, of_tier, remembered, tags, is_world;
levels/residents.json "memory" for the numbers (spread 3, held 2,
hold_days 3, max 200). Nothing is erased: a belief nobody holds is left,
with its history; over max the oldest left goes first.

How a belief is born: a resident's own words. When a resident answers and
the line passes Hearsay.worth_asking, the speaker gets the claims ask 378
runs for hearers, on their own line (Main._own_tale, the same queue,
marked "own"); each claim beyond what they know is a tale of their own:
into their heard as believed (the new fits "own": one believes one's own
tale) and into the town's log said by them, to whoever asked
(TownMemory.told). Under today's speech rule ("towns people don't
fabricate") only a speaker whose voice may embellish is asked: a free type
(bards, scoundrels, thieves) or creativity high, as 378's BOUND already
lets them; never an official. The wider rule (the proposal's a, b or c)
waits on Jeff and is that one condition. A player's words a hearer comes to
believe are logged too, said_by "player:<id>" (the hearers' claims asks
carry the speaker's id now), so phase 2 can leave them out of what goes
to an outside API. Gossip reads and writes the log: a passed belief that
is believed adds the hearer to holders and raises spread (and logs a thing
not yet logged with its source); an overturned belief drops its holder.

Candidates: on the town's gossip tick, a belief held by "spread" people in
all, still by "held", and "hold_days" old becomes a candidate for town
memory, for the lawspeaker (448). The guardrail in code, before any model:
a tale whose names are lore's (Lore.name_forms and entries, drafts
included: a draft name is still the world's) or that bears the world's
words (kings and lords, gods, peoples, war, the land's features) is marked
world and never a candidate; small life is free (neighbours, kin, ailments,
chores, quarrels, animals, weather), the world is not. The voice changes
nothing here: a resident already repeats their own beliefs through heard;
"The town remembers that ..." (TownMemory.remembered) waits for memories
to exist (448).

memory_test (pure sim, no port, no scratch): the tags and the world guard
(a lore name, a king, a war; a dog and a smith are small life); a tale
told, into heard as own and into the log with its source, told again as
the same entry; held by others, dropped, left and taken up again, the cap;
candidates by the thresholds and never of the world; gossip holding a
passed tale and the tick making it a candidate; what the town remembers.
Protocol unchanged; new class_name TownMemory.

Rejected: a model deciding what counts as a new claim from raw transcripts
(the claims ask is 378's structured judge: the line and what the speaker
knows, nothing more); logging every line said (only claims beyond what
the speaker knows, from one allowed to embellish); erasing a belief when
nobody holds it (kept as left, the proposal's "reconcile, never erase").

Amended: a shield (an item tagged "shield") is turned a quarter about its grip's
axis in the hand, so its face (+z, as art_style has it; art-kit centres its grey
box on the grip, 46a81d1) looks out of the back of the hand and its thin side lies
across the forearm.
Amended (the coordinator, 2026-10-17): a town is founded with rules'
start_food (120, Jeff's to tune, like start_gold) in its store
(Towns._found), so it reaches its first harvest: in the 90-day run its
first two weeks went from 114 hungry meals to none.
## 448. The lawspeaker's rulings, offline, by batch

Phase 2 of Jeff's lawspeaker proposal (docs/lore/lawspeaker.md: "the
lawspeaker is perhaps a higher-powered API"; the coordinator's approval
2026-10-18), on the town memory log (447), companions' Claude voice (363)
and the builder's Claude client. Many cheap voices, one careful mind: the
residents' small model handles the talk; the lawspeaker's model handles
judgment, which is rare and bounded.

Every "lawspeaker.every" steps (a day) a town whose log holds candidates
gets one structured request (Lawspeaker.request, sim/lawspeaker.gd, new
class Lawspeaker): the town's name, what it remembers, the lore facts that
bear on it (Lore.known_by for the town's knower, the first lore_facts), and
each candidate with its text, who first said it and to whom, who holds it
now of how many heard it, and its age; and the rules in the system prompt:
he never writes lore and never invents the world (no factions, history,
places, gods, rulers, wars or the land's names; small life is free),
reconcile never erase, lore as fact and memory as memory. He answers JSON
rulings only ({"rulings": [{candidate, ruling, memory, because}]},
Lawspeaker.parse: fences stripped, anything else is no answer), and code
applies them (Lawspeaker.apply): accept, the candidate becomes town memory
(tidied into "memory" when given); reconcile, a new memory entry said by
the lawspeaker with his explanation, the candidate marked reconciled and
pointing at it, its history kept; leave, a belief again, rested
"rest_days" (7) before it can be a candidate again; move_in, marked ready
and nothing more until phase 4; propose, memory and marked proposed for
the list lore keeps for Jeff (phase 5). A memory text that trips the world
guard (TownMemory.is_world) is refused by code and the candidate left, the
reason logged. Each ruling goes to mind.log (kind "ruling": the town, the
model, the candidates, the rulings, what was applied, the request id and
the cost) and to the town's log ("the lawspeaker ruled: the town remembers
that ..."). A player's words ("player:<id>" sources) are left out of the
request unless Net.lawspeaker_players is on (--lawspeaker-players; the
proposal's outside-API note: fine for Jeff and Dire, to be stated before a
public release).

What town memory does once it exists: every resident of the town is told
it as memory, not fact: Resident.world_facts adds TownMemory.remembered's
"The town remembers that ..." after lore's facts within the lore budget,
officials included (378's binding: lore as fact, memory as memory, the
proposal's rule for the most official person in town).

The model path: the builder's ClaudeClient (the Messages API; send(body)
awaited with a long timeout; usage, cost and request id logged; the key
only from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, read by the client and never logged), not
ClaudeMind, which is shaped for one companion's voice with an inner mind
to fall back on; the rules are ClaudeMind's: off by default (Net.lawspeaker
"off"; --lawspeaker=<haiku|sonnet|opus> or PSYKINETIC_LAWSPEAKER turns it
on, the server only), one request per town per day (Lawspeaker.tick from
Main's world tick), and one budget: every round's calls, tokens and cost go
through ClaudeMind.note_spend into the session's counters and no round is
asked once ClaudeMind.spent() (CALL_BUDGET, COST_BUDGET), so the same key
never spends two budgets and the console's `mind claude` line shows it all.
Any failure (an error, a timeout, words that are not rulings, the budget
spent) leaves the candidates for the next round and the lawspeaker's
record says why: the town runs without him. No test and no default
configuration makes a request or needs the key: lawspeaker_test answers
through a stub that stands where ClaudeClient does (send(body) awaited),
as the builder's StubClaude does.

lawspeaker_test (pure sim, no port, no scratch, no network): the request
(memory, lore, the candidates with source and holders, a traveller's words
left out by default and in when allowed, nothing to rule on), the answer
parsed (fenced JSON, words, an error, an unknown ruling), each ruling
applied and the world refused, a round through the stub (asked once a
day, applied to the saved log, the record and the town's log, the budget
counted, nothing when off), a failed answer and words leaving the
candidates, the budget spent stopping a round, memory in the voice's
words. Protocol unchanged; new class_name Lawspeaker.

Phases 3 to 5 on this: 3, the lawspeaker a Resident of trade
"lawspeaker" (an official; a 404 routine "rounds" of a few homes a day),
the batch built per visit from the people he stands with; 4, "ready"
entries become residents through economy's add_worker with a card written
from the talk, within the town's room; 5, "proposed" entries to lore's
list for Jeff. Open for Jeff: the speech rule (a, b or c), the starter
town's lawspeaker's name and face, disputes brought to him, whether
remembered people can leave or die by memory alone, the model.

Rejected: rulings on a player's question (the world tick, unwatched);
the lawspeaker editing cards, logs or lore directly (rulings are data,
code applies them); a budget of its own (one key, one cap); erasing a
belief a ruling overrides (reconciled, with its history); running with a
key by default (off until turned on).
## 453. Accessibility: the interface size, the text size, distinct colours, and keys

Roadmap `ui`, step 6 (the coordinator approved it as written; release asked
for two landings, the sizes and colours first, the keys after). This entry
is the first; the keys amend it.

- Interface size: the whole interface is laid out in canvas units and the
  window stretch scales it, so one number sizes it all: the root's
  content_scale_factor (Net.set_ui_scale; ui_scale= 0.5 to 2, Smaller 0.8,
  Normal, Larger 1.25, Largest 1.5 in the Options' Video section). The 3D
  view is untouched.
- Text size: the theme's font sizes alone (UiTheme.apply_text_scale: the
  default size, the sized variations Title, Heading, Hud, Caption, Small,
  Display, TooltipLabel, the Psykinetic sizes and RichTextLabel's, from the
  base the .tres has; Net.set_text_scale; text_scale=, Normal, Larger 1.25,
  Largest 1.5). Everything on the theme and everything reading UiTheme.size
  follows at once; a size a class kept in a static var at load (the pack's
  slot captions) follows at the next start.
- Colours: the meaning colours are the only hues that tell anything, and
  nothing is told by hue alone (docs/ui_style.md); the Distinct set
  (UiTheme.COLOUR_SETS, Net.set_colours; colours=normal|distinct) keeps
  brass and rust and moves friend to a light blue, party to a pale cyan and
  alarm to a dark magenta, each pair apart in lightness as well as hue (ui_test checks the
  luminance gaps), so a red-green simulation keeps them apart. Applied at
  start by Net from the settings before any panel loads; a change in the
  Options shows in full from the next start (static colours), said so.
- Every setting is read in Net._apply_access_settings before the first
  frame and written back as the others are.

Client only; nothing on the wire. tests/ui_test: the rows, the theme's
sizes scaled and restored, the colour swap, the set's lightness gaps.
Shots in docs/ui/shots/step6/: the Options rows, Largest text and
interface, and the two colour sets side by side for Jeff.

Second landing, the keys: `Keys` (render/keys.gd, new class_name) is a
client-side table, action -> keycode, with the defaults the game has
always had (open E, pack I, pick_up F, drop G, throw T, talk Enter,
talk_log Tab, map M, lantern L, reset R, options O, hints H, debug F3,
fullscreen F11, builder B, the four phrases 1 to 4, attack_friend Shift:
items' 454), read from settings.cfg key_<action>= lines and written back
by Net.save_settings for every binding that differs. Main's handlers and
builder's B ask Keys.pressed(event, action), Keys.matches(keycode, action) or
Keys.held(action) in place of a keycode test, in one mechanical pass that
changes no behaviour (ui_test checks every default against today's key);
the controls list and the cursor's hint say the bound key (Keys.name_of).
The Options' Controls section lists the actions with their keys: a key
pressed waits for the next key and binds it (Net.set_key, a swap with
whatever had it; Esc cancels and is never bound), Reset keys puts the
defaults back. The WASD walk keys stay as they are in this pass: the walk
reads the letters themselves. Also Jeff's playtest line: the first time a
townsperson stands within hearing, one line at the top of the screen says
"Click a townsperson to talk, or press E" for eight seconds, once
(hinted_talk=on). Owners glanced at their lines before it landed.

Jeff's playtest on v0.1.150: "big notes are clicking on npcs attacks them,
thats not good. its not obvious how to interact with them". A left click
attacked any creature but your own companion, residents included. Now a
friend (Main.is_friend: a Resident, any Companion, a Player) is never
attacked by a plain left click, in either scheme: it is the interact
order. Within TALK_REACH (RESIDENT_EARSHOT, 2) talk opens at once; from
afar the player walks to the free cell beside them and it opens on
arrival (_talk_wanted, forgotten after TALK_WAIT_MSEC or a new move
click; holding the button does not steer that walk away). Talk is the E
path's: a resident's conversation panel (open_converse); a companion's is
the chat box addressed to her ("Wren, "), a player's the chat box. In
WASD a left click toward a friend beside you talks too, instead of the
attack. Attacking a friend takes Shift held on the click (never your own
companion, as before); monsters and animals stay click-to-attack. The
cursor hint, agreed with ui, says "LMB  talk" over a resident or a
companion ("LMB  talk   E  her pack" over your own, "LMB  talk   E hold
bandage" over a player), "LMB  attack" over a hostile; the controls list
adds "Shift+LMB  attack a friend". ui's Keys pass (453) makes the Shift a
rebindable action, "attack_friend". Rejected: no way to attack a friend
by mouse (a thief or a turned resident must be fightable) and a right
click to talk (329 gave the right button to the off hand).

The same playtest: "items from kiling a deer couldn't be picked up or

client's World.ground_at read Zone.ground, which only the server fills,
so the "F  pick up" hover never showed on a client over any pile. A

## 458. The proposals list for Jeff: what the lawspeaker would make lore, never made lore

Phase 5 of Jeff's lawspeaker proposal (docs/lore/lawspeaker.md: "Propose to
lore: good enough to be bedrock. Goes to a list for Jeff, never straight
into lore"), on the town memory log (447) and the rulings (448); the
coordinator's defaults 2026-10-18, each phase its own decision. Built
before phases 3 and 4 so the list exists from the first "propose".

The page: docs/lore/proposed.md, lore's page, written by code, never by
hand except its status lines. TownMemory.proposed_page renders it from
the towns' logs: one section per town, one block per entry the lawspeaker
marked "proposed" (448: it is town memory too), oldest ruling first: the
sentence the town remembers, who first said it and to whom and on what
day, who holds it of how many heard it, the day of the ruling and its
reason, and a status line ("open" until Jeff writes "agreed", "declined"
or his words). TownMemory.proposed_statuses reads the status lines back
by town and entry id, so a rebuild keeps what Jeff wrote. A traveller's
words stay "a traveller"; nothing of a player is named.

Two writers of the same page: the server, after any round that proposed
(Lawspeaker.tick, Main._write_proposed), to Net.proposed_path (the box's
/var/lib/psykinetic/proposed.md when that folder exists; --proposed=<path>;
"" for clients and tests: nothing written); and the headless tool
tools/proposed_page.gd (--snapshot=<world.json> --out=<proposed.md>), which
rebuilds the repo's page from a local or test snapshot's towns' memories and
production's names, keeping the statuses it finds; it refuses the box's
path and the shared user:// one by name, so it never reads the box's
world.json (copy one down first if that is wanted). Nothing here touches
lore's entries or files: lore reads the page and agrees or declines, and
an agreed line becomes lore by lore's own hand.

lawspeaker_test: the page's head, a town's section, a proposed entry with
its source, holders, day and reason and an open status; an accepted
entry not on it; a hand-written status read back and kept on the next
rebuild; the empty page. Protocol unchanged; no new class_name
(TownMemory grows; the tool is a script).

Rejected: writing proposals into levels/lore (Jeff only, the proposal's
guardrail); the server writing the repo's page (an exported build has no
repo; the tool does, from a snapshot); the tool reading the box's save
(release's rule: local or test snapshots only).

## 459. The lawspeaker in the town: his rounds, and the batch from the people he stands with

Phase 3 of Jeff's lawspeaker proposal (docs/lore/lawspeaker.md: "the
lawspeaker goes and talks to the people, and keeps everything straight";
"he makes rounds through town, a few people a day"), on the memory log
(447), the rulings (448) and the routines (404); the coordinator's
defaults 2026-10-18: rolled like everyone else, with hooks left for Jeff's
Q2 (a name and a face) and Q3 (disputes brought to him).

The man: a resident of trade "lawspeaker" (lore's roles.json gives the
profession its binding, official, "lore as fact, memory as memory"; until
it does he speaks as townsfolk), one per town, appointed by economy as the
priest is (459's economy side: worker id "lawspeaker:<town>", origin
"appointed", named from economy.json official.lawspeaker.names, seated
once a town has six residents of its own, paid by the bank, no building:
his work place is the square). His day (residents.json "lawspeaker"): the
square at dawn, rounds through the morning, the inn at noon, rounds in the
afternoon, the square at dusk, home at night.

The rounds: a new place "rounds" (Townsfolk.PLACES; Resident.Doing.ROUNDS):
of the town's homes, in the order Main gives them (the residents sorted),
he visits "rounds.homes_a_day" (3) a day in turn (Townsfolk.round_stops:
day d's stops are indices d*3, d*3+1, d*3+2 round the town, so every home
has its day), the day's rounds hours split among them (round_stop). Main
gives his body places["rounds"], the homes with who lives there
(_sync_residents), and he walks to the day's door (Resident._round_area);
his voice is told "You stand at Mara's door." and what he is for ("You are
the town's lawspeaker: you keep what the town remembers and hold it
straight. Lore is fact; what the town remembers is memory; one person's
talk is talk."), and each dispute before him. With no player near, no body
walks, and the rounds still happen: who he stands with on a day is a
matter of the calendar (Townsfolk.visits), not of a body.

The batch (448) from the people he stands with: Lawspeaker.request takes
the town's "visits" (Main: Townsfolk.visits over the town's sorted
residents) and, when there are any, keeps only the candidates those people
hold or said, plus every entry marked a dispute, which comes first (Q3's
hook: the thief's catch, 461, logs one; a player's dispute brought to him
can log one the same way); with no lawspeaker in the town the whole batch
goes as before. The request names him when the town has one ("You are
Hrolf. You are the lawspeaker of Ashford...": Q2's hook; the name is the
record's, rolled or given). The settings block of 448 in residents.json is
"rulings" now, since "lawspeaker" is his day.

lawspeaker_test: his day from the file; the stops in turn over the days and
a small town's repeating; the day's hours among the stops; who he stands
with, himself left out; the batch filtered to the visited with the dispute
first and a traveller's words out; the name in the request; the whole
batch with no rounds. resident_test's bodies are untouched (no lawspeaker
in its town). Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

Rejected: the rounds only when a body walks (nothing would happen with no
player watching); a scripted greeting at the door (facts, and the voice
greets); his own building (he has the town).
## 468. A level chest's stock reaches a saved world once

Jeff (2026-10-17, through the coordinator): "make sure that there is a bow
and arrow bundle in the town chest for practice". The town's chest is the
cache at 221,225 in the wilds (food sack, coin purse; Chest4 by Level's
count); the depot and the shop counter by the starts keep nothing. The box's
saved world keeps its own chest contents (433), and the admin console has
no give, so the change delivers itself:
- A level chest entry's props may list "stock": ids it starts with (also in
  its "slots", so a fresh world has them).
- Loading a save (Main._spawn_saved -> _top_up), a chest whose level entry
  (found by its spawn key, 433) has stock gets each id it was never given
  minted ("stocked") into a free slot. "Never given" means not in its saved
  props' "stocked"; one already in the chest counts as given. "stocked" stays
  in its props, which the snapshot keeps, so a bow taken never comes back.
  With no free slot it is logged and waits for the next load.
- Logged for release: "[state] Chest4 topped up: bow, arrows".
The wilds chest at 221,225 now lists slots food_sack, coin_purse, bow,
arrows and stock bow, arrows. The castle has no listed chests and players
start in the wilds, so it has none. Rejected: an admin "stock <chest>
<item>" command (a step for release on each deploy; the level file as the
source of a chest's kit comes up again).

## 469. A slow tick names where its time went; the dedicated server shows no pack

The box's journal gave a minute's tick average and worst (NetStats) but not
why: Jeff's session of 2026-10-17 had ticks of 219, 90 and 105 ms that no
log line explained. World now times each part of a tick where it runs
(World.part: the act phase by what acts, monsters, companions, players and
others; tiers and roster; hits; hazards and ailments; stamina, wounds and
buffs; Main's respawns, camps, residents, retire and recall, temple and
voices; what else listens to the tick; the net; raids; the sky; far and
sleeping monsters; towns, production and economy; herds; what runs after
the tick, the snapshot among it), and a tick over 50 ms is told in one
line, its six biggest parts first: "[net] slow: 1 tick over 50 ms, the
worst 164.7 ms (tick 1): act: companions 156.4, ...". A frame over 100 ms
whose ticks were quick is told as outside the sim (a mind's answer, a
save). At most one line every 10 s, with how many slow ticks and frames it
stands for (release: a bad minute must not flood journald). On the box's
own world, run here, it named a companion's first turn after a wake (156
ms) and a herds tick (60 ms) at once. And a dedicated server stops
refreshing the pack panel every frame (0.4 ms of a HUD nobody sees).
Rejected: Godot's profiler on the box (an editor connection, and costly);
timing every function (the parts are enough to know whose it is).

## 463. A link can be closed: shown, not travelled yet

way should be on the map, and say so, without taking anyone anywhere.

  (links' "closed"); a closed link may name a level that does not exist
  yet, and WorldMap.problems does not flag it (no level, no way back).

  plain walkable ground.

  reads the flag from WorldMap.build.
- Opening it later: drop "closed" once the level exists.

Protocol unchanged.
