## 462. Archery's look: the bow drawn, held and loosed

Jeff: "we need to prioritize bow since archery is already working, it needs play
testing". The bow's moves had pistol stand-ins (399) that nothing played. Now four
clips of our own, authored by tools/humanoid_clips.py on the UAL skeleton (so on both
human bodies and the goblin) for a right-handed archer, side on, the head turned to
the shot: Bow_Idle (a loop, the bow held low), Bow_Draw (from the bow low to an arrow
nocked before the chest to full draw, the drawing hand at the jaw; its end is full
draw), Bow_Hold (a loop at full draw, the aim) and Bow_Loose (the release, the hand
flying back, and the recovery to the bow held low). The bow hand is rolled thumb up
so the bow stands upright (451's sockets: a held piece's length along the fist).

Client3D plays them from items' signals (456; World.draw_of, raised, raised_tick,
the shot), on AnimRig's upper layer (390) so an archer can step while drawing:
a bow in hand and nothing raised, Bow_Idle; raised "draw", Bow_Draw held still at
the sim's draw rather than played (amended at ui's ask, so the draw reads on the body
without the HUD's percentage): Client3D.bow_pull scrubs it, the nock (the clip's first
BOW_NOCK_END, 0.3) by the ticks toward draw_min while draw_of is still 0, then the
pull, the rest, by draw_of from where it starts (draw_min over draw_full, a quick
bow's too) to 1, carried on between ticks by World.tick_alpha; AnimRig.upper_at holds
the upper layer at a time with its speed 0; full draw, Bow_Hold; the shot, Bow_Loose, then
Bow_Idle; a draw let go with no shot, back to Bow_Idle. A raised shield ("block")
holds the guard, Block_Idle, on the same layer. AnimRig.upper gains a speed and a
restart (upper(clip, speed, from_start); perf's shape: upper_clip, upper_seek,
upper_speed as the action layer has them; the same clip asked again only changes its
speed). A bow is always drawn in the left hand and the other hand's thing (its arrows)
in the right, whichever slots they are in (Client3D.held_ids). While drawn, the bundle
is put away and one arrow (art-kit's fx.arrow, the bundle's kind's variant) sits on
the bow's string at its nock, the string part pulled back toward the drawing hand;
the bow's layout is art-kit's (origin at the grip, back toward the target, "string",
"nock", "rest").

Client only. A monster archer's draw shows on clients once enemy-ai's 455 replicates
raised on monsters (revision 16). anim_rig_test: the upper layer timed (half way at a
quarter second at speed 2, going on when asked again, back to the start on from_start,
a new speed without a restart). view_test: the bow left and the arrows right, Bow_Idle,
the draw from the nock with the bundle put away, its speed for a 2 s draw, an arrow on
the string, the hold, the loose, a cancelled draw, the shield's guard. Rejected: the
draw as a whole-body strike (the legs would stop); one clip played at a fixed speed
(full draw would not come when the sim's does).

Amended (Jeff on v0.1.158: "tested archery, it's clean but bow holding and firing animation
is awkward"; "arm and bow clipping body is probably one of the more obvious things to fix"):
the held pose, the nock and the release reworked in tools/humanoid_clips.py, Bow_Idle,
Bow_Draw, Bow_Hold and Bow_Loose extracted into goblin.res again (only those four: no other
clip, nor any monster's, changes). Held (BOW_LOW): Bow_Idle's left arm had swung back, the grip
0.33 m behind the body, the bow (its length out of the thumb's side) up behind the shoulder
through the back; now the arm hangs a little out and forward, the grip at the left side (0.25 m
ahead, 0.84 up on the man) and the hand turned (BOW_LOW_HAND) so the bow stands upright, its top a
little forward and out, clear of the shoulder and the leg. The nock, from that pose, has the bow
upright, not flat across the body. The release (Bow_Loose) had its string hand swing through the
front to the bow (the forearm turned some 150 degrees in one key, the blend going the short way
round): now the hand slides back past the jaw, the forearm turning out a little, the bow arm
dipping with the kick, held a moment, then the nock and the bow down. anim_rig_test
_test_bow_clear: on five builds (the man as built, heavy, broad, lean; the woman), the bow and
the arrows socketed as Client3D does, walking and standing in the held pose, at the nock, at full
draw and at the release, no vertex of the bow nor of the left forearm inside the trunk (each
against the nearest trunk vertex's normal, the body skinned on the CPU with its shape keys: a
headless run registers no skin to bake); the old clips fail it (the man's bow 28 vertices into
his back standing). Not changed, asked of Jeff: the body turned to the target before the release
(the puppet's facing, an aim layer if the shot goes off-axis) and the pull's pace (the sim's draw
ticks, items').

Amended (2) (Jeff on v0.1.160: "the bow draw back arm is all wrong, it clips through the body then
is held as if the arm is behind wrapping behind the head to hold it"; "bow arm is too long, bow is
held out too far away from body too"). The string arm had been aimed bone by bone (a direction for
the upper arm, one for the forearm) and the check above counted the bow and the left forearm only:
at full draw the string wrist sat 0.22 m behind the head, at head height, the elbow 0.26 behind the
shoulder, and on the way there (nock to pull) the forearm crossed the chest. Now the arms are
reached, not aimed: humanoid_clips.py gains REACH (an arm's two bones solved so its wrist meets a
point, the elbow bent toward a pole; the point a weighted sum of bones' heads plus offsets, so a
pose is placed against the head and the bow hand, not guessed) and GRASP (the hand turned so a held
piece's length and flat lie along given directions: the socket's +Y is the hand's own +Z in the
pack's bones, measured). Full draw: the string wrist beside the right jaw below the ear, 0.11 m
out from the head's centre line, the elbow out to the right and level behind it; the bow arm's
elbow soft (wrist 0.49 m from the shoulder of the arm's 0.52, grip 0.60; it was straight, the grip 0.61), aimed
a touch to the right so the arrow runs nearly along the shot. The draw keyed more densely so the
blend cannot swing through the body: carried, the bow lifted out before the leg, the nock low
before the belly with the trunk only a fifth turned and the right shoulder brought forward, raised
with the string hand out before the chest, pulled along the jaw, full draw; the release slides the
hand back past the ear and comes down the same way. Carried (BOW_LOW): the arm hanging at the side,
the wrist by the thigh, the bow upright beside the leg, its top forward (the grip 0.16 ahead of the
hips, was 0.22), the bundle's arm a little out from the hip. No bone is stretched: the arm's
shoulder-to-wrist never passes its bones' length (measured on every build; the builds share the
skeleton, shape keys move only the skin). anim_rig_test _test_bow_clear now takes ten moments (carried
walking and standing, lifted, nocked, raised twice, pulled, full draw, released, coming down) on the
five builds and counts the bow in the trunk or the left leg, the left forearm in the trunk, and the
right forearm and hand in the trunk or the head; and at full draw the string wrist within 0.2 m of
the head and not behind it. The clips before this fail both (the right arm in the body at the lift,
nock, raise and coming down; the wrist 0.22 behind the head).

Amended (3) (Jeff on v0.1.162: "running with walking carrying arrow bundle and bow at side needs to
be bow swinging with arm, arrows should just be a quiver on the back and right arm swinging while
running like normal. bow string doesn't bend, it needs real physics"; the coordinator approved the
method). The carry: at a walk or run with the bow down (Client3D's bow state "carry", the base clip
one of the puppet's gaits) the upper layer lets go, so both arms swing with the gait, and the bow
turns in the left hand to BOW_CARRY (a quarter turn about the socket's x, 0.04 m out from the
grip), found by trial so its limbs clear the hip and leg through the walk, jog and sprint on the
five builds (anim_rig_test _test_bow_clear: twelve carried moments, the bow alone counted, the arms
being the gait's own); standing, Bow_Idle again, the bow turning back over BOW_TURN_SECONDS. The
arrows leave the hand: while a bow is held and arrows are in the other hand's slot, that hand
shows nothing and a quiver hangs on the body's "back" socket (between the shoulder blades, up and
over the right shoulder): slot gear.quiver, art-kit's, kind held, not an item of its own, its
variant the arrows' kind (1 plain, 2 flame, 3 barbed, as fx.arrow's), a grey box until its art
lands. No arrow count is shown (the pack's count isn't replicated to the puppet; a fixed
fletching). The string: art-kit's straight "string" box is hidden and drawn instead as two closed
boxes of its thickness and material (seen from every side), tip to nock and nock to tip, the tips
read off the box's bounds, so every bow and variant bends with no new art. Drawn, the nock follows
the drawing hand (never past it, never forward of the brace) and the arrow sits on it. Let go,
the nock goes back by Client3D.bow_string: to the brace in STRING_SNAP (0.03 s, a quarter swing),
then a damped ring about it (9 Hz, damping ratio 0.2) whose first swing past the brace is 0.12 of
the draw and never more than 0.05 m, still after 0.4 s; a function of the time since the loose, so
a long frame can't fling the string across the body. The arrow leaves the string on the loose
(_on_shot's flight takes over). Next, if Jeff wants more: the limbs flexing with the draw (a
vertex bend keyed to the pull). Fixed on the way: a hand's old thing is taken out of its socket
before it is freed, so the new one is the socket's "Held" (two in one frame, the new one had been
renamed and the bow's string and the bundle looked up on the old).

Amended (4) (Jeff on bow3: "bow3 is perfect ... final task would be to make the bow bend slightly on
full cock"; the coordinator approved the method). The limbs bend with the draw: each held bow's
own meshes (all but its string) get their own copy of their mesh once, when the string is first
drawn as segments, freed with the bow (built with dynamic update, so a bend writes only the moving
positions into a copy of its vertex buffer, no new mesh); while the nock is off its brace the
copies' vertices are moved by Client3D.bent: in the bow's frame (limbs along y from the grip, the target +z) nothing
within the grip (BOW_GRIP, 0.12 of the limb's length), then toward the string (-z) as the square
of the way out to the tip, BOW_BEND (0.05 m, about 5 degrees) at the tips at a draw of BOW_DRAW
(0.45 m, a full draw as the clips pull it), no more past it, the height drawn in so a limb keeps
its length. The string's segments start from the bent tips. The bend reads the nock's place
behind its brace, so on the loose it follows the string's spring (bow_string): straight in 0.03 s,
a little forward as the string rings, still by 0.4 s, when the art's mesh is put back; a CPU
deform rather than a shader (the bow draws in the shared palette material) or limb bones (every
bow re-rigged). Its cost, capped at release's ask: only archers within BOW_FLEX_RANGE (14 m) of the
camera's mark bend (the rest keep the rigid bow, their strings still drawn), and a bend is written
again only when it changes by BOW_BEND_STEP (half a millimetre), so nothing while the draw holds
still or the bow is at rest. Measured windowed under the bench lock (build/bow4_raid.gd): one
drawn archer a median 0.022 ms a frame (worst 0.11); eight drawing, holding and loosing together a
median 0.052 ms a frame for all eight, 0.39 at the 95th percentile, 0.57 at worst (the first
version, rebuilding the mesh each frame, was 0.21 ms for one). The string's pull is bounded too
(BOW_DRAW_MAX, 0.75 m), so a pose not yet applied can't stretch it across the field.
## 460. Moving in: a person the town remembers arrives, with room and the lawspeaker's word

Phase 4 of Jeff's lawspeaker proposal (docs/lore/lawspeaker.md, Jeff: "when
someone speaks of Old Marta and her sick son Timmy, they could then
silently move into town"), on the memory log (447), the rulings (448), the
rounds (459) and the cards (398); the coordinator's defaults 2026-10-18,
with Jeff's Q4 answered by default: they leave or die only through the
world.

When the lawspeaker rules move_in (448) the entry is marked ready. On the
town's tick (Townsfolk._arrive), each ready entry not yet arrived is tried,
oldest ruling first (TownMemory.arrivals): it must name someone (its tags)
and not touch the world, and the ruling itself says they live in or near
the town. Then economy's door: Towns.move_in(town, who_id, name, trade)
(460's economy side: false when the town's residents are at its room, the
same growth that takes in rescued captives, so invented people never
crowd out rescued ones, or the id is a worker already; else add_worker
with origin "remembered", the residents list, the town's log line "<Name>
is found to have lived here all along", a seat, no founding gold, no
rescue xp, no rescued signal). The person is the talk's: the name its
first name word ("Old Marta" gives Marta; "old" makes the card's age
old), the trade a trade word in the talk when the town's trades know it
(TownMemory.TRADE_WORDS: miller, smith, cook, carpenter, farmer, hunter,
priest, guard, healer, tanner), else the stand-in (hauler); the id
"remembered:<town>:<name>". Their card is rolled as anyone's
(ResidentCard.roll, origin "remembered") and then written from the talk:
came "has lived here all along, as the town tells it", and every memory
naming them a card fact (TownMemory.talk_of: "Marta's boy Timmy is sick
again"), so their voice has the life the town gave them; kin and a grudge
are rolled among the neighbours as at any founding (Townsfolk
._found_among). The entry keeps "arrived": who_id and stays memory, so
the town goes on saying what made them. They get a body, a home and a
day like anyone (355, 404), and no memory ever removes them: a town's
talk can say Timmy does not mend, and only the world can make it so.
Transcript and mind.log (kind "arrival") note the arrival.

memory_test: who is ready, named and not of the world, oldest ruling
first; the person from the talk (name, old, the trade when the town has
it); two arrivals through economy's door in order, the resident and her
card from the talk, the entry marked; nobody twice; no room, they wait,
and arrive when there is. Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

Rejected: arriving on one mention (the lawspeaker rules first, after the
talk has spread and held); a card invented by a model (the talk is the
card, and the rest is rolled as for anyone); dying by memory alone (Q4's
default); a founding gold share (a newcomer's, not a neighbour's who was
always here).

Economy's side (2026-10-18): Towns.move_in(town, who_id, name, trade,
origin := "remembered", type := "") as above; origin and type are for
471's Snagfin (a type like the thief's, 461). Origin "settled" (471: he
brings his own stall; npc's ask, 2026-10-18) passes the room check, which
the talk's "remembered" arrivals keep. rescue_test.
## 465. Regenerating levels: the shifting halls, anchors kept, the rest laid again

Jeff (2026-10-17): "castle stays persistent, its the entrance marker for
the shifting halls which are underground"; his lore pages: "The overworld
stays consistent. The labyrinths under the castle are the delve-again
places: they make new maps fairly often. The tower's inside shifts too."
Maps' design, approved by the coordinator 2026-10-17 and moved to the
dungeon tree with the roadmap row ("floor loot outside anchors lost to the
shifting halls"). Infrastructure only: the mark, one generator, tests; no
real level is marked until Jeff says.

- The mark: level.json "regenerate": {generator, every_days, anchors:
  [{rect, name}], monsters: {kind: count}} (Level.regenerate_from,
  level["regenerate"]). The authored files are the template
  (Level.template, never the overlay); each anchor's cells are copied
  verbatim every generation, and every link, spawn point and start must
  sit in one (Level warns otherwise: the next generation loses it).
- The generator: sim/level_gen/<name>.gd, static generate(template:
  LevelMap, config, seed) -> LevelMap, loaded by name. "maze": a perfect
  maze on the odd cells outside the anchors (recursive backtracker), a
  doorway or two per anchor on an open side, the parts the anchors cut
  apart joined by straight corridors, monster markers on dead ends first.
  Regen (sim/regen.gd, a new class_name) seeds it with hash(area,
  generation, attempt), flood fills between the anchors, tries 8 seeds,
  and keeps the last map when none joins them; the generated level.json
  is the template's with entities, starts, places, buildings outside the
  anchors dropped and "generation" written in.
- When: Main checks every WORLD_TICK_STEPS (World.stepped) and on travel
  into a level (travel, _open_zone); a due level (every_days of the
  world's days since its last generation, or never made) is laid again
  only when its zone is not open or asleep, never awake. The state is the
  snapshot's "regen": {area: {generation, at_step}}.
- What stays and goes: the zone's live state goes through Snapshot's
  form and Regen.keep_section keeps the entities, respawn timers, records
  and floor piles whose marker cell (decision 433's key) or cell sits in
  an anchor; the rest is dropped and its things ended in the ItemBook as
  "lost in the shifting halls"; _start_level rebuilds the zone on the new
  map with that section. Places outside the anchors leave the holdings
  (rebind) and each record's known_places, and those players are sent the
  full "world" message again (no new field there: a full message starts
  the client's state over, decision 446). A companion left waiting in the
  zone is remembered with no tile, to come back beside her owner.
- Clients: Regen.write registers the generated level (Level.register,
  a test's template kept aside first) and writes it to Level.overlay_dir,
  so Level.overlaid is true and _show_zone_to sends the "terrain" message;
  it refuses a level that sits in the overlay without the mark (a level
  edited in the game is never written over). The "map" message gains
  "generation": a new field in an existing message, PROTOCOL_REVISION 18
  (release's ruling).
- Coming back: PlayerRecord.seen_generation {area: n}; _join_player tells
  "The ways have shifted since you were last here." when the generation is
  newer than the one seen, nothing on a first visit, and a returning
  player whose zone shifted since lands at the nearest anchor spawn point
  (Regen.anchor_spawn_near), else the nearest floor, their companion
  beside them.
- The castle and the tower are never marked: the halls and the tower's
  inside are separate levels linked from them, the link's cell an anchor
  on the shifting side.

tests/regen_test (port 17860): the generator (anchors verbatim, the rest
different between generations, joined, the same seed the same map,
monsters laid, the shrine and imp outside dropped), the mark's warnings,
travel into a level never made, never while awake, laid again on the tick
once asleep with the corridor's thing lost and the deep room's kept (the
chest's things too), the known places pruned, the line on coming back
(once), the returning player at the deep room's spawn with his companion,
the edited level refused, the snapshot and records round trip, no real
level marked. level_test: a link outside an anchor warns.

Rejected: regenerating a zone with players in it and moving them (never
under anyone's feet, Jeff's words on the castle as the persistent
marker); a new prune field in the "world" message (the full resend does
it); marking levels/castle (the halls are a level below it); keeping
entities outside the anchors by name (their markers are gone).

Amended (maps' side: raids take the regenerated map). Raid groups kept
the WorldMap they were made with, its routes and every group's route, so
after a generation they walked the old floor. WorldRaids.use_map(map)
waits for the old routes, takes the new map and drops the routes and the
groups' legs; each group's route is made again from where it stands when
next it moves, and one with no way on from there breaks up as any group
with no route does. Main._regenerate calls it after the holdings rebind
(dungeon's side). Holdings.attach keeps any number of routes up with who
holds what, held weakly on one place_taken connection (it connected once
per routes, and a second set logged an engine error). raid_groups_test:
a group under way when its camp's level is laid again without the way to
the town breaks up.
Amended (2026-10-26, the coordinator; perf, after 368 amended): a laid
level never waits for the routes' fields, and nothing asks a route of fields
not yet in. Main._apply_generation hands the new world map to
World.raid_groups and World.trade (use_map), and each finish()ed first,
waiting for its WorldRoutes' distance fields. The raid groups' routes are
made even with raids off: trade's wagons use them (World.trade.get_routes)
and so do companions' guides. Their fields take 46 to 52 s on the world's
map here, and a use_map while they were being made waited 31 s. Laid 30 s
apart, the second level waited for what the first one's map started, as
368 amended found for the richness.
- WorldRoutes.retire: its tasks stop at their next portal (Shared.stopping).
  busy() says whether any still runs, never waiting.
- WorldRaids.use_map and TradeRoutes.use_map retire their old routes and
  keep them (_retired) until they are not busy, then drop them on a world
  tick (freeing routes waits for their tasks). finish(), at quit, still
  waits for all.
- Holdings.ranked (a fallen player's place of return, a camp's home town)
  does not ask routes that make fields but whose open layer is not in. It
  ranks the same area's places as the crow flies, then every other area's
  by id (NOT_IN_STEPS), so a fall in an area with none of its own still
  finds one (economy). An area the routes lack still gets none, as a route
  from it found none (resident_test's town, not on the world map). A route asked of fields not in walks the world on
  the main thread, 5.6 s in one probe.
  Trade already waits a tick for them (routes_in) and guides for
  is_ready. The raid groups' own ticks still ask raw, as before (raids are
  off on the box).
After it, use_map takes 19 to 23 ms with the fields mid-way, and a retired
set's tasks stop at once.
regen_test: use_map does not wait for routes being made, and retires them;
the routes asked next are new ones; trade waits for them; places ranked
over routes not in come the same area's first, then the others', and one
from an area with none still finds another's; retired routes are let go
once stopped. raid_groups_test, trade_routes_test, respawn_places_test,
relief_test and townsfolk_test pass. Server only, protocol unchanged, no

Amended (2) (2026-10-26, the coordinator; maps, after perf's amendment
left the raid groups' own ticks): nothing in WorldRaids asks a route of a
side whose fields are not in. Raids route per faction layer
(Factions.side), so WorldRaids.routes_in(side) asks that layer alone
(routes that make no fields are always in; fields_in stands in for tests,
as TradeRoutes'). Raids stay off on the box until this is live.
- _send_some: a camp whose side is not in sends nothing that tick, so no

- _move: a group out whose side is not in holds where it is, its plan (its

- threat_of: _distance gives the steps last measured for that camp and

world_tick's _drop_retired still runs first, before the "if not on" return.
raid_groups_test _test_fields_not_in: not in, the threat is the last
measure and none without one, and no camp sends; in, it sends; not in
again, the group holds its cell, walked and plan; in, it walks on. Server

## 466. A forest's canopy: trunks as void cells, a cover layer on every peer

Jeff (2026-10-17, through the coordinator): "a forest zone - while walking
through it would be dark because of the canopy overhead, with trees nearly
everywhere.. but spread enough to walk around.. with small clearings where
sunlight shines through". The pieces are terrain's, environment's, sound's
and maps' (levels/forest, maps' 464); this one is what the rest read.
- A trunk is a void cell. Void already stops walkers, sight, light and heat,
  so the sim needs nothing new for one, and a chase through a packing keeps
  going: a prototype ran 16 chases each against open ground and packings of
  2.6, 3.0 and 3.4 m. The player struck the fleeing deer in all of them and
  never lost sight of it; only the first strike came later in the trees (18,
  30 and 43 ticks).
- level.json "canopy": {"kind": "evergreen" | "broadleaf"} and "clearings":
  [{centre: [x, y], radius}]. Level.canopy_from works out each cell's
  cover from the trunks: each void cell within CANOPY_REACH (3.2) cells adds
  1 - d / 3.2, the sum capped at 1, and a clearing's cells are open (0).
  Gaps where the trunks are sparse fall out of it; environment finds them
  there. Level's terrain carries "canopy" (cell -> cover), "canopy_kind"
  and "clearings"; Fields.canopy_at(cell), canopy_kind and clearings give
  them to the sim. A client parses the same level files (a "terrain"
  message carries files, not the parse), so nothing new goes over the wire.
- Client3D.canopy_texture: the cover, an R8 texel a cell on the ground
  mask's grid from canopy_origin (Client3D.canopy_mask), for environment's
  look and the ground.
- ForestPack.from_trees(map, trees_path) (editor/, new class_name): a void
  cell under every tree of 3 m or more, live or a snag, in a grown stand's
  trees.json (467), on grass only, never on the path's dirt or a marker.
  maps' make_forest lays its ground and calls it last.
What reads it is the other trees': environment's daylight cut in
Fields.ambient_at and its look and light shafts, sound's deep-forest bed,
and terrain's drawing of the grown trees (467). Rejected: a canopy image of
its own beside layout.png (a second thing to keep in step with the trunks);
packing the trunks by rule (ForestPack.pack, the first plan) once the trees
were grown (467); a new cell kind for a trunk that stops walkers but not
sight (the forest is meant to hide things).

## 467. Trees grown by a simulation, offline: tools/forest_grow.py and trees.json

Jeff (2026-10-17): "the idea for the trees was to build a sim outside the
game to model how trees look in a forest.. not necessarily in game". The
rule-built pines (a cone of whorls, branches cut short at a neighbour) were
not that. tools/forest_grow.py (Python and numpy) grows a pine stand year by
year from a crop of seedlings and writes what stands to the level's
trees.json; the game draws from it and grows nothing.
- Where trees may stand: a level's grass cells, not its dirt (the path), not
  within a clearing's radius + 1 (--level levels/forest). Or a stand-in map
  of the same kind (--standin N).
- The model, on 1 m cells at the game's scale (pines top out near 13 m):
  - Light: a grid of 0.5 m voxels, 14 m high. Every live branch lays
    needles along its outer part into the voxels it passes. The light at a
    voxel is the sky seen through the needles above it, overhead and along
    four 45-degree slants, each voxel passing exp(-0.9 x its needles). The
    map wraps, as the forest goes on past its edge.
  - Each year a tree's leader grows by the light at its top, at its own
    pace (lognormal), slower near 13 m. Each 0.42 m of new height starts a
    whorl of 4 to 6 buds.
  - A branch lengthens by its tip's light up to 2.4 m, and stops where
    another tree's needles fill the voxel ahead. One whose middle sees under
    0.14 for 3 years dies; a dead branch drops after 6. So crowns lift as
    they close, and trunks go bare below.
  - A tree has a bad year when its needles catch less light than its upkeep
    (0.8 x height^1.5), or too little reaches its crown or top. After 5 bad
    years in a row it dies, stands as a snag for 10 to 25 years, then falls.
  - Seedlings come up where the ground's light passes 0.3, once some tree is
    15 years old.
- Nothing is placed or tuned by hand afterwards. The one rule chosen was the
  upkeep, from what a healthy 12 m crown needs; values from 0.4 to 1.5 only
  shift the density, from about 1 tree in 6.5 cells to 1 in 10.
- The first run, on a 96 x 96 stand-in: 4,879 seedlings; 2,539 alive at
  20 years, 1,058 at 50 and 913 at 100 (881 over 3 m, about 2.2 m apart,
  12.6 m tall, crowns from 3.8 m). At 100 years 90 % of the ground under
  them is dark. It takes 7 s. Sheets for Jeff: C:\dev\review\forest\.
- trees.json: {"decision", "years", "stats", "clearings", "path", "trees":
  [{at: [x, y] in cells, height, radius, lean, age, state "live" | "snag",
  whorls: [{y, branches: [[angle, length]]}], dead: [[y, angle, length]]}]},
  every tree of 3 m or more and the live undergrowth. --snapshots writes
  trees_yN.json at those years.
- Grown crowns close over small clearings, as real ones do: a clearing that
  should stay sunlit needs a radius of 6 or more.
Rejected: growing at level load (minutes in GDScript, and the same every
load); growing per player chunk (the same stand everywhere is the point);
the space-colonisation broadleaf of the first study (no years, no light, a
preset crown).

The client's drawing (GrownTrees, client3d/grown_trees.gd; the coordinator's
approval of the pad pass, 2026-10-18):
- In a level with a canopy (466) and a trees.json in its own folder (never
  an overlay's), a tree of 3 m or more is drawn where its cell is not land
  (ForestPack's trunk), a smaller one where it is floor; any tree the
  layout no longer agrees with is left out. A tree's cell is its "at"
  floored (the grower's cell x spans x to x + 1). Those trunk cells are left
  out of the forest's ring and the border (put in the "wooded" set) and the
  ground runs under them.
- A trunk, needles as small pads along each live branch (one each 0.62 to
  0.88 m by tree, none over 0.55 m), a stick for each dead branch; every
  crown its own by its place: droop, pad size and shape, reach, tone, turn.
  A tall tree's live branch below 2.1 m is a stick only; a pad below 3.4 m
  droops and thickens to a branch's tip, not a shelf at head height.
- Chunks of 8 x 8 cells, two ways: far (a trunk and one pad a whorl) built
  for all with the room; near (every pad) built on worker threads for the
  chunks within 34 m of the view's middle (panned or not), dropped past
  46 m, and added one a frame (16-cell chunks cost a 14 to 27 ms frame each
  as they came in).
- The see-through (Jeff, 2026-10-18: "use transparency that moves with
  player to see through the tree tops since its a isometric game"):
  round the line from the player's body toward the camera, whatever is
  above their knees and on the camera's side is faded toward the near
  walls' NEAR_ALPHA (see_through.gdshaderinc). How wide: Jeff on the
  concept, "larger circle, probably even most of visible screen", so 0.8
  of the view's half-height (Net.see_through, settings.cfg see_through=
  0.2 to 1.5, read only, to try sizes without a build) to the middle of a
  3.5 m soft edge, with the zoom: the faded part reaches the screen's top
  and bottom, the roof stays at its sides and corners. It is decision
  188's fade: the chunks within its outer edge + 17 m of the player draw three
  passes, opaque but for the region (season_cut, dithered where the two
  meet, at alpha near 1), the region's depth (season_see_depth, at
  NEAR_DEPTH_PRIORITY), its colour faded (season_see, at NEAR_PRIORITY), so
  a faded crown shows its nearest surface only; the rest draw the opaque
  pass alone. It moves with the player's drawn place, so nothing pops. Each
  piece has a shadow-only twin, so the canopy's shadows and the dark under
  it stay whole; the crowns stay opaque outside the region, in the rain's
  heightfield.
- The ground under the roof (on environment's 477 canopy uniform in
  ground.gdshader): grass turns to the forest's needles where the cover
  passes about a half, raggedly by noise (the path's dirt and floors
  stay); a third as much snow lies under full cover; and a grass cell
  whose cover passes Client3D.SCATTER_ROOF (0.6) takes the forest's
  sparse scatter, not the grass's tufts.
- levels/forest: its trees grown from maps' 464 layout (740 at 100 years,
  710 trunks about 2 m apart, 12.6 m tall), 716 void cells (snags too) laid
  by make_forest. In the game's view there (map_bench, 6 s each): 500 to
  780 fps on average; the worst single frame 4.5 to 6.5 ms standing, 7.5 to
  10 ms while the view pans into new chunks or turns and walks.
  With the see-through at 0.8, at zoom 1.1 (map_bench, 8 s): frame time
  median 1.4 to 1.7 ms, 99th 3.7 to 4.4 ms, standing, walking or turning,
  as at 0.45; every frame over 5 ms in the first 0.1 s (start-up).
- Winter (amended; the coordinator, from the midwinter shots, 2026-10-18):
  the swaying scatter's snow lies from each plant's own height (custom data
  per instance: g one over its mesh's height, so the tips go white and the
  straw shows below, where a tuft's tip had sat above the whole fade and
  gone white to the ground), r how much: full in the open,
  Client3D.SCATTER_ROOF_SNOW (0.12) under the roof (0.3 still read as
  white flowers there: from above a tuft is mostly tips); b shades its
  dried straw there (SCATTER_ROOF_STRAW, 0.5: the scatter takes no shadow). The wilds'
  tufts too. The grown crowns hold GrownTrees.SNOW_COVER (0.5) of a lone
  pine's snow, only on what faces up past SNOW_FROM (0.75), broken in
  patches SNOW_PATCH (0.8 m) by world noise (season.gdshaderinc's
  snow_cover, snow_from, snow_to, snow_patch; 1, 0.3, 0.8, none for
  everything else), so under full cover the forest reads dark, its needles
  green-grey with a dusting, white only in the clearings.
  Second pass (the coordinator, 2026-10-19: in the open a tuft at full
  cover still read as a white rosette on white snow): under the snow a
  plant is buried, not iced. Custom data a (1, but 0 for reeds, which
  stand in water) sinks it SNOW_SINK (0.7) of its height times the cover,
  more or less by SNOW_SINK_SPREAD (0.35) by where it stands, so some are
  gone and some show a few straw tips; the tips' white is SNOW_TIPS (0.35),
  faint (scatter.gdshader).
Rejected: fading whole trees as the ring's are (hundreds of nodes to test
a frame, and a whole 13 m tree gone for one crown in the way); a dithered
hole over the player (the first cut: Jeff asked for transparency); every
chunk drawing the see-through's passes (three times the vertices for
crowns it never reaches); full pads for every chunk (2.5 M triangles,
150 MB for a 96 x 96 forest).
tests/farm_test (the look through a year with a late storm: bare, sown,
growing, flattened, ripe, bare; each change told once); protocol_test.

## 461, economy's side (npc's thief: Jeff, "thieves could be the answer to balancing the economy")

The hooks npc's thief calls; numbers are npc's (townsfolk.json "thief").
- Production.lift_gold(worker, gold, thief): up to gold from a worker's
  purse into the thief's, never more than it holds; gold only moves.
- Production.return_gold(thief, victim, gold): a caught thief gives back up
  to gold, never more than they hold.
- Economy.fence(town, merchant, thief, what, factor, margin): a lifted
  resource sold back to the store at raw_price x factor, the treasury
  paying (never below gold_floor; nothing moves when it can't), the
  resource banked by the merchant, who keeps margin of the gold, the thief
  the rest.
- tools/town_balance.tscn: the coordinator's balance run as a tool (the
  wilds town, nine residents, a field, the real rules, no players; --days,
  --thief=<resident>, --no-field), printing a line a week; no state, no
  shared overlay. Run through the gate (bench), its output to a file.

larder_test (a lift, never past the purse, given back, a fence's split,
gold conserved, the floor).

## 457. The field's look: the crop's stage in the "town" message

On 449 (farms) and buildings' 452 (building.field), for art-kit's state
parts. The coordinator's approval of 2026-10-17. PROTOCOL_REVISION 17.

- Towns.crop_look(town): "sown" (spring, once sown), "growing" (summer),
  "flattened" (for a day after a storm flattened it), "ripe" (autumn, not
  yet brought in), "" otherwise (unsown, harvested, rotted, winter, no
  field).
- The "town" message's buildings ({town, buildings}: Towns.buildings_of)
  carry it on the field's entry: buildings["field"] = {state, level, crop}.
  The town tick keeps the last look on the crop record and, when it
  changes (a few times a year), emits building_changed(town, "field"),
  which Main already sends to every peer; a peer coming to the zone gets it
  with the town's buildings (_send_towns). No new message: the "town"
  message's content changed, hence the revision.

## 472. An item's character: only a thing held and used grows

Coordinator's defaults while Jeff's growth questions wait (2026-10-17):
"only a named or held-and-used item grows: a plain drop has no character
until a player has carried and used it for a while (say 20 kills or a
season), when it earns a name slot and starts counting; blessing at the
temple or reforging with special materials starts it at once". This
supersedes part of 415 (every thing tallied what it felled, a monster's
dagger too) and of 417 (any thing could take a bane or a grudge).
- ItemBook.grows(uid): the thing has a "character" ({how, step}, saved),
  earned by give_character for life, noted "character" in its history (a
  kept event). Only then does it tally kills (fell), and so become a
  bane, or take a grudge (set_grudge). A bundle of arrows never grows (its
  bow does: shots credit the bow).
- Earned at 365's naming threshold: one named holder (a player or a
  companion) has held it held_days with deeds done, or done deeds_alone
  however long (items.json "naming": held_days 7.0, a season at the default
  Season.season_days, with 10 deeds; deeds_alone 20). The character comes
  whether or not a name form is agreed yet (the name follows once it is:
  Jeff, "for now Wren's Dagger is sufficient", lore marking the holder form
  agreed). A blessing (424) gives it at once, and so does any set_name. A
  reforge with a special material will, once lore's materials (D3) exist.
- With no name to tell it by, the party log says "<thing> has seen enough
  use to grow: it counts what it fells now" (World.item_grew "character").
- A save from before: a named, blessed or tallied thing has grown already.
Protocol unchanged (all of it is the server's book and the notes' text).

## 470. The labyrinth generator: dwarven rooms and halls, or the old caverns, between the anchors

The second generator for regenerating levels (465), the coordinator's
go-ahead 2026-10-17 ("dwarven rooms and halls between the anchors (a
gatehouse, halls, chambers, the older style below), content-free"), from
Jeff's lore: dwarven work plain, heavy, built to last; lore's proposal of
a third, older style for the labyrinths themselves. Content-free: no real
level is marked; the sample halls live in the tool and the test.

- sim/level_gen/labyrinth.gd, the same contract as maze (generate(template,
  config, seed) -> LevelMap), with "style": "dwarven" or "old". A style
  is a vocabulary for a whole level (each real level later picks one and
  its own walls and floors sets), never mixed on one map.
- Rooms: "rooms": {"count": [lo, hi], "size": [least, most]} placed at
  random in the rock, a cell of rock between any two and from the anchors;
  dwarven rectangles, the first two great halls (wider, every other
  interior cell a pillar); old caverns, a blob grown from the rectangle's
  middle to two thirds of it. The anchors and rooms are nodes joined by a
  minimum spanning tree over their centres (Prim's, by walking distance)
  plus "loops" (0.2) times the nodes of extra ways drawn among the
  shortest left, so the halls loop and the ways are never the same twice.
- Ways: out of each node by its exit nearest the other (an anchor's only
  through an open edge of the template); dwarven straight with one bend,
  two cells wide when neither end is a plain room, a door edge where it
  meets a room, with the cell inside remembered; old a walk leaning toward
  where it goes (LEAN 0.65), finished straight. Never into an anchor.
  Blind ways: dwarven alcoves a cell deep off about half the rooms; old
  crooked ways four to ten cells off a corridor, touching nothing. Then
  gen_tools' join_up and Regen's flood fill as before.
- Light and things: dwarven torches on the cell inside each door and
  every eighth corridor cell; the old style none. "chests" on the blind
  ways' ends, then room corners, then rooms; "crates" in rooms;
  "monsters" {kind: count}, brutes in the halls first, every kind in rooms
  and corridors; never beside an anchor. What the kinds and loot mean is
  enemy-ai's and items'.
- Level.regenerate_from passes the block's other keys through as the
  generator's own; sim/level_gen/gen_tools.gd holds what the generators
  share (clear_outside, carve, parts, join_up, l_path, shuffle), maze
  moved onto it.
- tools/plan_sheet.tscn (write_sheet): a generation drawn at --scale (8)
  pixels a layout pixel in the legend's colours, each anchor outlined in
  blue, with a line of what is on it; --level=<name> for a marked level,
  --sample=dwarven|old for the built-in sample halls (48 x 40: a
  gatehouse, two halls and a deepest chamber). Jeff's sheets go to
  C:\dev\review\dungeon\.

tests/labyrinth_test (port 17861): the block's keys through, and for each
style the anchors verbatim, generations differing outside, rooms (3 x 3
blocks of floor), every anchor reached, the same seed the same map,
doors between floor cells and torches in dwarven and none in old, the
markers counted and none beside an anchor, the sample's links and spawn
points kept; the sheet written and refused without an out or for a level
that does not regenerate. No protocol change; no new class_name.

Rejected: mixing the styles on one map by depth (a level has one walls
set; the deeper level is the older one); sunk caverns and stairs in the
old style now (the coordinator: flat first); the generator choosing
treasure (items' and enemy-ai's).
## 444. A companion's bond with her player

The coordinator's design, approved 2026-10-17, on npc's Standing (443): Jeff
wants the bond between player and companion to grow from what they do
together. Her record holds "standing" ({player_id: {score, met, since,
why, own}}, Standing's entries), saved with it, read through Standing's
COMPANION ladder: fond to start, wary at -3 and below, close at 3, devoted
at 6 (residents.json "standing"). Gossip never touches it (443).

What moves it, each by companion_traits.json "bond" (drafts for Jeff),
with the reason kept as Standing has it: her player bandages her (+1,
"bandaged your wounds"), gives her gear or a named thing (+1, "gave you a
sword"), shares food with her (+1, "shared food with you"), frees her from
raiders (+4, "carried you out of the raiders' camp"), falls with her
beside them (+1, "fell with you at their side", the coordinator's: loyalty
is the saga's note), keeps her named thing from her (-1), strikes her
(-1, once a day). A day travelling together is +1 once a day, but only
below close: devotion is earned by deeds. Main._tend_bonds, once a world
tick, counts the day and, only while she is apart from her player
(resting in town, held by raiders), lets Standing.decay fade it; never
while they travel. A fall while with them is the world's doing and
counts against no one.

Her voice is told one line (Companion.bond_words, Main's: Standing.fact
on her record as it stands): "You are close to Jeff: they carried you out
of the raiders' camp." First met at her join when there is no entry, so
a record from before starts fond. PlayerRecord.from_dict keeps
"standing" and the day counts. companion_test covers it. Protocol
unchanged.

Rejected: a model judging the bond (the world's events move it, as 443);
decay while they travel (a bond does not fade beside its friend); days
alone reaching devoted.

## 473. The hurt tally, and one growth per thing

Coordinator's defaults while Jeff's growth questions wait (2026-10-17): "the
hurt tally and one growth per thing, keeping the sidegrades (the agreed
rule; a damage number only if Jeff asks)". On 472. This supersedes 417's
grudge rule (a thing took a grudge when its holder fell to a kind) and its
bane and grudge side by side (a thing could hold both).
- ItemBook.hurt(uid, kind, hp) / hurt_of(uid): a thing with character
  (472) counts the hp each kind has taken from whoever held it while it
  was in their hands ("hurt" {kind: hp}, saved). World.damage reports the
  hp actually lost (World._take_grudges(who, by, amount)), on every blow
  from a monster to a player or a companion, not only the last one.
- A grudge forms once one kind has done it items.json growth
  "grudge_after" (30) hp, more than any other kind has: the vengeance is
  against what has hurt its bearers most. Its sidegrades stay 417's (its
  blows stagger that kind, they seek its bearer first); paid as before
  (grudge_paid of them felled with it), when that kind's hurt starts over
  so it does not come straight back.
- One growth per thing, bane or vengeance, whichever count gets there:
  a bane (25 of one kind felled, 415's tally) takes no grudge, and a thing
  that becomes a bane drops the grudge it held (ItemBook.drop_grudge: its
  kind's hurt forgotten, "gave way" in its history, a kept event).
- The party log says "<thing> has seen its bearers hurt by <kinds> enough:
  it holds a grudge against them".
No damage number: the growths stay sidegrades unless Jeff asks. Protocol
unchanged (the server's book and the notes' text). items_test's _test_bane.

## 478. The orc and the kobold: the Blood Rot's allies' own bodies

Lore and Jeff (416, the primer): brutes are orcs, paid muscle, big and heavy,
standing guard; sneaks are kobolds, who dig the Blood Rot's shafts, patrol
and come from the side; the imp is the Blood Rot goblin. Both drew the
goblin's mesh. The coordinator approved the design; Jeff's veto comes off
the review sheet (C:\dev\review\orc_kobold\) or in game, as for art picks.

- Built by tools/body_gen.py as the humans are (419), `--people orc|kobold`
  (human the default, byte for byte as before), on the same UAL skeleton, so
  every humanoid clip (the shared library, through art/models/bonemaps/ual.tres)
  and HUMAN_SOCKETS' grips work on them: no new rig, no clips to author.
- Proportions by moving the skeleton's joints (PROPORTIONS: legs, arms,
  shoulders, hips, spine, neck, hands, feet, each bone's offset from its parent
  scaled by its parent's segment, the feet put back on the ground), not only
  by scaling: the clips are rotations and the hips' one position track is
  retargeted by each body's own hip height, so they play on an orc's long arms
  and short neck and a kobold's short legs (checked on the sheet; no fallback
  to whole-body scaling was needed). Then the body is scaled whole so its top
  is at its people's height: an orc 1.95 m, a kobold 1.0 m.
- The orc: very broad chest and shoulders (TORSO_WIDTH and DEPTH), bare thick
  arms, a bull's neck, big hands, a heavy brow ridge and broad jaw, two tusks,
  small ears swept back, a leather harness strap across its chest and back
  (harness), a kilt over trousers, wrapped feet; may crop or bind
  its hair (Hair_Cropped, Hair_Bound). The kobold (reptilian-leaning,
  unfussy: no fur, scales only in the faceting): small and crouched, a large
  head drawn out into a snout with nostrils, eyes to the sides, two horns swept
  back, no ears, long arms with big hands and three digging claws, long bare
  feet, a stiff tail, a jerkin; may wear a miner's leather cap with a candle
  stub (Cap_Candle). The tusks, horns, claws and candle are a new region,
  "Bone", on the palette's accents row (body_build PALETTE_ROWS).
- In game (Client3D.MODELS): the brute is orc.glb and the sneak kobold.glb,
  drawn as people are ("parts"), each its own PersonLook with the word
  people=orc or people=kobold (look_for adds it from the model's "people"):
  one body, PEOPLE_SKINS (the Blood Rot's greens), only its people's parts
  (an orc's hair or none, a kobold's cap at KOBOLD_CAP_CHANCE), its people's
  posture (an orc slouching, a kobold stooped), shape keys and stature as a
  person's; its kilt or jerkin in its look's colours, not its sprite's.
  Sized by its look, not its mass (by_mass false). Gaits by tools/gait_pace.gd
  (ORC_GAITS, KOBOLD_GAITS: a kobold scurries, its jog 1.8 m/s at speed 1),
  their backpedals scaled from a man's; sockets ORC_SOCKETS, KOBOLD_SOCKETS.
  Held things keep their one size (a kobold's bow is a longbow on it, as on a
  goblin).
- The rot's changes on the allies near the mine (lore's open question) are
  left for a later variant. The kobold fights with items' dagger (the sneak's
  backstab stays; its "wields" are enemy-ai's, levels/monsters.json); items' pick
  (479, two-handed) is a chance drop from kobolds, and a digging kobold that wields it
  comes with the mine (the coordinator with enemy-ai). HUMANOID_MOVES strikes a pick
  with Axe_Overhead, as the hammer, checked on both bodies' arms.
- Art-kit's slots creature.orc and creature.kobold (04d9a66) let ArtCheck
  cover them.

view_test _test_allies (each its people's skin, parts and posture, its clips
playing and its hands; an orc about 1.95 m, a kobold about 1 m; two orcs
differ); _test_goblins_differ's brute an orc, much bigger than an imp.

Amended (Jeff, 2026-10-18: "not happy with orc and kobold" and, from art-gen's redo v7,
"p1 kobold from redo", the sleek scaly climber with a long tail): the kobold restyled to it.
Light red (the "Skin" tint, PersonLook's kobold PEOPLE_SKINS) on its head, chest and hands,
purple (the "Trousers" tint, KOBOLD_LIMBS) on its arms, legs, feet and tail, its little fur a
crest of spines from the brow over the crown and a ruff down the nape (the "Hair" tint,
KOBOLD_CREST), long ears swept back where the horns were, two teeth, a loincloth (the kilt,
shorter); its tail long and whip-thin, rigid on the pelvis so the legs swing clear (checked in
Walk and the crouch), curling up at its tip; slighter (TORSO_WIDTH), less crouched (posture
slouching). No cap, no candle: kobolds see in the dark (art-gen's notes). It fights with the
dagger (481). The orc stays as built until Jeff picks one. Then a second pass (the coordinator on the
first beside the concept: "a stick figure"): a broader chest and shoulders, thicker forearms
and thighs, bigger hands and feet with four claws each, a shorter neck, a longer snout with
its mouth's line; digitigrade legs on the same bones (the knee forward, the hock back, a long
raised foot, kobold_foot); the tail twice as thick at its root, tapering, longer, rooted under
the loincloth (widened over the thighs); scales as banding (kobold_bands: every other band of
SCALE_BAND on its back, the tail's top and the shins' fronts the crest's dark tint), its belly
pale (a new palette region, "Belly", body_build); the crest and ruff half the size, the ears
swept out.

Amended (Jeff, "orc p2 from redo": art-gen's redo v7 p2, the hulking hunched brute, grey-blue,
an iron shoulder plate and a chain): the orc restyled to it, at the kobold's second-pass effort.
Grey-blue skins (PersonLook's orc PEOPLE_SKINS), bald (no hair parts), its loincloth brown
(ORC_LOINCLOTH), stooped (PEOPLE_POSTURES). body_gen's orc: shoulders set far wider (its arms
hang out from its body), a huge chest and traps, a very short neck (its head low), arms and hands
far bigger, shorter thick legs, bare legs and feet (the "Skin" tint), a broader jaw and bigger
lower tusks, the head a fifth larger; an iron plate rigid on its left shoulder with a dark rim

for Jeff to choose the route.

Amended (Jeff on the brute in game: "still pretty clunky, it's going to need a revision or a

## 481. A kobold fights with a dagger and drops a pick 1 time in 5

The coordinator, on the kobold's look (pc-character's 478) and items' pick
(479): the sneak keeps its verb. A pick in its hands (windup 4, a slower
swing, a knockback that shoves its target off the back it circled to)
would make the flanker a small brute, and hiding what it holds would break
338 (a monster drops what it carried). So:
- The sneak's row wields the dagger (decision 338's "wields"): backstab,
  twice the hurt from behind, quick. It drops it when it dies, as 338 says.

  roll is spent on it, so every row without one drops as before
  (Monster.dropped). The sneak's row: a pick, chance 0.2, so a raid leaves

  level's monsters get): Raids spawned them from Level._spec_for alone, so
  a raid's kobolds would have come bare-handed. A server-side change; the

## 482. The minimap draws again only when what it shows changes

The minimap (321) called queue_redraw() in _process, so it drew every frame
whether anything had moved or not (ui's measurement, for perf's regression
hunt; Jeff: "performance is suffering lately yes"). Now _process asks Main
for the marks (you, your companion, the other players, the doors) and draws
again only when their hash changes: you stepping or turning, a player or a
companion moving, a door's mark made again differently. rebuild (a new
zone), toggle (M) and zoom queue a draw themselves; a resize redraws as any
Control does; hidden, it neither asks nor draws. Nothing else on it moves:
the picture, starts, ways out and places change only on a rebuild.

Measured with map_bench on the wilds, windowed, standing still: before,
drawn every frame at 0.13 to 0.14 ms a frame (its _draw alone), the frame
median 1.63 and 1.78 ms over two runs; after, drawn 0 times in some 7,000
frames, the median 1.36 and 1.32 ms (the canvas not recorded again either,
so more is saved than _draw's own time). Turning the camera (--spin=30)
the pointer turns, so it draws every frame as before (0.12 ms a frame).
Minimap.draws and draw_usec count it; map_bench prints them.

tests/minimap_test: ten frames with nothing changed draw nothing; a step, a
turn, opening, zooming and a rebuild each draw once; hidden, nothing.

Rejected: drawing at a fixed rate (late when you move, wasted when you
don't); a texture the marks are baked into (the marks are a few dozen
shapes, the picture is already one texture).

## 477. Under a forest's canopy: the light cut, drips, the darker look, shafts of sun

Environment's part of the forest zone (Jeff, 2026-10-17; terrain's canopy
layer, decision 466, gives each cell its cover, Fields.canopy_at, 0..1, the
same on every peer, open in the clearings).

The sim. Under the open sky a cell's light over the night's is cut by its
cover: Fields.ambient_at is NIGHT + (light - NIGHT) x (1 - cloud's dim) x
(1 - canopy_shade x cover). canopy_shade is DayNight.CANOPY_SHADE (0.7,
a placeholder) for a level with a canopy, set with the weather each tick
(DayNight.canopy_shade); a broadleaf canopy takes BROADLEAF_WINTER (0.6) of
it less in winter, its leaves down, an evergreen none. So noon under a full
roof is about 0.44, over Senses.DARK, and once the open sky's light is under
0.7 (the morning, the evening) it is dark enough to hide in there while the
clearings are lit. Senses, sneaking and companions read World.light_at and
follow with no change of their own. Checks of "is it night" (Animal,
Companion, DayNight.describe's dark) stay the open sky's: where one is is
the caller's, as indoors. No protocol change: the cover comes from the level
data every peer has.

Drips. Weather.drip_at(region, steps, cover), 0..1, a function of the clock
as Weather.at is: the cover while the rain is DRIP_RAIN (0.3) or more; after
it, the cover fading linearly to nothing over DRIP_SECONDS (90) x cover, so
a full roof drips longest and an open cell not at all; rain over 0.3 again
starts it over. Snow does not drip (at's rain leaves it out). The seconds
since the rain are found by looking back through Weather.at DRIP_LOOK (3 s)
at a time, kept per region for that look. Agreed with sound: its drips
(amb.drips) read the same call, with the cover round the listener.

The view. Client3D eases the cover round the view's middle (the mean within
CANOPY_AROUND cells) and:
- canopied_look darkens the ambient (CANOPY_AMBIENT of it at full shade)
  and tints it and the haze green; the sun's light is left as it is: the
  crowns cast their own shadows (terrain's), so the clearings stay sunlit
  and the patches move with the sun. Rejected: a shadow-only sheet at crown
  height (the crowns' shadows do it; it stays the fallback if their shadow
  pass costs too much).
- The ground is lit as the sim lights it: ground.gdshader reads the cover
  (its canopy, Client3D.canopy_texture) and lights the floor between
  sky_floor (the open) and sky_floor_roof (under a full roof).
- WeatherView.set_canopy: what falls is thinned by the cover (rain by all
  of it, snow to CANOPY_SNOW), the canopy drips instead (a few big slow
  drops from under the crowns, as many as drip_at says), the low fog lies
  CANOPY_FOG thicker, and the clouds' shadows fade. The crowns are in the
  rain's heightfield (every layer but RAIN_LAYER), so drops stop on them;
  the thinning keeps rain from pouring through the cutaway hole over the
  player.
- Light shafts (client3d/light_shafts.gd): a quad glowing additively,
  turned about its length to face the eye (fading when seen end on), hung from TOP (9 m) over each clearing (up to three, by its
  radius) and each gap in the canopy (a cell under 0.5 cover, the most open
  of its neighbours, inside the canopy, GAP_SPACING from another), their
  feet on the floor and leaning toward the sun. At most SHOWN (8) at once,
  the nearest the view within REACH, fading toward its edge and close to the
  eye. Their strength: the day's light x clear sky x no rain, best in light
  haze, none in thick fog, and none with the sun under SUN_LOW (15 degrees).
  Rejected: Godot's volumetric fog (a cost on every frame for a few shafts).

Placeholders all: the shade, the drips' length, the look's numbers, the
shafts' strength, until Jeff has walked the forest.
## 461. The thief balances the town: gold from the rich, the store through a fence, and getting caught

Jeff (2026-10-18): "thieves could be the answer to balancing the economy".
On 393 (the hidden thief, who lifted one thing a day from the store with
no name on it) and economy's side above (Production.lift_gold and
return_gold, Economy.fence, tools/town_balance). The coordinator's design
of 2026-10-18; the numbers are npc's drafts in townsfolk.json "thief", for
Jeff to move.

What the thief does, on his day (Townsfolk.tick, which now takes the
economy; the same seeded draw as before says whether he works at all):
- Gold first. The mark (Townsfolk._mark) is the richest of his town's
  people whose purse stands above economy's line for a rich purse
  (economy.json folk.rich_above, the line its dole and prices already
  use; read from the economy given, else its file) with gold_take to
  spare; never himself, a resting companion, anyone on the dole or hungry,
  and never the coffer. Production.lift_gold moves gold_take (3) from that
  purse to his, and the victim's card learns a loss with no name on it
  ("Odo missed 3 gold from his purse."). That is the balance Jeff asked
  for: gold piling in one purse goes back into circulation through a man
  who buys his bread and pays his rent.
- The store only when nobody is rich: the lift of 393, one of "takes"
  above "leave", the ledger's "missing" line. What he lifts there comes
  back the same day through the town's merchant (type "merchant", 440;
  Snagfin once 471 lands) by Economy.fence: the store buys it back at its
  raw price times "fence" (0.5), the treasury paying, the merchant keeping
  "margin" (0.4) of that and the thief the rest; the ledger shows the
  merchant banking it "from a dealer". Gold is conserved throughout: what
  the coffer pays is what the two hold.
- Caught (Townsfolk._catcher, one seeded draw per lift): the victim, when
  the routines put both at the same meeting place that hour (the well, the
  inn, the square, the temple), against "caught" (0.06); a guard there, or
  at his post for a store lift, against "caught_guard" (0.12). Caught, the
  gold goes back (Production.return_gold) or the goods are "returned" to
  the store; the catcher's, the victim's and the thief's cards learn it
  ("Odo caught Sly with a hand in Odo's purse."), the catcher and the
  victim hold a grudge against him (card "grudge", 398: gossip and the
  voice already read it), and the town's memory log (447) gets the catch
  as a dispute, which the lawspeaker's rounds take first (459). Caught
  "caught_before_lying_low" (3) times within "caught_season_days" (90) he
  lies low "lie_low_days" (30): no lifts, the count cleared.

Not here: a thief among players' things (the store and purses only); the
thief's own words about it (his card says he is a thief and keeps it
hidden, 393, and now what he was caught at); a jail or a fine (the
lawspeaker's rulings are words, 448).

The 90-day proof (tools/town_balance, the wilds town, nine residents and
the field, no players; economy's tool, which now ticks the thief with its
economy and takes --merchant=<id> for the fence; its folk hold no guard,
so there only a victim catches):
- With Ash (a hauler) the thief and Bea the merchant: 44 gold lifts in 90
  days (chance 0.5 a day), 132 gold moved, every one from Pell the
  carpenter or Odo the smith, the only purses above the line; the store
  never lifted (someone was always rich), so nothing fenced; nobody caught
  (the victim's 6% applies only when both stand at a meeting place at the
  hour he picks: under one catch in 90 days is what the numbers say).
- Day 90, thief against none: loans 77 against 107; dole meals 61 against
  73; bought meals 348 against 319; hungry 222 against 207 (hunger is the
  food supply's, not gold's); the two rich purses 59 and 79 against 114
  and 26 (the lifted gold goes to the thief's own meals and rent, so to
  the cook and the treasury, and from there round again). So he evens the
  rich out and lowers the town's debt a quarter, and moves a gold and a
  half a day: a modest balance at npc's numbers. More needs gold_take or
  chance raised (townsfolk.json), which is Jeff's to say; the catch rate
  wants a guard in the town to mean much.
townsfolk_test: the gold lift from the richest purse above the line, never
the poor, the dole or the coffer; the store when nobody is rich; the fence's
split and gold conserved; caught by the victim at the well with the gold
back, the cards, the grudge and the dispute; lying low after three. Protocol
unchanged; no new class_name.

Amended 2026-10-19 (Jeff, through the coordinator: "5 gold", the stronger
hand the proof offered): townsfolk.json "thief" gold_take 5 and chance 1.0,
so the thief lifts five gold from the richest purse above the line every
day he has one; the catch and the fence as they were. The 90-day proof's
numbers above are the draft's (3 on half the days).
