## 488. Buildings as blocks: kinds, sizes and their stamps

Jeff (2026-10-18): "buildings need more variety and natural structures,
boxes is too simple and some way too small". Proposed by buildings with
art-kit, approved by the coordinator as infrastructure (steps 1 to 3; this
is step 1, 489 the composer); nothing in a real level until Jeff asks.
- The grid stays the rules, the look stops showing it (terrain's rule,
  2026-10-14; Jeff today): a building's cells are cells only because its
  walls and doors are the sim's edges. Nothing drawn is held to a cell:
  a wall may sit inside its edge by any offset and be any thickness, jog
  or bay by a fraction of a cell, eaves and ridges at any height, eaves
  overhang past the footprint, a porch or step stands outside it, so long
  as what blocks is the edges. No building should read as whole metres.
- A building of a kind is blocks: levels/buildings.json "kinds", each kind
  its words, wall and floor sets, storeys (eaves STOREY 3 m a storey unless
  it names "eaves"), roof ("gable", "round"), place (temple, healer's hut)
  and sizes ("small", "large"), a size its blocks [x, y, w, h, role] (main,
  wing, leanto, outshot, bay) and doors [x, y, side] in its own frame,
  front +y. Kinds: hut, round hut, shed, stone cottage, house, L-house,
  house with a lean-to, house with a wing, two-storey house, longhouse,
  barn, stable, inn, hall, mill, watchtower, temple, healer's hut. Sizes 1
  cell = 1 m: hut 4 x 5 / 5 x 6, shed 3 x 4 / 4 x 5, house 6 x 8 / 7 x 10,
  temple 6 x 10 / 8 x 12 and so on.
- A level.json building entry {kind, size, at, facing, seed, ruined, use,
  town} stands its blocks there turned to its facing (Level._turned, the
  same turn as Prefab.rotated's, so a kind stamped turned is its facing's);
  its footprint is their union, its outline the edges round the union
  (Level.blocks_outline, building_outline), checked as a slot's rect is:
  all on clear floor of one height, walled but its doors. Its "rect" is the
  box round its blocks (what places, homes and nearness use); its "blocks",
  "words", sets, "eaves", "seed" (the entry's, else from its cell, so every
  peer draws it alike), "doors" and "front" (outside its first door: its
  place's cell) are its own. A slot's building (building.hut and the rest)
  is one block, as before: the wilds town is unchanged.
- A ruin ("ruined": true) is any kind without a roof: no inside, nothing
  roofed, its walls as walls.
- What asks "inside which building": level["building_cells"] (cell ->
  building index; Level.inside_cells, made once as the level is read), so
  Companion.know_level fills its per-zone cache from the level Main already
  parsed (perf: no per-call parse, a lookup not a scan); Fields roofs the
  blocks' cells; the client's _building_at, rain cover and inside-wall fade
  go by blocks (its outward side the one off the inside), the near walls
  of a wing faded as the main block's.
- Stamping: each kind and size is a prefab "building_<kind>_<size>"
  (Prefab.kind_prefab, kind_names), made from the kinds file as it is read,
  never saved: the blocks' cells ground, walls round them but the doors, a
  ring of dirt. The editor's stamp panel and builder mode list them (the
  builder's prompt says each in a line, not a grid). A stamp over a
  building takes it by its blocks' cells.
- Drawn for now (489 does the rest): walls and floors in the kind's sets
  from the map's edges; a gable over each block at its eaves, its ridge
  along the block's longer side, all one "roof" off while inside; roof set
  thatch (Jeff's default; shingle until art-kit's thatch set is there).
- No message carries buildings: a client parses its level, and a builder's
  edit goes as the level's config in the "terrain" message, where an older
  client leaves a kind entry out (said) and plays the same walls. Protocol
  unchanged.
level_test _test_kinds (every kind's sizes: blocks meeting and not
overlapping, doors on the outline and one in front; every kind prefab at
four turns stands walled with nothing said; an L-house's wing inside and
roofed, its box's empty corner neither, a ruin neither, the wall where the
wing meets the corner); view_test _test_kinds (an L-house: a roof piece
per block, inside by its blocks, walled round both, its doorway);
companion_test's know_level by cells.
Rejected: a mesh per kind (boxes again, and no variation); footprints
off the grid (the sim's walls are edges); saved prefab folders per kind
(two sources for one shape).
Amended (Jeff: "building sizes all need space inside, minimum 5x5 - no
more 3x3 shacks"; the coordinator's approval): a kind's main block (its
role "main", else its first; Level.main_block) is at least Level.MIN_ROOM
(5) floor cells each way. Its walls are the edges round it, so a 5x5 house
has a 5x5 floor, room for a bed, a table and a hearth with a walk round
them. A wing, a bay, a lean-to or an outshot may be less: each is room
added. Regrown: hut 5x5 and 6x6 (were 4x5, 5x6); shed 5x5 and 5x6 (3x4,
4x5); watchtower 5x5 and 6x6 (3x3, 4x4); round_hut and healers_hut a main
block of 5x5 and 6x6 (3x5, 4x6), their bays kept, 7x5 and 8x6 round. The
rest already were. Level.kinds() pushes an error for a kind under it, so
one cannot come back (an engine error fails the suite), and level_test
says which. The kind prefabs are made from the file (Prefab.kind_prefab),
so they follow; no real level used the regrown kinds. The slot buildings
(265: hut and healers_hut 3x3, shed 2x3, house and temple 4x6) are meshes
and stay; the town that used them is laid fresh in Held as kinds (maps,
Jeff's Held answer), and the wilds keeps its own.
Amended (two kinds, the coordinator's approval: the forge for Held's core,
maps' ask; the butchery for economy's meat chain, Jeff's herder, butcher,
cook): a kind's size may name "open", outline edges given as its doors
are, left with no wall and no door (Level.kind_open; the prefab leaves
them, parse does not call them open edges, building["open"]); its front
and its site cells (566) come from its doors, else its open edges
(Level.entrances). "forge": stone, a stone floor, a 6x5 smithy and a 6x2
lean-to across its front, that front open (7x6 and 7x2 large), always a
chimney. "butchery": wood walls on a stone floor, 6x6 with a 4x2 outshot
behind (7x7 and 5x2), a front door, a chimney one time in two. Neither is
in a real level. level_test: the forge's front open, its front and work
cell found from it. No counter or hooks yet: no art-kit pieces for them.

Amended, builder's side: a plot (564) narrower than Level.MIN_ROOM either
way holds no building, so BuilderSession.street_checks says so for each
plot in the area ("the plot p2 is 4 x 6: too small for a building, whose
room is 5 x 5 at least: make it bigger"), reading the constant, so the
number lives in one place. Builder's prefab list was already the kinds
file's. builder_test _test_plots.

## 486. A quarrel brought before the lawspeaker

The coordinator's assignment of 2026-10-18 ("errands from what is
between people", half one; half two is 487), on 435 as Jeff amended it
("try to minimize quests that are just 'go get object A from location
B'"; "make them so they are auto completed, no need to talk to the NPC
first. Just give player a notice that it was completed and the reward,
and the NPC will remember"), on the grudges of 398, the town's memory
447 and the lawspeaker 448/459. Approved with one condition: with the
lawspeaker off, a grudge pair stays as it is today.

- The source is the grudge two residents' cards hold (398, rolled at
  founding, grown by events such as the thief's catch, 461). In a town
  with a sitting lawspeaker and rulings on (Offers.ctx "lawspeaker_of"
  and "model"), the gossip tick (Townsfolk.note_disputes) writes one
  entry per grudge pair into the town's memory if none is open for the
  pair: "A and B are at odds" (with the card's latest fact naming the
  other as the reason: "since Odo caught Sly with a hand in Odo's
  purse"), said by the one whose grudge it is, to the other, a candidate
  from the start (a dispute is not talk to be spread) with "dispute" and
  "pair", so his next batch takes it first (459's order). The quarrel
  goes before him on its own, as the town's business, players or none.
  461's catch entry is written the same way now (it was a belief, which
  never reached his batch).
- The plea (Offers._plea_offer), in place of 435's carried word in such a
  town: "Speak for me": "Lay my quarrel with B before the lawspeaker when
  you see him; say I was wronged." Taking it records interest on the
  card's asks and nothing else (an errand ask, sub "quarrel").
- Speaking to the lawspeaker with the plea open (Offers.spoke_to, which
  runs on every word to a resident) marks the pair's entry "brought" by
  that player: his facts say who laid it before him, his request to the
  model says so too ("Laid before you by Jeff, a traveller"), and the one
  spoken for gives a "heard" point. A conversation he was going to have;
  nothing handed in.
- His ruling completes it (Lawspeaker.apply calls Offers.ruled for any
  ruled entry with a pair), whichever it is: reconcile (the town
  remembers his sentence of it), accept (the complaint stands as memory),
  leave (talk, resting: "the matter may lie"). In every case the quarrel
  is closed: both cards drop the grudge and learn "The lawspeaker ruled
  on the quarrel between A and B: ...". Every player holding the plea
  gets the party-log notice, the treasury's pay through economy's
  pay_commission at rules "commissions.dispute" (5, economy's key,
  80c41d6; Offers.DEFAULT_PAY until it is there), standing "word" (2)
  from the one they spoke for and one more from the other when the ruling
  reconciled them; the card remembers who spoke for them. Nobody holding
  the plea, the matter still closes and nobody is paid: the world moved on
  its own, as the rule says.
- Lapse: a quarrel's ask waits the lawspeaker's pace, a batch plus his
  rest (rulings.every + rest_days), instead of offers.days, so no player
  is marked lapsed for his slowness.
- Off (the box today, --lawspeaker off): no entry is noted, no plea of
  this kind is offered, nothing is shown; the grudge and 435's carried
  word stay exactly as they are. That is the documented behaviour of the
  server until Jeff turns rulings on.

Numbers: commissions.dispute 5 (economy.json); standing word 2 and heard
1 as they are. offers_test (the note once, the plea, taken, speaking to
the other carries nothing, speaking to him marks it brought and his
request says so, the ruling closes both cards and pays the one who held
the plea, a ruling with nobody holding it pays nobody, off and no sitting
lawspeaker fall back to the carried word); townsfolk_test (the catch's
entry a candidate pair). Protocol unchanged (offers are an existing
message; "carry" stays the accept verb); no new class_name.

Rejected: the player choosing a side (the lawspeaker rules, 448); a
fine or a jail (rulings are words); the quarrel as a thing to deliver; a
new accept verb (the client knows four).
## 485. Heel: walking at someone's heel, shared by companions and escorts

npc's escorts (435's next errands, the coordinator's go-ahead) need a
townsperson to walk home with a player, and the coordinator gave that
walking to companions' movement (381's heel) rather than new pathing.
sim/heel.gd (class Heel, RefCounted) is that following cut out of
Companion, with no change to how she walks: one per follower,
follow(body, leader) once a tick (set off at START 3, or at once when in a
doorway or across a building's walls from the leader; make for the heel
cell; stop there, or within STOP 2 and not ahead, once the leader has stood
WALKING_TICKS; with no heel cell free, close to CLOSE 1, and one that
cannot get closer waits), static cell(body, leader) for the pick (never a
door's cells, the leader's side of a building's walls, behind their facing,
nearest them, then the follower) and step(body, goal, occupied_ok) for one
A* step when the body's next move is due. Companion holds a Heel (heel)
and keeps her own stalking rule (332) in front of it; her FOLLOW_* constants
are Heel's, _catching_up reads its catching_up, and _step_toward is
Heel.step. A body with a Heel is moved on the grid like any other; a zone
change is the owner's (Main.travel respawns a companion beside her player
from her record; npc's escort stays in one zone by design). Doors and
buildings are still read through Companion.door_cells and building_at
(391; Main hands her each level, 391 amended). companion_test covers a
plain body following a walk with a Heel. Protocol unchanged; new
class_name Heel.

Rejected: npc calling Companion's own _follow (her members: keeper, the
stalking rule); a node per follower (no scene, nothing to draw, a ticked
RefCounted is enough).
Amended (Jeff: "no birds at night, maybe owls bats"): birds belong to the
day only. The drips' take with birds (freesound 841641) is dropped, and the
deep night bed's owl-dense takes (475376, 151241) are replaced by two quiet
night woods (662095, 532301), so night's voices come as sparse calls, not
in a bed: Ambience.calls(zone, daylight, weather, canopy, tower) gives each
call's rate and Ambience._call plays it from round the listener (Sfx.play,
heard as any sound there):
- amb.owl (four takes, CC0): now and then, up in the trees 4 to 10 cells
  off, every OWL_SECONDS (45) on average under a full roof, four times as
  long in the open;
- amb.bat (four takes, CC0 and CC BY): overhead near by, every BAT_SECONDS
  (20) where they're most at home: a canopy's edges and clearings (cover
  half way, 4 x c x (1 - c)) or within TOWER_NEAR (4) cells of a town
  wall's drawn tower, none by TOWER_FAR (12); the lore's tower joins when it
  is a level;
- both at night only, hushed by rain as the birds are, never under stone.
The retired takes are kept in the sound library's retired/ folder, out of
the game and its credits.

## 487. Someone walked home

The coordinator's assignment of 2026-10-18 ("errands from what is
between people", half two; half one is 486), on 435 as Jeff amended it,
398's kin, 355's bodies and companions' Heel (485). Approved with two
conditions: the stray's cell is chosen off held ground and walkable from
the town by the routes of 206, and the stray is never a resident with an
official's seat or a counter, only the trades listed.

- Who is lost (Townsfolk.stray, on the world tick; townsfolk.json
  "strays": every 54000, chance 0.1, days 3, far 24, trades hunter,
  hauler, farmer, tanner): by town, a seeded draw a day sends one of its
  people of those trades beyond the walls, never an official (origin
  "appointed"), the merchant or an outcast, one at a time per town. The
  card says so ("strayed": {since}), economy counts them away
  (Production.set_away: no work, no meals, not taken in a raid; rent
  still due, as for a captive), a fact on the card. After "days" the
  lost find their own way home (Townsfolk.came_home with nobody: back,
  not away, a fact), so no one is ever stranded and nothing of this
  needs a player.
- Where they stand (Main._stray_cell, chosen once with the zone in hand
  and kept on the card): a walkable free cell of the town's own zone at
  least "far" from the store, not inside a building, off held ground
  (Holdings.covers of any place not held by the town's holder: a camp, a
  keep), among the farthest dozen one a path over the zone's own grid
  reaches from the store (World.find_path, doors opened: the condition
  "walkable from the town"; 206's routes join areas, and within one zone
  the grid is the finer truth and knows a test level too), picked by a
  draw seeded by the day. One in three cells is looked at and at most a
  dozen paths are tried, once per stray, which finds the far edge at no
  cost worth naming. A zone with no such cell leaves them unplaced and they come
  home on their own.
- The body (Main._sync_residents): as a town body is (355), made while
  a player is within recall_tiles of the cell and unmade when none is,
  labelled "<Name> [<trade>]", friend to a click, standing still
  (Resident.Doing.STRAYED); their facts say they are lost, which way the
  town lies and that they follow whoever speaks to them. A zone change
  by the player despawns it as any resident; the card keeps the cell, so
  the body is made there again. One zone by design: Main.travel is
  untouched and no body crosses a portal.
- The plea (Offers._plea_offer, first of the pleas, it is urgent): on the
  card of their kin (398), "Walk B home": "My sister B has not come back
  from beyond the walls; if you find her out there, walk her home."
  Taking it records interest only (a commission ask, sub "escort"). The
  lost one's own first words ask the same.
- The walk: a word to the lost one (Main._ask_resident) and they follow
  that player (Resident.start_escort; Doing.ESCORT) at heel with
  companions' Heel.follow(self, leader) once a tick while the player is
  within FAR_TILES; beyond it, or with the player gone, they stand where
  they are and wait for the next word. No pathing of npc's.
- Home (Main._came_home, when the followed body stands within the
  store's radius and a step): Townsfolk.came_home (the card clear, back,
  the fact "Jeff walked B home from beyond the walls" on their card) and
  Offers.walked_home: every plea to walk them home is met; the player who
  walked them gets the party-log notice, the treasury's pay through
  economy's pay_commission at rules "commissions.escort" (8, economy's
  key, b90b957; Offers.DEFAULT_PAY until then), standing "walked_home"
  (3) from the kin who asked and from the one walked home; a player who
  never took the plea is paid the same (the arrival is the event); a plea
  held by another player closes with the notice and no pay; home on
  their own, the plea closes with the fact and no pay. Nothing accepted,
  nothing handed in.
- Danger: a lost body is left alone by every monster but a raider's
  group (enemy-ai: targeting by class), and wakes none (World.sought
  ignores Residents); the player beside them wakes what the player
  wakes. If Jeff wants the escortee hunted, enemy-ai offers one more case
  in the target filter, not asked for now.

Numbers (npc's drafts, Jeff's to move): strays every 54000, chance 0.1,
days 3, far 24, the four trades; commissions.escort 8; standing
walked_home 3. townsfolk_test (who is lost and who never is, one at a
time, the cell kept, home on their own after three days); offers_test
(the kin's plea, taken, walked home by the one who took it: notice, pay,
standing both ways, both cards; by another with no plea: notice and pay;
on their own: the plea closes unpaid); resident_test (the body at the
chosen cell far from the store on walkable ground, her facts, her kin's
plea, a word and she follows, home at the town's ground: back, the card
clear, her body the town's again). Protocol unchanged (a resident body
is an existing spawn; no new message); no new class_name of npc's (Heel
is companions', 485).

Rejected: a body carried through portals (a Main.travel change for one
errand); the escortee as a far record (never away from a player); the
stray as a captive (that is the rescue, 435); a verb to parse ("come
with me": any word to the lost one is enough; they want to go home).

Amended 2026-10-19 (the soak, 496): a stray who finds their own way home
closes the kin's pleas to walk them home unpaid, with the fact and the
party-log line "Tam came home on his own" (Townsfolk.stray calls
Offers.walked_home with nobody); before, the pleas stayed open and lapsed
seven days later against the players who had taken them.

## 490. The bard sings what the town remembers

The hidden types' side-doings (393: "scoundrel, thieves, and bards isn't
a profession might be more of a hidden personality type"; the thief 393
and 461, the scholar and the merchant 440), the coordinator's assignment
and approval of 2026-10-18 with two adds (lore at most every other night
with the lawspeaker off; a founding fact). Rules: the source is the
town's memory (447) and the lawspeaker's rulings (448), else lore's
facts; never a sentence that is not in one of those; no model call;
prompts say what is true, never what to say.

- When: on the gossip tick (422) in a town whose inn stands
  (Towns.building "inn"; Offers.ctx "has_inn") with a bard whose
  whereabouts is the inn (residents.json "types".bard: 18 to 23), once a
  night (the card's "sang"). Townsfolk.perform.
- What, in this order: a town memory (TownMemory's MEMORY tier: the
  lawspeaker's accepted and reconciled sentences) that names a player in
  the inn tonight (said by them, or their name in it) and has not been
  sung to them ("sung_to" on the entry), so a player hears their story
  told back, once per story; else the newest memory not sung within
  "again" days (30); else lore's agreed facts for the town (Offers.ctx
  "lore", 448's source), the weightiest not sung within the same span, and
  lore at most every "lore_every_nights" nights (2), so the inn does not
  hear the same three facts nightly. Nothing else exists to sing.
- The words: a kind drawn by seed (the bard and the day) round the
  entry's own sentence: "At the inn, Tam sings of how / tells the tale of
  how / has a song of how <sentence>." The sentence is the entry's text,
  its first letter lowered unless the first word is somebody's name (a
  deed starts with its doer); nothing added inside it. A second line, "The
  lawspeaker's word on it: <because>.", when the ruling has one. The body,
  when one stands in the inn, says "Hear now how <sentence>." for the
  bubble (Main._sung, the usual speech message).
- Who hears: every player standing in the town's inn (Main's "listeners":
  the inn's rect in this zone, the players whose tile is in it), a "party"
  line each (and the second), and the named one "It is your own deed Tam
  sings of."; nobody outside the inn. Residents at the inn that hour hold
  the memory (TownMemory.hold): a song spreads what the town remembers.
- After: each listening player's standing with the bard moves "song" (1;
  Standing, a new key beside heard), twice for their own deed, their entry
  made if new (Standing.met); the bard's card learns "Tam sang of ... at
  the inn tonight" (the voice knows it after, 398); the entry keeps the
  night and whom it was sung to. At founding, a bard's card gets "Tam sings
  at the inn of an evening." (Townsfolk.card_of), so the voice can say what
  they do when asked.
- Lawspeaker off (the box today): the town remembers nothing (memories
  come only from rulings), so a bard at an inn sings lore every other night
  at most, the weightiest facts first and round again after 30 days, and no
  player's deed is ever sung, since no ruling ever names one. That is the
  server's behaviour until Jeff turns rulings on.
- Cost: one table lookup per town per gossip tick; a line a night; no
  model.

Numbers (npc's drafts, Jeff's to move): residents.json "bard" {again 30,
lore_every_nights 2, kinds}; standing song 1. gossip_test (the founding
fact; Jeff in the inn hears his own deed first with the ruling's word,
twice the notch, the entry marked, Mara holding it; once a night; the
newest memory the next night; lore when both are lately sung, every other
night, the next fact after; no standing inn, no song). Protocol unchanged
("party" and "speech" are existing messages); no new class_name.

Rejected: a model writing the song (invention); singing beliefs or
rumours (422 passes those as talk); every zone hearing it (the inn's
walls); pay for the bard (Jeff may want a hat passed, later).

Amended (art-kit's side, 2026-10-22; Jeff, through the coordinator: "bard
could wear a hat yes"): the bard's hat is art-kit's gear.hat, a held slot
(category items, not an item) worn on pc-character's "head" socket: a red
felt cap peaked toward the back, the brim turned up behind and drawn to a
point over the brow, a buckled band, a long feather on the left; 304 tris.
Its frame, agreed with pc-character: origin at the inside of the crown on
the skull's top (the socket measured per body at the skull's middle, front
to back), +y up, +x toward the face, the band 0.075 m below ("base"); sized
to human_m's head and fitted by pc-character on the five builds with no
scaling (0.6 to 4 cm off the head at the band, nothing through). Nothing
draws it until pc-character's socket and npc's "hat=bard" land; client art
only, protocol unchanged.

Amended (2026-10-24, the bard's hat, npc's side; Jeff: "bard could wear a
hat yes"): the bard's body wears art-kit's gear.hat, a red felt cap with a
feather, on pc-character's new "head" socket (people only, measured per
build). npc's side is the word: ResidentCard.look_spec takes the worker's
hidden type (Main._spawn_resident passes it) and puts "hat=bard" into the
bard's look spec, before the apron word; Client3D.HATS maps the word to the
piece, a word it does not know or a build without the piece wears nothing
new, and an old client ignores the key, so the wire is unchanged (a line
under PROTOCOL_REVISION 35, the open one, records the new look word). The type stays
hidden: the hat says bard to anyone who knows bards wear them, which is
the point of a bard. resident_card_test: the hat in his look and in nobody
else's.

## 493. Short measure on an item instance

For npc's scoundrel (393's hidden types; its 492), approved by the
coordinator with Jeff's rule: a thing a scoundrel makes may come out short,
but only a thing measured by count or weight, never a weapon, a tool or a
piece of gear (no quality tiers on gear).
- Items.measured(id): a resource with a yield (a sack, a bolt, a hide) or a
  bundle of arrows with a count (its condition). Everything else, gear and
  whole things like a ration, is never short.
- ItemBook.make_short(uid, fraction := 0.6): once, for life. A bundle's
  count drops to that share of its most (rounded down, at least 1: 6 arrows
  of 10). A resource keeps "short" (saved), and ItemBook.yields_of(uid),
  which banking (World._bank_thing) and Production's made goods now read
  in place of Items.yield_of, gives each count's share (rounded down, at
  least 1: a food sack banks 3 food of 5; a single hide stays 1, so a stack
  comes up short by count, economy's call). False and nothing for a thing
  not measured or already short.
- Noted "short" (a kept event) naming no one: the maker is in its "made"
  event, and a hidden scoundrel is found out by his debts, not his sacks.
  Its note adds "short measure", and so does its story.
- npc calls it once, when economy says a worker finished the thing, before
  it is banked.
Protocol unchanged: a client reads no yield, and the note is the server's
text. items_test's _test_short.

**Amended (the bard's hat, pc-character's side; Jeff said yes via the coordinator, 2026-10-22).**
People get a "head" socket, and a hat drawn on it from a look word.
- The socket: on the Head bone at the top of the skull, at its middle front to back, +x to the
  face and +y up, level in the body's frame as the shoulder's is (`Client3D._head_socket`). It is
  measured once per body mesh from its own vertices, so the man (0.228 m above the bone) and the
  woman (0.216) each get theirs; the builds' shape keys leave the head alone. People only (their
  sockets' "crown").
- The word: "hat=<word>" in a look spec (npc's `ResidentCard.look_spec` gives the bard "hat=bard"),
  read from `PersonLook.words`. `Client3D.HATS` maps it to an art slot and variant ("bard":
  art-kit's gear.hat, a felt cap with a feather, made in the socket's frame). `_wear_hat` puts it on
  and hides the look's own hood, brimmed hat or cap.
- A word not in HATS, or a build without the piece, wears nothing new and leaves the look as it
  was, so an old client ignores the word.
- Fitted on the five builds: nothing through the band, at most 4 cm off the head. The first
  socket, at the skull's top vertex, sat forward of the skull's middle, and the back of the head
  came 3 cm through the band.
- Tests: view_test `_test_head_socket`. Client only, protocol unchanged.

## 491. The scholar's chronicle

The hidden types' side-doings (393; the scholar's first three in 440),
the coordinator's assignment and approval of 2026-10-18; ui's answer on
the talk log (one message, the lines joined by newlines, wrapped and
scrolled as one entry; accept word "read", which the offers panel
renders from its word table). Rules: everything on the page is a
sentence the town holds already (447's memory, 448's rulings, 458's
proposals, lore's facts); nothing written by a model; prompts say what is
true, never what to say.

- The page (TownMemory.chronicle, pure, 458's shape): "The chronicle of
  <town>, kept by <scholar>." Then, oldest first, what the town set down:
  each MEMORY entry as "On day N the town set down that <sentence>." with
  the lawspeaker's "because" after it ("The lawspeaker's word: ..."); the
  newest "chronicle.lines" (12) of them and "The rest is in the book."
  when cut. Then the proposals to lore (458's "proposed" entries) with
  their status read as 458 reads it from Jeff's page
  (TownMemory.proposed_statuses of Net.proposed_path; Main's "statuses").
  Then the open disputes before the lawspeaker (486's entries). With
  nothing set down: "The town has set down nothing yet." and what lore
  knows of the town ("Of <town> it is known that ...", the townsfolk's
  agreed facts, weightiest first, "chronicle.lore" (6) at most). A name at
  the front of a sentence keeps its capital (TownMemory.clause).
- Whose: the scholar's (type "scholar"). A town without one has no
  chronicle (the lawspeaker keeps memory in his head, the bard in his
  songs). The desk is the scholar's home (404's routine): the offer "Read
  the chronicle" (Offers kind "page", accept "read", cost 0, first in the
  list) appears only while the scholar's whereabouts is home; at the
  counter or the well they offer nothing of it. Taking it records no ask
  and pays nothing: Offers.accept returns the lines ("read"), Main sends
  them to that player's talk log as one "party" message from the scholar
  with the lines joined by newlines (Main._read_page; never "speech",
  which would pop the page as a bubble); standing: met only.
- Read aloud: the scholar's voice holds the same truth as facts (the
  memories already, 447; now "You proposed to the lore-keepers that ...:
  it is open/accepted"), so a question in words gets what is set down and
  no more.
- "What is true" in the facts (Resident.facts_now): a lawspeaker in a
  town with a scholar gets "X, the town's scholar, keeps the chronicle:
  what is set down there the town remembers; send a doubter to X."; a
  scholar gets "You keep the town's chronicle: what the lawspeaker set
  down, what the town proposed to the lore-keepers, and the disputes
  before him. When asked what is true, say what is set down and no more."
  Statements of what is true of them, not lines to say; the lawspeaker's
  request to the model (448) is unchanged.
- The page tool (458, tools/proposed_page.tscn) takes --chronicle=<town
  id> (and --statuses=<proposed.md>) to write a town's whole chronicle from
  a local or test snapshot for Jeff; the server writes no chronicle file
  (the proposals page is Jeff's channel; one more file later if he wants
  it).
- Lawspeaker off (the box today): the town sets down nothing, proposes
  nothing and notes no disputes, so a scholar's chronicle reads "The town
  has set down nothing yet." and lore's facts of the town; the facts above
  still hold (the chronicle exists, and is empty). That is the server's
  behaviour until Jeff turns rulings on.
- Cost: the page is built when read (one pass over the log, at most 200
  entries); no tick work; no model.

Numbers (npc's drafts, Jeff's to move): residents.json "chronicle"
{lines 12, lore 6}. memory_test (empty with lore to the cap; the parts in
order with the ruling's word, a name kept, the status from the page, the
dispute; the newest twelve and the rest in the book); offers_test (the
offer first and only at home, only from a scholar; the read returns the
lines; no ask, no pay, met); resident_test (the lawspeaker's and the
scholar's facts). Protocol unchanged (the new kind and accept word ride the
"offers" message as data the client renders from title and words, "read"
as "Read" until ui's word table has it; accept uses the "offer" verb
with no new field; "party" exists); no new class_name.

Rejected: a model writing the chronicle (invention); a new message kind
for a page (ui's work and a protocol bump for a dozen talk-log lines); a
chronicle file on the box; the chronicle as an item to carry.

## 492. The scoundrel: short measures and a bad loan

The hidden types' side-doings (393; the thief 393/461, the scholar and
merchant 440, the bard 490, the scholar's chronicle 491), the coordinator's
assignment and approval of 2026-10-18 with Jeff's rule on gear; economy's
side is 8c65639 ("492, economy's side": Production.made, folk_factor and
repay by type, rules "scoundrel" {buy 1.0, sell 1.1, repay 0.0}); items'
side is Items.measured and ItemBook.make_short (their number). Rules: no
model; nothing invented; the town learns of him only through what he does.

- Short measures (Townsfolk.made_short, on Production.made, which
  economy emits before the thing reaches the shelf and, for a made
  resource, between the mint and the yield's banking, so a short sack
  banks short: items' ordering point): when the maker's type is scoundrel and the thing
  is measured by count or weight (Items.measured: a food or ore sack, a
  cloth bolt, an arrow bundle, hides by the stack; never a weapon, tool,
  armour or piece of gear: Jeff's rule, no damage or quality tiers on
  gear), a seeded draw (the maker and the instance) against
  townsfolk.json "scoundrel.short" (0.5) makes it short to "scoundrel.weight"
  (0.6) of its full through ItemBook.make_short (an arrow bundle's count,
  a sack's per-instance yield; items' side), noted in the thing's history
  as "short measure" and nowhere else: the counter sells it at the full
  price, and the thing tells on him only in the hand (the look reads its
  measure and its story). A scoundrel who makes gear just makes it. The

## 494. No two goblins alike, by name: build, skin, gear and a mark

The backlog's "body variation for monsters", its look half (the coordinator: "a raid shouldn't
be clones"). The goblin is the pack's own model: one painted mesh, one material, no parts. Each
goblin is now its own by its name, which every peer has (162's seed), with no protocol change:
Client3D.goblin_look(name), seeded by an FNV-1a hash of the name's bytes (not the engine's
String hash, so every build agrees; release), gives

- its build: a width on x and z, GOBLIN_WIDTH (0.88 to 1.12), on top of 162's size by mass;
  drawn only (its mass, if it is to follow, is enemy-ai's);
- its skin: the paint's green texels shifted in hue, saturation and value (GOBLIN_SKIN_*),
  within the Blood Rot's greens, yellowish to bluish, darker to paler;
- its gear: the paint's other texels (hood, wraps, leather; not the eyes) tinted toward one of
  GOBLIN_GEAR, row 5 to 7's browns, greys, a dull red, ochre and straw, keeping their shading,
  or its own (GOBLIN_OWN_GEAR of the time);
- a mark, or none (GOBLIN_UNMARKED of the time): a scar across the left eye, white cheek
  stripes, or a red hand over the mouth, a channel each of goblin_marks.png (tools/goblin_marks.py
  draws them over the paint's UVs);
- its words ("build=lean skin=dark gear=red mark=scarred", a word only where it stands out),
  kept on its puppet ("goblin_look") for a companion's voice to say "the scarred one" if lore
  wants it later; nothing reads them yet.

One ShaderMaterial for every goblin (goblin_body.tres, goblin.gdshader with
goblin.gdshaderinc), its look as instance parameters (skin, gear, mark), so a raid batches as
before: 20 animated goblins drew in the same 100 draw calls with it as with the pack's own
material, their frames within noise (0.76 to 0.85 ms mean against 0.80 to 0.83, a scratch bench
under the bench lock). The hover outline's stencil copy of it is goblin_marking.gdshader, the
same drawing marking the stencil (Client3D._marking_copy). Roughness from the paint's shine, no
metal, as the pack's material had it.

Next, as this amended: the hood split from the mesh (a scalp patch if the head is hollow), so it
can be down by seed, and the ears scaled about their root.

view_test: each goblin its own by name, alike for the same name; one shared material, the look
as instance parameters; a raid of 40 with marks and builds; the outline's stencil with the
goblin's shader. Sheet of ten for Jeff: C:\dev\review\goblins\goblins_v1.png.

## 489. BuildingComposer: a kind's look, seeded, off the grid

Step 3 of Jeff's building variety (488 is step 1; art-kit's slots are
step 2), approved by the coordinator, client only. 488's rule binds it:
the grid is the rules, the look need not show it.
- BuildingComposer (new class_name, client3d/building_composer.gd) draws
  what stands over a kind's walls: each block's roof by its role (488's
  "roles"), the main block's a gable along its longer side at the kind's
  eaves; a wing's a gable 0.25 to 0.5 m lower; a lean-to's, an outshot's or
  a bay's a single slope rising to the block it leans on, its low eave 0.7
  to 1 m under the main eaves and its high side LEAN_TUCK under them; a
  round kind's one faceted cone (FACETS, each point straying FACET_STRAY)
  over all its blocks. Every roof reaches 0.3 to 0.5 m past its walls,
  rises 0.75 to 1.1 of its half-span, sags 1 to 2.5% of its length in the
  middle of its ridge (its eaves straight), is shifted up to SHIFT and the
  whole tilted up to TILT off true, its ends closed down to the eaves in
  the kind's wall set. A chimney at one gable end of a house's main block,
  a little off its middle, by kind (CHIMNEYS' odds; a ruin's less):
  art-kit's chimney.stone on the roof line when that slot is there, else
  a stack and cap of the stone set. A ruin has no roof.
- Seeded: each block draws from its own stream (the building's seed and
  its index), its eaves first, so Client3D draws each outline wall to its
  block's eaves (wall_heights: a wing's and a lean-to's lower, at heights
  no whole metre) without building the roof; the building's own (tilt,
  chimney) from another. Every peer draws one building alike.

  look, the copies (Node.duplicate) sharing their meshes (the coordinator's
  condition: a street costs one build each).
- Client3D._add_kind places the composed node; its "roof" is what hides
  while the player is inside, fades and sags damaged as a slot's roof does.
  A ruin's outline walls are drawn broken here and there (RUIN_BROKEN of

- Not yet: a wall set inside its edge or of another thickness, and the
  stone plinth (terrain's advice: a second surface in the wall sweep, the
  profile split at 0.6 m, its top cut at each edge's base), and the
  porches, cruck frames, shutters and signs when art-kit's slots come; the
  thatch roof set when art-kit makes it (shingle until then).
- tools/kinds_town (a scene; APPDATA a temp folder only) writes a street

## 495. Shader warm-ups: a material drawn once at load, not first at play

A material's pipelines are compiled the first time it is drawn, so its first
draw can cost a frame: pc-character's goblin outline (494, its stencil
twin) took 20.6 ms on the first hover on a fresh profile. Perf asked for a
warm-up; the coordinator approved it on one condition, that it never shows.
- Client3D.warm_ups: Array[Callable], each a static func's Callable taking
  nothing and returning a Node3D drawn as in play (a skinned instance, its
  next pass or stencil twin, its shadows), or null. Never a lambda: a
  lambda held in a static Callable array has crashed Godot at exit here
  (exit 139) and one capturing objects leaks at exit. Registered from client
  code only; the server builds no rooms and its pck has no art.
- After a room is built (setup and rebuild; not a glimpse's), each not yet
  warmed in this process is added WARM_DEPTH (6 m) under the ground at the
  view's middle, at its own size, for WARM_FRAMES (2) frames, then freed.
  Its draws are issued, so its pipelines compile (colour, depth prepass,
  shadow, next pass, stencil), but every fragment fails the depth test
  behind the opaque ground: nothing of it shows on screen or in a shot, and
  its shadow falls below the ground. A scale of 0.01 just past the near
  plane was the first idea; rejected, as a drawn speck could show.
- Godot's own help, to check before adding a warm-up: Forward+ on d3d12
  (project.godot rendering_device/driver.windows) compiles pipelines in
  the background with ubershaders (4.4 and on), and keeps a shader and
  pipeline cache in user data (the defaults; none set here); occlusion
  culling is off, which a warm-up behind the ground relies on.
- The first registered: GrownTrees.warm, a pad of needles in the forest's
  see-through passes and its shadow-only twin (467). Its own case was
  small: a fresh profile's forest start's worst frame 7.7 ms before, 5.4 to
  7.1 after, the wilds 7.4 to 8.7, all within a run's noise; the goblin's
  first hover is the number that matters (pc-character measures it).
view_test _test_warm_ups (drawn under the ground after a build, freed after
WARM_FRAMES, never twice in a process; the forest's registered); map_bench
on a fresh profile exits 0 with no resources left at exit.

## 496. The living-world soak: the town run for a month, and what it found

The coordinator's ask of 2026-10-19, before the lawspeaker is turned on:
run the wilds town locally for 30 days as the box runs it (the lawspeaker
off, Snagfin seated, the thief, the bard, strays, the scoundrel) with test
players standing in the inn of an evening and at the counter by day, read
the transcripts and the talk log, fix what is npc's, route the rest. The
proof Jeff's "living world" line asks for.

- The tool: tools/town_soak.tscn (a scene, so the autoloads load; headless,
  through the bench gate: --days=30 --players=3 --out=<a local folder>).
  It boots Main as the server on the wilds with a scratch world (never the
  box's), seats the balance tool's nine folk and a guard with their hidden
  types set outright (a thief, a bard, a scholar, a scoundrel), admits two
  far peers beside the host's player, gives each sixty gold, and steps the
  world a day in about forty seconds. Every hour it stands the players
  where a player would be (the inn's rect from 19 to 22 when the town has
  one, a cell beside the counter at 10, 11, 15 and 16, the square else),
  and at the counter each hears what the bodies within reach offer, takes
  the first commission, plea or page and buys the first sale they can pay
  for; every third day one speaks to the nearest body. It counts what
  happened through Main's own Offers context (offers by kind, taken,
  done, paid, bought) and prints "SOAK ..." lines: the ledger's moves,
  every resident's stints seen, purse, loan, facts and standing with each
  player, the songs, the errand lines, the party log's tail; transcripts
  and the mind log go under --out. scratchpad soak_read.py (npc's, not
  committed) reads a run: events, repeated lines, lines a day per resident.
- The first month (before): 13 residents, 3 to 5 transcript lines a day
  each; 4,587 offers heard (2,526 rumours, 1,582 pleas, 479 sales), 6
  taken, 6 done (all lapses), 0 gold paid out, 18 bought for 43 gold; 15
  gold lifts by the thief, 0 store lifts, 0 caught, 0 fenced; 2 strays, both
  home on their own; 0 songs (the wilds built no inn in the month); the
  scoundrel's debt 22 of the cap 30; 619 gossip passes.
- What was npc's, fixed here: gossip told the same pair the same line up
  to 36 times a month (a thing that fell off a hearer's heard cap could be
  told them again; a hearer's card now keeps what it was told, "told",
  TOLD_MAX 64, and nothing is told them twice: 422 amended); a stray who
  came home on their own left the kin's pleas to lapse against the players
  who took them (Townsfolk.stray now closes them unpaid through
  Offers.walked_home: 487 amended); the promise words lower-cased names
  ("walk ash home"; Offers._promise has words for an escort and a quarrel:
  435 amended). gossip_test, offers_test, townsfolk_test.
- Routed with the line: to economy, the carpenter who "waits for tannery:
  its materials went to work that came first" 5,399 times in the month and
  never built the inn the town wanted from day 0 (so the bard of 490 is
  silent on the box until that moves), the treasury at its floor all month
  with the officials unpaid 85 to 88 times each, and the hunter's "found no
  game" 484 times. Not fabricated anywhere: every transcript line traced to
  a card fact, a belief or lore; no resident stuck in one stint; no errand
  paid twice (none paid: no raid, no captive and no camp threatened the
  town in the month, so no commission was ever offered).
- The second month (after): the same town, same month: 1.0 to 4.5 transcript
  lines a day each (no line said to one hearer twice; the only repeats
  left are the test players' own question and the stub mind's answer);
  gossip passes 619 to 467; 3,097 offers heard (the fewer because the
  players stood at the counter's four cells, not its corners), 6 taken, 6
  done, all "came home on their own", unpaid and with no lapse against
  anyone (the kin's standing with the players 0 where it had been -1 and
  -2); 15 gold lifts again, 0 caught; 2 strays again; still no inn and no
  song, the carpenter's line 5,399 times again, which is economy's.

Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 497. The woodcutter: wood into the town's store, so a town can build

npc's 30-day soak of the wilds (496, 2026-10-18) found the town had built
nothing in a month: no wood was ever banked, and every building costs
wood. Only players brought it. Jeff (2026-10-18, through the
coordinator): yes to a woodcutter at these numbers; "makers have more
expense - raw material", so gatherers feed the store.
- A trade, woodcutter (economy.json "woodcutter": trade, every 3000
  steps, wood 2 a cut, per_level 1 more for each level of a standing
  woodshed): each one in town, not away, brings wood into the store on
  the hunter's pattern (Towns._woodcut, the next cut per resident saved as
  the town's cut_due). About 34 wood a day; Jeff's to move.
- The woodshed (buildings.woodshed: trade woodcutter, by the carpenter,
  xp 10, cost nothing, 1500 steps, max level 3): free, so a town without
  wood can still build it. The woodcutter works without one.
- How one comes: by rescue (rescue.trades weight 3), or, as the field gets
  its farmer (449), by growth: a town with a planned building whose wood
  it lacks and no woodcutter gets a newcomer after woodcutter.growth_days
  (2), named from woodcutter.names.
- The inn costs leather 5 instead of cloth 5 until a weaver exists (cloth
  has no source; the tannery makes leather from the hunter's hides).
Selling wood to the store at a price (Jeff's maker expenses) is the next
step. Protocol unchanged. farm_test (a day's cutting, the woodshed, away,
a newcomer only when a building waits on wood, and only one).

Amended 2026-10-19: the words soak. tools/town_soak takes --ask: each day
one test player asks each resident with a body one of five things in
rotation ("Who are you?", "What is new in the town?", "What do you need?",
"What do you think of <another resident>?", "Is it true that <a lore
fact>?"), the player put beside them, and the loop waits for the answer
(driving Main._resident_voices, which otherwise runs on the world tick)
up to a minute, one request per ask and no retries, so the box's Ollama
is never tied up; it writes cards.json (every card, belief and standing,
and lore's facts) beside the transcripts and the mind log, whose "voice"
entries carry each prompt and answer. Run with --llm-url and --llm-model
pointing at the box's Ollama over the ssh tunnel (the box's world stays
on the box: only prompts travel), and only when nobody is on the box's
server. scratchpad words_read.py (npc's, not committed) reads a run:
each answer against its prompt (sentences, names not in the prompt,
talk of a thief or a debt the prompt does not hold, narration).

The first five days (before): 60 asks, 60 answered (one timed out in
the smoke); 11 answers over two sentences, 2 beginning with the
speaker's name; no secret spoken (no one named the thief or another's
debt, only their own); every name and place a card's, a player's or
lore's; the bard embellished a blade onto the priest, the thief (a liar
by 378) an invented meeting; Snagfin's card words called him "a
merchant, and keeps it hidden"; the scholar spoke as the chronicler, the
lawspeaker as the keeper of memory, Snagfin as a merchant with bees (his
hobby) and never as a goblin though his prompt said so.
The second five days (after): 60 asks, 60 answered; 0 over two
sentences and 0 beginning with a name (the code's rule; the model still
ran on in 10 of 60 and the cut took it to two); no secret spoken; every
name a card's, a player's or lore's; the embellishers kept to their
cards; what remained, fixed here too: a self-told fact passed on lost its
subject ("Odo told me he's a goblin": a retold belief that begins with a
pronoun now carries who said it), and asked about someone they know
nothing of, four voices invented a past mention ("Gar spoke of him once,
though not kindly": the voice is now told to say plainly it knows little
of them). Still the model's, noted for Jeff: a liar lies about a
neighbour (378's tier, lore asked), a plain or official voice slips a
trait onto someone once in sixty, Snagfin never volunteers that he is a
goblin though his prompt says so, and the soak tool now reads
Townsfolk.tally instead of the store's windowed ledger.

Amended 2026-10-19: the soak's players at the counter. The 30-day run of
2026-10-19 refused 360 buys with "you must stand at the town's counter":

hour. The earlier runs' bought and buy_failed counts read against this.

## 501. Sickness (npc's), items' side: the remedy

Jeff (2026-10-18, through the coordinator) said yes to sickness: a sick
resident is cured by the medicine man's visit, a walk to the healer, or
a remedy a player puts into their hands (443's gift path). The coordinator
agreed the cure is its own item, not the bandaging kit (a kit is a tool
that is kept, never used up).
- levels/items.json "remedy" ("healing remedy", tag medical, value 4, art
  slot item.remedy, 0.3 kg, one hand): one dose, a whole thing. It is not
  measured (Items.measured: no yield, no count), so a scoundrel's short
  measure (493) never touches it.
- No "made": there is no healer trade and no herb resource. The healer and
  the medicine man sell it from stock (economy). No "use" for a player:
  it cures by being given, and npc's side consumes it.
- slots_items.json and the art status regenerated.
npc's sickness itself follows under this number. Protocol unchanged; no
new class_name.

## 498. Gathered, hauled and paid for: the store buys, makers pay for materials

Jeff (2026-10-18, word for word): "gold economy - makers have more expense
- raw material and apprentices - trade with other town", and "everything
has to be gathered and someone paid to do it, wood cutter, hauler, hunter
etc". Phase 1 of three (trade routes and luxury goods follow); the
coordinator's approval with two guards. Numbers are economy.json's,
Jeff's to move.
- Pay on delivery: whatever a resident brings into the town's store (the
  hunter's meat and hide, the farmer's harvest and roots, the woodcutter's
  wood, a maker's raw like the tanner's leather) goes through
  Production.deliver_to, which Main and the balance tool point at
  Economy.deliver: banked, and bought at raw_price x store.buy (1.0), the
  same table the shop's prices read, from the treasury above gold_floor.
- Hauling is paid per load: the town's hauler who carried longest ago
  (in town, not away) carries it, haul.fee (1) for every haul.load (5),
  out of the gatherer's price. With no hauler the gatherer keeps it all.
  Haulers lose their time wage (official.hauler): pay is for work done.
- What the treasury can't pay now is owed to the worker (Production
  "owed", saved), paid first as gold comes in (Economy._pay_owed on its
  tick). Guard 1: once the town owes a worker store.owed_cap (30) the
  store buys no more from them ("the town can't pay Bran for more wood",
  once, in the ledger), so a stalled treasury shows instead of piling up
  debt. A maker's raw it won't take stays theirs, on their shelf.
- Makers pay for materials: a make or rework job's resources are bought
  from the store when it starts (Production.buy_materials ->
  Economy.buy_materials) at raw_price x store.sell (1.1). Guard 2: never
  under the last unit price the store paid for that resource (x sell), so
  a maker never buys for less than the gatherer and hauler were paid.
  Paid from the purse or a loan (the bank as for anything); a maker who
  can't pay waits ("its maker can't pay for the materials"). Town work
  (builds, the town's mends) costs the town nothing, and so do the town's
  meals (store.town_account: things tagged food, the cook's): a cook at
  her loan cap still cooks, and a meal's sale sends its materials share
  to the treasury as before.
- Players bank goods for gold (Jeff, 2026-10-18: "players bank goods for
  gold and if they want they spend gold later to help the town ...
  players lose gold through spend"): raw goods a player (or their
  companion) banks at a store are bought at the same delivery price
  (Economy.bank_sale, from World._bank_thing; a counter sale is paid at
  the counter as before), the rest owed and paid as gold comes in
  (Economy.owed_paid -> World.gold_changed). Past owed_cap the goods are
  the town's as a gift, said in the ledger. Player gold is never lost to
  death or theft, only to spending.
- A sale's tax by class of goods. Jeff (2026-10-18): "taxes can be most
  higher on luxury goods which the rich prefer then wages are paid by
  town". economy.json tax_class {staple 0.1, made 0.2, luxury 0.5}
  (Economy.goods_class: a thing tagged luxury, then food and raws as
  staples, the rest made) in place of tax.sale; the luxuries themselves
  are phase 3's. From the treasury it fills, the town pays its wages:
  the officials and what it owes gatherers and haulers.
- A shop sale no longer sends the made thing's materials value to the
  treasury once makers buy their materials (it would charge them twice):
  that share is the maker's.
Apprentices come as 498 amended. Unset hooks (tests, tools) bank free, as
before. Protocol unchanged. larder_test.

Measured with npc's soak (496), 30 days, 3 players, the woodcutter (497)
on both sides of it: before (main), no building in the month; after, the
tannery on day 2.3, the field and the woodshed on day 2.5, the inn on day
26.2 and the field at level 2. The inn comes late because it waits on
leather 5: the hunter brings home about 1.8 animals a day (the herds'
take_share), each one hide, and the tanner works them into leather among
his other work. That's a number, the hunt's rate against the tannery's,
for Jeff to move if he wants the inn sooner. Officials unpaid: 464 times
before, 249 after. Loans: 32 taken and 2 repaid before, 48 and 31 after,
223 outstanding at the end against 137. The smith and the carpenter end
with 170 of the town's gold. The treasury still sits at its floor: phase
1 moves the same founding gold faster, and apprentices (the makers'
second expense), players' contributions (499) and the luxury tax (phase
3) are what bring it back.

## 502. What grows wild: herbs as ground piles near the towns

npc's sickness needs herbs for the healer's remedies, and Jeff's rule is
that everything has to be gathered. The coordinator approved this on
2026-10-18 and set it on in the real wilds: it's a seeded system like the
herds, not placed content.

**The server lays real things.** The client's scatter is seeded and drawn
on the client only, so the server can't make anything out of it.
- A new server class, Forage (sim/forage.gd), keeps what grows wild.
  World keeps one (World.forage); Main makes it at boot, and the world
  tick's first slice moves it on.
- Once a game day, in each loaded outdoor zone whose area has a place the
  town holds, it first withers, then lays:
  - Withering: things that grew more than wither_days ago leave the ground
    and end "withered".
  - Laying: it lays per_day new ones, but only while fewer than most of the
    grown ones lie in the area. Each is minted "grew" and laid with
    World.put_on_ground, so it's an ordinary ground pile.
- Each cell is drawn by area, item and day, and taken only if it is:
  - grass (WorldMap's new per-area "grass" bytes)
  - under the sky (WorldRichness.under_sky)
  - dry, walkable floor with nothing lying on it and no fire
  - within reach of a town-held place, and outside every such place's ring
  - on ground nobody holds (Holdings.ground), so a camp's herbs are the
    camp's
- A town's ring is the larger of two distances:
  - the rule's ring
  - the furthest cell of any building within reach, plus clear cells
  
  In the wilds the houses reach about 22 cells from the store, so herbs
  lie outside the houses, not between them.
- The rules are levels/economy.json "forage", one entry per item:
  {per_day 4, most 10, reach 48, ring 14, clear 4, wither_days 3}.
  Economy owns them from here.
- An item the catalog lacks lays nothing. Items' "herbs" lands on its own.

**It keeps no state of its own.** What it laid is in each zone's ground,
which the snapshot already saves. The item book keeps when each thing
grew, from its first event. So a restart counts and withers them as
before, and the cap holds across saves. A restart lays that day's herbs
again, but never past most. A zone not loaded is left alone.

**Taking.** Forage.take_near(area, cell, reach = 1, id = "herbs") takes
the nearest one within reach off the ground and returns its uid, held by
nobody yet; it returns 0 if there is none or the zone isn't loaded. It's
for the medicine man's rounds (npc's side, 404): what he gathers on his
way is the same herbs a player sees. A player picks herbs up as any pile
and banks them at the store, where economy's delivery price (498) pays.

**Drawing.** Client3D.growing_slot: a pile holding only herbs stands
upright as the first of Forage.PLANTS the kit has (plant.herb, with
plant.fern as the stand-in). It's about GROWING_WIDE (0.5 m) wide, turned
by its cell, and keeps the pile's pale ring. An older client draws it as
an ordinary pile.

Protocol unchanged: piles already replicate. The new class_name is
Forage. forage_test boots the game on the wilds, with the herbs item
added for the test.

## 501. Sickness: to bed, the medicine man, the healer, a remedy

Jeff (2026-10-19, through the coordinator): "yes" to sickness in the
world, so a sick child to the medicine man can be an errand (the open
item from 486/487). The coordinator's shape and approval of the same day,
with one guard; economy's side ("501, economy's side": Production.set_sick
and "sick" on the record, Towns.died with its "died" signal,
commissions.healing 6), items' ("501, items' side": the "remedy" item, one
dose, a whole thing, sold from stock by the healer and the medicine man),
companions' ("501, companions' side", after this: the line on taking her
up, her voice's narration, companion_test), lore's names as proposals. No
plague and no contagion in this step.

- Falling sick (Townsfolk.sicken, on the world tick, once a day by town,
  seeded by the town and the day): every resident not away and not sick,
  a companion resting there too (442), draws against townsfolk.json
  "sick.chance" (0.01) times "winter" (3) in winter, "hungry" (3) after a
  hungry or doled day, "old" (2) for the old; one new case a town a day.
  The record {since, kind, treated, cured_by} is on the townsfolk card
  ("sick"), or for a companion on her player's companion card
  (companion["sick"], written here through Main and read by companions;
  "was_sick" {since, ended, cured_by} left behind once, which companions
  erase after their line). The kind is a word of "sick.kinds" (a fever, a
  cough, the shakes), for the words only. Facts on theirs ("Ada took to her
  bed with a fever.") and their kin's ("Ada, his sister, lies sick at home
  with a fever."). Economy counts them out of work but not out of need
  (set_sick: no job, wage, hunt or shop, not raided or counted for
  defence; meals, the dole and rent as ever).
- In bed (Resident.Doing.BED): the body keeps to its home all day, its
  facts say what ails it, how long, and whether anyone has seen to it;
  spoken to with a hut in reach, it lets that player walk it to the
  healer (Doing.ESCORT, companions' Heel as 487).
- Treatment, three ways, the treatment the event (435: nothing accepted,
  nothing handed in). The kin's plea (first of all pleas): "Bring the
  medicine man" when the town's zone has a healer's hut with its medicine
  man (404), else "Take <name> to the healer" when it has the hut. A word
  to the medicine man with the plea open (Offers.spoke_to) puts a visit on
  his day (Main._send_healer: Resident.Doing.VISIT to the sick one's home
  for "sick.visit_hours" (2); his body walks there with its routine when
  one stands; the visit treats them when its hours run, watched or not:
  Main._visits_due). Reaching the hut's ground at heel treats them (the
  healer's). A "remedy" put into their hands (443's gift path) is used up
  and treats them at once. Treated (Townsfolk.treat), the sickness breaks
  that night and they are on their feet the next morning; untreated it
  runs "sick.days" (5). Nobody is rolled again the morning they got up or
  died. A remedy used up, or a gift banked (443), leaves a resident's
  slot by the server's own act (Main._out_of_hands: World.set_slots and
  the instance placed): nobody reaches a resident's slots by
  World.reaches, so the gift's banking by take_item never moved it.
- The end (Townsfolk._sick_ends): on their feet ("thinner for it" when
  untreated); or, untreated, one of the town's own who is old dies with
  "sick.death_old" (0.25): the coordinator's guard for this step, never a
  named arrival with a player's story (origin "rescued:..." or "settled":
  a rescued captive, Snagfin) and never a companion, so Jeff does not lose
  a person he brought home to a dice roll before he has seen the system
  work; lifted when he says. A death goes through economy's Towns.died
  (the purse to the loan then the treasury, the house freed, the town's
  log line), the kin's card learns it, and with rulings on it is a
  candidate memory for the lawspeaker ("Ada died of a fever in the
  winter"), so it may be set down (447), sung (490) and read (491).
- Pay and memory (Offers.healed): every plea to see to them is met; the
  player whose word, walk or remedy did it gets the notice, the treasury's
  "healing" (6, economy's key; Offers.DEFAULT_PAY until it is there) and
  standing "healed" (3) from the kin who asked and from the sick one;
  another's hand closes a plea with the notice and no pay; recovered or
  died, with the fact and no lapse against anyone (illness is nobody's
  promise broken).
- Lawspeaker off (the box today): everything above runs but the memory
  candidate, which waits for him. Stated as the server's behaviour.
- Companions' part: a resting companion rolls the same (her own seed,
  only while she rests in town), keeps to her bed, is cured by anyone in
  the same three ways, never dies of it; her player learns it on taking
  her up and in her voice (companions' side); taken out of town sick, she
  is well after Townsfolk.sick_days() (companions' side, in the party). A
  remedy in her hands in the party is not this step.

Numbers (npc's drafts, Jeff's to move): townsfolk.json "sick" {chance
0.01, winter 3, hungry 3, old 2, days 5, death_old 0.25, visit_hours 2,
kinds}; economy's commissions.healing 6; standing healed 3.
townsfolk_test (one case a day, the cards, its course, the death of the
old of the town's own and never a rescued one, treated it breaks that
night, a resting companion's record on her player's card and no death);
offers_test (the two pleas, the word to the medicine man, the treatment's
pay and standing, a death closing a plea with no lapse); resident_test
(in bed all day, the medicine man's visit by the clock, a remedy in hand).
Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

Rejected: contagion and plague; sickness for players (372 stands); a
companion dying of it; sickness as a stint word in residents.json (it is

## 503. A death's way to the nearest temple: A* inside an area, no walk where there is no way

perf found a player's death stalling the server 1.5 to 2.8 s ("hits" in
the tick's slow line, decision 469): Main._return_place asks
Holdings.nearest for the nearest temple or healer's hut, three times (all
kinds, then each), and each asks WorldRoutes.route for every such place.
A route inside one area walked _flood from the fallen's cell, which stops
only once it reaches its cell, so most of the wilds each time; before the
distance fields are in (the raids' routes are made on the first death),
every portal of every area was flooded to, and a portal it cannot reach
floods the whole area; on netbench, with no links, the routes to the
wilds' temple flooded the wilds though nothing could get there.

Now:
- WorldRoutes._steps_between: A* by buckets in half steps, aimed by the
  octile distance (never more than the walk, so it finds a shortest one;
  world_map_test checks it against the flood on every cell of a room and
  on the wilds). The walk inside one area uses it.
- A route to an area the from area cannot lead to returns none at once
  (_areas_from), nothing walked.
- Until an area's fields are in: a walk inside it is its own walk alone
  (not every portal's as well); its portals are joined pairwise by A*;
  the walks from the start and to the end to its portals are A* each.
- Holdings.ranked: the reachable places of the kinds nearest first
  (nearest is its first); Main._return_place takes the first that is
  manned, routed once. That is the doc's "nearest manned return place";
  before, a second temple manned behind an unmanned nearer one was missed.

Measured on levels/ (the wilds' healer's hut and temple), one nearest
call: from the middle of the wilds 653 ms with the fields in and 3785 ms
before them, to 24 ms either way; across the wilds 420 to 18 ms; from the
castle before the fields 719 ms to 411 (other areas' pairs still walked);
a death made three such calls and now one ranked. On netbench (no links)
the routes to the wilds walk nothing.

Rejected: building the raids' routes at boot so the fields are always in
(threads in every hosted test, and the fallback still has to be cheap);
caching each place's distance field (a field per temple per faction for a
lookup made at a death).

## 504. Trade routes: caravans between a town and a market, raidable where they pass a camp

Economy's phase 2 of the gold economy (Jeff: "trade with other town. think
about establishing trade routes, also introduce luxury goods that traders
seek, sell to the rich"; the roadmap: "traders carry goods along maps'
routes between towns, routes on the world map and raidable"). Maps owns the
route, the walking, the raid hook and the arrival; economy owns the goods,
the prices, who goes and the trip home.

- Ends: a town (its store's place id) or a market, `market:<key>` from a
  level's new "markets" key (Level.markets_from, WorldMap.markets(); a
  market off the floor is a WorldMap problem). levels/castle has one, "the
  castle market" at (16, 9) in the keep (the coordinator's placement, one
  entry to move). Today's route: wilds/store>market:castle; town to town
  needs nothing more once there is a second town.
- TradeRoutes (sim/trade_routes.gd, World.trade, server only): routes()
  each town to each market and each pair of towns that can be walked,
  {id "<from>><to>", legs, steps, areas, exposed}, over the world routes'
  open layer (Main: the raid groups' routes, one set of distance fields):
  the caravan is the town's, held ground no wall to it; a closed link
  (463) is no way, as for every route, so the forest's way on exposes
  nothing. Made when asked, again when a place changes hands and on
  use_map (465's regeneration).
- exposed: every sample_steps (4) along the way on ground nobody holds,
  the nearest camp in raid_reach (30) cells whose side is hostile to the
  town's. eta(route) is world ticks at steps_per_world_tick (10); risk(route)
  the chance of at least one strike, from each exposed sample's world-tick
  share of its camp's strike chance (strike_chance 0.15 at full worth, or
  enemy-ai's `strike` Callable). Economy prices from both. Rules from
  economy.json trade.routes, these by default.
- send(route, {items, goods, members}, from_end) -> caravan id (either
  end); position(id) {area, cell, fraction}, kept for visible traders
  later; walks on the world tick; saved in the snapshot ("trade"); signals
  caravan_left, caravan_arrived(at_end), caravan_raided(camp, taken),
  caravan_lost(why: "taken", "no way").
- A strike (each exposed sample passed this tick, each camp once) takes
  food goods (economy's is_food Callable; "food" and "meat" unset) and the
  people: each member through Towns.resident_taken, held at the camp
  (captive_held), rescuable as raid captives are. Nothing else: items and
  other goods stay (Jeff: raids take food and people only); no gold goes
  on a caravan (economy settles at the market). A caravan with neither

## 505. Streams with fords and bridges

Infrastructure for streams (the outdoors backlog; the coordinator's split:
maps the level data, the walking and routing, the editor and a generator;
terrain the drawing; art-kit the bridge's slots; environment's spate later).
Agreed with terrain on the data, with art-kit on the slots.

- Streams are ordinary water cells. level.json "streams": [{"path":
  [[x, y], ...]}], each stream's cells in order from source to mouth along
  its middle (Level.streams_from, terrain "streams"); terrain takes the
  flow from the order. A path cell that is no water, or not beside the one
  before, warns and the stream is left out; water with no entry is still.
- A ford is a legend kind, "ford" #6fa8e0: floor, its footing the ground
  round it (Level terrain "fords"). World.is_ford is new; World.is_water
  stays deep water (the throw splash and the walk checks read it so), false
  on a ford. World.step_ticks makes a step into a ford FORD_TICK_SCALE (2)
  times as long, the same on the server and in a client's prediction;
  WorldRoutes charges FORD_COST (2) a step into one (step_cost, in _flood's
  _relax, A* and distances_from), WorldMap areas carrying "fords". A ford
  beside no water warns ("in no stream").
- A bridge is a building entry {slot: "bridge", at, facing, length, width
  1 or 2} (Level.BRIDGE, in the new Level.SPANS_WATER: the well stands in
  water, a bridge spans it). Its rect is width across by length along its
  facing; all of it over water or fords, clear of other buildings, with a
  floor bank of one height beyond each end (Level._bridge), else left out
  and said. Laid into the terrain (Level._lay_bridges): its cells floor at
  the banks' height and footing, out of "water" and "fords" into "bridged"
  (the water still drawn under it), railing wall edges on its long sides
  ("railings"), which Fields.fences lets sight through, as a field's fence.
  No inside (has_inside), no roof (Fields skips it), no walls drawn (the
  client's fences), no slot node: terrain draws art-kit's bridge.<set>.deck
  (a 1x1 segment repeated), .rail (on the outer long edges) and .end.
  Level banks only for now: heights are whole levels, and a ramp between
  two is a stair's work; art-kit's tilt (capped near 0.3 m a cell) comes
  with ramps if wanted.
- Companions and every walker use World's terrain rules, so they wade the
  ford and cross the bridge with no change of their own; stream_test walks
  a companion over the bridge behind her player.
- The editor: "ford" in the palette; the path tool's "as a stream" lays
  water path_width wide (3 at most) through its points and writes their
  course to "streams", one undo step; a resize or turn moves "streams"
  (and 504's "markets", which it did not).
- Streams.lay(map, from, to, {seed, width, waver, fords, bridges,
  keep_dry}) in sim/ (dungeon's runtime generators too): a wavering course
  1 to 3 wide, a ford where a given path crosses it or a bridge entry, cells
  in keep_dry left dry (terrain's ask: no stream under canopy over 0.6
  unless meant); the same seed the same stream. Streams.course and widen
  are the editor's.
- levels/sample has a stream at x 12 (rows 7 to 10), a ford at (12, 8) and
  a bridge at (12, 10); no stream in the wilds, the forest or the castle
  until Jeff asks.
- PROTOCOL_REVISION 19 (release): a level carried in the "terrain" message,
  or served (the box serves sample), now holds a legend kind and a slot an
  older peer cannot represent, and it would predict water where the server
  walks.

stream; a stream with a gap or off the water, a bridge on dry ground or
