## 538. A screenshot key, for Jeff's feedback

Jeff (2026-10-19, through the coordinator): "also a folder for screenshot
feedback, I don't know how to upload screenshots here." Ui's, client
only.

- Keys action "screenshot", F12 by default, rebindable in the Options and
  named in the controls list with its folder. Main.take_screenshot saves
  the viewport as PNG in Main.screenshot_folder(): settings.cfg
  screenshot_dir= when it exists or can be made (Jeff's NAS folder, shared
  by his machines), else the game's own user://screenshots; a folder that
  will not take the file (the share away) falls back to the game's own
  and the talk log says so, never silently (release's ask). The file is
  Main.screenshot_name: <zone>_<x>-<y>_<hour>h_<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>.png, the
  zone's id, the player's cell, the game hour and the clock, no name or
  id of anyone (release's ask). The talk log gets "Screenshot saved:
  <path>"; the first time, a line at the top says the folder and how to
  change it (hinted_shot=on, as the talk hint 453). The hint label is
  shared (_show_top_hint).
- Tests never write the shared user://screenshots: ui_test points
  screenshot_dir at test_ports' scratch, and the game's own folder is
  made only when a shot is saved there (release's ask).
- --test-show=shot takes one a moment in, for the shot of the log line
  and the hint.

Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 543. A WASD walk keeps to the server's queue

Jeff, playing v0.1.158: "some rubber banding around movement near the town
chests". The client shows each WASD step as it sends it, and the server
walks the queue of steps sent on its own clock (42). Once the server fell
behind on a held walk (a step it took late, a hauler in the way, a wrongly
paced step: 3a3f5335 fixed the pace), it never caught up. Logged on both
sides, every step had the same pace (3.75 ticks) but the server's queue held
2 the whole walk. Each step went past its deadline (18's blend, 24's rule),
was corrected, and dropped the shown steps the server still had queued; each
of those came back as "the server moved it elsewhere". Measured in the wilds
town by the chests: 39 to 73 corrections a minute. MovePrediction (client
only, protocol unchanged):

- The server's queue as the client has it: the WASD steps sent and not yet
  seen taken (_sent, followed from _server_at). A correction shows them again
  from the server's tile, as the server will walk them. A refused step, which
  empties the server's queue (GridEntity._on_move_refused), forgets them, and
  so does a move order (World.order_move).
- A step past its deadline that the server simply has not taken yet (the
  oldest unconfirmed, the walker still on its start) is waited for, at most
  CATCH_UP_WAIT_STEPS (2) of its length, before it counts as a misprediction
  as before.
- A new step starts no earlier than the server's last confirmed step's end
  (_server_done) plus the shown steps after it, less one step. More than a
  step behind that, the step's deadline runs from when the server will take
  it, and it is drawn up to CATCH_UP_STRETCH (half) of its length longer, so
  the gap closes. With the server keeping up, that limit is a step or more in
  the past and nothing changes: no new pause on a clean link.

Bounds: a step is never drawn more than 1.5 times its length, and a late one
is waited for at most two steps' length past its deadline. A 300 ms round
trip with the server keeping up gives no corrections and no slower step
(tests/prediction_test).

Measured: the chest walk (tools-style repro: a local wilds server, a WASD
client starting by the chests, keys held 0.5 to 2 s each, through
net_proxy), corrections a minute, before (main with 3a3f5335) and after,
two passes each:
  clean link (rtt 22 ms): 73, 54 -> 2, 1 (back steps 149, 122 -> 11, 15)
  wan (60 +-20 ms each way, 1% loss): 57, 16 -> 12, 3 (back 103, 37 -> 38, 22)
What is left on wan: the client's first step at join (before the server takes
steps), real refusals, and the link's losses.

tests/prediction_test: MovePrediction against a scripted server, one-way
trips each way and the server's tick clock: keeping up (40 ms), no
corrections and no step stretched; the first step 5 ticks late, none (main:
2, and still 2.67 ticks behind at the end), caught up to within a step; 12
ticks late, past the wait, corrected once and no more; a 300 ms round trip,
none corrected or slowed.

Rejected: pausing a held walk until the server confirms (a stutter on every
slow link); sending the held direction instead of steps (42's reasons stand).

proposal; an oath-ring was the other), one half the player's, the other
their companion's return token, both bound to the player.

  places it); World.carries_bound(entity, id, owner) says whether any of

## 547. The barrow's dead and its robbers (the crypt's monsters, step 2)

The coordinator's rulings on Jeff's crypt.md: each skeleton has a grave, a
niche of the layer it was taken from, and walks up to it; there it lies
down and goes still, a body still, till the curse renews; "in the way
means in the way": it fights what blocks its path, or strikes it, and
lets one beside its way be; the altar's guards fight on sight within the
altar room and never leave it; the robbers are human outlaws who fight and
flee when beaten. Three kinds in levels/monsters.json, their sides in
factions.json (545): "dead" skeleton and skeleton_guard, "robbers" robber.

- skeleton: idle "homeward" (Monster.Idle.HOMEWARD). Its grave (choose_grave,
  the first time it idles) is one of its level.json's "graves" ([x, y,
  band], band 0 shallowest; dungeon's Regen writes them for the barrow)
  in a band shallower than the grave nearest where it stands, else one no
  deeper, else any, never one another monster of the zone has; of those
  one by its name. It walks there (HOMEWARD_SEARCH_TILES, a barrow's
  breadth; the world tick walks it far from everyone too) and lies down
  (lay_down): laid, and GridEntity.down_until held ahead (LAID_HOLD_TICKS,
  renewed), which the views already draw as lying (343), so nothing new
  goes to clients. Struck, it stays down. rise() (the draugr's step 3) gets
  it up; one that lay at its grave then guards it. Its grave and laid are
  kept in its spawn spec's props (copied first, never the level's), so a
  save finds it lying; one killed comes back at its marker and walks again.
  A level with no graves: it wanders.
- In the way (_in_the_way, its only targeting): a step it cannot take, it
  fights whoever stands beside it on a cell nearer its grave (_blocker)
  that it may fight (a player, a kept companion, a resident as its side
  fights the town, a monster of its foes; never one of its own side, it
  waits behind); and whoever strikes it (_struck_by, moved up from
  Animal). It keeps them while it sees them; then it walks on, hunting
  nobody and going after no noise.
- skeleton_guard: GUARD, "keeps_room": its room is the level's anchor
  (the "regenerate" block's) round its post (room_of); it sees nobody
  outside it, so one leaving is let go, and hunts and follows noises not
  at all. dungeon paints two or three into the altar anchor.
- "fearless" (both dead kinds): never flees (_should_flee).
- robber: flank, wanders, cautious or cowardly (it flees when beaten),
  a dagger. Going for the altar's gold is economy's, later.
- The level.json is read once each terrain load (Monster._zone_config;
  Zone.terrain_loads counts them, since a reload or a generation keeps the
  zone).
Legend colours: none in Level.LEGEND. The barrow's level.json "legend"
carries monster_skeleton, monster_skeleton_guard and monster_robber, read
by every client through Level.legend's overrides, so no protocol bump
(release's check); a client before these kinds draws them as the stand-in
shape any monster without a model is. Server only; protocol unchanged; no
new class_name. monster_test (_test_homeward, _test_room_guard).

## 544. The draugr's blessing: downed, not gone, and brought back where they fell

Jeff's crypt page (docs/lore/crypt.md, 2026-10-19): beating the draugr
blesses you, and a companion who goes down with you and finishes it;
"a blessed player can be brought back in the field"; the draugr gives a
two-part device, the player's item and the companion's return token,
with 5, 10 or 15 uses by the difficulty, "the uses are the blessed
player's own count", spent on anyone blessed, oneself included; a fallen
companion is brought back by the player "standing still and not hit for
a few seconds ... Being hit breaks it"; the unblessed start again in town.
The coordinator approved companions' design; dungeon's barrow (540, 542),
items' halves ("544, items' side"), economy's offering (546) and
enemy-ai's draugr are beside it.

- The blessing: Main.bless(player_ids, difficulty), enemy-ai's call when
  the draugr is beaten, for the players in his lair. Each is marked
  "draugr" (540's mark_player, the mark the sealed shortcut reads) and
  given PlayerRecord.barrow {uses, of, difficulty, day}, the count by the
  field rules' uses (a harder win's count replaces a smaller one; a
  spent count is renewed as Jeff decides), and the device's half (items'
  World.mint_bound, bound to "player:<id>", into a free pack slot or on
  the ground). Their companion, if she stands alive in the same zone, is
  blessed too: "draugr" in record.companion["marks"] (saved; economy's
  offering reads it), the return token bound to her player, and the fact
  "<Name> went down into the barrow with <player> and laid the draugr to
  rest." A companion who was not there is not blessed, whatever her
  player is. Her mark gates nothing at the seal: she crosses with her
  player, as on any link (540).
- Downed, not gone: World.downed, a hook beside 314's spared (asked after
  it), set to Main._downed: a blessed body (a player marked "draugr", a
  companion with it in her marks) whose player's count has uses left,
  beaten to 0 HP, is not killed but laid downed (World.lay_downed): 1 HP,
  downed_until the field rules' window on, lying (down_until, 343's pose)
  and stunned as long, so no moves, attacks or words (chat and her voice
  are dropped). No blow lands on the downed (World.damage) and no monster
  picks them (Monster._nearest_visible_target: no finishing blows, the
  coordinator's draft). When the window runs out with nobody bringing
  them back, they die as ever (cause &"bled"): 396's return, or the town
  for the unblessed. The unblessed, and the blessed with no uses left,
  die as ever. A player who leaves while downed has fallen: brought back
  as ever.
- The channel: World.try_channel(by, body, ticks): beside the body (can
  melee), holding still; done unless meanwhile the channeler moves,
  exerts itself, is hit or is downed, or the body gets up or dies
  (World._tend_downed, World.channel_changed started / broken / done).
  Who may is Main._start_channel's: a blessed channeler carrying its
  half bound to its player (the player's barrow_half, a companion's
  return_token), with uses left on that player's count. Done: one use off
  the channeler's player's count, the body up at the field rules' hp of
  its most (World.raise_downed), and "<X> brought <Y> back (<n> uses
  left)." in the party log; companions there hear it and it is a fact of
  theirs. A player begins it by holding E on the downed (the bandage
  command, on a downed body: no new command). Anyone blessed may bring
  back anyone downed.
- Her part, Intent.REVIVE: her own player downed and she able
  (Main._can_revive: blessed, her token on her, uses left), she fights off
  a foe at her, then goes to a cell beside them and channels (Main's
  revive), holding still till it is done or broken, and begins again. Her
  voice is told and asked when they go down. This step she brings back
  only her own player.
- Rules: economy.json "return" "field" {window_s 30, channel_s 4, hp
  0.5, uses {easy 5, normal 10, hard 15}}, Jeff's numbers to move.
- Wire: downed_until, channel_of (the body's name) and channel_until
  replicate on players and companions (SUBCLASS_REPLICATED), and a body
  at 0 HP may now be downed rather than gone: PROTOCOL_REVISION 24. The
  views draw the downed lying (343's down_until); a countdown and the
  channel's ring are the HUD's to come.

Open for Jeff: the word ("barrow-blessed" or "hallowed"; "blessed" is
424's), renewing a spent count (gold, the draugr again, or both), the
blessing for life (drafted yes, only the uses run out), finishing blows
on the downed (drafted no).
companion_test _test_field_return. New class_name: none.

## 548. The draugr (the crypt's monsters, step 3)

Jeff's crypt.md: "give gold to the draugr and he offers a deal: beat him,
and you can be brought back without the offering"; the coordinator's
rulings: a fight by pact at a difficulty that sets the token's uses (5,
10, 15), per challenger, he rises again in time (three game days, a rules
number), and laying him to rest stills the skeletons. A new class_name,
Draugr (sim/draugr.gd, extends Monster), the kind "draugr" (the dead's
side, 545), whose row names its script: a kind's "script" in
levels/monsters.json is what Level._spec_for spawns it from.

- Seated (awake): he fights nobody unless struck (then he fights back and
  yields as ever, but blesses nobody: a fight without the pact winning
  nothing is the draft, Jeff's to decide). He talks first (npc's offer
  contract): Monster.talks, and a player coming within HEARING_TILES in
  his lair is spoken to once a visit (offer_spoken); offers_for gives the
  one deal, {kind "deal", cost the offering (economy.json
  return.offering, 8), most three measures}; accept_offer refuses under
  the offering or past the purse, else takes the gold (World.add_gold, a
  spending, "the draugr's pact") and starts the pact.
- The pact: the gold's measures of the offering (1, 2, 3 or more) set the
  difficulty, easy, normal or hard (Main.bless's names); his hp and blows
  times 1, 1.5 or 2, and 0, 2 or 4 skeletons raised round him in his lair
  (World.spawn_spec), guarding. He fights the challenger and their
  companion while they are in his lair (the anchor round him, keeps_room,
  547). Lost when the challenger falls or leaves the lair: he heals, his
  raised dead go, he keeps the gold. Nothing stands while it is on
  (offer_withdrawn to everyone).
- Beaten: at 1 hp he yields (Draugr._world_damaged sets 1 back, so World
  never kills him) and World.bless (Main.bless, 544) is called with the
  players standing in his lair and the difficulty: their mark, uses,
  halves and companions are 544's. Then he rests RISE_DAYS game days
  (rests_until in World.steps, kept in his props so a restart finds him
  resting), lying (down_until, as the dead lie, 547), and every one of
  the dead in his zone lies still (lay_down), any that stir again
  (respawns) every STILL_EVERY_TICKS. Per challenger: a new pact raises
  him from his rest, which runs on; struck resting, he stays down.
  Rested (the world tick too), he sits up and the dead rise (Monster.rise).
- A pact does not survive a restart or a far world tick (forfeit, the gold
  kept).
- World.bless is the hook (as World.downed, 544), set by Main; unset in a
  test, Draugr.blessed_last says who would have been blessed.
Protocol: PROTOCOL_REVISION 25 (release's; one bump with npc's side of
the talk): a draugr spawns from a script an older client lacks, and the
"offers" message's "standing" may name a monster that talks. No new
replicated property. dungeon's barrow swaps its stand-in for a
monster_draugr marker in its level.json legend. monster_test
(_test_draugr); level_test, protocol_test, builder_test unchanged.


## 546, npc's side: the crypt's people, and a speaker that is not a townsperson

Economy's 546 holds the offering, the alms and the altar's ledger; this is
npc's side of Jeff's crypt (docs/lore/crypt.md), landed in parts as the
pieces it waits on arrive. Part 1 (2026-10-20): a speaker that is a
Resident or a monster that talks. 536's spoken-offer path keyed everything
on a resident's worker id; now a Monster with talks (enemy-ai's 548: the
draugr, Monster.talks) and offers_for(player_id) is a speaker too
(Main._monster_addressed: named in the line within hearing, else nearest
within RESIDENT_EARSHOT, looked at only when no resident takes the line).
Its offers come from its own offers_for in 536's shape; an ask for wares,
work or news speaks the first (asked again, the next) and it stands, keyed
by the entity's path (Main._standing "worker" holds a worker id or a path;
_standing_for reads either); a yes word or an amount said goes to its
accept_offer(player, offer, gold) with the amount (0 for a bare yes: the
monster's own refusal in its words, the offer still standing), after Main's
one check, the purse ("You have but 9 gold."); its reply {ok, say, line} is
spoken and logged, and on ok nothing stands; a no clears. It talks first
through its offer_spoken(player_id, offer) signal (the draugr's, when a
player comes near him in his lair): Main speaks the words and sets them
standing unasked; offer_withdrawn(player_id) clears (the pact begun, the
challenger gone). Hooked as the monster spawns (Main._spawn, once per
instance). The "offers" message for a monster carries its path, its name,
its offers and the standing offer: 548's PROTOCOL_REVISION 25 covers an
offer from a monster, so this lands on it with no bump (release). The
difficulty from the gold (floor(gold / offering), 1x to 3x), the pact, the
mark and the fight are enemy-ai's and companions'. tests/talker_stub.gd (a
talking Monster with the contract and nothing of the draugr's) and
resident_test. Parts to come: Pip's bodiless alms run on the world tick
(economy's take_altar and altar_down), lost only once a player knows
Aldous's secret, the gossip and the lived fact; Aldous's secrets as lore's
entries with knowers; "Take the offering down" (a kept offering births the
"cheated" standing key from Jeff's list) and "Find the runner".

Amended (2026-10-22, lore's old gods, lore-18's find): world_facts reported

## 549. Seeing the player through ground that hides them

525's hills can hide the player: at the foot of the plateau's face on
levels/hills, the camera on the plateau's side, the plateau's edge stands
between them at any pitch the camera has (the ridge lift's 70 degrees did
not show them; the review shot h3-game-under-cliff). Walls fade for this
(188), piece by piece by material; the ground and the cliff faces are one
mesh a chunk, so they cannot. The coordinator's design. Client only.

- Hidden: Client3D.hidden_by_ground walks the camera's line back from the
  player's middle (RIDGE_AIM over the feet) over the drawn ground, RIDGE_REACH
  metres at the camera's pitch (its ridge lift's if higher); never on a
  level with no relief.
- _update_sight eases sight_cut toward 1 while hidden, 0 when not, over
  SIGHT_EASE 0.25 s (a wall's fade feel), and sets three global shader
  uniforms (project.godot's shader_globals): sight_focus (the player's
  middle, w their feet's height), sight_toward (toward the camera), sight_cut.
- sight.gdshaderinc's sight_cut_here: a fragment in front of the player
  toward the camera, within SIGHT_RADIUS 1.3 m of that line and SIGHT_ABOVE
  0.4 m or more over their feet, is dropped by a 4x4 ordered dither, SIGHT_KEEP
  0.3 of it left (a faded wall's 0.3), soft at the edge. Opaque throughout:
  no sorting, no flicker (188's trouble with translucent pieces). The ground
  (ground.gdshader), the scatter (scatter.gdshader) and the cliff faces
  (cliff.gdshader, new: their vertex colours, rough, both sides, as their
  plain material was) take it. Rocks and props on the strip stay drawn.
- Cost: the castle at night, map_bench under the bench lock, 4.64 ms median
  before, 3.76 after (noise); levels/hills at noon 1.49 to 1.92 ms: a
  discard in a shader costs its early depth test whether or not it cuts.

plateau's side and the valley floor not; the cut eases in and out; the
castle never hides). Shots: C:\dev\review\hills2, sight-before/after-under-face.

## 551, maps' side. A guide's routes: a leg's cells, a route round a camp, and the leg walk on slopes

Companions' guide (551: a companion who knows a place leads her player
there on the world's real ways) needs three things of WorldRoutes and
Main; the coordinator routed them to maps, signatures agreed with
companions.

**WorldRoutes.leg_cells(leg, faction := OPEN) -> Array[Vector2i].** The
cells of one leg of route() or route_round(), its "from" to its "to" both
in, each a step can_step allows from the one before, along a shortest
walk: the leg's own "cells" if it carries them, else _walk_cells (down the
distance fields, or a field walked then where they are not in). A leg
from a cell to itself is that cell. She keeps them and steps along them.

**WorldRoutes.route_round(from_area, from_cell, to_area, to_cell, avoid,
faction := OPEN) -> Array[Dictionary].** route()'s legs, each leg in an
area of avoid (area name -> {cell: true}: a camp she knows) walked again
by A* round those cells and the faction's held ground, there and then: no
distance fields made for a one-off. Such a leg carries "cells" (leg_cells
and along() follow them) and its own "steps". The crossings stay route()'s:
it never takes another way to keep clear, which would need fields per
avoided set. A leg's own start and end are never avoided (a portal inside
the camp is passed through). [] if a leg cannot get round, and the guide
falls back to route() (she goes through, or refuses). _steps_between's
A* is now _a_star, which also notes where each cell was reached from.

**Main.travel and a led pair.** travel(peer, ...) already takes a player
and companion together (her tile null: beside him on arrival). Companions
take the crossing in their Guide: standing at the leg's exit or beside it,
her player within 3 cells in her zone, Main calls travel with the way's own
data, deferred as the player's own path is (a link: to and to_spawn; an
edge: {side, cell: exit + the side's step}), and sealed_open is asked for
her player again. She never stands on a link cell, so she never blocks his
step, and he still goes through by the usual path if he steps on it.
Nothing in travel changes; maps' OK.

**A fix to the existing route walk (206's layers, the leg walk).** _step_down
matched a step down a distance field by a flat 1 or 1.5, but _flood pays a
climb (Relief.pace, decision 525) and a ford (505) into its steps, so on a
slope, a stair or a ford no neighbour matched and the walk stopped there:
_walk_cells (held ground's cut, 206) ended a leg early, and along() left a
group standing at the foot of the first climb until its leg was done
(TradeRoutes' wagons, 504; raid groups). Now every walk pays one cost,
_step_halves (climb added, the whole FORD_COST times into a ford: _relax's
rule; _steps_between had paid the ford on the flat part only), and
_step_down matches the step the field was walked by, from the next cell to
this one. Wagons and raiders now move along a leg over hills and stairs
instead of waiting at the foot and arriving at its end.

tests/world_map_test: the r_room legs' cells (round the wall, 10.5 steps);
a leg's cells up and down a slope at the leg's steps (the downhill walk
stopped at its first cell before the fix); route_round round a camp
(longer, no camp cell, along follows it), [] against a wall edge to edge,
unchanged by a camp in another area.

companions-ba). `threatens(entity) -> bool` answers for now, without
distance or sight: those stay the asker's (her Senses, her range).

- Never while the monster is gone, dead or lying in its grave, nor for a
  body gone, dead, downed (544) or in its spawn grace.
- A monster: a player or a kept companion (not one it has given up on a
  while); a resident when its side fights the town (545) or it is a raider
  made real in a zone (World.townsfolk, as its targeting has it); a monster
  of a faction it fights on sight. A room keeper only one in its room; a
  skeleton walking home counts (547: it fights who is in its way, and a
  guide leading through its path is there).
- Animal: prey never; a boar the one it charges; a predator its diet, and a
  player or kept companion while bold or just hurt (as its targeting).
- Draugr: in his lair, one that struck him or his pact's party; resting,
  nobody; seated and unprovoked, nobody.

A waiting companion with no keeper is never threatened (monsters do not go
for one). Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name. monster_test
_test_threatens.

## 336 amended. The words said, and one clause of how

Jeff, from his play on v0.1.160 (2026-10-20): "town npc verbalize their
thoughts." On the box (grepped mind.log lines) nothing a resident says
is unprompted: the voice asks fire only on a player's line (336), the
bard's song in earshot (490) and an offer when asked (536). What he saw
is the shape of the answers: the model wraps the resident's words in
stage direction and inner state, second person, and the whole of it went
to the bubble, the transcript, the party log and the gossip of those in
earshot. Aldous: "You nod, your voice steady despite the rain. \"Jeff,
I've been meaning to thank you for the food you brought last time.\"";
Snagfin: "You look up from your workbench, your voice low and careful.
\"I owe the town 29 gold.\"". Worse, the two-sentence cut then kept the
narration as sentence one and cut the words themselves. The prompt already
forbade it ("never describe what you do"); the model ignores it. Then
Jeff, on the fix: "might be interesting if there's some sort of narration
quality, such as 'Jeff, I've been meaning...' his voice steady despite the
rain." So the narration is turned, not dropped.

The rule, by code, on the one path Main holds every answer to
(Resident.spoken, new; two_sentences keeps its contract over it):
asterisked and bracketed actions come out of the line; when the answer
holds quoted speech, the quoted words are the speech and the rest
narration; else each sentence of second-person narration is (one
beginning "You" and a gesture verb: nod, shrug, sigh, smile, glance,
lean, pause, turn, look up / down / over / around / away, set down...; or
naming your voice, eyes, hands, face, gaze, brow, jaw, shoulders). The
speech is cut to two sentences as before (Resident.sentences keeps an
unfinished tail); an answer left empty is "not said". The narration
becomes one clause of how it was said (Resident.aside_of): third person
in the resident's pronoun ("your" to his / her / their, the name's
possessive to the pronoun's, a clause still naming the speaker dropped:
ui's row heads with the name), lowercase, no end mark; a clause naming
the voice is preferred ("his voice steady despite the rain"); else a
gesture turned to its participle ("looking up from his workbench",
"nodding", a tail after "and" cut); a gesture with something after its
verb joins the voice clause's words when the two stay within eight words
("looking up from his workbench, low and careful"), a bare gesture gives
way to the voice, and over eight the voice alone ("his voice low"). A
clause of walking, giving, taking, sitting, standing, or of thought, plan
or wish (NOT_DONE) is never an aside: the sim did not do it. "You look
tired" and "You've got a better trade than me" are speech and stay.

Where each goes: the bubble carries the speech alone; the "speech"
message gains "aside" (String, "" when none; PROTOCOL_REVISION 27),
which ui's talk log shows after the speech on the same row, after a
spaced dash, dim, in the sans (ui's side, landed beside this); the
transcript keeps both, the aside marked "[aside]"; the server's party log
the aside in brackets; gossip (_heard_near) and a resident's own tale hear
the words alone. The prompt gains one line against narration, asterisks
and quotation marks, so the model has less to turn. The cost: a true line
naming "your voice" becomes an aside; rare. Unprompted greetings or
gossip in earshot stay a design of their own. resident_test _test_aloud:
the two lines from the box and ten shapes round them (the join, the
over-eight fall-back, the name, the movement that is no aside). Server
only beyond the key; the bump rides v0.1.161.
## 525 amended (2). Escarpments: a face on one side, a long slope on the other

Jeff, walking the gentler hills on the box: "slopes slightly perceptible,
big ledge with slope looks quite good though." The cue that reads is a real
drop with a walkable way up beside it (the plateau's face and its spur), so
landforms become escarpments rather than rolling ground alone (coordinator's
approval, after a trial sheet at 2, 3 and 4 m; maps' pick 3 m).

**Relief.lay "escarpments".** Each entry is `{line, face, height (3), back
(24), taper (8), ways, way_width (4)}`. On the side away from `face` (a
side's name or a Vector2i: the way the face looks), the ground rises over
`back` cells to the line, `height` metres over the roll there, eased to
nothing over `taper` cells at the line's ends. On the face side it stays as
laid, so the line is a face about `height` high. The 4-neighbour edges
across the line are kept out of the slope's cap, as a plateau's faces
already are: a face is a cliff by the sim's rule (a step over WALK_RISE),
nothing new to the sim, the routes or the views. The cap still holds:
- within `way_width` / 2 cells of each of its `ways` (fractions along the
  line);
- where the taper brings the face under the walk;
- where, after the cap, the face came out under FACE_LEAST (1 m), the roll
  against it near an end, so no ledge a few centimetres over the walk, or
  one the wrong way round, is left. The ground is capped again without it.
There the cap's raising pass makes ramps that fan out below the face: the
ways up, "the big ledge with slope". A per-cell cap (steep_bands) can't make
a cliff: the raising pass takes the lower cell's cap and the lowering pass
the higher's, so the neighbours smooth it away. Hence edges, kept out by
the faces' set _limit already had.

**lay() returns "faces"**: the edge keys it kept out of the cap (plateaus'
and escarpments'). A later _limit over the same ground (make_hills' ford)
passes them, or the faces come back as slopes. Terrain draws cliffs from
the relief itself, as before; the set is for the level tools.

**levels/hills, laid again.**
- The west ridge and the knoll across the stream become two escarpments:
  - the west one from (30, 4) to (32, 66), a 3 m face east over the valley,
    a back slope of 22 cells, a way at 55%;
  - the south-east one from (50, 57) to (87, 65), 2.5 m, facing north to
    the plateau's foot, a back of 20 cells, a way at 30%.
- The valley is 4.5 m deep (was 3.5) and the roll is kept.
- The ford's banks are walked to over 4 rows either side (FORD_FREE, was
  2): with the deeper valley the stream's fixed banks two rows off stood
  too high to ramp to.
- make_hills says any cliff on neither the plateau nor an escarpment
  (none).
- Measured: 61 face edges besides the plateau's 40, the west face's median
  3.06 m. Every floor cell is reached from the link. Grass 5839 and dirt
  897, no stone; the stream is 85 cells.
- Terrain shoots it in game at 09:00, noon and 16:00 from the valley floor,
  the way and the crest; Jeff vetoes from those or on foot.

way and its end, its back rising, no other cliff, every cell reached, its

## 551: a companion guides her player where she has been with them

Jeff's companion_rewards.md (2026-10-20): "a companion who has been to a
place can guide you there: you follow her on autopilot", and next time she
could refuse a road that is not safe. The coordinator approved the design
in three phases. Its rulings, flagged to Jeff as the coordinator's: real
time at the player's own pace with no time-skip (the world is shared and
moves on, so autopilot means the player stops steering); talking her round
waits (it needs a judgement the mind cannot act on); only her own player is
led, and the rest of the party walks. This is phase 1: what she knows, the
walk, and the stops. Phase 2 is refusal by the weight of the dangers on the
route against her boldness and bond, with the world clearing them. Phase 3
is her birthplace, once lore gives birthplaces world places.

- What she knows is her record's "roads": {areas, places, dangers}.
  - areas: each area she has stood in while out with her player.
  - places: each place she came within 7 cells of, on the same beat as her
    player's own fog (Main._tell_world, now _observe_roads too).
  - dangers: what she lived through in an area, each with a weight:
    downed 3, carried off 3, her player falling near her 3, a blow leaving
    her or her player under hurt_mark (25%) of their hp 2. One entry a day
    for each area and kind. Nothing reads them yet; phase 2 weighs them.
  - It starts empty: an old record cannot say where she went.
  - PlayerRecord.from_dict keeps it.
  - Her player's map is told it as the "world" message's "guide" key,
    {companion, places, areas}, sent by Main whole when it changes and kept
    through a full message (WorldNews.merge).
  - Her voice gets one sentence naming the nearest few places she knows the
    way to (places_told).
- Asking:
  - A spoken line to her that asks to be led somewhere (Guide.ASK: "take me
    to ...", "show us the way to ...") and names a place or area she knows
    (Guide.named_in, the longest name) sets her off. The sim decides, before
    her voice answers, and her voice is told once (Companion.guide_note)
    that she agreed, that she does not know the way, or that they are there
    already.
  - "lead on" takes a stopped walk up again within keep_minutes.
  - The map's command "guide" {to: a place's Holdings id or an area's
    name} sets her off the same way.
  - A place goes by its cell; an area by its first start.
- The walk: new class_name Guide (sim/guide.gd), one per walk, held by Main
  by her player's id (_guides), so it survives the zones it crosses.
  - Her intent is GUIDE (Intent.GUIDE, after a reflex or an errand). She
    walks the route's first leg (WorldRoutes.route from where she is; maps'
    leg_cells once it lands, a walk there until then). She goes round a body
    in her way by a short walk a few cells ahead.
  - Her player's body follows her: their move order is set to her heel's
    cell (Heel.cell, with the roles swapped) whenever they are two or more
    cells off, so they walk at their own pace.
  - She waits whenever they are more than wait (3) cells behind.
  - Before the world's routes are in, a walk in her own area goes straight
    there; one beyond waits.
  - At a way out (the leg's end, with her player near), Main takes them both
    through after the tick: Main.travel for a link (closed, or sealed to her
    player, stops the walk instead), or the edge's crossing. The walk binds
    to the new bodies on the far side and goes on, routing afresh.
- Control comes back, and the walk stops:
  - "moved": the player's own step, move order, strike or swing, or any
    command but talk, the map's guide or facing.
  - "danger": a monster in her sight range she sees that would fight her or
    her player. enemy-ai's Monster.threatens(entity) is used where it
    exists; until it lands, a monster she counts hostile.
  - "struck": either of them loses hp.
  - "hurt": her player under hurt_below (half) of their hp.
  - "downed": either of them downed.
  - "lost": her player gone from her zone.
  - "no_way": no route, or a way out that cannot be taken.
  - "arrived": within arrive (3) cells of the place, with them near; the
    party log says she has brought them there.
  - Each stop but moved and lost is in the party log and asks her voice.
- Wire: Player.led_by, replicated, is her name while she leads them ("" when
  not). It is for ui's HUD line ("Following Wren to the Barrow - move to take
  the lead"). Their body is walked by the server's own move orders, which a
  client already draws as it draws any server move (Prediction keeps no
  target for them). PROTOCOL_REVISION 28 (npc's 336 amended took 27).
- Numbers in levels/companion_traits.json "guide".

tests/companion_test _test_guide covers:
- what she comes to know;
- the ask, and a place she does not know;
- the walk, with their body at her heel;
- each stop: their step, a command, danger, a blow;
- lead on;
- arriving;
- a danger kept, and roads kept through a save;
- the map's message, and the map's command;
- across test_room's link to sample, and the same walk going on there.

## 551 phase 2, npc's side. What she knows of the roads

Jeff's companion_rewards.md: "next time she could refuse: it isn't safe,
there are bandits on that road." The coordinator split phase 2 with
companions (2026-10-21): npc owns what a companion knows of a road and how
fresh it is; companions owns the refusal (temper and bond tipping it),
her words, who hears the news and the stop.

- RoadKnowledge (sim/road_knowledge.gd, static, a new class_name) reads,
  fades and prunes the roads.dangers on her card (Guide's 551 shape);
  Guide.note_danger still writes the lived ones. It never names Guide,
  so the Guide -> WorldNews -> PlayerRecord -> Companion chain stays
  open: the guide rules come in as an argument (Guide.rules()).
- heard(card, news, holdings, rules): the road's news of 551 npc's side.
  "raided" adds one heard danger in the camp's own area {area, camp,
  faction (its display word at the time, "" for nobody), goods, why
  "raided", from "heard", day, weight: heard_weights.raided 2}; the same
  camp on one day is one entry. "lost" adds nothing (no camp, so no
  guessed area) and "arrived" adds nothing (a wagon that got through was
  lucky: time and the world clear roads, not luck; companions dropped
  "wagon_arrived lowers" from their design for this).
- weigh(card, areas, day, holdings, rules) -> {weight, worst}: the sum
  over the dangers on the route's areas, each whole for fresh_days of its
  kind (heard 4, lived 8: lived outlasts hearsay), then straight down to
  nothing at twice that. worst is the heaviest standing entry with its
  "standing", so companions can name the road even when the camp is gone.
- The world's three answers: prune (weigh's first step) drops a danger
  faded to nothing and a heard one whose camp nobody holds any more
  (Holdings.holder NOBODY) or that is no place; the days fade them;
  passed(card, area, day), Guide's to call when she leads through an area
  to its far side without a stop, halves that area's dangers once a day
  (roads.passed {area: day}), rounded down so a restart's whole numbers
  (PlayerRecord._numbers) keep it; at nothing the entry is pruned next.
- reason(worst, day, world_map) -> a fact clause for her voice's
  guide_note and the stop words, not a line: heard "there are bandits on
  the road through the Wilds: the Blood Rot struck a wagon carrying 3
  wool there four days back" (the area's display name, else its id's last
  word); lived, first person, "I was carried off there, six days back";
  day words today / yesterday / N days back.
- Rules in companion_traits.json "guide": heard_weights {raided: 2},
  fresh_days {heard: 4, lived: 8}; companions' refusal numbers go beside
  them in their commit. Companions' half: the refusal at the ask and at
  each new leg's area as she crosses, the same goal refused again the
  rest of that day ("talking her round waits"), who hears (her player in
  news.told or her resting in that town), PlayerRecord.from_dict keeping
  roads.passed.
- road_knowledge_test: the news heard (one a camp a day; home again,
  lost and an unknown camp add nothing), the fading by day and the
  pruning, lived outlasting heard, the cleared camp, the passage halving
  once a day, the words, the rules. Server only, no protocol change.

## 551 phase 2, companions' side. She refuses a road that is not safe

Jeff (companion_rewards.md): "next time she could refuse: it isn't safe,
there are bandits on that road". The coordinator approved the split with
npc (2026-10-21): npc's RoadKnowledge keeps what she knows of a road and
how fresh it is; this side decides when she refuses, what she says, who
hears the road's news, and when a walk stops for it.

- Her nerve (Guide.nerve): boldness by her temperament (companion_traits
  "guide" boldness: fearless 5, cheerful or restless 4, steady, warm or
  quiet 3, quick and wary or careful 2; boldness_default 3 for one not
  listed), plus her bond with her player (Standing's COMPANION word: wary
  -1, fond 0, close 1, devoted 2), plus company (1) for each other player
  within hearing of hers. Drafts for Jeff.
- The road (Guide.road_of): the areas WorldRoutes.route crosses from where
  she stands, in order, each with the cell it is left by; before the
  routes are in, here and the goal's area.
- The refusal (Guide.refusal): RoadKnowledge.weigh over the road's areas;
  refused when the weight is above nothing and reaches her nerve. Her
  reason is RoadKnowledge.reason's clause (the worst danger). Her offer:
  the last area before the dangers so far reach her nerve, and the place
  she knows there nearest its way on; none when the danger is where she
  stands, the goal itself, or where she already is.
- Asked (spoken, the map's "guide" command, or "lead on"), Main weighs
  the road before the walk starts. Refused, no walk: her voice is told
  "you will not go: it isn't safe: <reason>", with her offer, the party
  log "<she> won't lead the way to <there>: it isn't safe". The same goal
  is refused again the rest of that day, whatever changes (talking her
  round waits, 551's ruling): Main._guide_refused, by player id and goal,
  for the session only. "lead on" the same day takes her offer.
- On the way: come into a new area (the walk bound afresh after a way
  out), or road news heard while walking, the road on is weighed again;
  refused, the walk stops ("unsafe"), her voice told why.
- A clean passage: a walk that came into an area by a way and leaves it by
  a way with no stop (Guide.clean, set at bind after a crossing, cleared
  by any stop) calls RoadKnowledge.passed for the area, halving its
  dangers once a day.
- Who hears the news (Main.road_heard = _road_heard): a companion out
  with her player in the town's zone (news "told" holds her player's id),
  or resting in that town (resident.place is the town).
  RoadKnowledge.heard decides what she keeps.
- PlayerRecord.from_dict keeps roads.passed {area: day}.
- companion_test _test_guide_refuses: the nerve, the road, the refusal and
  its reason, the fearless going, the faded going, no offer for a danger
  underfoot, refused at the ask and again that day, stopped on the way,
  "lead on" for the offer, a clean passage, the news heard by her player's
  companion only, passed kept. Server only, no protocol change, no new
  class_name.

section could rebind every key but the four a player presses most. Now the

## 554. Residents speak unprompted: the hail

Jeff's talk notes (2026-10-19): "town npc verbalize their thoughts", and
his liking for the narration that followed (336 amended). The coordinator
held the design back until the aside landed, and approved it 2026-10-21.
This narrows 336, "residents speak when spoken to", which also turned
down idle chatter: a resident now says one line unprompted, once, when
they have something real to say; the rest of 336 stands.

- When: every HAIL_CHECK_TICKS (a second), Main._hails_tick: a resident
  out and about (spawned; not strayed, escorting, hiding, in bed, or a
  companion resting in town) sees a player within TALK_REACH it has not
  hailed today. Silent to a player who is led (_guides), gave or took a
  blow within hail.quiet_seconds (GridEntity.hurt_tick; a blow given is
  remembered by _hail_struck on World.entity_damaged), was answered by a
  resident within the minute (a talk), or heard a hail within
  hail.minute_seconds, so a street is not a chorus. One hail a tick.
- Lowest of all asks (the coordinator): none while any resident ask waits
  or is out, or the mind's last answer took longer than hail.slow_ticks
  (_mind_last_ticks), so a greeting never delays a plea or a commission
  on the box's Ollama; a skipped hail is not counted as one.
- What (Resident.hail_cue, pure, from the card, the news and the memory
  only; nothing invented), the first that applies: their own plea
  (Offers' plea: kin sick, a loan, a grudge, the panel's own words); what
  the town noted today (TownMemory's newest entry first said today: the
  road's news among it, "I heard today that ..."); a memory the lawspeaker ruled today (the
  ruling's step, with his "because"); the sky (DayNight.describe's
  sentence) when it has changed since they last spoke of it; a greeting
  by Standing.words (stranger, known, trusted, wronged). A cue text said
  before is skipped (the card's hails.said, the newest hail.said_kept);
  nothing applies, nothing is said, and that pair is not looked at again
  for a world tick (_hail_tried).
- How: Resident.hail_ask, voice_ask's shape (system_for, now shared)
  with the cue as the user turn ("<name> comes within speaking distance
  of you. One thing is on your mind: <cue> Say one line to them about
  it, unprompted, as yourself and in your own words, not the words
  above. Say only what the thought holds: add no place, cause, name or
  detail it does not give, for nothing else is true."), trigger "hail:
  <kind>", queued in _resident_asks like
  any ask (the mind's timeouts drop a slow one) and answered through
  _resident_answered unchanged: Resident.spoken's words and aside, the
  mind log, the transcript, the party log, the "speech" message. Never a
  panel; the player answers in chat as ever.
- Remembered: the card's hails {to: {player id: day}, said: [...], sky}
  (Resident.hail_done), written with the card.
- Rules: townsfolk.json "hail" {on, quiet_seconds 10, minute_seconds 60,
  slow_ticks 50, said_kept 8}. No new class_name, nothing on the wire
  ("speech" carries the aside since 336 amended), server only, no new
  content in levels.
- resident_test _test_hails: the cue order and the skip of a said text;
  Main's hail to a stranger within reach, once a day, the card's memory,
  none out of reach, led, after a blow given or taken, in a talk, within
  the minute, while an ask waits or the mind is slow. The transcript
  check (the box's qwen3:14b through the tunnel with the game's own
  prompt from the test's mind log, two lines a cue kind, 2026-10-21):
  the news, the ruling and the plea come back as her own first-person
  echo of the cue, the sky and the greeting paraphrased from the card's
  facts (the town's wants, the mill); the cues are written in her own
  voice for that reason, since a bare fact in the third person was
  echoed as narration and a loose turn invented a stag and a barrel of
  salt.

Amended (2026-10-21, after the coordinator's soak): a day's hails against
the box's qwen3:14b with the game's own prompt (tools/town_soak.gd
--hail-day) showed four things, fixed here. (1) The news cue took the
newest memory noted today whatever its source, and a resident's hail,
heard by the residents beside it, became a belief, which became the
next hail: "I heard today that goblins did it." Now Townsfolk._remember
marks the town's own event lines "event": true (a wagon struck, home or
lost, the runner, the town's notes), and the news cue takes only those,
never one the resident said themselves nor one the lawspeaker ruled
(that is the ruling cue). (2) Twelve residents told one player the same
news in a round: Main._hail_heard keeps, by player and day, every cue
text they heard from anyone, and hail_cue skips it (its heard argument),
so a thing is said to a player once a day by the whole town. (3) A name
at the head of a line lost its capital through Hearsay._lower_first
("hew says she saw Nix"): Resident._lead lowers the first letter only
after an article or pronoun (LEAD_WORDS). (4) The ruling cue in the
third person drew three inventions in seven (an opinion, wet boots, a
wrong teller); it is in her own first person now, like the news: "I
heard the lawspeaker rule today that ..., because ...". Two more from
the next day's run: the heard filter applies to the shared cues only
(SHARED_CUES: news, ruling, sky), since a greeting's text is the same
from every neighbour and one greeting a day had silenced the rest; and
the sky is a cue only with weather in it or snow on the ground
(DayNight.describe's weather and ground, and never Weather.at's
"clear" kind, whose words are "the sky is clear"), a clear sky being
the cue that drew the narrating lines ("your bones remember"). And from
the day after: a hail the mind did not answer (timed out, "not said")
gives its marks back (Resident.hail_undone and Main._hail_heard), so the
town's one news line of a day is not lost to one slow answer. And the
coordinator's ruling on the soak's page (Jeff's to move): twelve
greetings on a first day is a chorus, so greetings by standing are
capped at hail.greetings_a_day (3) a player a day from the whole town,
the first three residents met (Main._hail_greetings; hail_cue's
greeting_ok), the other cues under their own limits as before: a
newcomer is greeted, not mobbed. Jeff accepted the cap as built (2026-10-22, his draft
deleted): three a player a day from the whole town is his ruling now. What the day
also showed, left as it is and told to the coordinator: the news, the
ruling and the plea come back as her own echo of the cue, flat but true;
the greeting and the sky are paraphrased, and the sky's lines are the
liveliest and the ones that invent (a bell, blood from the mine, the
hunters lost in fog); no line carried narration (no aside at all); two
of nine timed out at the voice's five seconds over the tunnel, which the
box's own Ollama does not pay. The soak tool counts hails a day by
resident and player, repeats, hails with another ask out, the mood's
gossip a day and the road's news through RoadKnowledge (--days=30), and
--hail-day writes the day's lines to C:\dev\review\npc\hails.md for
Jeff.

Amended (2026-10-22, the lively trial; Jeff: "trial with livelier"): the
hail's one strict sentence ("add no place, cause, name or detail it does
not give") is loosened as a trial on Jeff's word, behind townsfolk.json
hail.lively (true for the trial; false is the strict sentence back for
every cue, one edit). The trial's sentence (Resident.HAIL_USER_LIVELY)
allows one small everyday detail of the speaker's own things and names the
bound: no person, place, building, name, price, weather or cause invented,
no doubt cast on the thought, nobody named it does not. It applies to the
news, the ruling and the sky cues (SHARED_CUES) only: a plea is an ask with
a number in it and a greeting a table word, and both keep the strict turn.
Measured first by the tunnel method on the five hail days' real prompts,
strict beside lively for the same twenty cues (C:/dev/review/npc/
hails_lively.md): the first sentence let 3 of 20 past the bound (a ridge, a
mill, a fog), 2 undercut a ruling and 5 pleas took on weather; the sentence
that ships, on the fourteen news, ruling and sky cues, 11 clean, 1 past
the bound, 1 undercutting, 1 with old rain; the pleas lost their sum twice
under either, hence the kinds gate. Jeff judges it in play; the
nothing-invented rule stands for everything but this colour.

## 555: a companion's loyalty shown in what she does, and the warning signs before leaving

Jeff's companion_rewards.md (Loyalty, Leaving; his students: "a companion
should change her behaviour based on what you do"). The coordinator
approved the design (2026-10-21) with one change: sullen, she still takes a
gift and food, since those are the amends path. Steps and numbers are
drafts for Jeff. Nothing random: her bond moves only by Standing.bump
naming what her player did (444), and fades toward nothing only while she
is apart (Standing.decay), which is the way back. Leaving itself waits on
Jeff's answers (does she take what she earned; how far it goes). This is
part 1, what each step changes. Part 2 (555 amended) adds the new events.

- Her step (Main.bond_step_of): from her Standing score with her player,
  devoted at Standing's top (6), close at its trusted (3), wary at its
  wronged (-3), cooling at -1, sullen at -5 and apart at -7
  (companion_traits "loyalty" steps); else fond. Main._set_mood writes it:
  - on her record as "mood";
  - on her body as Companion.bond_step;
  - while she rests, on her worker record ("companion:<her name>", via
    Production.set_mood) as mood and mood_why, the newest reason
    ready-made in the third person ("they struck her"), for npc's resting
    body and the town's gossip (555, npc's side).
  It runs at her join, at every bond move, and when a fading moves her
  while apart.
- The wire: Companion.bond_step and bond_why are replicated. bond_why is the
  newest reason as her player reads it ("you struck her"), for ui's mood
  read. SUBCLASS_REPLICATED gains both; PROTOCOL_REVISION stays 28
  (unshipped; release).
- What each step changes, on Companion:
  - Heel: how far her player gets before she sets off (Heel.start, now
    per follower, START by default): devoted 2, wary and colder 5.
  - Fighting: wary and colder, guarding or pressing, she fights only what
    is at her or going for her or her player (_after_us). She holds no door
    of her own choice, and pulls back under retreat_below (0.5) of her hp,
    not REFLEX_BELOW. Devoted, she stands over her downed player within 2
    cells (HOLD), low or not.
  - What she takes (Companion.turns_down, asked by World.try_transfer):
    food always. Grave goods (items' World.items.is_grave, "555, items'
    side") she won't touch below close when her superstition (442) is
    grave_superstition (6) or more. Sullen and colder, she takes only food
    and a gift (gear into a free slot, nothing back): no loads, no swaps.
    She says why in the party log.
  - Guiding (551): sullen and colder, she leads nowhere. Her voice is told
    by step whether she offers to lead (close and devoted), waits to be
    asked (cooling, wary), or won't (loyalty guide_words).
  - Voice: Standing's fact, plus one sentence for the step (loyalty
    words: cooling "unhappy with them, and may say so", wary "keep your
    distance", sullen "do as little as you can", apart "thinking of
    leaving"). Every drop is told her voice once, as it happens ("Jeff just
    struck you."), so she says so.
- companion_test _test_loyalty: the steps by score, the reasons both ways,
  sullen on the record, the body and the wire, hanging back, the voice,
  leading nowhere, a monster not after them left be, a load refused, food
  and a gift taken, fond as before, devoted closer. Server and wire, no new
  class_name.

## 555 amended: what her player does moves her bond

Part 2 of 555: the new deeds beside 444's (rescued +4, gift +1, fed +1,
bandaged +1, day +1 up to close, stood_by +1, kept_from -1, struck -1).
Each is a Standing.bump naming what her player did, in companion_traits
"bond" (drafts for Jeff):
- blessed +2: the draugr laid to rest together (Main.bless, her blessed
  beside her player): "laid the draugr to rest with you".
- cleared +1: a place taken from a side hostile to the town by one that is
  not (Holdings.place_taken), with her and her player in its area: "cleared
  <the place> with you". Jeff: "areas affect loyalty".
- left_alone -1: she goes down (World.entity_downed) or dies with her
  player out of her hearing, or gone: "left you to fall alone". Downed
  and then bled out with them still away counts once.
- let_bleed -2: downed, she bleeds out (cause &"bled") with her player
  within hearing, blessed with uses left: "let you bleed out".
- grave -1: grave goods put on her by her player (World.item_given) while
  her superstition is grave_superstition or more and she is short of
  devoted: "made you carry grave goods". Below close she refuses them
  (555's turns_down), so this is the close companion's cost. It is no gift.
- warned -1: her player takes her into the area she refused that day as
  unsafe (551 phase 2's refusal keeps the worst danger's area), once a
  refusal: "ignored your warning and took you there".
- Unpaid days wait: the game has no companion pay (economy and Jeff).
- companion_test _test_loyalty: left alone, let bleed, warned once and
  wary after it; cleared, and not by the Blood Rot (where the test room has
  a place). Server only, no protocol change beyond 555's, no new class_name.

## 553. The water's edge unsquared

Jeff: the world reads as squares. The coordinator approved terrain's
unsquaring design (2026-10-21), the water's edge first: start at 0.35 of a
cell and show it; the well's water stays its own art.

**The shore field** (Client3D.shore_image): an L8 image over the ground's
mask, SHORE_RES 4 texels a cell, 1 in the water, 0 on land, the water's
edge where it is a half.
- The wet cells (water, fords, a bridge's bed) at a texel a cell are
  scaled up bilinearly, a box a cell wide over them. A straight run of
  cells keeps its edge, a corner rounds, and a lone cell is near a disc.
- A stream's one-wide cells (both sides dry) are left out of that and drawn
  along its path instead: a Catmull-Rom through their middles, wandering
  STREAM_WIND 0.2 either side by a noise along it, STREAM_HALF 0.42 wide
  each side. It winds within them.
- The bound: a texel further than SHORE_BOUND 0.35 (box distance) from a
  cell of the other kind is its own cell's, water (at least 0.55) or land
  (at most 0.45). The edge never strays further from its cells', so what
  the sim calls water or land is what is drawn there, give or take a third
  of a cell.
- Client3D.shore_at reads it on the CPU (bilinear).

**The shaders read it.**
- water.gdshader: the shore line, foam and the water's inside come from
  the field, warped SHORE_WARP 0.1 of a cell by its noise (SHORE_WANDER
  dropped). The depth toward the middle is still the box distance from the
  land.
- ground.gdshaderinc: the wet bank is a smoothstep of the field (0.3 to
  0.55) instead of the mask's water byte.

**The bank drawn finer, on relief only.** On a level that gives its relief,
a shore cell is drawn as SHORE_RES x SHORE_RES quads (Client3D._shore_band,
_shore_cell). A shore cell is ground or water, not a building's floor, a
rock's or a ramp's, with water and land in the 3 x 3 round it and no cliff
on its sides. A point's height eases from the ground as the cells draw it
to the bed (under the water's mean, _water_corner, by SHORE_SINK). It
follows smoothstep(0.3, 0.5) of the field, so the bank is under the water by
the field's edge (its half, not the cell's), where the foam is drawn. The dry side is the drawn ground, not
the land's own height: 525 already brings a bank down to the water across
its cell, and lifting it back to the land's height made a dark wall along
the hills' stream in the first A/B. A corner touching a
cell drawn whole keeps that cell's height (only the shore cells' own, as a
cell across the corner may stand a cliff over them), so there is no gap.
Vertex keys are in SHORE_RES units for every cell; _height_in reads a shore
cell's finer triangles. A level without relief keeps its ground mesh: its
water lies over the ground, and the shader alone draws the curve.

**The water over the bank, on relief.** _build_water's surface covered a
body's cells and the land beside them at its level. On a relief the bank
stands higher than the stream, so the surface stopped at the cells' edge,
and the field's edge and foam on the land side went undrawn: the first A/B
of the hills lost their foam line. On a relief the surface now covers the
unwalled land beside a body at any height, at the water's height there (a
bank's corner with no water round it takes the mean of its cell's that
have). Where the bank stands over the water it hides it; where the finer
bank dips under the field's edge, the water shows.

**Normals across the band.** The ground's normals are the sum of the faces
round each corner, weighted by area. A shore cell's finer triangle counts
SHORE_RES squared times its area, as the whole cell's would. Otherwise a
corner shared with a cell drawn whole took its slope from the big triangles
alone, and the bank's lean stopped at the band, leaving a light seam with a
straight edge in the second A/B.

What stays square: the cells the sim walks, builds and floods by; a
building's floor; the well's water (its own art); the forest's ring.

tests/view_test _test_shore: a lone cell wet in its middle and dry at its
corners; a pond's side keeps its edge, its corner rounded; on the wilds
and the hills every texel past SHORE_BOUND from the other kind is its

## 556. Ledges along a curve

Step 3 of terrain's unsquaring design, after 553's water's edge (Jeff:
"square rivers, square ledges"). The coordinator approved it, with the
escarpment hills and the sample's ledge by its stairs as the checks and
the castle as the level without relief.

**The rim.** A ledge's rim ran along the cells' edges, in straight runs
and right angles. Now each land cell under a cliff gets a cap: the higher
ground carried out over it to a curve, with a face down from that curve.
- A cell is under a cliff when a neighbour, side or corner, stands over
  it: the neighbour's drawn corners are over this cell's where they meet,
  and none is under.
- The cap is where the distance to those higher cells is under the rim's
  reach. The reach runs RIM_LEAST 0.12 to RIM_MOST 0.32 of a cell by a
  noise (seed 556), so it never passes SHORE_BOUND 0.35. It eases to
  nothing within RIM_TAPER 0.6 of a pinned corner: one where a cell round
  it is not rim ground (a ramp, water, a building's floor, a rock, the
  shore's finer cells, the map's edge), or where three heights meet.
- Client3D._rim_band finds the caps; _rim_cap traces each with marching
  squares on RIM_RES 8 samples a side.
- A cell's middle is half a cell from its edges, so it is never under a
  cap: puppets at the foot of a face stand clear of it. A ramp's sides
  stay on the cells' edges.
- The rim only stands out from the higher cells, never cuts into them, so
  the ground's mesh is not cut. The cap's triangles are added to the
  ground chunk at the higher cell's heights, lit by that cell
  (_vertex_cells), so night and torches light them as the ground beside.
- _add_cliffs lays the faces down the curve (_cliff_strip, one column a
  segment) with cliff.gdshader, so 513 amended's night darkening and
  549's cut-out apply as before. A cell edge whose cap covers it whole
  (its first samples in all on the cap, past CLIFF_JITTER) no longer
  draws its straight face. _cliff_edges still lists every cliff edge.
- Where a puppet stands is still the cell's ground (_ground_height).
  Client3D._drawn_height takes the caps in (_rim_top), and
  hidden_by_ground (549) reads it, so a player at a curved face's foot is
  hidden as at a straight one.
- Scatter skips a point under a cap.
- A level without relief (the castle) keeps its straight faces.

**Cost**, map_bench A/B, 10 s at noon, alternated, two passes each:
- frame time unchanged: hills 1.20 ms, the sample 1.57, the castle 3.07;
- rebuild: the hills about 810 ms to about 960 (824 and 797 before, 971
  and 944 after), the sample 31 to 54, the castle unchanged.
- _add_cliffs takes about 400 ms of the hills' rebuild apart from 556,
  worth a look of its own.

tests/view_test _test_ledges: on the hills and the sample, caps found; no
cap over a cell's middle; every cap sample within SHORE_BOUND of a cell
over it; faces within their cells; capped cells side by side meet on
their edge; the drawn height takes a cap in and a puppet's doesn't; the
castle and the wilds without caps. Shots and A/B in C:\dev\review\ledges

## 557. Streams as ribbons

Step 2 of terrain's unsquaring design, on 553's spline (Jeff: "square
rivers"). The coordinator approved it with two cares: a ford still reads
as a crossing (shallow, the stones showing), and sound hears where the
falls are. The hills' stream and the sample's are the checks.

**The ribbon.** A stream's water was the body's cell quads, its flow a
texel a cell (flow_mask), turning at cell edges. Now each stream is a
ribbon (Client3D._build_ribbons):
- It runs along the Catmull-Rom through its path cells' middles, the line
  553's shore field draws a narrow stream along, at RIBBON_STEPS 8 points
  a cell and 3 across. It goes half a cell on past each end.
- Its width comes from the stream's own cells: at each path cell, the
  stream's cells across the flow each side, out half a cell past the last
  one and RIBBON_UNDER 0.3 more under the banks. It eases between path
  cells. The shore field (553) still draws the visible edge and its foam,
  within SHORE_BOUND.
- Its surface is the water's surface along it (_water_surface: over the
  cell it is in, the bilinear of _water_corner, as the bed's _shore_bed
  is), so the bed stays SHORE_SINK under it and a stream slopes down its
  valley as before.
- Each point's colour carries the way it runs (r, g), how fast (b: faster
  where the ground drops more down the path) and a fall's foam (a).
  water.gdshader drifts the ripples that way in two cross-faded phases,
  as it did by flow_mask, which is gone.
- A fall is a step down the path of more than FALL_LEAST 0.25 m of
  ground (relief). It foams white over its step. Client3D.stream_falls
  lists the falls as {cell, drop}, a new array each build, for sound's
  ambience (sound-33's ask: a splash at each fall, later, its own design).
  The hills have one, at (46, 79), 0.46 m.

**Ponds, fords and bridges.**
- A stream's own cells (_streams_cells) are its path's and the water
  beside them that is not a pond's inside (water all round). They are
  marked in the water mask's a.
- The bodies (_build_water) leave them out, and a ribbon leaves a pond's
  water (the mask's r without a) to the pond's body, so the two meet on a
  cell edge.
- A ford is on its stream's path: the ribbon runs over it, and the shader
  draws it shallow and clear over the stones from the mask's b, as before.
- A bridge's cells are on the path too: the ribbon runs on under the deck
  at the water there. Its width is the bridged cells', so the deck's ends
  stand on the banks past it.

## 558. The ground relaxed

Step 4 of terrain's unsquaring design, after 553, 556 and 557. The
coordinator approved it with one care: the drawing only, and no seam where
relaxed ground meets ground drawn as before.

**Drawing only: the sim's walk and cliff_between are untouched.** They read
the cells' heights as before; nothing here changes a cell's height or which
steps are cliffs. Client only, protocol unchanged.

**Why it was square.** Every cell was two triangles with the same diagonal
(top-right to bottom-left), every vertex on the grid, so the hillshade's
facets lined up in rows and columns on a slope.

**The move.** Client3D._relax, on a level that gives its relief:
- A ground corner is free when the four cells round it are natural ground
  (_relax_ground: the level's floor, not water, a bed, a ford, dry water, a
  ramp, a rock, a building's floor, the shore's finer cells or a ledge's
  cap) and all draw it at one height.
- A corner on an edge two cells draw apart (a face, or a wedge's thin end)
  stays, so the faces still meet the ground.
- A free corner moves up to RELAX_MOST 0.2 of a cell sideways, by a roll of
  where it is (the same every build). Its height is re-read there: the
  bilinear of the corners of the cell it lands in, the relief's surface. The
  shape is kept; only the facets' lines stop running straight.

**The diagonal.** A cell with all four corners free is split along the
diagonal whose middle is nearer the cell's own height (Relief.at): on a
crest or in a trough it runs along it. _relax_flips holds the cells split
the other way.

**What follows it.** _height_in reads the drawn quad (_quad_height): the
cell's own, or a neighbour's where a moved edge put the point past it.
Puppets, scatter, props and 549's sight check all go through it. A cell
with no moved corner and no flip keeps the old path. Normals stay the sum
of the faces round each vertex.

**What stays.** Levels without relief (the castle, the wilds) are drawn as
before: _relax does not run.

**Cost**, map_bench A/B against main, alternated, two passes:
- frame median: the sample 1.60 to 1.68 ms, the hills 1.22 to 1.25;
  _height_in reads each relaxed cell's quad, cached at build
  (_relax_quads), with no allocations. Building the quad per call first
  cost the sample +0.27 ms.
- rebuild: the hills about 826 to 893 ms, the sample 47 to 52.
- In the shots the change is slight. From the game's camera the grass
  texture dominates, and the facet lines show only where the light runs
  along a slope. Jeff may veto it in game.

tests/view_test _test_relax:
- On the hills (6054 corners moved, 1265 cells flipped) and the sample: no
  corner past RELAX_MOST, none on a cliff's edge, each moved corner a vertex
  of the mesh on the ground's surface.
- Every edge between a relaxed cell and a cell beside it drawn from the same
  two points at the same heights along it (no gap, no sliver).
- _height_in the drawn triangle's inside relaxed cells.
- The castle and the wilds unchanged.
_test_relief's slope check reads the drawn corners, and its ridge test sets
the relax aside while it lays a ridge on the corners. Shots and A/B in
C:\dev\review\ground (ab-*.png). No new class_name.

## 560, economy's side: barter at the shop's counter

Jeff's barter rework: clicking "barter" shows the resident's goods beside
the player's pack; a hover says what the resident pays or asks; the player
picks items on either side and sees the running sum. ui leads the design
and lands the window; the coordinator approved it, with these rulings
(Jeff's to move): phase 1 is the town's shop, fronted by its merchant.
Prices are per item with no bundle discount, and grave goods are taken
fenced at half price. Economy lands the wire and the sim:
- Economy.buys(town, ids): id -> {gold, up_to}. gold is offers()' price.
  up_to is how many the town takes before it has enough: a raw good's
  yields under "comfort", or gear's room under its tags' "wants".
- Economy.barter_quote(town, player, gives [{id, fenced}], takes [uids]):
  each priced as its hover showed it, all or nothing. It refuses with the
  town's own reasons, past up_to, when a take is gone or named twice, when
  the treasury can't pay the gives above gold_floor, or when the purse
  plus the gives can't pay the takes. The balance is what the player gets
  less what they pay.
- Economy.fenced(paid): grave goods (ItemBook.is_grave) are paid half, at
  least 1. The other half is never paid, so it stays in the treasury.
  There is no refusal for the mark. Economy.sell(..., is_fenced) applies
  this, so a grave good dropped into the counter (World._sell) is fenced
  too.
- Economy.sell and buy take a quoted price ("at"). A barter settles at the
  prices the player saw, even though each give moves the town's need
  before the next.
- World.try_barter(by, shop, give uids, take uids, balance) finds each give
  in the player's slots by uid, so an item moved before confirming still
  trades. It refuses with "the prices have moved" when the quote's balance
  is not the player's. It checks room for the takes once the gives are
  out, then sells the gives (World._sold, split out of _sell) and puts
  each take in its slot. "" when done, else why nothing moved.
- Main: the "barter" command {shop} opens or refreshes the window; the
  "trade" command {shop, give, take, gold} trades. Both answer with the
  "barter" message {shop, town, gold, goods [{uid, id, price}], buys,
  fenced {uid: gold}, pack [{slot, uid, id}], why}. pack is there because
  the client never learns its own uids (slot_items isn't replicated). The
  player must be within reach of the counter or of a merchant of its town
  (the merchant trade or type), else "too far from the counter".
- The client keeps Main.barter_data and emits barter_told; ui's window
  reads them by name.
"barter" is a new message kind, which changes the protocol by itself;
there is no PROTOCOL_REVISION bump (release). Phase 2, a maker selling
their own make and buying their trade's materials from their own purse,
follows without asking again. economy_test _test_barter and
_test_barter_in_town. No new class_name.

## 560, npc's side. The resident stops and addresses you

Jeff's rework of the resident click (ui leads the design, approved by
the coordinator 2026-10-21; ui's and economy's sides have the same
number): the left button on a townsperson is "interact": they stop, turn
to face the player and address them; clicking their bubble opens the
text bar with talk (536's say line, unchanged) and barter (economy's).
npc's half is what the resident does and says.

- The "greet" command on the request path (World.command(player,
  "greet", {"resident": path}), by name like companions' "guide"; no new
  message kind), handled by Main._greeted. It does not end a companion's
  lead (551): it is talk.
- Two tiers, so a click answers at once and the mind is never spammed.
  The resident stops and faces the player for greet.stop_seconds
  (Resident.address: Resident.addressing, a new replicated String with
  the addressed body's node path, "" when none, read by pc-character's
  look and talking clip; their _sim_tick stands while it lasts and they
  stay within ADDRESS_REACH), and says one word at once from
  townsfolk.json "greet" without the mind (Resident.greet_word: the
  standing's word for one the town knows, wronged, known or trusted;
  else one of the trade's lines, picked by the day), through the spoken
  path with no aside (Main._resident_says: transcript, party log, the
  neighbours' hearing, the "speech" message, the player's offers for
  the bar). Then, if they have something real to say to that player
  today, 554's hail follows at once (Main._hail_now with clicked: the
  cue, the limits, the heard and greeting caps all as 554's; only the
  pause after a pair found nothing is skipped), its trigger "greet:

- Refusals: in bed, hiding, strayed, escorting, a companion resting in
  town, or with an ask of theirs waiting or out to the mind: no stop,
  the greet.refuse word at most ("Not now.").
- One greeting a pair in greet.again_seconds: a click within it turns
  them to the player again and says nothing new.
- Rules: townsfolk.json "greet" {stop_seconds 8, again_seconds 10,
  refuse, standing, trades}. net.gd SUBCLASS_REPLICATED gains
  "addressing": the protocol hash moves, no PROTOCOL_REVISION bump
  (release: a new replicated field keeps old clients out by itself).
  resident_test _test_greet. Server and client in one landing; ui's
  client side (the hint, the bubble's click, the bar) lands by the
  command's name.
