## 559. Water and roads are curves; the cells are rasterised from them

Jeff, on the unsquared Hills in game: "what i'd like to see is a meandering
stream not a straight lines", and then, a design rule from now on:
"somethings just really off with the level generation -- I don't want
isometric minecraft levels. I want Rivers, streams, roads and shorelines are
drawn as smooth curves, then rasterized to cells. Never cell regions with
rounded edges. A river's course meanders with smooth turns and varies in
width; no straight runs or right angles. Nothing inside the water shows the
grid." A stream found by the water's own way down follows the valley's
floor, as straight as the valley, and a ribbon drawn from cells can only
curve as much as the cells do.

**The curve is the level's data.** level.json:
- "waters": [{points: [[x, y, width], ...], closed}], control points in cell
  units; open, a river or stream, source first, a width per point; closed,
  a pond or lake, the curve its shore (width unused);
- "roads": [{points: [[x, y, width], ...], kind: "dirt" | "stone"}].
Curves (sim/curves.gd, new class_name, all static) is the one place a curve
becomes points or cells, so the sim, the tools, the editor and the views
agree to the bit:
- sample(points, widths, closed): a centripetal Catmull-Rom through the
  points (no cusps or loops at uneven spacing; round to the start if
  closed), a point every SPACING (a quarter cell) of its length, the widths
  eased between the points' (a one-dimensional Catmull-Rom kept within the
  two, at least LEAST_WIDTH), each point's tangent; {points, widths,
  tangents, length};
- nearest(curve, at): {distance, along, width, index}; inside(curve, at);
- cells(curve, closed): open, each cell whose middle lies within the width
  / 2 there of the curve, and middle()'s, -> the middle index it was laid
  from (the nearest point of the curve's); closed, each cell whose middle
  lies inside, -> -1;
- laid(curve, closed, ground): cells() on the ground, an open curve's
  only those laid from the longest run of its middle on the ground (its
  "path"), so a river running on under the void lays nothing there;
- middle(curve): the cells the curve runs through, a side step at a time
  (a corner turned through the side cell nearer the curve, so nothing steps
  diagonally between two water cells), a loop that comes back on itself
  cut out;
- parse(config, key, warnings), to_json(points, widths).

**On load** (Level._lay_curves, after the bridges and the solid buildings):
each water's floor cells in Curves.laid (the ground its floor and the
water) become water (a ford's and a
bridge's kept; under the void it runs on unseen); each road's floor cells
not water take its kind. An open water's path (laid's) is a "streams" path after level.json's own, checked by streams_from
as any (no rise), so ambience, the flow mask, the routes and the fords are
unchanged. The layout carries the same cells, written by whatever lays the
curve; a floor cell it has dry under a water, or not of a road's kind, is
made so and said ("water 0's curve covers 3 cells the layout has dry"), so
a curve moved without its cells is seen. terrain "waters" and "roads" carry
the parsed entries with their samples, for the views: terrain draws the
water and the roads from the curves (distance to the curve, inside the
shore), never from the cells.

**Relief.lay "rivers"**: [{line, wavelength (18), amplitude (6), width (2 or
[least, most]), seed}], laid as a curve:
- the course a sine-generated curve (the way it heads swings either side of
  the line's own as a sine of the distance along it: Langbein and
  Leopold's meander, round all through, no straight runs), about a smooth
  curve through the line's points; the swing solved so a loop wavelength
  cells of the line long reaches amplitude either side (over a loop the
  river runs wavelength / J0(swing) and reaches wavelength S(swing) / (4 pi
  J0(swing)), S the integral of sin(swing sin t) over half a turn); the
  loops 0.6 to 1.4 as long and the swing 0.83 to 1.07 of its own by the
  seed; eased in over half a wavelength at either end, a slow pull against
  drift off the line, and run on to the line's end;
- control points every tenth of a wavelength along it, to level.json's two
  places (so the curve laid is the curve loaded), each its width wandering
  between least and most;
- its cells Curves.laid on this ground, each at the surface of the middle
  cell it was laid from (STREAM_DEPTH under the ground there, never over the
  one upstream), its banks raised to SHORE_LIP over it, the ground round
  walked again; its curve in lay's "waters", its middle in "streams".
A level keeps it to a valley's floor (valley_floor at least amplitude +
most) or its banks are cut deep into the flanks.

**levels/hills, laid again**: the valley's stream is one river along the
valley's line (wavelength 26, amplitude 7, width 1.6 to 3.2, seed 5: of the
first six, the loops that keep clear of the south escarpment's tapered
foot, the others leaving a stray step there), on a floor 9 cells either
side (RIVER_FLOOR; was 3): wider, the held floor reaches the escarpments'
feet and leaves faces a few tenths over the walk, which the view draws no
face for, or flattens them. An escarpment's low faces are capped in one
pass (Relief._cap_low_faces, as before): repeated, each ramp lowers the
faces beside it and the face is eaten. 61 face edges besides the plateau's
40. level.json carries its curve in "waters" and no
"streams". The ford and the bridge are found as before, on rows the river
crosses 1 to 3 cells wide (was 2): a 3-wide ford's middle cell has no ground
beside it, so its footing is stone (the riverbed). Every floor cell is still
reached from the link, through the ford or over the bridge; make_hills
names any stray cliff's cell.

The 557 ribbon (terrain's, until it draws from the curves) holds its
surface between two path cells within theirs and never rising: a wide
river's cells across a bend, each laid from its own point along the curve,
lifted the sampled field a few millimetres off the path.

plot is ground the town keeps for a new building, laid out in the editor,

not said). Builder mode fills them: the request lists the plots near the

## 563. Roads laid as curves

559 made "roads" a level's data (control points, a width each; the cells'
ground from the curve on load); this lays them. Jeff's rule holds for roads
as for water: smooth curves, then cells; no straight runs or right angles.

**Relief.road(map, from, via, to, width, crossings)** returns {points,
widths, cells} for level.json "roads":
- the walk: A* over the map's walkable cells, eight ways (a diagonal only
  where both its sides are open), never into water but the crossings (a
  bridge's cells; a ford is ground), never up or down a cliff (a step over
  WALK_RISE); a step costs its length, ROAD_CLIMB (6) cells a metre of rise
  and ROAD_EDGE (2) more beside water, void or a cliff, so it keeps to the
  flat and its width clear; through each of via in turn;
- the shape (_road_shape), between crossings: the walk's corners cut
  (Chaikin) up to four times, swung across its way up to ROAD_SWING (2.5)
  cells by a noise over ROAD_WAVE (24) cells, eased to nothing at the ends,
  a control point every ROAD_SPACING (4) cells, to two places; a crossing's
  cells and two either side kept as walked, so the curve runs straight over
  a bridge;
- the fit (_road_fit): the curve's cells (Curves.cells) must lie on
  walkable ground or the crossings with no cliff between two of them; a
  cell that fails narrows the control point nearest it by a third, down to
  one cell (eight tries). The wander, then the rounding, is given up only
  as far as that needs: the roundest, most winding road that fits.
On load (Level._lay_curves) a road's floor cells not water take its kind
without a word: a marker on the road takes its ground from its neighbours
in the layout, so the layout cannot say it, and the curve is the road's
data. (559 said a cell the layout had otherwise; for roads it no longer
does.)

**levels/hills**: one dirt road (make_hills _road), from the link's arrival
over the bridge (via its east and west banks, its cells the crossings) to
14 cells past the west escarpment's way (WEST_WAY, now a constant), width
2; its cells bare dirt in the layout. 31 control points, 199 cells.

Level data, protocol unchanged since 559's 29; it ships in the same full
cut. Terrain draws it from the curve.

tests/relief_test: a road alone (over the only bridge, its cells on the
ground and no cliff between them, the water crossed only on the bridge,
from its start to its end, no turn over 0.35 rad a quarter cell; none with
no bridge); the Hills' dirt road from the link over the bridge to the west
of the west way.

## 559, terrain's side: waters drawn from their curves

Jeff's rule (2026-10-21): "Rivers, streams, roads and shorelines are drawn
as smooth curves, then rasterized to cells. Never cell regions with
rounded edges... Nothing inside the water shows the grid." Maps' 559 lays
each water as a curve (terrain "waters": Curves.sample's points, widths,
tangents), its cells derived from it. This is the drawing from that curve,
approved by the coordinator. A level without curves draws as before (553,
557).

**The field.** Client3D._read_curves keeps each water's curve, its cells
(Curves.cells), and for every cell near it the nearest sample.
_curve_near gives a point's signed distance to the curve: the width / 2
there less the distance, positive inside; a pond's from its closed curve
by Curves.inside. It searches CURVE_SEARCH samples round the cell's
nearest, never the whole curve. _curve_field writes from it:
- the shore texture: 0.5 plus the distance (the edge at a half, a cell
  from dry to wet);
- a depth texture of its own (_depth_image, L8): half the distance into
  the water, out to two cells.
The cells' bilinear, its clamp, and the water shader's distance over
cells (into_water, is_water) are not used for a curve's water. A water
without a curve gets its depth worked out the same way (_water_depth: only
its own texels written), so the shader reads one depth for both. The sim's cells are the curve's
raster, so the drawn edge and the cells agree by construction.

**The water.** A river is a ribbon along its curve's own samples
(_build_curve_ribbon), out to its width / 2 and RIBBON_UNDER more under
the banks, trimmed to the stretch over its own cells.
- Its level is the river's surface along it (_curve_profile): the ground
  under each sample (a bridge's water at its bed), smoothed over
  CURVE_SMOOTH samples each side, never rising downstream.
- The flow comes from its tangent, how fast from its drop, and a fall's
  white water where the ground under it drops more than FALL_LEAST over a
  cell (_curve_ground, unsmoothed, the relief even under a bridge, as
  stream_falls measures a step).
- A ford is a stretch of the curve: its cells' nearest samples, easing in
  and out over a cell, carried in UV's x (water.gdshader's "curved"), not
  the mask's cells.
- A pond (closed) is its curve's polygon pushed out RIBBON_UNDER,
  triangulated (none laid yet).
- A stream laid from a curve is drawn by its curve. Its falls are still
  listed from its path (stream_falls).

**The bank and bed.** Every cell of a curve's water, and the band beside
it, is drawn finer (_shore_band, _curve_fine).
- Each point is the ground as drawn, easing under the water's edge (the
  curve's distance, smoothstep 0.3 to 0.5 of the field) to the bed:
  SHORE_SINK under the river's surface there (_curve_surface), and
  WATER_BED_DEPTH more toward its middle.
- So the bed under clear water shows no cell corners.
- A point on an edge or corner shared with a cell drawn whole takes that
  cell's ground as drawn (its sunk corners too), so they meet with no gap.

Cost: the bench A/B (map_bench against 9322dfb1, alternated) follows as
a docs-only note. It was stopped mid-run when windowed Godot was paused
(Jeff in Blender), and the coordinator had this land on its headless
tests and the shots. A first pass, noisy, gave the hills' rebuild
unchanged (about 1000 ms). It also showed the wilds' rebuild up about
60 ms with no curves there: a copy of the whole shore image, since gone
(the depth its own image, only water's texels written). The wilds have no
curves yet (their ponds are to be traced); the cost on ponds is to be
measured when they are laid.

tests/view_test:
- _test_shore on the hills: the field in or out by the curve's distance
  wherever it is past 0.15 of a cell, its edge at a half within an eighth
  (1565 points); the finer cells drawn at their _height_in and meeting the
  ground beside.
- _test_relief: the ribbon on the river's surface, never rising, over its

## 566, maps' side: a building's walls stand once they are up

566 ruled that a town building's wall edges block only from the walls stage
(economy's Towns.walls_up: standing, damaged, a level already up, or built
to BUILD_STAGES[1], 0.35); below that, or only planned, its outline is open
both ways. Level.parse is static and runs before any town state, and the
progress moves while the server runs, so the edges are opened live, not at
load.

**World._open_walls(level, fields)**, beside open_roofs (it runs at the end
of it, so on the same triggers: a town's change, building_changed at every
build stage, and a terrain read):
- Fields.town_buildings now carries each town building's outline
  (Level.building_outline, or its rect's for a roof);
- the outline of every town building whose walls are not up is opened: its
  WALL edges taken out of the level's edges (World._edges for the current
  level, the zone's edges for another) and kept in _walls_down; put back
  when the walls are up. Doors are left (they open anyway);
- the server reads its Towns (buildings_of's "walls"), a client the "town"
  message's (World.towns_seen), so net/prediction walks the same; with no
  word, the walls stand;
- everything that reads the edges follows (edge_kind, edge_blocks, sight,
  the path step cache, which is dropped when they change);
- a terrain read restores the level's edges, so _walls_down is cleared
  there and the walls opened again.

WorldRoutes keeps the outlines as walls (its copy of the edges is made once):
a wagon or a raid never plans through a half-built house, the cautious way.
The view draws an unbuilt building as buildings' staked plot.

Protocol: a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 29 (what walking means between the
stages, on the server and in a client's prediction alike).

tests/view_test: a town building with its walls not up has its outline
open and the path cache dropped; up, its walls stand again.

of 550's rule: a solid building with no door. Every cell of one is out of
the floor and in terrain "solid" (nobody walks onto it, routes go round,
sight stops); its outline has no walls, none expected. Level.solid_door_of
(entry or record) gives a solid building's door, or Level.NO_DOOR for a
doorless one; _lay_solid sets "door" only where there is one.

  1) and "yaw" (a free turn in degrees over its facing's), kept on the
  record: the ring's stones mix the three variants, each turned its own way.

it by its yaw if it has one (else its facing, as before), and dresses a slot
whose spec has "leaf" in season (season_dress, as the forest's trees), so
the great tree's crown browns in autumn and takes snow.

## 568. The wilds' landmarks, layer three: the water

The landmarks design's water: a river down 565's valley, and the wilds'
ponds as curves (559: water is curves, the cells rasterised from them).

**Curves.trace(cells, tolerance)**: a region's shore as a closed curve's
control points: its outline (the cells' squares' outer edges, chained into
loops, the longest kept) cut at each edge's middle, so no grid corner is
left, then the fewest points within tolerance (0.6 cells; Douglas-Peucker
round the loop, split at the point farthest from the first), at least four.
A disc of 63 cells traces into 12 points whose curve holds all 63 (67 in
all). For the ponds now; the editor's curve tool later.

**Relief.river_curve(river, seed)**: what Relief.lay "rivers" lays (the
control points and widths along _meander), split out of _river, so a tool
can see the curve before the lay.

**levels/wilds** (make_wilds_marks' water layer, once: with "waters" in
level.json the ponds are left and the river laid again the same):
- the groves (void inside the land, not joined to the forest round it)
  under the river's curve and a cell round it made grass, 67 cells, so the
  river's cells (laid only on the ground) run unbroken; the forest round
  the land is kept and the river runs on unseen under it at both edges;
- the three ponds of 6 cells or more traced into closed curves (5, 7 and 6
  points), their cells the curve's on the ground (16 to 22, 16, 11 to 10);
  a well's lone water cell left;
- the river (Relief.lay "rivers" in the same lay as 565's relief: wavelength
  34, amplitude 7, width 2 to 3.2, the valley's floor 11 either side, was
  6): 878 cells, clear of every pad (the town, links, spawn points, starts,
  buildings, the camp), its curve in level.json "waters";
- a ford where it runs straight and level nearest row 40 (row 41, 2 cells),
  its banks walked to (make_hills' ford: the ground near it capped again,
  the ridge's faces kept, the rest held); a bridge nearest row 128 (row
  128, 3 cells, (94..96, 128)), its banks levelled, where layer four's hills
  road will cross;
- each pond level under its shore; the river falls as laid.
level.json gains "waters" and the bridge, written into its text; layout.png's
water, ford and grass cells and relief.png are written.

**What changes for walking**: the river splits the wilds west and east; it is
crossed at the ford (row 41) and the bridge (row 128), and nowhere else (no
other fords). Every floor cell walked to on flat ground is still walked to
(through a crossing). Checked: world_map_test, trade_routes_test,
raid_groups_test, raids_test, camp_fall_test and herds_test pass, so the
trade routes' and raid groups' legs still have a way; no camp or herd home
is cut off (nothing on the floor is). A saved spot on a cell the river or

## 562, economy's side: the medicine man barters (barter phase 2)

Jeff: "hob can have a stamina potion that improves run speed and trades for
herbs - other npcs don't find herbs useful". The coordinator approved it as
one piece: items' side has the potion, the "speed" buff and the remedy's
maker fix; npc's side is a check; this side is the medicine man's trade.
It is the first case of 560's phase 2, a maker who sells their own make
and buys their trade's materials from their own purse. The numbers are
drafts for Jeff. (The stamina potion, its run speed, duration and herb
price, accepted by Jeff 2026-10-23: no longer a draft.)
- Production: Hob's hut is a holding of its own, in the defend tier, whose
  wants never named a medical thing. So economy.json always_want gains
  "medical", and the remedy and the potion are made whatever the tier.
  _serves caps a recipe at its own "made" "stock" when it has one (the
  potion 3, items' side), else shop_cap. _bid puts a recipe of rules'
  first_when_sick (["remedy"]) first while any resident (not a companion)
  is sick (Townsfolk.is_sick). npc's check: his own tick makes them with
  nothing new on npc's side, and 501's visit stays his skill.
- Economy.maker_materials(worker): the resources their trade's recipes use,
  times each recipe's shelf (its stock, else shop_cap). For the medicine
  man that is 3x3 + 6x2 = 21 herbs.
- Economy.maker_buys(worker, ids): id -> {gold, up_to}, only for things
  yielding those materials. Each yield is priced at its value times the
  maker's own need: factor(_short(the store's count, the materials'
  want)). up_to is that want less the store's count, and no more than
  their purse pays for.
- Economy.maker_goods(worker): their own make on their town's shelf, at
  maker_price, which is the shop's price but never under value_of. His hut
  wants no medical thing, so the shop's price would halve it; the potion
  asks 4.
- Economy.maker_quote: barter_quote for a maker (their own make only;
  "<name> has no use for that", "has enough of that", "can't pay for it
  now"). Economy.maker_sell takes the price from the maker's purse
  ("makers have more expense") and gives it to the player; they earn it
  back as the maker's share when their make sells.
- Herbs elsewhere: economy.json "maker_only": {"herbs": "the medicine man
  buys herbs"}. refuses() gives it as the reason (the barter hover "won't
  buy"). bank_sale banks such a resource unpaid at a town's store. His own
  gathering (502) still delivers to his store at the delivery price.
- World.try_barter(..., maker): with a worker id, the place is their town;
  the gives are sold to their purse (maker_sell) and banked in their
  store (_sold), and the takes bought off their shelf at the quoted price.
- Main: "barter" and "trade" take {resident: a Resident's path} in place
  of {shop}, within World.reaches of them, else "too far away". The
  "barter" message carries "resident" (and "shop" ""), its goods and buys
  the maker's. PROTOCOL_REVISION 29, for this cut's meaning changes.
economy_test _test_maker_barter. No new class_name.

reply carries "resident" with "shop" "", the goods are only their own

barter (560, {shop}: the town's shop, the merchant's, every maker's goods,

  (BarterPanel.with: the counter, a Chest, or the maker, a Resident).

562's soak found the medicine man gathering nothing in 30 days. Forage
(502) lays herbs only round the towns' held places (within reach 48,
outside a ring of 14 or past their buildings), and Hob's hut is about 56
cells from Held's store. The hut, where it is town-held, also kept herbs
outside its own ring, while his gather (502, npc's side) takes only within
HERB_REACH 6 of the hut. The coordinator ruled (2026-10-22) that herbs grow

  of those kinds, whoever holds them) while fewer than most lie within its

## 505 amended. A bridge's deck kept out of the relief

Level._lay_bridges wrote a bridge's deck elevation (its banks' height) into
terrain "relief" under it, so walkers crossed at the banks' height. But the
relief is the ground and the water: terrain's falls (557 amended), reading
the ground along a river's curve, found a 0.41 m fall where the wilds' river
left its bridge and a 0.46 m one at the hills' (the only falls either map
had), artifacts of the deck in the relief. The coordinator: the relief
shouldn't carry the deck.

Now terrain "relief" keeps the water under a bridge, as relief.png has it,
and terrain "decks" {cell: elevation} carries each bridge cell's deck.
Level.walk_relief(terrain) is the relief as walked: a copy with the decks
laid back. Everything that walks or stands a body reads it, so crossing a
bridge is as it was:
- World._load_relief (steps, cliffs, sight, the server and a client's
  prediction);
- WorldMap's areas (WorldRoutes: the routes over bridges);
- Client3D's own relief (bodies stand on the deck; its ground under the
  bridge is drawn from the bed as before, _bed_levels);
- Level._check_water (a deck is the water's shore beside it).
Terrain's falls read terrain "relief" (or the bed), so no fall at a bridge.

## 571. A level link's cell is kept clear, and a body on it never shuts the way

Jeff, on the box: "i cant get into the castle zone from wilds". The link at
(128, 20) was sound in the level (floor, free, no edges; a step onto it took
the castle, checked on a local world with v0.1.162's files and main's). His
walks there all ended a cell short from several sides: a player's move order
paths to its target even when someone stands on it, and when its last step
is refused the walk gives up ("the contest is decided"). The journal named
nothing on (128, 20), but herd bodies and residents don't log their steps.
A body resting on a link's cell shut the zone to players.

**Kept clear** (World, so every kind of body is covered: herds, strays,
residents, companions at heel, monsters):
- Level puts the links' cells in terrain "links_at"; Fields keeps them as
  link_cells; World.is_link_cell(at);
- try_move refuses any body but a player a step onto a link's cell;
- each zone tick, a body but a player on a link's cell (spawned or saved
  there, pushed on) steps off it the first free way when its step's timer
  lets it (World._clear_links);
- nothing is put down on one (_ground_room passes it over).
A link mid-corridor would now be a cell no monster passes; links stand at
ways out (edges, doors, a mound's door), where none needs to.

**A body on it never shuts the way**: when a player's step onto a link's
cell is refused (someone there, the terrain not blocking), World emits
link_bumped and Main takes the link as for a step onto it (Main._take_link,
which _on_entity_moved now calls too): closed and sealed links answer as
before. A click (a move order, walked by the server) and a WASD step (sent to
the server whatever the client predicts) both reach it, so today's clients
take it without a change.

Server rules; the protocol is unchanged (clients do not predict other
bodies, and a player's step is the server's to take). It ships with the next
cut (the box runs 28, main 29).

## 396 amended. The fallen back on time, and told how long

From Jeff's play (2026-10-22): he died in the castle, was queued for Hob's
hut, and came back 70 s later with the HUD saying only "dead, respawning".
A return job's work only moved on the world tick (every
WORLD_TICK_STEPS, 30 s), so return.steps 600 (60 s) took 60 to 90 s. A
keeper who stopped mid-job (off work, away, his place down) left the
player waiting up to give_up 6000 steps (10 minutes). The coordinator's
rulings, which Jeff can move:
- Return jobs are checked every step: Production.returns_due(at), which
  World.step calls, finishes one on the step it is due (_rate, split out
  of _advance, is the keeper's pace). The wait is return.steps of the
  keeper's work exactly; 60 s stands as a draft.
- A dead player never waits on a keeper's day: if the keeper stops
  mid-job, returns_due gives the player's job up at once, and they come
  back by the plain respawn (RESPAWN_TICKS, 2 s; the give-up now waits
  that too, where it was at once). A companion's or a resident's still
  waits, up to give_up.
- give_up drops to 1200 steps (2 minutes), the ceiling for any other
  stall.
- The "return" message, a new kind (ui's design, the coordinator's
  approval), goes to the fallen player's peer as {by, where, seconds}:
  - by: the keeper's name; where: the place's kind from rules'
    return.places ("temple", "healers_hut"); seconds: the steps left at
    the keeper's pace (Production.return_left) over TICK_RATE, rounded
    up, or -1 if not known.
  - Sent when the job opens (Main._start_return).
  - Sent as {"", "", 2} at a death with no manned place, and when a
    return is given up on (Main._tell_return).
  - Each message restarts ui's countdown ("Hob is bringing you back to
    the healer's hut: 58 s").

A new message kind moves the protocol hash and needs no bump.

tests/return_test _test_due:
- A job opened off the world tick's beat is done on exactly its
  600th step.
- The keeper going away gives the player's job up on the next step and
  keeps a companion's.
- give_up is 1200.

In Main, the player is told {Ned, healers_hut, 60} at death and is back
at the hut 600 steps later; with nobody manned, {"", "", 2}. The test's

## 572. A companion never holds a freed node (crash fix)

The box's server segfaulted twice (v0.1.162, 2026-10-22, 02:20 and
02:25), each within seconds of a player's death in the barrow, with no
script error logged. The cause: a freed Player held by Companion.keeper,
dereferenced in the release template. World.despawn frees a dead player
at the frame's end, but Companion.keeper still pointed at it; her voice,
asked a moment later (the kills she saw, once nothing hostile was near),
built _wound_words from `for each: GridEntity in [self, keeper]`, which
puts the freed node into a typed variable. A debug build checks that and
logs "previously freed"; the release template skips the check and reads
the freed object to learn its class (locally on Windows it logged "an
object of type 'Object'"; on the box's Linux build, by every sign, a segfault before any
line). Reproduced on a local dedicated server with one client: moved to
the barrow, killed there by the skeletons or outright; the errors on
every death are gone with the fix. The castle death that night did not
crash: no kills were waiting for her voice there.

The rule: a companion lets go of every node the moment it leaves the
world. Main, on World.entity_despawned (before the free), calls
Companion.forget(entity) on each companion: her keeper, intent target,
quarry and stalked animal are cleared, an errand naming it ends, and a
voice ask's offers naming it are dropped whole (a [DO: n] counts from
that list). A reader of keeper checks _alive / is_instance_valid first,
and a node that may be freed never goes into a typed variable (the loop
over her companions in that handler is untyped). A player's leaving
cleared keeper already; a death now does too.

companion_test _test_death_and_respawn: at her player's death she holds
nothing of them (keeper, an errand, an offer). Server sim, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.

## 573, economy's side. A player's charges and the draugr's deals

Dungeon's design (C:/dev/review/dungeon/crypt_tokens_design.md, Jeff's
corrections taken, the coordinator's approval). Economy owns the
arithmetic, so the win (dungeon's Main.barrow_won), the channel
(companions') and the pact (enemy-ai's Draugr) each call one helper. All
are static on Economy; no new class_name.

- **The record.** PlayerRecord.barrow becomes {tokens, best, containers}:
  - tokens: the charges held, a number on the record (not gold, not an
    item).
  - best: the hardest deal beaten ("" unblessed).
  - containers: the named sources of more capacity, each once (none
    yet).
- **Capacity is derived, never stored** (economy's correction), so it
  follows the rules when Jeff moves them. Economy.barrow_capacity is
  capacity_step × (1 + the hardest deal's place among the deals) plus
  capacity_step per container: 25, 50, 75 from the barrow, 0 unblessed.
- **The rules,** in return.field:
  - "deals": [{name, gold, charges}] from the least: easy 20 gold for 5,
    normal 50 for 10, hard 100 for 15.
  - "capacity_step": 25.
  - Economy.deal_for(gold, field): the highest step the gold reaches, {}
    under 20 (enemy-ai's pact reads it).
  - Economy.field_tokens(deal, field): the deal's charges, read from the
    deals by name. The rules' old "uses" is kept and read as the fallback
    until the callers move to the deals; dungeon's side drops it.
- **Economy.barrow_won(barrow, deal, field)** returns {barrow, took,
  spilled}. It raises best only to a harder deal, never lowers it, and
  takes the deal's charges up to the capacity. What is over is spilled,
  for dungeon's line.
- **Economy.barrow_spend(barrow)** takes one charge in place; false at 0.
  Economy.barrow_tokens reads the count.
- **Economy.barrow_migrated(saved)** turns a pre-573 {uses, of,
  difficulty, day} into {tokens: uses, best: difficulty, containers: []}.
  A blessed record (uses or "of") with no difficulty gets "easy". A 573
  record comes back as it was.
  - It is not wired into PlayerRecord.from_entry yet. Main's readers
    (bless, _uses_left, the channel's spend, the companion's REVIVE)
    still read "uses", so the migration lands with the landing that
    switches them, dungeon's, and companions' beside it. A record
    migrated before then would read 0 uses.
- **Nothing in gold** here: the deal's gold is the draugr's as today (a
  spending). 546's offering, Aldous's alms and the altar's gold are
  untouched.

tests/economy_test _test_barrow_charges: the deals by gold, charges by
deal and the uses fallback, a win's charges and capacity, the spill at
capacity, best never lowered, a container's 25, the spend and none at 0,
the migration both ways. Server only, protocol unchanged.


## 573. The Crypt: the blessing and the resurrection charges

Jeff (2026-10-22, his words through the coordinator): "the draugr gives the
blessings to any player or companion that takes the deal and wins. Before
blessing you respawn in the town at the temple. After you have the blessing
you can be resurrected by a companion as long as you have a resurrection
charge token counter; it's not an item, it's part of you, it doesn't trade.
The draugr gives more charges on higher difficulties; you choose the
difficulty by how much gold you donate: 20, 50, 100 for 5, 10 and 15 res
charges. The draugr's level is equal to base level + how many player
resurrection points are in the zone when he starts the fight. If a player
zones in while the fight is active, he heals 50% of his health immediately.
Once you have a charge you can resurrect anyone that is dead, but it drains
an active res token from you." Dungeon led the design
(C:\dev\review\dungeon\crypt_tokens_design.md); the coordinator approved it
with one ruling (only the blessed get the window; the charge drained is the
resurrector's). It replaces 544's uses and device as the return's gate, and
548's measures of the offering as the deal's price (explicit gold steps now).
Sides: economy's (the record's shape and the arithmetic), enemy-ai's (the
deals' steps, his level, the heal), companions' (the window), ui's (the pack
line), items' (below). This is dungeon's side.

- The win: World.bless (548's hook) reaches Main.barrow_won(player_ids,
  deal): each player standing alive in his lair is blessed if not yet (the
  mark "draugr", 540, never taken off) and takes the deal's charges up to
  their capacity (Economy.barrow_won: {barrow, took, spilled}); the party
  line says the count and the room ("The draugr yields. Bo is blessed and
  takes 10 charges (10 of 50).") and the spill ("The dead's gift spills: 5
  more than they can hold."); their companion standing alive in the zone is
  blessed too (her mark, her fact, the bond, 555 amended). Nothing is minted.
- The count: PlayerRecord.barrow {tokens, best, containers} (economy's
  shape), migrated on load from 544's {uses, of, difficulty, day}
  (Economy.barrow_migrated, wired in PlayerRecord.from_entry here). The
  channel's reads moved with it: _uses_left reads Economy.barrow_tokens, a
  return done spends Economy.barrow_spend ("(n charges left)"), no half is
  carried (_start_channel, _can_revive), the refusal is "You hold no charge.
  The draugr gives more."; the loyalty read of a bleed-out (555 amended)
  reads the charges. economy.json return.field drops "uses" (the deals carry
  the charges).
- On the wire: Player.charges and Player.charge_room (ints, replicated,
  SUBCLASS_REPLICATED), set from the record whenever it changes
  (Main._sync_charges: the join, the win, a spend), so a client reads them
  any time (ui's pack line). PROTOCOL_REVISION 30.
- For the draugr: Main.charges_in_zone(zone) sums the charges of the players
  in a zone (his level's rise at start_pact, enemy-ai's side);
  Main._living_came(player) on every entry into a zone (travel and join both
  go through _join_player) calls Draugr.living_came when he has it
  (enemy-ai's), so a player zoning in during a pact heals him.
- Items' side: the barrow_half and return_token kinds stay as keepsakes for
  the ones held; World.mint_bound, carries_bound and ItemBook.bind stay; no
  item text named the uses, so nothing changes in items.json.
- Open for Jeff (drafts in his folder): a failed pact costs the gold alone;
  capacity +25 the first time a bigger deal is won (25, 50, 75), later
  containers from other areas' bosses; the halves no longer minted.

level_test _test_barrow_won; companion_test _test_field_return adapted (no
device, the charges counted). No new class_name.

## 573, enemy-ai's side. The draugr's pact by the deals; his level by the charges; the living's coming heals him

Dungeon's design as Jeff corrected it, the coordinator's approval: "you
choose the difficulty by how much gold you donate ... 20, 50, 100 for 5, 10
and 15 res charges. The draugr's level is equal to base level + how many
player resurrection points are in the zone when he starts the fight. If a
player zones in while the fight is active, he heals 50% of his health
immediately."

- **The deal.** `Draugr.deals()` reads economy's `return.field.deals`
  (`Economy.deals`; `DEALS` the same three steps when the rules give none);
  `deal_for(gold)` takes the highest step the gold reaches, {} under the
  least. `offers_for` offers the pact at the least step (cost 20; what
  {offering, least, most, steps}); `accept_offer` refuses under it, else
  takes the gold (as ever, its own spending) and starts the pact at the
  deal's name (easy, normal, hard: `World.bless`'s second argument, Main's
  `barrow_won`). The measures of 548 (`offering()`, `difficulty_for`,
  `OFFERING`, `DIFFICULTIES`) are gone. A lost pact keeps the gold; the
  run goes on (a retry).
- **His level.** At `start_pact` he asks `World.charges_in` (a Callable,
  Main's `charges_in_zone`) for the charges held by the players in his
  zone (`charges_met`). His hp and blows are his kind's times
  `SCALE[deal]` (1, 1.5, 2) + `CHARGE_SCALE` (0.05) a charge; he raises
  `RETINUE[deal]` (0, 1, 2) of the dead and one more each
  `CHARGES_PER_RISEN` (10), `MOST_MORE_RISEN` (3) more at most. Drafts for
  Jeff. The halls do not scale.
- **The living come.** `Draugr.living_came(player)`, called by Main's
  `_living_came` on every entry into the zone: in a pact he gets
  `LIVING_HEAL` (half) of his most back at once, capped at it; his level
  stays as it began. Seated or resting, nothing.
- **Words.** WORDS and the accept line name the gold steps and the returns
  (drafts for Jeff's wording, through the coordinator).

The yield, the rest (548) and the hook are as they were. monster_test
_test_draugr: the steps offered, 19 refused, 60 the normal deal, 10 charges
making him 60 hp with 2 risen, the living's coming healing 30, 20 gold the
easy deal. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 570, terrain's side: a tall fall's curtain, and waters that meet

maps' 570 lays the hills' first real fall: a stream off the plateau's
west cliff dropping 7.9 m into a pool (the curve widened there), meeting
the river below. Two view_test checks failed on it, and the approved
design (the coordinator, 2026-10-22) answers both. The order: this
first, maps' 570 straight after, so main never has the fall's data
without its drawing.

**Waters that meet.** Where a stream runs into a river a point inside
the river can lie nearer the stream's end sample than any of the
river's, and read dry.
- The nearest-sample map keeps one sample per curve near a cell
  (_stamp_near: the first curve's in the map, any other's in an "also"
  map), and _near_on takes the one the point is furthest into: the
  field is the waters' union (roads' too, where they cross).
- An earlier water keeps a cell a later one reaches (as the level lays
  them: the stream stops at the river).
- A stream ending in an earlier river is no lower than the river's
  surface there (_meet_at_end), so the two meet with no step.
- Its ribbon runs on over the river's cells (it used to stop at its own,
  a cell short, a strip of dry ground and a straight cut between them),
  fading out over a cell (UV's y under a half, water.gdshader's alpha).

**The profile keeps its falls.** _curve_profile smoothed over
CURVE_SMOOTH samples before its running minimum, so across a tall step
it pulled the surface metres under the bed above the lip. Now a drop of
over FALL_LEAST from one sample to the next starts a new run, and each
run is smoothed on its own; the running minimum is as before. For a cell
past a fall the pool stands on its ground (the smoothing had it under the
foot cell's, a dry band between the curtain and the water).

**The bed under the curve's water.** A narrow stream's cell beside a
cliff is drawn whole (not finer: _curve_fine skips cells with a cliff
edge), its corners at the mean of its cells' water, which can stand
over the curve's own surface. _shore_bed takes the curve's surface where
that is lower, so no dry corner shows inside the water. Across a tall
fall a water cell's corners (_water_corner, _shore_bed with its level)
and a bank's take only the water within FALL_TALL of their own level: the
mean of the lip's and the foot's water had ramped the bed between them, a
slope of ground in front of the curtain's lower half; now the cliff's
face stands there and the curtain hangs on it.

**The curtain.** Where a river's surface drops FALL_TALL (1 m) or more
from one sample to the next, _build_curve_ribbon hangs a curtain from
the lip to the water below: CURTAIN_ROWS rows, out down the stream as
the square root of the drop (as water falls), from the lip's width to
the foot's, white, facing down the stream, their UV's y 1.
water.gdshader streaks a curtain by its height (world y) falling fast,
keeps its own facing rippled a little, all of it white. The white water
past the foot is the fall's as before (557 amended). Mist waits (the
coordinator). Sound's cue plays at the fall's true drop (stream_falls,
unchanged in shape: the 7.9 m drop clamps to FALL_LOUDEST).

Rejected: having the data end the stream in a pool short of the river
(maps offered); streams meet rivers, and Jeff wants rivers.

view_test: _test_curves_meet (two curves, a point in the river by the
stream's end); _test_relief: a 3 m step down the hills' stream hangs a
curtain from its lip to the water below, its surface never far under
its bed (a lip's corner over the foot's water is the face, not a dry
bed); the falls check down any stream's path. Shots in
C:/dev/review/falls (maps' 570 data, before without this and after).
Client only, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.

## 570. Falls: a river crossing a face drops its height into a pool

The approved design's falls: where a river (559's "rivers") crosses a face
(a plateau's, an escarpment's) the water drops the face's height between
two cells of its middle, into a pool at the foot; on the hills a side stream
off the plateau's west cliff; on the wilds none (the river's course does
not cross the ridge's face). Terrain draws the curtain (its tall-fall side,
cd3c4453), which lands first.

**Relief.lay "rivers"**: a river's surface already falls with the ground
(never rising), so where its curve crosses a face it drops between two
middle cells. Where a drop is over WALK_RISE it is a fall: lay's "falls"
lists {cell, drop}. Its pool is the curve's own: the control point a cell
past where the water lands is widened to POOL_WIDTH (3.4), and the curve is
laid again, so the pool is the curve's raster (laid, loaded and drawn
alike) and the stream is as narrow as it was up to its lip (_river_run, the
lay of a curve on the ground, split out). A bank raised to its shore lip is
never another water's cell (a stream raised the river it ran into).

**A stream into a river**: a later water's cells stop where an earlier one's
are. Relief.lay laid it so (taken); Level._lay_curves now does too, the
earlier waters' cells no ground to a later one, so a tributary's cells and
its "streams" path end where it joins (it took the river's cells past the
junction, which rose).

**levels/hills**: a second river, FALL_STREAM, from the plateau's top at
(84, 12) west over its cliff to the river at (53, 22) (wavelength 14,
amplitude 2, width 1.4 to 2.2): it falls 7.9 m at (62, 22) to (61, 22) into
its pool, and a ford across it at (56, 20) below the pool (_fall_ford, its
banks walked to as the river's ford), so the ground between the river, the
stream and the cliff is still walked to. Every floor cell is reached; no
stray cliff.

Level data, protocol unchanged (no new field); a full cut.

tests/relief_test: the hills' river and the fall's stream; a fall off the
plateau's cliff over 5 m into a pool of water at its foot's level.

## 575. The forest's edge drawn from curves

Jeff's rule (2026-10-21): "never cell regions with rounded edges". The
forest's edge was the cells' edge: a tree on every cell of its first ring
(nudged at most 0.42 within it), the ground turned to forest floor by the
cells' mask, the scatter's kind by its cell; a straight run read as a
row, a diagonal as steps, a grove as a block. The coordinator's approval,
2026-10-22.

**The curve, traced here.** The land's cells stay the truth: the sim, the
walk and sight never see the curve, and nobody authors the forest's shape,
so the client traces it (_read_edges) round the cells the forest grows
round (_wooded):
- every loop of their outline (the land's rim and each grove in it;
  _outline_loops, turning right where two cells meet at a corner alone,
  so each loop keeps round its own cells), as its edges' middles;
- simplified within EDGE_SIMPLIFY (0.3: a staircase's run is a line), a
  point a cell along each run (through a long run's ends alone the curve
  bowed half a cell off it), each moved up to EDGE_WOBBLE (0.14) across it
  by a slow noise;
- a closed curve through them (Curves.sample), within EDGE_BOUND (0.45)
  of the cells' edge everywhere: no walkable cell's middle reads forest,
  no forest cell's open;
- an authored forest's shape would be maps' "forests" curves in level.json
  later, read here the same way (the door is open; nothing laid now).

**Which side.** _edge_signed: the distance to the nearest curve near a
point, positive on the forest's side, by the way the curve runs (the land
on its right going round), searched round the nearest sample of the point's
cell (_stamp_near's maps, as the waters'). Its field (_edge_field, RG8 at
the shore field's texels near an edge) turns the ground to forest floor
along the curve (ground.gdshaderinc "forest_edge"); the cells' mask still
holds it away from an edge.

**The trees at the edge** (_add_edge_trees) come from the curve, not the
first ring's cells: one every EDGE_SPACING (0.7 to 1.1) along it,
EDGE_DEPTH (0.3 to 1.4) into the forest, the nearest kept EDGE_NEAR_KEEP
(0.75) of the time, a tree a cell, only on the forest's cells and side;
where a pine stand or a deeper tree has the place, just inside the first
ring instead. A felled one's stump and a sapling by a tree now and then, as
the first ring had them. The deeper rings as before.

**The scatter** by an edge: the land's kinds and the forest's both offered
in a cell near it, each point kept on its own side of the curve; the edge's
roots on the land within EDGE_ROOTS (0.7) of it.

Not in this step: tall grass's patch edge and the rocks' cells (a grey
square where the wilds' grove thinned) still follow their cells; the hills'
straight runs stay straight, as its land is (its shape is maps').

Shots in C:/dev/review/forestedge (the hills' north edge, east edge and
corner, the wilds' north edge and three groves, noon and 16:00; before is
main 2a65179b). Cost: map_bench rebuild, alternated twice with main:
hills 1149/1123 ms before, 1232/1232 after (+95 ms, 8%); wilds 5167/4911
before, 5488/5460 after (+435 ms, 9%), the field and the trace. Frame times
read nothing that hour (the machine's 30 fps cap, 570 amended's note): a
frame re-bench is owed when the display wakes.

view_test _test_forest_edge (hills, wilds): the curve within EDGE_BOUND of
the cells' edge; its sides as the cells' away from it, nought on it; every
tree on the forest's cells and side; the scatter by it on its own side.
_test_forest: the first ring's every-cell check became a tree (or stump)
within 2.2 of every stretch of the edge; the lane's trees either side

## 578. No insects in the cold; no ticking water

Jeff, on v0.1.163, in the wilds at night with snow falling: "with the sound
there an annoying noise that sounds like bugs or a hard drive noise...it goes
away with ambience slider to 0".

**What it was.** The open forest's night bed, amb.forest_night, which plays
over all the open wilds by night: its first take is crickets (nearly all of
its sound above 4 kHz), and nothing told the beds the season, so they
chirped in the snow. The town's night bed and the deep forest's are insects
too. Measured, not heard (sound's band and kurtosis report over every
ambience take): beside the crickets, three water takes ticked, their band
over 4 kHz full of sharp clicks (kurtosis 8 to 11 where smooth noise is 3):
amb.stream's 231536 and 446019 and amb.falls' 727048. A stream's loop is
heard 16 cells off, and 568's river runs down the whole of the wilds, so
that crackle had come within earshot of most of it in v0.1.163.

**The night's insects follow the cold.** Ambience.weights takes the
season's cold (Season.at's, the listener's region); the night beds
(amb.forest_night, amb.forest_deep_night, amb.town_night) are scaled by
1 - smoothstep(INSECT_COLD): all of them below 0.5 (the equinoxes), none
from Season.SNOW_FALLS' first (0.62), the cold snow starts falling at. A
winter night is still but for the wind, the owls and the bats.

**The ticking takes are dropped**, not re-cut (the clicks are in the
recordings): amb.stream keeps 415053 (Brook 2, smooth), amb.falls 191879
and 537681. Their files are moved aside in the library
(takes/_dropped_578), not deleted; takes.json, THIRD_PARTY.md's sound
block and sound_status regenerated without them.

sound_kit_test: the night beds whole at INSECT_COLD's first, none at its
second. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 576. Capabilities: what each area teaches, and the world as a lock

Jeff (2026-10-22): "companions do learn everything -- ability is more like
metroidvania, each helps you in higher difficulty areas ... each area in
turn add capability; an example would be visiting the elven lands for an
ability that counters 'rot' allowing you to explore the deeper areas of
the blood rot caverns." The coordinator approved the design
(C:/dev/review/companions/abilities_focus_design.md, part a), with
party-level gates until Jeff says otherwise.

- A capability is a mark (a player's record.marks, a companion's
  record.companion["marks"], 540 and 544) with an entry in
  levels/capabilities.json: words, area, teacher, holders, status (live,
  or draft: no area yet, nothing gives or checks it), companion_line,
  fact, bond and bond_why, gates. Marks have no cap, so everything can be
  learned. New class_name Capabilities (sim/capabilities.gd, static):
  catalog, entry, live, held (the live ones among some marks, for her
  card), said (a line with {her} and {player} filled in).
- The catalog: draugr live (the blessing, 544/573: moved onto it, no
  change in play); rot_ward, dwarf_craft, healer_lore and dark_gift as
  drafts, their teachers and places following lore's pages.
- Main.grant_capability(id, player_ids): each player in the game marked
  (holders permitting), and the companion with them, alive and up in
  their zone: her mark, the catalog's party line, its fact on her card,
  her bond event (the blessing keeps "blessed"; others "earned", +2 in
  companion_traits.json "bond"). A draft is given to nobody. barrow_won
  marks through it; its own lines (the charges) stay its own.
- Main.party_has(peer, id): the player's mark, or the mark of the
  companion out with them (alive, in their zone, not resting in a town).
  Main.sealed_open reads it, so a link sealed by a mark opens when either
  holds it: bringing her opens the way.
- Her player's map is told what she holds: the "world" message's
  "capabilities" {companion, held: [{id, words, teacher}]}, sent when she
  joins and when she learns one, kept through a full message
  (WorldNews.merge) like 551's "guide". For ui's card page; the client
  draws nothing of it yet. Protocol: a key in an existing message, under
  revision 30 (release; net.gd's comment).
- The other gate kinds (hostile air, a locked craft, a fight's counter)
  are built with the first area that needs them, by items, economy and
  enemy-ai.

companion_test _test_capabilities: the catalog, a draft given to nobody,
the grant (both marked, the fact, the world message, kept through a full
one), her mark alone opening a sealed way while she is with them, not
while she rests in town. Server and client (the world message's merge),
no replicated field.

## 572 amended. The world's jobs never hold a freed node

The same crash class as 572, in World: its per-tick jobs are kept in
dictionaries keyed by entities (_buffed, _bandaging, _mending, _winders,
_channels, _downed), some naming another entity (a bandaging's patient, a
channel's body), and each tick loops `for entity: GridEntity in
dict.keys()`. Nothing took a despawned entity out, so once one left the
world (died, or went to another zone) with a buff on (anyone who had
eaten), mid-bandage, mid-channel or downed, the next tick put the freed
node into a typed variable: the debug build logs "Trying to assign
invalid previously freed instance", the release template reads freed
memory (572). companion_test's 577 checks found it: the companion ate,
then travelled.

- World.despawn calls _forget_jobs(entity) before the free: its buff,
  mending, wind-up and downed entries go; a bandaging or a channel it was
  in, as either side, ends as broken off (bandage_changed "interrupted",
  channel_changed "broken", said as ever).
- _fade_buffs takes its keys untyped and checks them before the typed
  variable, for a node freed some other way.

Server sim, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 566, buildings' side: a building seen being built, and its lamps

Approved by the coordinator with npc's visible-work page (Jeff,
2026-10-21: "building a half constructed building, sleeping at night");
economy's keys under protocol revision 29 carry what it reads, nothing on
the wire of its own.
- Stages by the town record's progress (economy's "progress", 0..1, on a
  use's record while a job is on it): BuildingComposer.stage. A first
  build (planned, or building at level 0) is PLOT under 0.1 (stakes and
  string round its outline, a woodpile), FRAME to 0.35 (sills along its
  walls, its corner posts a storey tall), four WALLS stages to 0.75 (its
  walls a quarter of their height higher each, scaffold from the half),
  RAFTERS to 0.9 (its main roof's rafters a metre apart), COVERING to its
  job's end (its roofs on), then STANDING as drawn today. Its windows,
  door, chimney, porch and cruck come with whole walls or standing.
  The cut-offs are economy's Towns.BUILD_STAGES, which it resends the
  record at. Anything
  else is STANDING; a raise (building, level 1 or more) or a repair under
  way (damaged, with progress) stands in scaffold.
- A planned building with no progress yet is its staked plot
  (PLANNED_AS_PLOT, the coordinator's ruling, one switch should Jeff
  overturn it). A fresh town's first look changes: its unbuilt buildings
  show as plots where they stood whole. The box's Held, mostly built,
  changes little.
- Drawn only: the client marks a stage's outline edges "plot" (no wall,
  no post) or "frame" (no wall, corner posts) in its wall states, cuts
  _wall_heights to the stage's part, hides the doorway, and draws the
  edges again (rebuild_walls) when the stage changes; a roof not yet on is
  none to hide or fade. Whether a wall blocks is the sim's (from 0.35:
  economy's Towns.walls_up and maps' loader).
- Site pieces: art-kit's site.stake, frame.sill, scaffold.bay (edge
  pieces, along z, outside +x; scaffold.bay_ladder on the bay nearest the
  door, both stretched to the eaves from their 3 m), roof.rafters (a pair
  for a 4 m span rising 2 m, origin at the apex, stretched to the roof's),
  and prop.woodpile (its state_full to the frame, state_half through the
  walls, state_low under the roof) with prop.planks beside it through the
  walls, and prop.sawhorse on its own cell to the frame (its log turned
  across the way its sawyer faces it), where the kit has them, else
  plain timber boxes.
- Level.site_cells(building) -> {work, woodpile, sawbuck, saw} (in the sim, so the

refinement" and "we also need a combat work-tree"). A worktree,
C:/dev/psykinetic-trees/combat (branch combat, port offset 3800), owns how
fighting feels for the player: the player's melee verbs and their timing,
hit feedback, blocking, dodging and their cost, the damage model shared by
players, companions and monsters, the fights' pace, and, once the archery
refinement of 2026-10-22 has landed, World.shoot and the ranged verbs. Its

  tree's brief: its [decided] lines are Jeff's and stand; its [proposed]
  ones are built as data and tuned by play.

  a design with them), bodies and clips (pc-character), what weapons are
  (items), the screen (ui), and mass, force, knockback, momentum and thrown
  bodies (the physics tree, from 2026-10-22): combat sends a move as an
  intent and a physics event, physics resolves it.

  the bow's right button stays the draw (462) or becomes the doc's defend
  and backstep.

## 572 amended (2). A reset forgets the world's jobs too

World.reset takes a zone's entities out with _world_remove, not despawn,
so 572 amended's _forget_jobs never ran for them: a body left downed, a
channel, a buff or a bandaging outlived the reset and was read freed on
the next tick (enemy-ai-17 found it with a test that left a body downed).
reset now calls _forget_jobs on each entity it removes. A typed
dictionary refuses a freed key even to look one up or erase it, so
_forget_jobs and _fade_buffs rebuild theirs from keys and values side by
side, keeping the live entries (items_test's rebuild left a bandaging
holding a freed body). Server sim, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 592: knockback by impulse, mass, momentum and angle (physics step 1)

The physics tree's first step (C:/dev/review/physics/model.md and step1_design.md;
the coordinator's approval, 2026-10-22). The sim's push had no velocity, so moving into a
blow added nothing (a blow mid-step is refused); it went only the eight compass ways; two
clamps flattened mass (max_force 4 made every body under 20 kg fly as one of 20, the ratio
clamp 1.5 stopped it mattering under 53 kg) and mass counted twice; and a body knocked into
a body passed on "force left - 1" whatever the two weighed, with the mover's mass a budget.

- A push's "force" is now the speed it gives its body. A shove's impulse is strength x the
  shover's mass x shove_scale; the body's speed is that over its pushed mass (exhausted and
  downed still halve it). One division by mass, no clamp. A blow carries
  ATTACK_FORCE_FACTOR x its verb's force of it (World.blow_impulse), held to
  knockback_min_force as Jeff's rule says (decision 305), now a speed. The guard (340)
  weighs the same number, so guards are unchanged.
- The slide: slide_per_speed cells per unit of speed, at most max_travel 10 (a sanity
  limit, the coordinator's: bodies under about 16 kg are all flattened by it, the one place
  mass is), along the push's line at any angle, traced a cell at a time (the longer axis a
  whole cell each step), speed lost as it goes (each cell, diagonal or not, 1 over
  slide_per_speed, as before).
- Momentum: a step sets the body's step_velocity (direction / its step's ticks, server
  only, never sent) till momentum_ticks after it ends (World.body_velocity). A blow, shove
  or bash adds momentum_scale (a swing's share) x the attacker's mass x that velocity over
  the target's mass, as a vector: along the blow it adds, across it it angles the push,
  backward along it it is dropped. A toss is aimed and takes none.
- What a sliding body meets, with speed u left: a wall, a closed door or a step up stops it
  and hurts impact_per_energy x 1/2 m u^2 (a door takes the same), so the same shove hurts a
  light body more against a wall (240 / m with the defaults). A body: a collision along the
  line with restitution: the one met goes on at (1 + e) m1 u / (m1 + m2), the mover stops
  behind it, the energy lost is shared between them as impact, and the one met may knock on
  another. The mover's mass budget is gone: a body moves when its speed carries a cell. Drops
  (falls keep their 3 a level), water and fire are as before; stuns as before, by speed left.
- The braced spear (344): the charger's whole momentum (a body run onto a stop, not a
  swing's share) turned back, (1 + brace_restitution, 1 at most) x its speed, plus the
  spear's blow, not held to the threshold; BRACE_FORCE_PER_KG is gone. A charging boar at its
  pace goes back 1 cell, where it went 3: the one feel number this step changes.
- For combat (combat-1d's interface, agreed): World.apply_blow(source, target, {impulse,
  direction: Vector2, stagger}) pushes at once (not queued), the source's momentum added,
  and returns and emits blow_resolved {moved, distance, cells, stopped_by, impact_damage,
  struck, knocked_down, speed}; stagger is combat's beat past a slide (-1,
  knockback_stun_ticks). World.body_velocity and World.mass_of for its timing and costs.
  Damage stays combat's, collision damage physics'. _push returns each body's
  {body, from, to, cells, stopped_by, impact}.
- The numbers are in levels/physics.json (World.load_physics_rules at start; a value missing
  or not a number at least 0 keeps its default, warned), for combat and Jeff to tune. Drafted
  to keep today's feel: for bodies under 53 kg the distances are today's exactly (the old
  ratio clamp was 1.5, now slide_per_speed); heavier ones go a little farther (a hammer moves
  a 70 kg brute 2 cells, was 1); a fist or a sword still moves a 70 kg brute nothing.
- The client's guess of a shove (predict_push_end) reads the same speed and slide, the mover
  standing. Thrown things (try_throw) keep their old impact rule (impact_per_force,
  mass_ratio) till a later step makes them move what they hit.

tests/physics_test (new: the rules file; one hammer blow on 25, 40, 70, 90 kg, 7, 4, 2, 0
cells; an 85 kg body standing still under a hammer blow, knocked 2 when the blow comes
stepping in, unmoved when backing away; a push along (2, 1) six cells off every compass
line; the same shove into a wall 10, 6, 3 hp by mass; goblin into goblin, into a boulder,
brute into imp; the brace). push_test's numbers where the rule changed: a monster shoved into
a monster takes 2 and gives 2 (was 6 and 6: the energy goes into moving the second), a shove
just after a step 7 against the wall (was 6) and the lane's last shove 1 cell (was 0), both by
the step's momentum, and the one run into stunned 6 (was 4) by the speed left.

## 580, economy's side. The grave robbers carry gold

Jeff's words, routed by the coordinator from dungeon's barrow in layers
(580): "the grave robbers would have gold on them, either from stealing or
from other jobs". Approved as written, the thief's cut by default. Nothing
is minted ("everything has to be gathered and someone paid to do it"), and
no player's gold is taken.

- **The band's purse.** Economy keeps the robbers' gold by barrow level
  (economy.json robbers.barrow, "barrow", layer 1, where the altar is),
  in the snapshot ("bands", "band_day"). It fills two ways:
  - **Stealing, from the altar.** Once a game day, on the world tick
    (Economy._band_turn), the band lifts robbers.altar_share (0.5) of
    the gold below at every town's altar (Economy.lift_below, which
    nothing called before). This is the plunder: the robbers' pilfering
    of the altar's gold is what angers the old gods in lore (the
    pilferers), so the share they take is the plunder. Pip's runs still
    lay the alms down (546); half is gone by the next day.
  - **Other jobs, as the thief's fence.** A town's thief pays
    robbers.thief_cut (0.25) of each lift he isn't caught at from his
    own purse to the band (Economy.thief_cut, from
    Townsfolk._lift_gold), for moving what he took.
- **On a robber.** A robber's gold leaves the band only when he falls,
  so nothing goes back when the barrow sleeps or is laid again.
  - Main._robber_fell, on World.entity_died: a monster of robbers.kinds
    (["robber"]) fallen in the barrow takes Economy.band_share.
  - The share is the band's gold over the robbers standing (him among
    them), at most robbers.most (40), in whole purses (coin_purse's
    yield, 10).
  - It lies where he fell as coin purses; the rest stays with the band.
  - An empty band means empty pockets. A respawned robber carries what
    is left, so farming them drains the band until the altar and the
    thief fill it again.
- Owners: economy only. Dungeon's levels need nothing (the altar stays on
  layer 1); enemy-ai's Monster.remains is untouched.

tests/economy_test:
- _test_robbers_band: a day's lift of half the altar's gold, once a day;
  the thief's quarter; a share in whole purses and the cap; the purse
  saved; no rules, no gold.
- _test_robber_falls (in Main, the test's zone standing for the
  barrow): one of two robbers falls with 50 in the band, two purses of

## 583, ui's side: the aim while a bow is drawn

Jeff (2026-10-22, his words): "for aiming bow and drawning back movement
mouse disappears and the game draws a semi circle for distance... aiming
is right now locked by tile which is hard for the player. so use a circle
which the aim can move along at many degrees"; then "the range has
increments, the arc goes along the semicircle". Pc-character's archery
redesign (583) with items (try_loose by angle, range steps, damage per
step) and enemy-ai; the coordinator approved ui's side as written, pips
first for the power read, Jeff to pick from the shot.

- The draw is Shift (the stand key, Keys "stand") with the left button,
  a bow in hand (583 amended (2); Jeff, 2026-10-22, via the coordinator,
  after a day on the left button alone and pc-character's quarter-second
  hold: "lets do this with archery, just like shift+LMB to draw back,
  mouse to move only"): the press draws at once (the "draw" stance), the
  release looses by the angle or cancels before draw_min; letting go of
  Shift mid-draw changes nothing. A plain left click with a bow never
  attacks (the coordinator's ruling): a chest is walked to, a friend
  talked to, anything else, a monster as the ground, walked toward
  (Main._click_with_bow); Shift with the button is the only shot. With a
  bow Shift draws instead of combat's stand swing (the bow is the
  weapon; combat's call). The hold wait (DRAW_HOLD_MSEC, 4fe7b404) is
  gone. The greeting bubble's click still opens the bar; the right
  button with a bow does nothing until combat's backstep; a shield's
  block stays the right button's.
- Drawn (Player.raised "draw"): the OS cursor hides (Input's mouse mode;
  the 2D view's own cursor too) and shows again on release or cancel
  (Main._show_cursor, never headless).
- The arc: a flat semicircle on the ground round the archer, its middle on
  the aim, its radius the current range step in cells (Main.range_now:
  items' World.range_of by name, else the verb's one range once the draw
  counts), jumping outward at each step, fading in over a fifth of a
  second from the step's first show (Main.aim_fade). Client3D.aim_arc
  draws it as a ground mesh (_make_arc, 48 segments, brass_bright) placed
  at the archer's grid point and turned to the angle; the 2D view a
  Line2D through the semicircle's points.
- The marker: a small brass disc on the arc where the line from the archer
  to the mouse crosses it, at any angle (Main.aim_angle, radians on the
  grid, Vector2.angle() with x as 0, Main.aim_point), no tiles.
  Main.aim_drawn says the draw stands; pc-character turns the body from
  the pair.
- The power read, diegetic: pips in a row just past the marker, four at
  the shortest step down to one at the longest (Main.aim_pips from the
  verb's "range_steps" by name; none when the steps are not known), no
  number, no bar.
- Release: the "loose" command carries {"angle": radians, "at": the arc's
  cell} (Main.loose_args): items' new try_loose reads the angle, today's
  reads "at" (the marker's cell is what the aim lands on), so either side
  lands first and the wire changes nothing from ui; before draw_min it
  cancels as before. The hit outline (475) stays on the first body the
  shot would cross to the arc's cell.
- --test-show=aim: the host puts a bow in the right hand and arrows in the
  left, draws with the aim fixed down the screen, for the shot
  docs/ui/shots/combat/aim_arc.jpg: the arc round the archer at the full
  draw's step, the marker and pips on it, "bow drawn" on the HUD. (The
  sample's origin comes from the player's tile: the body's 2D position is
  not yet placed when the state runs, so the first samples aimed at the
  map's corner and put the arc's middle above the frame. The mesh now
  carries the angle itself, the marker's own arithmetic, so the band and
  the marker can never disagree; a difference of the shot against the same
  scene without an arc shows the band on the marker's side, where a road's
  edge in the scene had read to the eye as a ring over the top.) The
  marker and pips were enlarged for the camera's height.

  orders the swing (World.order_swing). When it is due, World.stand_target
  names who stands that way within reach (the cell beside, a spear's
  further along; never its keeper's own companion) and that one takes an
  ordinary blow (a heavy weapon's wind-up, 392); nobody: a swing at the
  air. A friend there is struck, as Shift did before; from afar nobody is
  walked to. The WASD scheme's click-a-direction swing ("dir") goes the
  same way, so a crate or anyone beside it now takes a WASD swing.
- Ctrl and a left click (Keys "signature"): the held weapon's signature
  move (World.signature_of): "bash" with a shield that bashes in the left
  hand (379), else the right hand's verb "signature" (none yet; the bow's
  heavy shot, the spear's charge later, items' data). "signature" {at};
  the server orders it on the body beside it that way
  (World.order_signature, Order.SIGNATURE): out of reach it is dropped,
  never walked to. 379's bash on the left button with the shield raised is
  gone: a plain click with the shield up is a blow.
- The right button with a shield raised sends the cursor's point
  ("stance" {kind, at}) and the bearer turns to it: the shield's arc is
  aimed by the cursor. The bow's right button is untouched (Jeff,
  2026-10-22: the draw moves to the left button in pc-character's archery
  refinement, the right becomes combat's backstep, after it lands).
- B (Keys "bandage"; builder mode moves to K): a bandage on the cursor
  from the kit carried (Main._cursor_item {kind, slot}); a left click on
  yourself or an ally sends "apply_item" {slot, target} (the server: the
  slot's thing used to "bandage", then try_bandage, or the return on the
  downed, as E's hold); any other click, B again, the right button or Esc
  puts it back, and no click with it on attacks or walks. E held still
  bandages, until Jeff has played a cut with B. The cursor's look is ui's.
- Wire: PROTOCOL_REVISION 31.

## 597. Combat step 2: swings cost stamina, and being winded

Jeff's combat design (588): "swings cost stamina; larger weapons drain
faster" and "rapid repeated swings ... must deplete stamina" [decided]; the
rest [proposed]. combat's design (C:/dev/review/combat/step2_stamina.md),
approved by the coordinator 2026-10-22, its numbers drafts for Jeff (his
folder has the table and the about 30% a fight). Until now a blow cost
nothing (the audit: every bout ended at 100).

- levels/combat.json, combat's rules file, read at start like physics'
  (World.load_combat_rules; a key unknown or not a number at least 0 kept
  and warned): swing_base 3, swing_per_kg 2, ref_mass 70, whiff_scale
  1.25, recover_at 25, winded_move_scale 1.5, winded_blow_scale 0.5,
  winded_regen_delay 20.
- World.swing_cost(entity, whiff): ceil(swing_base + swing_per_kg x the
  weight of what it strikes with (wielded; fists 0) x ref_mass / its own
  mass (base_mass, without what it carries)), whiff_scale times it for a
  swing that strikes nobody. An 80 kg player: fists 3, sword 6, giant axe
  12; a 50 kg build 17 for the axe, a 90 kg one 11.
- Paid (_pay_swing, never below 0) by a blow in _try_hit (after its push
  is weighed, so a blow pushes by the stamina it had; push_force already
  scales by it, 592), by a swing at the air (try_swing, a whiff, and an
  exertion now), and by a wind-up as it begins (try_wind_up; its blow and
  its swing at the air are not paid again; given up, not refunded). Once
  per swing: the giant axe's arc is one swing. Shoves, guards and the bash
  keep their own costs.
- Who pays: GridEntity.pays_swings, true for players and companions; a
  monster by its kind's row "swing_stamina", false for every kind until
  enemy-ai's design (their AI must know to back off winded).
- Winded (GridEntity.winded, replicated): set in _regen_stamina when one who
  pays has 0 stamina, cleared once back at recover_at. Steps take
  winded_move_scale times the ticks (step_ticks; client prediction agrees),
  blows winded_blow_scale of their damage (at least 1), no bash
  (bash_ready; the signature), regen waits winded_regen_delay ticks;
  pushed as half its mass, as an exhausted body already was. Its look is
  pc-character's (stance, breath, the slower walk), the HUD's word ui's.
- The push fades by stamina in one place, physics' push_force
  (stamina_fraction, as a shove's always has): at 25 of 100 a blow pushes
  at a quarter, so winded_blow_scale takes nothing more off the force
  (agreed with physics, 2026-10-22).
- Wire: "winded" in GridEntity.REPLICATED, under PROTOCOL_REVISION 31.

tests/combat_test (no port: World stepped by hand): the rules file, the
cost table, paid on a blow, a whiff and a wind-up, whiffs till winded,
half damage, 1.5 times the step, no bash, the 20-tick wait, back at 25, a
monster's switch. No new class_name.

Accepted by Jeff 2026-10-23: the numbers in levels/combat.json (the swing
cost formula, whiff 1.25x, winded at 0 until 25, the 20-tick winded wait,
the rest as live since v0.1.165) stand as decided, no longer drafts.


## 580. The barrow in layers: the town's tombs, the Ossuary, the dark below and the Hall of Fallen Souls

Jeff after v0.1.163: "crypt is still too cramped.. its okay if its not
realistic, make the first room a large room with a burial table, slots in
the walls with ancient skeletons, these don't need to be animated. there
would be a hidden door that leads to deeper much larger structures... at
least 2-3 layers down.. its ancient and mysterious not built by the town,
the grave robbers are on the first layer, the undead on the second, and
finally the draugr has his own boss room that is large with room to
maneuver and use strategic positioning"; his answers to lore (the top floor
the newer dead, the wealthy's, rooms off the altar room; the ancient dead
moved to the second layer, the Ossuary; the oldest dead moved to a third,
damp and dark, too moist to light lamps, angry and animated by the draugr;
his hall the Hall of Fallen Souls, a castle hall with a round table, pillars,
broken tables, the hidden exit behind the throne, filled with ghostly
warriors; the plunder the robbers', not the town's); and his width rule
("halls need to be at least 2 tiles wider than the walls, this is because
otherwise all you see is wall... the gameplay is the top priority").
Dungeon led the design (C:\dev\review\dungeon\barrow_layers_design.md),
the coordinator approved it and the rework on his answers; realism gives
way to play. Sides: maps', art-kit's (the pieces, 2b9066b2), enemy-ai's
(the foes by layer, the rest by zone), lore's, npc's, terrain's and
environment's (the dark level's light), economy's (the robbers' gold).
This is dungeon's side, step 1: the levels.

- Three levels, one place: `barrow` (layer 1, 80 x 60: the first hall under
  the mound with the burial table and 14 niches, the altar room with its
  guards and Pip's niche, the robbers' camp with the Runner's pack, the
  town's tombs between), `barrow_deep` (layer 2, 100 x 80, the Ossuary: the
  ancient dead's tombs and graves, 6 skeletons), `barrow_lair` (layer 3,
  100 x 80, the dark caverns of the oldest dead with the Hall of Fallen
  Souls kept whole as the anchor `lair`: pillars, the round table, the
  dais with the draugr on his throne, the temple's sealed shortcut ending
  behind it). Each regenerates on its own every 3 days (465); stairs link
  them (links to "from_above", back to "from_below"); the wilds' shortcut
  link's `to_map` is `barrow_lair`. The old 72 x 60 barrow goes; a player
  saved in it lands on the nearest free floor of the new one.
- The barrow style's knobs (labyrinth.gd): `"layer"` 1 lays every room
  shallow (the town's chambers with doors and torches), 2 the tombs by
  depth as before, 3 every room deep (caverns, crooked ways, no doors, no
  torches); `"ways"` 3 or 5, the brush's reach, carved ring by ring so a
  cell is carved only beside one already floor nearer in (a wider brush
  left two cells cut off behind a tomb's ring in a test generation); a
  shallow tomb's ring grows with the brush, so its one door cell still
  leads in. Regen lists no graves and no niches for layer 1 (no dead walk
  it). Widths settled: five clear cells on every layer and rooms 8 x 7 to
  16 x 12 (terrain: a wall is 0.5 m thick, 3 m tall, and hides about 2.5
  cells behind it across the view at the camera's pitch; a game shot down a
  way checks it, and a near-wall lowering in levels is terrain's design if
  it still reads as wall).
- `tools/plan_sheet`: the three samples are the templates' twins
  (`sample_barrow`, `sample_barrow_deep`, `sample_barrow_lair`; the real
  levels are written from them); `--level=` draws a level that does not
  regenerate as it stands, its own "anchors" outlined.
- The templates carry what the other sides read: `"respawn_s"` by level
  (robbers 300 and guards 600 on `barrow`, skeletons 600 below),
  `"stills": ["barrow_deep", "barrow"]` on `barrow_lair` (the altar's guards
  are dead too) and its `"dead": {"temper": "bold", "sees_in_dark": true,
  "graves": false}` for the oldest dead (enemy-ai's reading: they hold
  nothing back, see the living by life not light, and lie in no grave), its
  `"damp": true` with `"ambient"` 0.03 (the coordinator's ruling on terrain's
  key: no flame burns well there, lanterns reach half as far, the look near
  black; environment's sim and terrain's look), the
  `lair` anchor in its regenerate block (Monster.room_of), `"grave_goods":
  true` on all three.
- Steps to come, each a landing: the hidden door (a `hidden` link, the
  zone's `found`, the niche's lines, the crack's marker, the "map"
  message's `found`: a revision line), the halls dressed (the table and
  pillars as building kinds, the dais raised, the niche variants), then
  enemy-ai's foes by layer and the ghost warriors, the dark level's light,
  lore's rows, npc's pack level, economy's robbers' gold, maps' pauper's
  graves; shots of each, then the box by `regenerate now` for the three.
