## 573 amended. The draugr's hall as a puzzle: the shut door, his two lines, the gold, the Draugr's Totem

Jeff (2026-10-22, his words through the coordinator): "I don't want the
draugr to explain everything in one sentence. Make it somewhat of a puzzle
to figure out. The door closes when you enter. "Why have you entered my
Hall, "name"?" after a pause, he says, "Return the gold your people stole
from this place, when you do that you may leave". Depending on how much
gold you turn in you get a different result, for < 20 gold, he attacks and
if you kill him the door opens and he says "...warrior, you have my
respect." if you turn in the right amounts of gold you get resurrection
tokens. He says "...you have honored the pact, I shall give you the power
to cheat death" the first time you kill him you get a Draugr's Totem that
holds the charges and the item explains "carrying this totem allows you to
recieve another chance to fight"." Dungeon led the design (the coordinator
approved it as written); sides: enemy-ai's (his behaviour and lines, the
`hall_door` signal), items' (the totem), companions' (the return reads it),
economy's (the helper), lore's (the lines verbatim, "receive" spelt right).
This is dungeon's side.

- The door: the Hall of Fallen Souls' one door (580, a door edge in the
  hall's north wall) shuts and locks behind the first player into his lair
  while he sits: the draugr's `hall_door(false)` reaches
  Main._hold_hall_door, which finds the door edges on the "lair" anchor's
  rim (_hall_doors) and holds each (World.hold_door: closed, the lock
  HALL_LOCK "draugr_hall" that no key opens, so it rattles and no walk goes
  through; stone, so no blow breaks it), either way, so others outside are
  kept out too (the blessed still come and go by the sealed shortcut behind
  the throne, the one way the heal rule fires mid-fight). `hall_door(true)`
  lets go (the lock lifted, the door shut till opened): a pact won, an
  unpaid fall, a fight lost. A player who pays nothing and will not fight
  has no way out but gold, his death or their own (the temple return): the
  puzzle's teeth. "The hall's door shuts behind you." / "The hall's door
  opens." to the party; E on a held door says "The door is shut." A restart
  spawns the doors afresh, unlocked (the pact was forfeit anyway, 548).
- The totem (items' shape): the charges live on the Draugr's Totem, an
  item bound to its player, never traded, dropped, sold or lost on death,
  minted at the first pact won (World.mint_totem), every win adding the
  deal's charges up to the capacity (World.totem_add; record.barrow keeps
  "best" and "containers", so Economy.barrow_capacity derives it as
  before, and drops "tokens"); the win line is Jeff's; Main.barrow_won
  mints and adds, _sync_charges and charges_in_zone read the totem
  (World.totem_charges of World.totem_of); the field return reads it
  (companions': _uses_left and the spend read the totem, carried here so
  main never has two sources; Main.migrate_totem runs on every join).
  Economy.barrow_migrated reads the new shape (best and containers with
  no count) as 573's own, keeping a saved count for the join's migration;
  it took a record without "tokens" for the old form. The look of a held
  door is the Door's own replicated lock.

## 601. Gold from humanoid enemies

Jeff: "one feature i really want before the cut is gold drop from
humanoid enemies". When a humanoid enemy dies it leaves a few coins where
it falls, through the coin purse every player already picks up and opens
into gold. There's no new pickup.
- A monster row's "purse": [least, most], whole gold (Monster.kinds, read
  by Monster._purse; [0, 0] when absent or wrong). Monster.remains rolls
  it with the rest of its drops (seeded by its name and the tick) and
  mints one coin_purse holding that much: ItemBook.set_gold, the
  instance's own gold, saved. It's minted, a small leak into economy's
  loop, so the numbers stay low. Grave goods mark it as any drop (555).
- ItemBook.gold_of / set_gold; yields_of gives the instance's own gold in
  place of the catalog's 10, so banking it and opening it (World.try_use
  "purse") both pay what it holds. Its note says "N gold". A shop won't
  buy a purse with gold of its own ("open the purse: it is gold
  already"), so a 2-gold purse can't be sold at a full purse's price.

  goblin) [1, 3], sneak (the kobold) [1, 3], brute (the orc) [4, 10]. None
  for animals, the undead, or the robber (economy's band purse already
  drops his share). A bandit, chief or captain row, when it comes, takes
  the same key (enemy-ai's draft for a captain: [8, 20]).

gold, banked and opened for that, kept through a save; a wolf's leaves
none. No protocol change: the purse travels as any ground thing, and its
gold is server-side (the note text rides the slot notes as ever). No new
class_name.

  spine_03, would cut into the legs.
- "=part" weights it so but keeps it its own mesh: the ghost's shroud, whose shadow the client
  turns off per mesh.
- "x1.2" scales the reference for the draugr.
- Each .glb is in its slot folder, imported through the UAL bone map. No clips are baked in; the
  human library plays through ual.tres.

**Drawn (Client3D.MODELS).**
- "skeleton" and "skeleton_guard" use the slot's two variants, with the human gaits and sockets.
- "draugr" uses `DRAUGR_SCALE` 1.2, with his gaits and sockets scaled to match.
- "ghost" is in ahead of enemy-ai's kind.
- All play `DEAD_FIDGETS`: a look round, a shift, a look back; no drinking or talking.
- Any surface in the `GHOST_MATERIAL` ("ghost") casts no shadow (the coordinator's ruling); the
  bones under it keep theirs.

**The slots.** Sizes are as measured. The skeleton's depth sits between the plain (0.33 m) and
the guard (0.58 m, its shield), at a tolerance of 0.3.

## 587, enemy-ai's side. Mortally Wounded: the downed are not hunted; the draugr's pact holds through a fall

Companions' design (C:/dev/review/companions/mortally_wounded_design.md,
Jeff's down screen): every player at 0 hp lies downed, the blessed 30 s (up
to about 150 s with Slow Heart), the unblessed 10 s. 544's rules stand:

things the longer window changed, the coordinator's nod on both:

## 603, enemy-ai's side. The draugr's mind in his fight

Combat leads 603 (C:/dev/review/combat/draugr/design.md, Jeff's words: the
telegraphed 1.5 s spin that leaves him at 10% stamina, the overhead axe
throw, the charge to retrieve it, fists if it is interrupted); physics
moves the bodies; this is his choice among combat's moves (World.try_spin,
try_axe_throw, try_axe_charge; spin_targets, axe_line_hit, axe_state,
is_disarmed, boss_busy).

- `Monster._special_tick()`, a kind's own moves before its hands' in a
  fight (none in Monster); the draugr's, each fighting tick, the first that
  applies (drafts for Jeff):
  1. **Back off** at BACK_OFF_STAMINA (10) or under, till no longer winded
     (combat's 25): he steps back from his target, swings nothing; on
     starting, a wave of his dead rises to cover him.
  2. **Spin** when 2 or more foes are in the sweep (spin_targets), or 1 that
     struck him twice within STRUCK_TWICE_TICKS (3 s); not winded; at most
     every SPIN_EVERY_TICKS (6 s).
  3. **Charge** to his axe when it lies on the ground and he is not
     disarmed.
  4. **Throw** with the axe in hand, not winded, no foe beside him, his
     target THROW_NEAR to THROW_FAR (6 to 8; 4 to 8 at first) cells off and
     first on the line (axe_line_hit); at most every THROW_EVERY_TICKS
     (10 s). Never at a target closing on him: its own step nearer within
     CLOSING_TICKS (1 s), his steps toward it not counted (the coordinator,
     for the morning cut: a thrown axe always leaves a real charge to make).
     Struck on at rest after yielding, he lies at 1 hp, silent (he gave his
     respect at each beating).
  5. Else he closes and strikes as any monster; disarmed, with his fists
     (combat's).
  Nothing is chosen while a move runs (boss_busy), and nothing at all
  before combat's moves exist (World.has_method).
- **The dead in waves.** With combat's moves in, 573's retinue no longer
  rises at the pact's start: `_risen_left` rises a share at each of WAVES
  (his hp past 75%, 50%, 25%) and at each back-off, the rest at the last.
  Till then (the coordinator: the waves are one of Jeff's drafts, riding
  with the fight) they all rise at the start, as before.
- **The waves are the difficulty (603 amended; Jeff: "the waves are what
  determines the difficulty of the encounter").** Not his blow or his
  health: his row's "waves" in monsters.json, one entry a wave, `{"at":
  hp share, "count": {deal: n}, "kinds": [kinds risen in turn],
  "per_player": n more per player past the first in his lair at the
  pact's start}` (rounded). Draugr.plan_waves builds the pact's waves from
  it; DEFAULT_WAVES (and the row as landed) are today's numbers: normal's
  one at 75%, hard's at 75% and 50%, per_player 0, skeletons. The
  charges' extra dead (CHARGES_PER_RISEN, MOST_MORE_RISEN) go each to the
  wave with fewest, earliest first, which splits them as the pool did. A
  back-off raises the next wave early, and it does not come again.
  RETINUE is gone. Tuning for a party is editing the row.
- **His bound axe (603 amended; Jeff: "its magically bound to him, only
  fulfilling the pact lets you take the axe"; combat's World.axe_bound,
  recall_axe, _tend_disarmed).** Disarmed, he walks back for it
  (`_walk_for_axe`, Monster._go_to; combat's World takes it up once he is
  on or beside its cell): at once with no foe beside him, else after
  FISTS_BEFORE_AXE (3, a draft) blows of his fists, so a foe staying on him
  buys a few blows, not the fight. His fight over (`_yield`, `_end_pact`)
  he calls World.recall_axe, so it never lies bound in his hall. Both
  behind World.has_method("recall_axe").
- **Landed inert.** This side landed before combat's 602/603 (the cut
  before the fight): every choice is behind World.has_method("try_spin"),
  and monster_test `_test_draugr_mind` skips till then. Its CHANGELOG
  bullet comes with the fight.
- **The axe for the winners.** A won pact calls items' `Monster.yielded`
  (his row's "yields", the battle_axe) before the blessing; a lost pact or
  the unpaid fight never.

monster_test: the waves (10 charges, normal: none at the start, one past
75%, the other past 50%). Server only, protocol unchanged, no new

## 596: a lunge, a body moving itself down a line (physics step 2a)

Physics step 2's first part (C:/dev/review/physics/step2_design.md, the coordinator's
approval, 2026-10-22), on 592's model, for combat's shield bash (its build step 3) and the
spear's charge down a line (the doc's example move).

- World.lunge(entity, toward: Vector2, cells, {blow: {impulse, stagger}, through}) moves
  the entity up to `cells` along the line (any angle, traced as a push is), each cell a
  step of lunge_ticks_per_cell (1 tick, about twice a run), so its step_velocity and
  step_until are real and its momentum counts (592). Walls, closed doors, ledges, the map's
  edge, fire for a creature and a link's cell for anyone but a player stop it, as they stop
  a walk. A braced spear meets it as it meets a charge: _meets_brace takes `rushing`, so any
  body lunging meets one, not only a charging monster, and the brace turns the lunger's
  speed back as in 592.
- Without `through` (the shield bash): it stops at the first body met, and the blow lands
  there through apply_blow, the lunge's momentum added. A lunge of 2 with an impulse of 40
  knocks a 25 kg body 3 cells and leaves a 70 kg one where it is.
- With `through` (a charge): each body met is a collision of the whole charger at its speed
  u, as the brace reads it. The one met is pushed (592's _push) at
  (1 + restitution) m1 u / (m1 + m2) plus the blow's impulse over its mass. The charger
  goes on at (m1 - restitution m2) u / (m1 + m2) if that is lunge_min_speed (0.5) or more
  and the cell came free, else it stops there. The energy lost is shared between the two
  as impact. A player charging with a spear's 41 knocks a goblin on twice (to 4 cells off)
  and stops at its third cell; a 200 kg ogre stops it dead with neither moving, 1 impact
  each. Mass decides, with no case for an ogre.
- The lunger may step again when its lunge steps are done (next_move_tick). It is drawn
  sliding from its start over its cells' ticks. On the wire it is a tile change, which a
  client already draws over a tick a cell (up to 3): nothing new is sent, protocol
  unchanged. A player's own lunge is drawn by its client as a misprediction blended away,
  until combat's input step predicts it.
- Returns, and emits lunge_resolved, {cells, stopped_by, struck: [{body, cells, impact}],
  impact_damage}, for combat's feel and pc-character's views.
- lunge_ticks_per_cell and lunge_min_speed in levels/physics.json.

tests/physics_test: the lunge (25 kg 3 cells, 70 kg 0; a wall ends it after 2 of 4), the
charge (the goblin twice, the ogre).

## 598: a launched body (physics step 2b)

Physics step 2's second part (step2_design.md, the coordinator's approval, 2026-10-22), on
592's model, for the staff's grab and throw (combat's build step 5) and the heavy shot.

- World.launch(by, body, toward: Vector2, impulse, stagger := -1) throws `body` along the
  line (any angle) at impulse / pushed_mass, through 592's _push, with `by` as the mover:
  it slides, and meets walls, bodies (a collision by mass) and drops as any push does. It is
  a throw, not a blow, so it is not held to knockback_min_force. An impulse of 100 throws
  25 kg 6 cells and 70 kg 2.
- Aimed back past `by` from beside it, the body goes over its head and lands behind, then
  slides on: _push's toss, as today's overhead shove.
- Combat weighs the cost (the staff's mind) by mass_of and decides when; physics only
  moves. The heavy shot is combat's call to launch what an arrow hits. Existing archery
  (World.shoot) is untouched, per the combat doc's rule. A pin is a body stopped against a
  wall with speed left; the stun already follows that speed, with no pin case.
- Returns apply_blow's result and emits launched(by, body, result). apply_blow and launch
  share _slide_result and _fill_slide.
- On the wire it is a push: the push event and the tile change, as 592 sends. Protocol
  unchanged.

tests/physics_test: 25 and 70 kg (6, 2), a goblin thrown into a goblin, a body thrown back
over its thrower (4 cells, 2 of them overhead), nobody throws itself.

## 604: a rush, a charge spread over time (the draugr fight, physics' half)

Jeff's draugr boss fight (combat-f6 leads; C:/dev/review/physics/draugr_physics.md, agreed
with combat; the coordinator put it on the prototype's path, 2026-10-22). His charge to the
fallen axe must be stoppable on the way, and 596's lunge resolves at once, in one tick. So
World.rush(entity, toward: Vector2, cells, {through, blow, to}) is the lunge spread over
time.

- From the next tick on (World._tend_rushes, in the zone's step before the act phase, in id
  order), it takes one cell each lunge_ticks_per_cell / u, through the same one-cell step as
  596 (_lunge_cell: the same stops, the same collisions through bodies, a braced spear), and
  is drawn a cell at a time. u is its speed, starting at 1. A rushing body does not walk or
  strike on its own (next_move_tick held to its next cell). World.rushing(entity) says if it
  is.
- One rule by mass stops it. Every hit on it (a blow or a shove through _resolve_hits, even
  one under knockback_min_force; apply_blow; launch) changes u by the hit's speed along the
  rush (impulse over its mass). The part behind it adds nothing, as 592 drops it. A slowed
  rush moves slower. It ends when u is rush_stop_speed (0.1: a charge this slow is no
  charge) or less ("blow").
- Its other ends: a push that moves it ("knocked", off its line); a braced spear ("brace",
  592's turned momentum); a body it cannot go on through, by 596's collision ("body"); the
  terrain ("wall"); a stun ("stunned"); its cell (`to`) reached, or its cells run
  ("arrived"). Each end emits rush_ended(entity, reason, at, result). Every reason but
  "arrived" is the interruption that disarms the draugr, which is combat's and enemy-ai's to
  apply.
- Numbers for the draugr, 120 kg at speed 1 (combat's asks):
  - A player's sword from the front takes 0.34, then 0.32, then 0.30 (each swing spends
    stamina, 597, and the push fades with it): three hits stop him.
  - A hammer (1.04) stops him dead in one, without knocking him back.
  - Nothing from behind stops him.
  - One player standing in his line is shoved a cell (1.2 x 120 / 200), and the rush goes on
    at 0.52, meets them again too slow to move them, and ends ("body").
- 596's lunge now runs through the same _lunge_begin / _lunge_cell / _lunge_finish; its
  behaviour is as before (its tests unchanged).
- rush_stop_speed in levels/physics.json. Server sim only: a rush is a tile change a cell at
  a time, as a walk is. Protocol unchanged.

tests/physics_test: arrived at its cell in 5 ticks; three swords from the front; a hammer
once; four swords from behind, nothing; a blow from the side, knocked; one player in its
line; a wall; a stun; a braced spear.

## 605: a sweep through a cone (the draugr fight, physics' half)

The great axe's sweep (draugr_physics.md, agreed with combat). World.sweep(source, toward:
Vector2, arc_degrees, cells, {impulse, stagger}): every body within `cells` of the source
whose angle off `toward` is within half the arc, and that a swing reaches (_sweep_reaches:
each step of the straight line to it open, can_melee, bodies aside), takes 592's apply_blow
along its own line from the source, so the push fans out.

- The bodies are taken as they stand when it starts, and struck from one edge of the cone to
  the other. One knocked out of the cone by an earlier push is passed over. Returns, and
  emits swept, each struck body's {body, result}.
- World.swing_impulse(wielder, item) = blow_impulse at the item's verb + its weight x
  swing_speed (20, physics.json): a weapon's own mass swung. The draugr (120 kg, strength 6)
  with items' 7 kg battle axe: 6 x 127 x 0.05 + 140 = 178, so an 80 kg player is knocked
  3 cells. (2 x blow_impulse, 76, would move a player nothing: combat's first draft.) Combat
  pushes first and knocks down after (a body down counts as half its mass).
- Server sim only: pushes on the wire as 592's. Protocol unchanged.

tests/physics_test: a 90 degree, 2-cell cone at 178 on 80, 70 and 40 kg (3 cells east,
3 south-east at the edge, 6 along (2, -1)) and one behind untouched; no sweep through a wall;
a giant axe's swing_impulse 142.5.

## 606: a thing thrown down a line (the draugr fight, physics' half; step 2c's first part)

The draugr's overhead throw of his axe (draugr_physics.md, agreed with combat).
World.hurl(by, slot, toward: Vector2, cells, speed): the thing in `by`'s hand leaves it and
flies along the line (any angle, traced a cell at a time), at most `cells`. A wall, a closed
door or higher ground stops it before.

- The first body on the line is launched (598) along it at the thing's weight x speed, and
  takes impact by 592's rule. A 5 kg axe at 20 knocks an 80 kg player 1 cell; a 3 kg hammer
  at 20 knocks a 25 kg body 3. The hit's damage is combat's.
- The thing lands at that body's feet (the cell it was struck on), else where its flight
  ended, on dry ground (put_on_ground, spilling if full), noted thrown in its history and
  heard as a thud, for anyone to pick up: the axe the draugr charges back to (604).
- Any body that holds_in_hands may throw, a wielding monster too. take_item's slot-clearing
  is now _take_out, which hurl calls after its own rules.
- The views are told the flight: GridEntity.hurled(item_id, to), a new RPC (_net_hurled) to
  the body's viewers, drawn with the thing's art by the views. A line under
  PROTOCOL_REVISION 31 in net.gd (31 still unreleased; the fight rides v0.1.165).
- Returns, and World emits hurled(by, item_id, to, hit), {landed, hit, hit_result}.
- try_throw (the pack's throw) is unchanged here; making it a hurl, so every thrown thing
  moves what it hits, is the rest of step 2c, later.

tests/physics_test: a hammer launching 25 kg 3 cells and lying at its feet, with the views
told; landing at the line's end; stopped by a wall; a monster throwing its axe at a player.
## 602. The ground telegraph: a danger area shown before its blow, the same cells it strikes

Jeff (2026-10-22, the draugr): "a small red cone on the ground indicates the
area" and, for the throw, "a longer narrow cone". combat's draugr design
(C:/dev/review/combat/draugr/design.md, section 1), approved by the
coordinator: designed once, for every boss.

- Telegraph (sim/telegraph.gd, a new class_name): a shape is {kind: "cone"
  | "line" | "ring", origin: [x, y], facing: [x, y] (any angle), length:
  cells, half_angle: degrees, width: cells, inner: cells}; Telegraph.cells
  is its cells by geometry (a cone or ring: cell centres within length +
  0.25, a cone within half_angle of the facing; a line: sampled every half
  cell along the facing, width lanes across), never the origin's own;
  Telegraph.cone and Telegraph.line build them; valid() refuses a shape that
  does not read.
- World.telegraph_cells(shape): those cells on this ground: floor only, and
  nothing stopping sight between the origin and the cell (a wall, a closed
  door: _sight_crosses_edge); a line ends at its first such cell. **The one
  function both the drawing and the blow read**: what is seen is what hits.
- World.telegraph(source, kind, shape, ticks) -> id (0 if the shape does
  not read): kept with its data {id, source (path), kind, shape, cells (the
  exact cells as [x, y]), from_tick, lands_tick, zone}, telegraph_started
  emitted. end_telegraph(id, landed): telegraph_ended (and
  telegraph_ended_in, with its zone). Its source despawned
  (_forget_jobs) or the room reset: ended, not landed. World.telegraphs():
  those showing.
- Main tells the source's zone (World.peers_in): the "telegraph" message,
  the data when shown, {id, landed} when over. A client keeps
  Main.telegraphs and emits telegraph_started / telegraph_ended for ui's
  decal (drawn from "cells", ui's side) and sound's cues. "kind" names the
  move: "spin", "throw", "charge" for the draugr (603).

## 603. The draugr's moves: the spin, the axe throw, the charge to his axe, disarmed

Jeff (2026-10-22): "the draugr will have a large battle axe that he drops as
loot, he has a telegraphed wind up spin that he stands still, winds up for
1.5 seconds thing a devestating swing, a small red cone on the ground
indicates the area, his stamina drops to 10% after that and slowly builds
back up, he might have another move thats a overhead axe throw. he winds up
and throws it, you can tell the direction he's going to throw it by a longer
narrow cone. after he throws the axe he uses charges to the axe to pick it
up, if you are able to interrupt the charge he is disarmed to only using
fists." combat's design (C:/dev/review/combat/draugr/design.md), approved by
the coordinator, with enemy-ai (his mind, which calls these) and physics
(604 rush, 605 sweep, 606 hurl). The combat side, in World, for any body
that holds a two-handed weapon. The numbers are drafts for Jeff, in
levels/combat.json "moves".

- try_spin(by): he stands. A 602 cone telegraph round his facing (spin:
  length 2, half_angle 150, so a 60 degree gap behind; fists_length 1
  disarmed) for windup 15 ticks. Needs stamina at least needs (90) and not
  winded. A stun or a knockdown, or being moved off his cell, before then
  gives it up, its telegraph ended unlanded: a shield bash's stagger does,
  a sword blow does not. Landing, every body on the telegraph's cells:
  - takes damage_scale (2.5) times his blow, its guard broken (_meet_guard
    crushing);
  - is pushed outward along its own line by apply_blow at swing_impulse
    (physics', when in; else blow_impulse + weight x weight_impulse 20),
    times impulse_scale (0.84, about 150 of physics' 178: the coordinator's
    default on Jeff's list, so a full-health player swept into a wall is
    left at a sliver, 8 + 9 of 20, the kill only on one already hurt; at
    1.0 it is 8 + 12, a kill from full);
  - is knocked down down_ticks (15).
  Then he is spent: stamina at leaves (10)% and winded (597's rules).
- try_axe_throw(by, at): costs cost (40). A 602 line telegraph toward
  [at], fixed at the start (throw: length 8, width 1), for windup 12. Then
  the weapon flies: physics' hurl (606) when in, else down the telegraph's
  cells here. The first body takes damage_scale (2.0) times his blow and is
  launched (weight x speed 14). The weapon lies at the struck body's feet,
  or the cell before it here, else at the line's end. Recorded as his
  thrown weapon (_axes).
- try_axe_charge(by): to his lying weapon. A line telegraph to its cell for
  roar (6) ticks, then physics' rush (604) through, to that cell (its
  rush_ended reason), else a cell a tick here (a refused step: "body" or
  "wall"; a stun: "stunned"). "arrived" with the weapon still there: he
  takes it up (set_slots: a monster's hands are filled that way, not by
  try_transfer's rules). Anything else, or the weapon gone from its cell
  (a player took it): disarmed (is_disarmed). No charge and no throw then;
  fists, and the fists' 1-cell spin, till enemy-ai's mind walks him back to
  it (Jeff's open line: or the rest of the fight).
- For enemy-ai: spin_targets(by), axe_line_hit(by, at), axe_state(by)
  {where: hand | ground | gone, cell, uid}, is_disarmed(by), boss_busy(by).
  _tend_boss_moves runs each tick after the wind-ups (392). A move's state
  goes with its maker (_forget_jobs).
- GridEntity.stamina_regen_every (a kind's "stamina_regen_every"): stamina
  comes back only every that many ticks. The draugr's slow breath: at 4,
  half a point a tick, about 5 s winded after the spin, full in about 20 s.
  His row also needs "swing_stamina": true and a max_stamina, enemy-ai's.
- The axe's flight for the views is physics' hurled (606). The telegraphs
  are ui's decal; the cues are sound's; the clips are pc-character's.
- No wire of its own beyond 602's and 606's (under revision 31).

## 609. Arrow impacts heard as far as a bow shoots

Jeff on v0.1.165: "arrow impact needs sounds"; the coordinator: an
impact by what the arrow meets, played where it stops, the flight's
whistle if cheap, client only. The impacts were already played
(Client3D._on_struck and _arrow_landed) but heard only within 4 to 6
cells (a body's hit within 5, the fight noise), while a bow shoots 8
(Items.VERBS ranged cells), so an archer heard nothing at range.

- Every arrow impact slot is heard 12 cells out (noise null, "range" 12):
  sfx.arrow_hit_flesh, _hit_wood, _hit_stone, sfx.arrow_land and the new
  sfx.arrow_water. These are the view's sounds, not the sim's. The sim
  still makes its own fight noise for a body struck, and monsters hear
  that at its own radius. So arrow_hit_flesh no longer names the fight
  noise, an exception to decision 269 kept to arrows: a player watches
  their own arrow land and must hear it.
- By what the arrow meets: a body, a thud; a closed door, or a tree by the
  cell past where it stopped (Client3D._trees, the forest's), a knock; a
  wall or higher ground, a crack and skitter; water, a plip
  (sfx.arrow_water, not the body-sized sfx.splash); else the ground, a
  soft thump (sfx.arrow_land's three stick-clatter takes are dropped for
  thumps).
- The whistle: sfx.arrow_flight, played at the point of the flight
  nearest the listener as the arrow passes it (Client3D._whistle), heard
  4 cells. It is not played for an arrow that starts within a cell of
  the listener (the archer; the loose has its own), nor for one that
  stops before passing the listener.
- tools/sound_take.ps1 measures a cut's peak with astats, not
  volumedetect: volumedetect reads at 16 bits, so a float source over
  full scale (freesound 789389, +12 dB) measured 0 dB, and its take kept
  the overshoot.
- The hook stays Client3D._on_shot's arrival, as before. Pc-character's
  583 flight is not on main; when it lands, its landing point is where
  these play.

## 610. A moved marker keeps its saved entity

Jeff, after v0.1.166: "i need the snagin tower to be bigger or the chests
outside for the weapons". Moving a level entity's marker broke its tie to a
saved world: decision 433 keys each saved level entity by its marker's cell
("x,y"), so a moved marker's saved entity found no slot, came back "as
saved, holding no slot", and the marker spawned a second, fresh one beside
it (a second set of free weapons in the box's world). Extending 433:
- main._level_spec_for: a saved level entity whose key the level no longer
  has adopts the marker it was moved to (_moved_marker): the nearest within
  MOVED_MARKER_REACH (2) cells either way of its old cell with the same
  script and the same slots, held by no living entity and named by nothing
  the snapshot saved (_saved_keys: its entities', records' and dead timers'
  keys, gathered before the load). It takes that slot and key and the
  marker's tile (a moved marker moves its entity; a keyed one otherwise
  comes back where it was left), its things restored onto it as ever. Past
  the reach, or with no match, it comes back as saved, holding no slot, as
  before. Held's migration (moving the town's markers) leans on it.
- The first use: the wilds' weapon chest {sword, spear, hammer, shield},
  inside Snagfin's 2 x 2 tower on its doorway's inside cell (220, 226),
  moves to (219, 226), outside against the tower's west wall beside the
  other weapon chest (219, 225); the doorway clear, both reached from open
  ground. Its entry is unchanged but "at" (items-4f); the layout's marker
  moved with it. On the box its saved chest, things and all, comes back on
  the new marker: no stray.
tests: spawn_key_test, a marker moved a cell brings its saved chest back on
it, alone; one moved three cells does not (the saved one as saved, a new one
on the marker); level_test's weapon chests by their new tile.
Server only, level data; protocol unchanged.

plan (a `found` field on the "map" message with its revision line,

- Level data: `"niches": [[x, y, dx, dy, kind, variant], ...]`, `(x, y)`
  the room's floor cell before a niche, `(dx, dy)` the step onto its wall
  edge, kind `"a"`, `"b"`, `"c"`, `"d"` (art-kit's four) or `"hidden"`,
  variant 1 or 2; `Level.niches_from` keeps one whose edge is a wall with
  rock behind it (a door with its alcove, floor, behind for the hidden one)

  generation makes inside the entrance anchor (465 keeps the rest);
  `Regen._lay_hidden` moves the link (hidden) and "from_below" with it.

## 612. The width rule: no passage one cell wide in a dungeon (dungeon's side)

Jeff, body-blocked by Pip in the barrow, 2026-10-22: "its also that the
crypt had multiple single tile corridors.. the game is a multiplayer game
with companions.. its not ideal"; and on how to build it: "dungeons need
procedural rule - whats different is just the arrangements". The
coordinator's rule: every passage at least two cells wide, so a player,
their companion and a second player pass each other; a doorway (a door
edge in a wall) the one cell allowed, never a run of single cells, the
cells either side of it two wide at once; the hall door, the hidden door
and the alcove stair link (608) stay doors.

- Where it lives: in the generator, not in levels fixed cell by cell. A
  level's template is its arrangement, the fixed rooms as its anchors
  (the barrow's first hall, altar room, Pip's niche and camp; the
  Ossuary's stair foot and stair room; the Hall of Fallen Souls and its
  stair foot) and where they sit; every passage and tomb between comes
  from the labyrinth's rules. The barrow's three levels were already so.
- The rules: the ring that narrowed a way to a shallow tomb's one door
  cell goes (the brush carves right up to the tomb's wall), and a room with
  doors is walled where a way or another room touches its border
  (`_wall_rooms`, run before and after the widening), so its doors are its
  only ways in, and a way that runs through such a room (a path cell
  inside beside one outside) gets a door there, counted among its doors;
  rooms and anchors keep two cells of rock between them (`ROOM_GAP`; one
  before), so a way squeezed between two walled rooms is two wide; dwarven
  corridors are two wide into plain rooms too; after the walling and the
  join-up, `Tools.join_all` joins every walkable part to the biggest by
  the shortest way that crosses no wall edge and enters no anchor
  (`path_through`: a room whose way failed, an alcove a wall cut off), then
  `Tools.widen` carves a cell beside every cell of a single-width run,
  across its axis, on the same side along a run where it can, rock alone,
  never the rim or an anchor's cell, into the ring outside a walled room
  only when the other side cannot be, up to six passes, and the rooms are
  walled again where it carved beside them. The caverns' crooked blind ways become two-wide stubs, no
  longer dead ends (a fair loss, the coordinator): the Ossuary's graves
  come from the tombs' alcoves, a cell deep, which the rule allows (a dead
  end nobody passes through), and the dark below lists none (its dead lie
  in no grave, 580).
- The check: `Level.narrow_runs_by` (a cell is narrow along an axis when
  neither side across it is open and a step along it is; two narrow cells
  joined along their axis are a run), `Level.narrow_runs` on a parsed
  level's terrain and `Tools.narrow_runs` on a LevelMap. labyrinth_test
  fails any generated style or layer with a run; level_test fails any
  regenerating level's template (its arrangement) with one. A run squeezed
  between two anchors cannot be widened and the test says so.
- The arrangement change: the first hall's bays, one cell each where the
  ways came in, are two rows tall (rows 9 and 10), so the niche rows are
  2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 14 and 16 and the hidden south-east niche (608) moves to
  (51, 16) with its alcove at (52, 16); terrain and art-kit told (the draw
  reads the data), enemy-ai's anchors unmoved.
- Release: the box regenerates barrow, barrow_deep and barrow_lair after
  the cut that carries it.

labyrinth_test (no run in either generation of dwarven, old, and the
barrow's three layers; the hall's floor count with the bays), level_test
(every regenerating template; the hidden niche at (51, 16)). Level data
and generator, no wire change, no new class_name.

## 611. A click on your own companion makes way

Jeff on v0.1.166, body-blocked by Pip: "with weapons LMB on companion is no
longer telling them to move and unblock". His way had been the click opening
the chat box addressed to her and typing "move"; 560 amended made a click on a
companion within reach do nothing, and in a corridor the click's walk beside
her found no cell, so nothing moved her but the bar's Talk. The coordinator's
design: a left click (or a bow's tap) on your own companion within melee reach
(World.can_melee) sends a new command "make_way" {target}; the server
(Main._make_way) checks she is the player's and in reach and calls
Companion.bumped with the direction from the player to her: the hands, no
mind asked, the bump's party-log line and its repeat guard, so a click held
or repeated is one step aside. From afar the click walks beside her as
before; where _beside finds nothing (a corridor) it walks at her tile, and the
bump swaps them. Another's companion and players: unchanged. The hook is in
Main._talk_to, not _open_talk, which also runs on arriving from afar and would
send her away as you reach her (agreed with ui, whose bow click reaches
_talk_to). Protocol revision 32 (release: on an old server the click silently
does nothing). tests: companion_test (the click yields her, logged, no mind;
out of reach, or not hers, nothing).
## 603 amended, combat's side. His own plain blow, and his breath

The coordinator, from the draugr clip's headless runs once he held his axe (the
arming fix, 8b958f55), on Jeff's draft list:

- His plain blow is a heavy strike: a monster's row may name its own verb for
  a thing it wields, "blows" (item id to a verb), read through Items.verb_from
  so it gets a catalog verb's defaults and warnings (items' ask), kept by
  Monster.read_kinds and set on the monster as Monster.blows; World.blow_verb
  takes it over the thing's own. The draugr's: battle_axe, knockback force 1.0,
  damage 1.6, speed 2.2, windup 8. The battle axe keeps its knockdown in anyone
  else's hands (a player who wins it); only his spin floors (the coordinator's
  (a); before it every plain blow knocked the player down, every 3.4 s in melee,
  from combat's own design section 2). This replaces items' interim 603
  amendment (0e32727b, v0.1.167: the axe's own verb made a plain blow for
  everyone): the battle_axe row is the knockdown again. The spin is its own move: its push
  still follows the axe's catalog verb and weight (physics' swing_impulse,
  605), not his plain blow's, on purpose (items' review).
- His breath: a row's "stamina_regen" is what each breath gives back
  (GridEntity.stamina_regen_amount; 0 keeps World.stamina_regen, 2). The
  draugr's: 8 every 7 ticks (was 2 every 4), so in a fight that goes on a second
  spin comes about a minute after the first (Jeff: "slowly builds back up").
  Measured headless, a sword player at him without a break: armed, 57 s between
  spins; disarmed (his fists cost less), 27 s. At 2 every 4 there was no second
  spin in three minutes: regen waits stamina_regen_delay after each swing, and
  his swings ate the rest.
- His axe bound to him (Jeff, answering the draft: "player can't pick up the
  axe mid fight, its magically bound to him, only fulfilling the pact lets you
  take the axe"): a thrown axe lying is World.axe_bound while its boss lives;
  try_pick_up refuses it (Main says BOUND_AXE_WORDS, "The axe will not leave
  his hall.", a draft), a monster's try_pick_up_weapon passes it over and the
  stockpile does not bank it. Not items' soulbound, which binds to a player's
  id. So the disarm is the stopped charge alone, and it lasts till he walks
  back to his axe: World._tend_disarmed arms him again once he stands on its
  cell or in reach of it, not mid anything (his mind walks him there,
  enemy-ai's). World.recall_axe(by) puts it back in his hands when his fight
  ends, won or lost (his mind calls it); the pact's prize stays his row's
  "yields" (items' Monster.yielded). Killed, he is forgotten (_forget_jobs)
  and the axe lies free as loot. On a pile, a pick-up takes the top thing not
  bound; the refusal line is said only where his axe lies alone. Known gaps
  (items' review): the bond is World's memory, so a server restart with the
  axe lying reloads it free; and the client's "F  pick up" hint still names it
  (the client does not know the bond).
- enemy-ai's side (THROW_NEAR 6, no throw at a target closing in; the walk back
  to his axe and the recall; the waves deciding the difficulty) is its own
  amendment.

combat_test _test_own_blow, _test_bound_axe; monster_test keeps "stamina_regen" and "blows";
draugr_fight_test takes his breath and blows from the row. Sim only, protocol

## 613. The sought: a town's newcomer is found, rescued and brought home (economy's side)

Jeff (2026-10-22, through the coordinator): "npcs for the town are found
in the wilds, the hills, or forest, or under the castle in the dungeons.
rescue and return to town, like the original black smith quest. black
smith could be a castle npc." The town's need spawns a person to find,
not an arrival, for every newcomer trade from now on. One number with each
tree's side under it (as 580): economy's here; maps' refuges and
place_sought, npc's body, lines and escort, enemy-ai's guards and the
follower downed but not killed, dungeon's castle cells follow. Approved by
the coordinator 2026-10-22 with npc's sight rule alone deciding when a held
one may follow (no holder_fell); Jeff may veto the specifics.

- **The need.** Every arrival (the farmer, the shepherd, the weaver, the
  woodcutter, 552's makers, and later trades through Towns._arrive) is
  sought instead of moved in once Towns.place_sought is set and rules'
  "sought" is given; unset, newcomers walk in as before (so this lands
  changing nothing in play until maps sets it).
- **The entry.** Towns._seek makes them a worker of the town at once,
  away, origin "sought" (npc's ask: their card, body and talk come free):
  no work, meals, rent or wage, not a resident, not in the room count; the
  town's record keeps sought {id: {id, name, trade, place, where, holder,
  since, next_try, freed_by}}, saved. A sought trade counts as had
  (_has_trade), so no second one is wanted.
- **Placed.** Towns._sought_turn each tick: an unplaced entry past
  next_try asks place_sought(town, trade, where_kinds, id) with the
  trade's kinds (rules' sought.where, else sought.default) less "camp";
  maps answers a refuge's place id or {place, where}, or "". Else, for
  "camp", a hostile camp whose freed go home to the town holds them as a
  captive (518's path), its fall bringing them home (note_rescue →
  sought_home). Else tried again a day on. A refuge whose where has a
  sought.guards row is held by that faction (enemy-ai stands its guards
  there, picking their kinds and count); otherwise nobody: the lost.
- **Freed, lost, home.** free_sought(id, player) when the escort starts
  (npc), out of a camp's held; sought_lost(id) back to unplaced, tried
  again after sought.restock_days (5) somewhere else; sought_home(id)
  when they reach the town: a resident at work, rescue experience,
  rescued(town, id, "sought:<place>"), what the trade brings (the
  shepherd's flock, now Towns._arrived on either path). sought_changed
  (town, id) on each change. A town that gets one of the trade another
  way (a camp's stranger) drops an entry nobody is leading home.
- **Words.** Towns.where_words(where) ("in the hills", "under the
  castle", "held at a camp") for the log and npc's officials: "word is
  Edda the farmer was seen in the hills".
- **Soak.** town_soak --rescue-after=DAYS stands a rescuer in: a stand-in
  refuge, each sought brought home DAYS after the word went out.
- economy.json "sought": where {smith: [castle_dungeon, camp], butcher:
  [hills, forest, camp], fisherman: [wilds, camp]}, default [wilds,
  forest, hills, camp], guards {castle_dungeon: {faction goblins, band: imp x3, brute x1
  (enemy-ai's pick, counts not yet confirmed)}}, restock_days 5.
  Jeff on the smith: "heard rumors of a great dwarven forge deep below -
  he brought a expedition of hired guards ... they got ambushed and he
  was captured, forced to work goblin weapons that supply the blood rot
  raids": held by the goblins at dungeon's great dwarven forge.

maps asked with the default kinds; placed, freed, lost, placed elsewhere

## 606 amended: the pack's throw is a hurl (the rest of physics step 2c)

The last push outside 592's model is retired. World.try_throw (a thing thrown from a hand
toward a cell) is now a hurl toward it, as far as throw_reach, at throw_speed (2 cells a
tick, physics.json), with two of hurl's new options:

- `lands`: "feet" (the default, the draugr's axe at the struck body's feet) or "before"
  (the cell before the body, the thrower's own if it stood beside it, as the pack's throw has
  always had it).
- `hurts`: the struck body takes impact_per_energy x 1/2 x the thing's weight x speed^2, its
  energy, at a real speed. The pack's throw sets it; a caller dealing the hit's damage itself
  (combat's axe, whose speed is a tuning multiple, not a real speed) leaves it off.

In every hurl, a struck body that is not moved still staggers by the hit's speed. The body
is launched at weight x throw_speed by mass: a 10 kg sack moves a 25 kg imp a cell and hurts
it 2; an 80 kg player is not moved (0.25), but staggered and hurt 2 (was 3 by the old rule).
The flight is hurl's line to the cell (Bresenham), not the old diagonal-first steps; a cell
in reach is landed on as before. THROW_FORCE_PER_KG, impact_per_force, mass_ratio and
impact_damage are gone. hurl's result also carries "thrown" and "impact".

tests/physics_test: the sack on 25 kg (1 cell, 2 hp, fallen at the thrower's feet) and on
80 kg beside the thrower (unmoved, staggered); items_test's and stockpile_test's throws pass
as they were.

## 607: the ground in one place (physics step 2d)

Physics step 2's last part (step2_design.md, the coordinator's approval). World.ground_drag(from,
direction) is one multiple for how hard the ground is to cross:
- uphill, Relief.pace (decision 525; a stair is not);
- times a ford's FORD_TICK_SCALE (2, wading), else tall grass standing, TALL_GRASS_TICK_SCALE
  (1.25);
- 1 on open level ground.

Both of its readers take it:
- **A walk:** step_ticks is its move_ticks, the diagonal's 1.5, winded (597) and the speed
  buff, times ground_drag. Walking is unchanged (the same factors, now in one place).
- **A slide:** 592's _push gives a pushed body slide_per_speed x its speed of ground to cross,
  and each cell spends its ground_drag of it. A slide through a ford, grass or up a slope is
  shorter, and the speed left at a wall is what the ground left it: the same shove that
  slides 40 kg 3 cells on open ground slides it 1 through a ford. An overhead toss's two cells
  are through the air, at 1 each.

Downhill and ice are no easier yet: a later step. Lunges and rushes read it too since
607 amended. Server sim only; the client's shove guess (predict_push_end) still counts open cells, a
guess corrected by the server as ever. Protocol unchanged.

tests/physics_test: the shove on open ground (3 cells) and through a ford (1), and a step into
the ford twice as long as before.
## 580, environment's side. A damp level: no flame, a short lantern

Jeff on the barrow's third layer, barrow_lair: "damp and dark, human
eyesight barely lights it up, its too moist to light lamps". The
coordinator ruled the key and the split (2026-10-22). Dungeon sets the key
on its level with a low "ambient" (about 0.03) and lays no torches.
Terrain draws the look (darker, a faint cold haze, small dim lanterns, no
flames) and lands after this.

- **The key.** level.json "damp" (true or false, default false). Read by
  Level.damp_from; a value that is not a bool is said and read as false.
  It is kept as terrain["damp"], and Fields.damp follows it. The level
  editor offers it as a checkbox ("too damp to light").
- **No flame burns.** On a damp level, Level._quench puts out its torches,
  lanterns and fire as it is read, with one warning per kind ("too damp to
  light: torches put out (n cells)"). Nothing in the game lights a torch
  or brazier during play, so the level check is the whole refusal; a
  later lighting action reads the same key.
- **A short lantern.** A carried light reaches Fields.carried_reach(damp)
  cells: CARRIED_REACH (4), or DAMP_REACH (0.5) of it when damp, which is
  2. Fields.light_at, Fields.carried_light and Senses._light read it, so
  the floor, what is lit and what a monster sees by all agree. Terrain's
  view scales its lantern by the same function. The lantern is still lit
  and still toggled with L.
- **Untouched:** the eyes (with an ambient under GLIMPSE, beyond a
  lantern's pool nothing is seen, which is Jeff's "barely"), carried heat,
  and the res-charge window (the channel is beside the body).

tests/day_night_test _test_damp: a dry level keeps its torch, lantern and
fire; a damp one puts them out and says so; a non-bool "damp" is said; the
reach is 4 and 2; a lantern's light three cells off is there when dry and
none when damp, one cell off lit. docs/levels.md. Sim and level parse,
protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 585. Ledges as curves

Jeff: "terrain needs to have smooth edges for ledges as and terraces as
well. it should not conform to tiles either. see stream examples". So
cliffs follow the curves rule (559) as water and roads do: a ledge is a
smooth line, the faces and rims drawn along it (585, terrain's side); the
sim's cliffs stay on the cells' edges (cliff_between rules the walk), and
the line keeps to them. Approved by the coordinator with terrain, refined to
one tracer for every ledge.
- level.json "ledges": [{points: [[x, y, top, foot], ...], up: "left" |
  "right", closed}]: control points in cell units, the ground's height
  above (top) and below (foot) at each, equal where a face tapers into a
  walk; "up" the high side of the way the points run (y down: walking
  east, south is right); closed for a mesa's or a pit's rim.
  Curves.parse_ledges samples each once (Curves.sample, raw: tops and feet
  eased along it); terrain["ledges"] = [{curve: {points, tangents, tops,
  feet, length}, up, closed}]. Level says where a ledge's steep points have
  no cliff across them in the relief (more than a quarter of them).
- Curves.trace_ledges makes them from the relief, for every level alike:
  - every cliff edge between two walkable or wet cells (a bank, water one
    side only, is the shore's and left; a fall's, water both sides, kept)
    chained along the cells' edges, cut where its high side changes;
  - each line's edge middles thinned by Douglas-Peucker to LEDGE_TOLERANCE
    (0.25 cells), keeping the faces' first and last edges, a middle on
    water (a fall's point), and any point whose drop its kept neighbours
    would not ease to within LEDGE_DROP_TOLERANCE (0.25 m);
  - a line ending where the drop comes under the walk runs on to its end
    corner with top = foot (the face tapering into the slope); lines
    meeting at a corner end on it, the same point; a loop is closed.
  Level.ledges_of(terrain) runs it over a parsed level. make_hills and
  make_wilds_marks write the ledges after laying; tools/trace_ledges.tscn
  writes a hand-made level's (the sample's outcrop); MapDoc.save writes
  them again whenever the relief changed, so the editor's height brush and
  stairs keep them in step.
- Relief.lay's faces leave the cells' lines: an escarpment's face follows a
  smooth curve through its line (Curves.sample), wandering "wander" cells
  either way of it over "wave" (WANDER_WAVE, 18) cells; a plateau's faced
  sides wander in and out of its rect the same way, eased to nothing over
  WANDER_EASE (8) cells toward a corner they share with a walkable side
  (its spur meets the face as it did) and near its "still" cells (a fall's
  lip: the fall lands below its line, its pool whole); the ground the face
  wanders over is held as its foot. "wander_seed" picks another wander.
  No wander unless asked (WANDER 0), so a face laid on a line stays there.
  A cell of land left with no walkable neighbour (a step jutting out
  alone) takes its nearest neighbour's height; one beside water is a bank
  and left.
- The rule (the coordinator: "what reads as a slope must be climbable"):
  no cliff step lower than FACE_LEAST (1 m), a face's edge or not. The
  views' shared corners draw such a step as a slope, so the walk takes it.
  Relief.soften_low_steps ends Relief.lay and runs again at the end of a
  level tool that moves the ground after laying (make_hills,
  make_wilds_marks): the step's high side lowered to the walk over its low
  side, or, beside water (a bank may stand higher than its water, never
  lower), its low side raised. A future lay keeps it.
- Laid again: the hills (the two escarpments and the plateau's west face
  wander 1.5 cells; make_hills' ford keeps the plateau's foot as laid in
  place of its one face column), the wilds' ridge (1.5 cells; the same
  places, pads and marks), the sample's outcrop traced as painted.
- tests: level_test, every level's ledges are its relief's (traced again,
  the same) and within LEDGE_BOUND (0.45 cells, terrain's bound) of its
  cliff edges both ways; the hills' rim found on its row; relief_test, the
  plateau's face over the columns it wanders across.
  view_test: a cliff step whose drawn corners agree (no drawn step) is
  counted apart as flattened, and none is allowed (the rule above);
  relief_test: soften_low_steps lowers a 0.7 m step, raises beside water.
PROTOCOL_REVISION 32 (v0.1.166 shipped 31): the level data the views draw from,
and the hills' and the wilds' relief, differ; a full cut. The wilds' ridge
face moves by up to 1.5 cells: a player saved on a cell that is now a cliff
step comes back on it as ground (nothing saved is keyed to a face).

## 595. Built water drawn square

Jeff's curve rule ("rivers, streams, roads and shorelines are drawn as
smooth curves... never cell regions with rounded edges") is for natural
water: its shorelines are natural ones. Every shipped level's natural water
is a "waters" curve (559 and maps', with the castle's ponds and the
sample's pool and stream traced in 568 amended). What no curve lays is
built: a well's cell (the wilds' farmstead and town wells), a basin, a
cistern. 553's cell path drew those with rounded corners, a noisy edge and
foam: the cell region with rounded edges the rule bans. Drawn as built.

- Client3D._built_water: water with no curve near it (within a curve's
  reach, so a bank cell the level lays beside a curve's own stays natural),
  not a ford, a bridge's or a stream's path; computed after the curves are
  read, each build. No level data, no protocol line.
- Its body (_build_water) covers its own cells alone, not the land round
  them: its edge is its cells' edge, crisp. Its material's "built"
  (water.gdshader): no shore field (left out of shore_image, so no foam or
  wet ground round it), an even depth, still (ripples a third as deep, no
  churn).
- On relief the shore band takes built water as land, so the ground round
  a well does not dip to it.
- 553 stays for natural water drawn without a curve only as the fallback
  of a level with none (tests); maps' level_test (568 amended) fails a
  level whose curveless water is neither under a building nor clear of
  natural ground (grass, dirt, sand) round it.

view_test _test_built_water: the wilds' wells built, each body over its own
cells, no shore field round them; the hills' water all natural.
_test_shore skips built water. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

## 585, terrain's side: ledges drawn along their curves

Jeff (2026-10-22): "terrain needs to have smooth edges for ledges and
terraces as well. it should not conform to tiles either. see stream
examples". maps' 585 traces every ledge from the relief's cliff edges into
terrain["ledges"] (curves sampled with tops and feet, "up", shared ends,
taper points, a point at each fall), within 0.45 of the cliff edges
(level_test checks both ways); cliff steps under 1 m are softened (the
coordinator's ruling: what reads as a slope is climbable). This draws
them. The sim's walk keeps the cells' cliffs (cliff_between).

- _read_ledges: each ledge's curve and a nearest-sample map, as the
  waters' (_stamp_near); _ledge_near: how far past the curve on its high
  side (negative on its low side), which ledge, where along it.
- The cells a curve crosses are split along it (_plan_ledge_splits): the
  square cut by the curve's high side (a polygon from its run through the
  cell), each part labelled by a point inside it (a sharp turn can fold
  the polygon; past an open end the cell's own ground holds). Each part is
  drawn at its side's ground (_ledge_cell): its own cell's corners' plane,
  or the plane of the cell across the curve carried on to it, so the high
  ground ends on the curve at the face's top and the low ground runs to
  its foot. A square corner is keyed as the whole cells' are, joining them.
- The faces (_add_ledge_faces) run along the curve's samples, from the
  high side's ground down to the low side's, facing the low side, faceted
  and coloured as cliffs are (_cliff_strip), under the cliffs' material:
  the sight cut-out (549) and the night darkening as before. Nothing where
  the two grounds meet (a taper's end).
- A cell edge's own face is left to a ledge (_ledge_covers) only where the
  curve runs along it (within half a cell of its middle) and drops there
  at least half the edge's drop: a bank (water on one side, which the
  ledges leave out) and a taper's end keep their cell faces. (The first
  shots showed a bank by the fall's lip with neither face: bare dirt.)
- The scatter leaves a split cell's other side alone.
- 556's caps (withdrawn) are not back: the curve is the level's data.

Shots in C:/dev/review/ledges585 (the hills' plateau faces, the fall's
lip, the escarpments, the wilds' ridge; before is the withdrawal with
cell-edge faces). view_test _test_ledge_curves (hills, wilds): every split
cell's parts fill it, each on its own side; the faces' top on the high
ground and foot on the low; cell edges left to the curves. map_bench,

## 616. Plain orders, read with no model (the hands' reader)

Jeff (the Dire play test; his "wow" moments were Nix bandaging when told and
carrying gear): "reliable plain-language commands for the core verbs
(bandage, carry, wait, rest, take the lead) come before combat polish". Until
now a line reached her acts only through the model: her voice's reply
carried a stance or [DO: n], so a slow or wrong model meant no act, or a
reply saying "I'll wait" while she followed.

Companion.order_in reads her player's own line (regular expressions, lower
case, a negation ahead of the verb voiding it) for six orders: bandage (me,
yourself, or unsaid: her player if hurt, else herself), carry (a thing her
player holds, named; "carry this" unnamed and she asks which) and give it
back, rest, follow, wait. Companion.obey does it on the same tick: wait and
rest set HOLD and a standing order (Companion.order) that calm does not undo,
past the instruction's 600 ticks, till "follow" or another order; follow sets
STAY_CLOSE; bandage and carry start errands (carry is the new "take": she
goes to her player, who hands it over). Her voice is still asked, told as
narration what she is doing, but as for a quick phrase its stance and [DO]
are not taken, so a reply never undoes the order. A voice quiet past
ORDER_ACK_TICKS (4 s) is covered by a word of her own (ORDER_ACKS). Lines the
reader does not take go to the model as before.

Resting (Intent.REST): out of a fight she stays and mends an hp every
REST_HEAL_TICKS (2 s), and gets up when whole, when a fight starts, or when
her player goes past REST_LEAVE (8); asked in a fight she says she will rest
after it. Take the lead stays 551's (Main._guide_said, read before her);
Guide.ASK also reads "you lead", "take the lead", "lead us"; asked with no
place, she leads to the nearest place she knows in her area
(Main._nearest_known), with "to" and an unknown place, as before, she says
she doesn't know the way.

Tier gates (wary refusing risky orders, devoted leading anywhere) wait on
Jeff's tier answer. tests: companion_test _test_plain_orders: ten phrasings
of each verb read (60), five near-misses each that are no order (30), and each
phrasing through the chat doing its act on the tick (wait holds past the
instruction's time; follow calls her on; rest mends and gets up whole;
bandage the one meant; carry takes the dagger, and gives it back); a voice
that never answers covered by her word; a voice answering PRESS to "wait
here" leaves her waiting. Lines in older tests that are now orders were
reworded to keep testing the model's path. Server only, protocol unchanged,
no new class_name.
## 586. Snagfin is the only fence, and only by night

Jeff, through the coordinator: "Snagfin could be the only fence, he will
buy stolen and grave goods, no one else wants them, he has a little larger
place on the outskirts of town, he might only do that at night ... he
sells overpriced goods during the day and wont buy stolen goods unless its
night time and at a fenced goods discount". This replaces 560's ruling
that any counter's merchant fences at half. Economy leads; npc, ui and
maps/builder have sides.

- **The fence:** economy.json "fence" {by: "snagfin", factor 0.5,
  day_markup 1.3}. Economy.fence_by() is the settled resident by, while
  he is in his town and not away; "" otherwise.
- **His counter:** World.fence_state(shop). It is the shop counter of
  his town nearest his home (residents.json settled "home"), so it
  follows him if maps moves his place to the outskirts.
  - Economy.FENCE_NIGHT while it is dark under the open sky
    (Economy.is_night: DayNight.daylight below DARK_LIGHT), else
    FENCE_DAY.
  - "" for every other counter.
- **Grave goods** (ItemBook.is_grave, 555), a player's stolen goods:
  - At his counter by night: bought at fence_price, half the town's
    price (Economy.sell, barter_quote).
  - At his counter by day: refused, "not by day".
  - At any other counter and with any maker: refused, "won't buy that".
  - At the store's depot: refused as a raw good's banking, so the gold
    can't come round the fence.
- **By day his goods are dear:** at his counter, Economy.goods,
  barter_quote's takes and buy price his shop's goods at day_markup;
  at night at the town's price.
- **The thief:** Townsfolk._merchant is the fence alone, in his own
  town (no fence there means no fencing; the goods stay lifted). The
  thief deals off-screen whenever he lifts: no night gate, a draft Jeff
  may move.
- **Wire:** the "barter" message gains "fence" ("" | "day" | "night")
  for the counter. "fenced" {uid: gold} is filled only at his counter
  by night. ui's hover reads "won't buy", "not by day" and "pays N gold,
  fenced". A line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 32.
- Drafts for Jeff's folder (the coordinator's): factor 0.5, day_markup
  1.3, his night prices the town's, no night gate on the thief.

## 587, economy's side. Back at once from near death

Jeff's down screen, through the coordinator (companions' design:
"Mortally Wounded", Slow Heart / Bleed Out): "if you bleed out you return
to the temple, the game says 'Aldous brought you back from near death' ...
If everyone dies you just automatically respawn". Economy's side lands
first, then companions' (the down state, the heart, the commands,
everyone-down's detection).

- **A player comes back at once.** Main._start_return opens the
  player's return with Production.open_return(..., at_once = true):
  needed 0 and "near_death", so Production.returns_due finishes it in
  the same World.step, after the zones have stepped. Every player death
  comes this way: Bleed Out pressed, the blood run out, or everyone_s
  up. It replaces 396 amended's 60 s keeper wait for players.
  - The nearest manned temple or healer's hut still brings them back
    (584's care will narrow which huts).
  - Nobody manned anywhere means the plain respawn, as before.
  - Companions' and residents' returns still take the keeper's
    return.steps, and give up after give_up.
- **The words:** the party line is "<keeper> brought you back from near
  death." The "return" message carries {by, where, seconds: 0,
  near_death: true}.
- **Everyone down:** Main.tell_all_fallen(peers) sends "return"
  {all_fallen: seconds}, the seconds from economy.json
  return.everyone_s (20; Jeff: "only a 15-20 second timer after
  'all have fallen' is fine", a data number he can drop to 15), and returns
  them. Companions' side calls it, keeps the clock and bleeds the downed
  out when it runs down. It sends {all_fallen: 0} when someone stands
  again: the wait is called off.
- A saved return job keeps "near_death".
- The message's new keys sit in the line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 32.

tests/return_test, in Main: a player who dies is told {Ned,
healers_hut, 0, near_death} and is back at the hut, at full hp, on the

## 584 amended: the healer's care, economy's side

Jeff (2026-10-22, through the coordinator): "5 herbs, 5 antlers or 10 gold
to bypass the quest, but doing his 1st quest can open up further quests
such as healing the sick, potion quests, etc." Agreed with npc and ui; the
coordinator's approval. Economy's half of 584 had not landed, so this is
all of it.

- **The rule.** A healer's hut brings back only a player in its care
  (Main._return_place passes over a healers_hut for a player not in it;
  companions and residents as before; a temple always). Rules'
  return.care {retainer 10, herbs 5, antlers 5, sick 1, word_days 1}:
  Economy.care_rule(in_town) gives sick and word_days (npc's kin errand)
  only at a hut a town has built; a hut out in the land (Hob's) asks the
  rest alone. Main.care_rule(place_id) reads which. 584's
  retainer_in_towns_only is dropped: any hut takes gold.
- **The record.** PlayerRecord.care: hut place id -> the way in, saved.
  Economy.CARE_WAYS: "gold", "herbs", "antlers" (the bypass) and "quest"
  (his first errand, npc's call). Economy.CARE_QUEST_WAYS ("herbs",
  "quest") count as the first errand done, which opens npc's chain; five
  herbs are the errand's object however they are handed. A paid way
  (gold, antlers) upgrades to the errand's when it is done later; nothing
  else replaces a way in (Economy.care_after).
- **Main.** grant_care(player, place, way), in_care(player, place),
  care_via(player, place = any), care_rule(place).
- **The "retain" command** {resident: the medicine man, pay: gold | herbs

  is in care, with the party line "<name> takes you into his care.", and
  the barter is sent again. A refusal's why: too far away, already in his
  care, not enough gold (10), 5 herbs needed (3).
- **Wire.** The barter message from a medicine man carries "care" {gold,
  herbs, antlers, in_care, by}. ui shows three offers and "In his care
  (paid / for the herbs / for the antlers / his errand)". These keys and

## 590. The meat chain: the herder, the butcher, the cook

Jeff: "farm animals do feed the town, but that employes the herder, the
butcher, the cook - its a supply chain". The coordinator approved
economy's design.

- **Today's meat:** the hunter (every 3000 steps, from the herds at the
  hunting ground) brings meat and hide into the store, paid at delivery.
  The cook's roast takes 1 meat and 1 food, and residents' meals and
  raids read the store's meat. All unchanged.
- **The herder:** the shepherd and Towns.flock, as since 500. At the
  autumn turn, after the shearing, with a butcher in town, he culls the
  flock down to butcher.keep (0.5) of the pasture's room (Towns._cull).
  - The culled sheep go into the store live as a new resource, "sheep"
    (Stockpile.RESOURCES; value 5), delivered at the price as wool is.
  - Without a butcher there is no cull.
- **The butcher, a new trade:** a newcomer (Towns._butcher_comes, as the
  weaver comes).
  - The town chooses a butchery once its flock reaches butcher.from
    (8). He comes once it has stood growth_days (3).
  - economy.json buildings.butchery: trade butcher, built by the
    carpenter, wood 8, 3000 steps, max_level 2. It is a kind for
    buildings-6f to draw at 5x5 or more; nothing in real levels.
  - At his manned butchery, each butcher.steps (900) of work turns one
    sheep from the store into butcher.meat (3) meat and butcher.hide
    (1) hide, delivered at their price (Towns._butcher).
  - It is a rule over resources, as the shearing is: not an Items
    "made", so no item and no Items.TRADES entry (items agreed).
  - wage_floor gains "butcher": "meat".
- **One meat pool:** the store's meat, whichever source brought it.
  Hunting stays the bulk; the flock steadies it when the herds thin.
  Raids never take sheep (they aren't in raids' takes).
- **The draft rate:** a level-1 pasture (room 12) culled to 6 lambs
  about 2 a year (lambs × (1 − count/room)), so about 6 meat a year; a
  level-3 one about 18. Small beside the hunter's, and Jeff may raise
  lambs or lower keep. A soak follows.
- "sheep" reaches no client: no message lists the store's resources
  (the counter's shortfall reads item recipes only). Server only,
  protocol unchanged.

## 591, economy's side. Wood from the forest standing, and stages toward a city

Jeff: "i eventually want held to be in its own map that leaves room to
grow, forests to chop down, town and city growing and becoming something
is one of the major gameplay components". The growth loop is one decision
with sides: maps (the clearing, Clearing.fell, plot_for, the woodlot
stepping out, regrowth), buildings-6f (STAGES, classes, the market kind),
economy (these).

- **The forest real:** Towns.fell, a Callable (town, site id, wanted) ->
  trees, which Main sets to maps' Clearing.fell once it lands. Unset, a
  cut brings its wood as before.
  - Towns._woodcut, at a town with a woodlot, calls Towns._felled. It
    asks for the cut's wood / woodcutter.wood_per_tree (2) trees and
    brings 2 wood for each tree felled: the wood follows the forest
    left standing.
  - A lot cut bare brings woodcutter.deadwood (1), never none, so a town
    never starves of wood while maps steps the lot out and the forest
    regrows (the coordinator's care). The log says "the woodlot is cut
    bare" once.
  - When the walk to the lot grows (Production.site_walk, read live),
    the log says "the woodlot has moved out: N steps there and back":
    the walk is the cost of growth.
- **Stages:** economy.json "stages" (drafts, Jeff's folder):
  - hamlet: from the founding.
  - village: 8 residents; temple and inn standing; a priest.
  - town: 16 residents; walls standing; a lawspeaker; 150 gold in the
    treasury; 100 wood in the store.
  - city: 30 residents; a market standing; 2 guards; 400 gold.
- **How a town rises:** Towns._stage_turn, on the town tick, raises it
  one step when it meets all of the next stage's needs (Towns._meets:
  residents, standing kinds, trades among its residents, gold, wood).
  It never lowers it. Towns.stage(town) reads it; it is saved. A rise
  is logged and emits Towns.stage_changed, which Main broadcasts as
  the "town" message.
  - The city waits on a market kind (buildings' and maps'); economy's
    buildings get it when it exists.
- **Wire:** the "town" message gains "stage", a field older clients
  ignore and whose absence means no stage shown. No revision line.
- Plots (plot_for), the town's move to "held/store" (rename_places) and
  the soak come with maps' landings.

  fell, as before.
- _test_stages: a hamlet at once; a village with 8 residents, temple,

## 594. The fisherman, and the fort as a town's outpost

Jeff (2026-10-22): "town can have fisherman that go to river and back with
fish". Builder's Old Tower at Held (Snagfin's ruined fort across the river)
is a place of kind "fort" whose counter is the town's shop.

- **Fish** is a resource (Stockpile.RESOURCES), worth 1. It is a meal from
  the store, as food and meat are, and raids take it at the same shares as
  meat.
- **The fisherman** is a work-site trade (sites.trades fisherman:
  "fishing", a place on the river's bank). Every fisherman.every steps
  (3000) he walks there and back (Production.site_turn, as the woodcutter
  does), and brings fisherman.catch (2) fish, scaled by the season, into
  the store at its price (deliver_to). A bank the town doesn't hold yields
  nothing. His wage floor is the fish he brings.
- **He comes** (Towns._fisherman_comes) once the town holds a fishing place
  and has reached fisherman.stage ("village", 591's stages), after
  growth_days. That goes through _arrive, so once 613 is on he is sought
  like any other newcomer.
- **Outposts.** Stockpile.OUTPOSTS ["fort"]: a counter inside a fort place
  that names its "town" is that town's shop (place_at), and the level check
  accepts such a counter away from the store.
- Level.PLACE_KINDS gains "fishing" and "fort" (maps adds "fort" too: one
  entry).

production_test (the fisherman's trip and catch, nothing from a bank not
held, the fort's counter the town's shop). Level data both sides read:

## 587, companions' side. Mortally Wounded: the down state, the heart, Bleed Out

Jeff (2026-10-22): "when a player is down, the game goes gray like now,
and the heart beat becomes the dominant sound ... 'Mortally Wounded' two
buttons, Slow Heart (Hold), Bleed Out (Respawn) - if you bleed out you
return to the temple ... you can slow down your heart beat to keep
yourself from bleeding out, until its safe, the companion then has to
cast resurrect on you when conditions are met ... from 120 to 80 to 40
bpm. If everyone dies you just automatically respawn a 60-90 seconds
later but in the temple." The coordinator approved the design
(C:/dev/review/companions/mortally_wounded_design.md), with the
unblessed's 10 s last moments.

- Main._downed: every player at 0 hp lies downed: the blessed the field
  rules' window_s (30 s), the unblessed unblessed_s (10 s, their last
  moments; nobody brings them back, 573). An unblessed companion dies as
  ever.
- The heart: Player.heart (replicated) is heart.beats[0] (120) when they
  go down. The "slow_heart" {held} command, the blessed only: held, it
  steps a beat down at once and one each heart.step_s (2 s); let go, a
  beat back up each step_s. Main._tend_hearts each tick: the blood runs
  at heart.drain of the beat (1 / 0.5 / 0.2), the window
  (World.extend_downed: downed_until, the lying and the stun) longer by
  what a slower heart saves; about 150 s at most held. Up, or gone, the
  heart is 0.
- Bleed Out: the "bleed_out" command kills the downed body with cause
  "bled", as the window's end does; economy's side returns them at once
  ("Aldous brought you back from near death").
- Everyone down: Main._all_fallen_tick: every player in the zone downed
  and each one's companion there downed or gone: "All have fallen.",
  economy's Main.tell_all_fallen (everyone_s, 20 s: Jeff, "only a 15-20
  second timer after all have fallen is fine"); when it runs out each
  bleeds out. One up again calls it off ({all_fallen: 0} to their peers).
- A revive waits for calm: _start_channel only when World.calm holds for
  both (nothing hostile within BANDAGE_SAFE, no blow in
  BANDAGE_CALM_TICKS); a player told "Not while they're fighting near."
  Never on an unblessed body; her can_revive also needs her player
  blessed.
- The other sides: economy-13 the at-once return and everyone_s;
  enemy-ai-17 no hunt of a downed target and the draugr's pact holding
  while the challenger lies downed; ui the screen; sound-4d the
  heartbeat.

## 587, sound's side. Mortally Wounded: the heartbeat over the ducked mix

Jeff: "the heart beat becomes the dominant sound to the player". The
companions' side gives the client Player.heart (replicated: 120, 80, 40 a
minute while downed, 0 otherwise); this is what the local player hears.

- The beat: client3d/heartbeat.gd (a preloaded script, Client3D.Heartbeat,
  no class_name), a node under Client3D reading the local player's heart
  each frame. Downed, a beat of sfx.heartbeat at once, then one every
  60 / heart s. Slow Heart's step is heard at the next beat: the wait is
  cut to the new pace if it is shorter, never stretched past the beat
  already due. Flat, on the UI bus, so no distance, wall or duck touches it.
- The duck: while it beats, every other bus (SFX, Voice, Ambience, Music;
  Sfx.DUCKED) sits DUCK_DB (-14) under its slider, through Sfx.set_duck,
  which apply_volumes keeps when a slider moves. Bus volume, not an effect:
  the muffled twins send through their buses and duck with them, and
  nothing is added to the audio graph. Eased down at 40 dB/s, back at 10.
- The end: the heart back to 0. If the local player is there with hp
  above 0 it was a revive: no last beat, the mix eased back. Otherwise
  (Bleed Out, the window run out, a killing blow, the player gone from
  the roster): one last beat, the mix held at SILENCE_DB (-60) for 2 s,
  then eased back. This reads only the heart and hp, not Main's "return"
  message: a death before the return is told still ends it.
- Client only, protocol unchanged. Takes: freesound 249716 (daandraait,
  "SLOW HEARTBEAT", CC0 1.0), three beats each spliced so the dub falls
  0.3 s after the lub; the Lunardrive takes 22440 and 22417 were rejected
  as clipped. They wait outside the shared take store until the push
  (_pending_587).
- view_test _test_heartbeat steps a Heartbeat by hand: the first beat at
  once on UI, the pace at 120 and after a step to 40, the duck on SFX and
  not UI, no last beat on a revive, a last beat then silence then the mix
  back on bleed out.
## 617. The archer's aim lead

Jeff (2026-10-22, his words): "archers should be able to zoom out further..
most animals end up being just off screen". The view's reach is held to
World.NEAR_TILES (ZOOM_MAX 1.1, decision 238) with the player mid-screen,
so a long shot's mark lands off screen. Perf's numbers: at zoom 1.1 the
reach is 14.6 cells on 16:9 (16.2 peeking) and 17.6 on 21:9 (20.1
peeking); one more wheel notch plus a lead would pass 22 on 21:9, so the
lead comes alone and the extra notch stays a question for Jeff beside a
NEAR_TILES 25 estimate (under a millisecond of server tick). The
coordinator's approval, with one rule: the lead starts with the draw, never
on a plain click, so walking with a bow does not tug the view.

- While the bow is drawn (Main.aim_drawn), the view slides off the archer
  toward the aim's angle: Client3D.aim_lead sets a target
  AIM_LEAD_CELLS (4) the aim's way, eased each frame at ZOOM_RATE like the
  pan, and the WASD lean and the lead together are held to AIM_LEAD_CELLS
  (Client3D.lead_offset: the lean alone, as ever, when no lead is on). The
  bow lowered or put away, the lead eases back to nothing. No zoom change;
  the pan and the peek unchanged; the 2D view unchanged.
- ui_test: lead_offset's three cases. Shot: docs/ui/shots/combat/
  aim_lead.jpg, the view led toward the aim at the longest step, the
  archer off-centre with the arc's marker in frame. Client only; protocol
  unchanged; no new class_name.
