## 583, items' side. Archery: range by held steps, damage by step, aim at any angle

pc-character's redesign (Jeff's combat feel and archery plan; the
coordinator's approval). This is the sim's shot.
- A bow's verb (Items.VERBS "ranged") has "steps", the cells each step of
  the draw reaches ([3, 5, 7, 9]), and "damage_at", each step's damage
  multiple ([1.5, 1.2, 1.0, 0.8]: the shortest hardest; Jeff: "you can
  aim shorter for higher damage, not depending on bow cock - there's no
  throttle"). The first step comes at draw_min (5 ticks), each next one
  draw_step (5) later; a quick bow's strength scales both. "cells" (the
  longest step) and "draw_full" (the ticks to it) are filled in from them,
  for what reads a bow's whole reach (an archer's band) or the pull's pose.
- World.draw_step(entity) (-1 before draw_min), World.range_of(entity)
  (the cells the step reaches now, 0 before), World.longest_range(entity).
  draw_of stays for the pose and the creak.
- World.try_loose(by, angle): radians on the grid (Vector2.angle(): 0
  east, PI / 2 south); loosed(by, angle, step). World.shoot(by, angle,
  step): damage is the blow times the bow's damage times damage_at[step].
- World.shot_ray(from, angle, cells): a ray from the cell's centre (a
  cell's centre is Vector2(cell)), walked cell by cell; where it passes
  exactly through a corner, both cells beside it count (a supercover:
  nothing slips between two bodies). Its reach is Chebyshev, as
  World.distance counts. It stops at a wall or closed door (as sight
  crosses edges), higher ground or the map's end. Over relief it aims at
  the height of the ground under its range's end, since only an angle is
  sent. World.shot_aim(by, angle, cells) adds the first body. shot_line is
  gone.
- GridEntity.shot(to: Vector2, struck: StringName): the point it stopped
  at, in cell units, and &"body", &"wood", &"stone" or &"ground" (its
  range spent: it comes down past the point). Client3D._on_shot reads the
  cell for now; the point and the sag are pc-character's.
- Walking while drawn: allowed at half pace (DRAWN_TICK_SCALE in
  step_ticks, read by a client's prediction too); a step no longer
  spoils the draw. This is the coordinator's default until Jeff answers.
  Jeff answered (583 amended): a drawn body stands firm and takes no step.
- The "loose" command carries "angle"; "at" is still read as a fallback
  (ui sends both). Monster archers loose at the angle to their target once
  range_of covers its distance or reaches the longest step, and
  _clear_shot reads shot_aim. monster_test's archer now shoots at 15
  ticks, at 7 cells.
- Arrows are not used up or picked up, as before.
Wire: PROTOCOL_REVISION 31. items_test, monster_test, cliff_test,
relief_test and view_test follow. No new class_name.

Changed by 669: the steps, their damage (now rising to full draw, then by distance band) and their times are 669's.

## 599, items' side. A cache: each player's find, once

Jeff, through the coordinator: "old farmstead in the wilds - abandoned,
tools and bandages found inside". A small one-time stash, per player,
that never respawns.
- A cache is a Chest with props {"cache": a loot table, "cache_place":
  where the find comes from}. Its own slots stay empty: a shared chest
  can't hold "once per player", since the first comer would empty it for
  everyone. Level._stock leaves a cache's slots alone (no level loot) and
  warns on an unknown table or a "loot" key on one.
- E on a cache (Main.open_other, so walking up to one from afar works as
  for any chest) sends "search" in place of opening the panel. There's
  no key hint: it reads as a chest (Jeff's no-hints rule of the day).
- Main.search(player, chest), on the server: the first time, the table
  is rolled by the player and the cache (the same if tried again); each
  thing is minted "cached" from cache_place (a thing with a condition at
  half: nothing fine) and put in a free hand or pack slot
  (free_slot_for), else on the ground at their feet. The cache goes on
  PlayerRecord.caches (saved), so it is once per player for life. They
  are told "You find in the old farmstead: bandaging kit (2), knife."; a
  second search is "Nothing more here." Companions don't search.
- World.story_line reads "cached" as "found in <place>".
- levels/loot.json "farmstead_cache": two bandaging kits, a knife, and a
  pick at 0.5. No new item kinds.
- Maps places it (599, maps' side): the wilds' north farmstead hut,
  (119, 139).
Wire: under PROTOCOL_REVISION 31 (with 583). items_test _test_cache. No
new class_name.

## 584 amended, npc's side: the medicine man's care and the quests behind it

Jeff (2026-10-22, through the coordinator): "5 herbs, 5 antlers or 10 gold
to bypass the quest, but doing his 1st quest can open up further quests
such as healing the sick, potion quests, etc." Economy's amended 584
(d53b2a92) holds the care: who is in it, the way in (gold, herbs, antlers
or quest; Economy.CARE_QUEST_WAYS counts herbs and quest as his first
errand done), the retain command, the rule by hut. This is the medicine
man's side of it: his words, his pleas, the chain.

- **His offers to one not in his care** (Offers._care_offers, from his
  card and economy's care_via for his hut, Main._care_hut_of): the
  retainer paid ahead (kind "care", his line "Pay me 10 gold now and I'll
  see to you after: fall where you will and you wake here, in my care.";
  accepted, Main._retain_care runs economy's retain command with the two
  bodies, so the gold, the party line and the barter again are economy's),
  and his first quest, the herbs (a plea "Bring him herbs": "Bring me 5
  handfuls of herbs and I'll count you in my care, and there is more you
  could do for me after."). Gold or antlers open nothing further; the
  herbs plea stays for one who paid.
- **The herbs are the quest however they come.** His card counts them by
  player (care_herbs: by gift, Offers.herbs_taken); at the rule's five,
  economy's grant_care(player, hut, "quest"), which also upgrades a paid
  way; his card learns it, the player's standing rises as for one who gave, his
  open herbs plea closes met with "<name> is in <his name>'s care now:
  fall where they will, he will see to them." Five herbs handed in
  economy's window instead (care_via "herbs") close a standing plea met
  the next time his offers are read. Antlers one by one (care_antlers,
  Offers.antlers_taken) are a way in at five ("antlers") and no quest.
- **The chain, one ask at a time, each once** (care_done by player): at a
  hut a town has built (rule.sick > 0) while someone in the town is sick,
  "Walk the sick to him" ("There is sickness in the town and I cannot be
  everywhere. Find one who is sick and walk them to my door."), met in
  Offers.healed when a townsman is treated by him with that plea standing,
  no pay of his own ("<player> walked <sick> to <him>, who saw to them.");
  else "The makings of a brew" ("Bring me 3 handfuls of herbs and a pair
  of antlers and I'll brew you something for the road; the potion is
  yours."): gifts of herbs and antlers count toward it over visits
  (BREW_HERBS 3, BREW_ANTLERS 1); at the count he hands back a
  stamina_potion (Main._hand_item: minted "made" by him, into a free hand
  or the pack, else at the player's feet) with "<he> brews what <player>
  brought and hands them the potion." Then nothing more of his care is
  asked, for now: later quests hang on the same card keys.
- **His words.** residents.json "care" (the titles, the lines, "kept",
  "voice": his prompt knows who is in his care, and "voice_quest" that

## 589. Zone transitions with built cues

Jeff: "there needs to be strong visual cues of where the zone transition
is, descending/ascending steps, arches, etc." (he couldn't find the
castle's link). Every link shows where it leads by a piece at its cell,
picked from where it goes, so a new link gets one with no work. Approved by
the coordinator with art-kit, dungeon and ui; maps leads.
- Level.link_cues -> terrain["link_cues"] [{tile, cue, facing, variant}],
  and each level link's "cue" (ui's big-map mark). The cue (Level.CUES):
  - a link's own "cue" in level.json wins;
  - hidden: "none" (not given away); sealed or closed: "sealed" (its own
    slab, no piece here); on a solid building's door: "none" (the barrow's
    mound is its own cue);
  - to a deeper level (level.json "depth", 0 if not said; dungeon's barrow
    layers 1, 2, 3): "down", a stair down with a dark mouth; to a shallower
    one: "up", a stair up or a climb;
  - between two outdoor levels: "arch", a gate arch over it, or "waystones"
    (a pair either side) where it stands within two cells of the map's
    edge, an arch hanging off it otherwise; facing out to the nearest edge;
  - else "none" (an indoor door between rooms of a level's depth).
  A stair faces away from the open ground it is walked into from.
  "variant" as the link says, 1 if not: art-kit's 1 is a timber arch and
  stone stairs, 2 a stone arch, a timber stair or ladder, the arrowed
  waystone. The castle's two links take 2 (a stone arch in the wilds,
  arrowed waystones at the castle's gate). level.json "depth" has its row in
  the level editor.
- Client3D._add_link_cues places art-kit's slot (Level.CUE_SLOTS:
  building.link_arch, building.waystone, building.stair_down,
  building.stair_up) on the cell, its front (+Z) the way out; waystones on
  the cells either side. Drawn only: the cell stays walked on (571), the
  arch's posts scenery.
tests: level_test, the wilds' castle link a stone arch facing north, the
castle's gate waystones, the barrow's stairs down and up, the mound's door
and the sealed shortcut, every link's cue, every cue's piece in the kit;
the castle's links with their cue; view_test, a waystone either side of the
castle's gate and its cell clear.
PROTOCOL_REVISION 32 (a line under it): terrain["link_cues"] and the links'
"cue" reach the client.

## 591, maps' side: the forest felled and growing back

Jeff: "i eventually want held to be in its own map that leaves room to
grow, forests to chop down, town and city growing and becoming something is
one of the major gameplay components", and "the server has to stay
persistent once you set a worker to harvest they keep working, but forests
can regenerate too if not built over". The Held growth loop (591, one
number: economy's Towns.stage and the woodcut's fell calls, buildings'
stages, classes and market kind as their sides); this is the clearing.
- Clearing (sim/clearing.gd; World.clearing, made by Main at boot from the
  snapshot's "clearing", moved on by the world tick's first slice whether
  or not anyone is in a zone). A tree is a trunk: a level's void cell inside
  its land, more than EDGE (4) cells in from the map's edge.
  - fell(zone, site, toward, wanted) -> trunks felled: the standing edge
    trunks (floor beside them, the level's or felled) within REACH (6) of
    the woodlot's site, nearest the town's store first; each a stump. None
    within reach: 0. economy's Towns.fell(town, site_id, wanted) wraps it
    from Main once both are on main.
  - step_site(zone, site) -> the floor cell beside the standing edge trunk
    nearest a bare site (within STEP_REACH 40): where the woodlot steps out
    to, keeping its id (economy moves the place).
  - Regrowth (drafts): stump, grass, scrub, saplings, each a season
    (Season.season_days, 14 days), twice that with no standing trunk
    beside it (a clearing closes from its edges); past saplings the level's
    own trunk again, leaving no trace (the coordinator), unless something
    stands or lies on it (it waits) or it is built over (a building's or a
    road's cell: never).
- Kept in the world snapshot, never the level overlay (the coordinator's
  refinement: builder's overlay reloads a zone a change, and is builder's to
  export): zone -> "x,y" -> [stage, day].
- Applied: Main._load_level lays a zone's felled cells on its terrain
  before World loads it (Clearing.apply: floor of the stage's kind, a stump
  dirt, the rest grass; terrain["clearing"] cell -> stage). A change in a
  loaded zone: World.set_floor for each cell (the walk at once), and the
  message "clearing" {zone, cells: [[x, y, stage]]} ("trunk" grown back) to
  everyone in it; a joining client gets {zone, whole: true, cells} before
  "map", and lays it as it loads the level (Clearing.apply_cells). The
  views redraw through Client3D.clearing_changed(terrain, cells) once
  terrain has it (its side: a stump, scrub, saplings, the edge retraced
  locally), else the whole zone.
tests: level_test, a woodcut fells the grove's edge nearest the town, the
far site fells nothing and steps beside the nearest trunk, applied as
floor, regrown a season a stage from the edge, a built-over cell never,
read back from the snapshot.
PROTOCOL_REVISION 32 (a line under it): message "clearing", terrain
["clearing"]. New class_name Clearing. The forest on the box is felled and
grows back over time once economy's woodcut calls it.

- The body (Main._sought_here, in _sync_residents after the strays): a

## 614. Giving gold

Jeff (2026-10-22, on the robbers' purses): "dropping purses of coins
isn't ideal, there no way to trade gold in game either. that should be
economies concern first. consolidate gold coins to being stackable in the
inventory but not taking up a pack slot." Gold is never an item: it stays
the record's count (Economy's purses), shown as one stack outside the pack
(ui), and lies on the ground as a count (items' 601 amended). This is
economy's side, the trade; the coordinator approved it 2026-10-22.

- **The command.** "give_gold" {to: path, amount} gives the player's gold
  to another player or to their own companion; {from: her path, amount}
  takes it back from their companion, keeper only. The other must be in the
  zone, standing, within World.COMPANION_REACH and in sight. Main.give_gold
  checks it, and each refusal is a party line to the giver alone: too far,
  only to a player or your own companion, say how much, you have only N.
- **The transfer.** Economy.give_gold(from, to, amount, from_name,
  to_name) moves the gold between two records, so none leaves the world
  (Jeff's rule: player gold is lost only through spending). Each log names
  the other ("gave to Bo", "given by Ann"). World.give_gold emits
  gold_changed for both, so each player's gold line updates through the
  "shop" message as before.
- **Words.** "Ann gives Bo 7 gold." / "Ann takes 3 gold from Wren." go to
  both players as a party line, from "Server".
- **The companion's purse.** It is kept as "companion:<keeper id>"
  (Economy.companion_purse), saved with the purses. companions show it on
  her card. What she does with it waits on Jeff's open question, whether
  companions are paid.
- No two-sided trade window: gold beside a hand-over (the "transfer"
  command) is the trade for now.

ui draws "Give gold" on the bar under another player's bubble, and "Give
gold" and "Take gold" on the companion's pack row, with one amount box.

## 619. Small things stack in a slot, each its own

Jeff on v0.1.168: "you cant hold 5, theres only 4 inventory slots haha" (Hob's
5 herbs). Items' design (C:/dev/review/stacking/design.md), approved by the
coordinator 2026-10-23.

- **A stack of instances.** A slot holds a stack of things of one kind, and every
  thing in it stays one ItemBook uid with its own history. The slot's first
  unit is its slot_items uid; the rest are kept on that first unit's book entry
  (ItemBook.stack_of / set_stack, saved with the book), so they go wherever it
  goes and old saves are stacks of 1 with nothing to convert. The stockpile,
  the shop's shelf, the ledger, banking, selling and the fence keep working on
  uids, one thing each: selling 5 herbs is 5 uids sold.
- **What stacks.** items.json "stack": N (1 when left out, as before). A thing
  with a condition, a weapon, shield, token or soulbound thing, or one used for
  anything but eating or bandaging never stacks (Items.stack_problem warns and
  keeps it at 1). Herbs, tusks and silver rings 10; meat, hide, leather,
  antlers, rations, roasts, remedies, bandaging kits and spice 5; stamina
  potions and wine 3. Economy may retune these without a decision. Arrows stay
  bundles: a bundle's condition is already its count of shots, and bundles do
  not stack with each other. Gold stays a count (601 amended).
- **Clean stacks.** A unit joins a stack only of the same id and style and the
  same grave mark, both with no name, binding, keeping, blessing, bane, grudge,
  short measure or condition (World.stacks_onto): a fenced or grave-marked
  herb never hides in a clean one.
- **The verbs.** F picks up every unit of the top kind on the cell that fits,
  filling a stack of its kind (hands, then pack) before a free slot
  (World.room_for). try_transfer takes a count (0: all): onto an empty slot it
  splits, onto a stack of the kind it joins as many as fit, onto anything else
  the stacks swap whole, each unit's history written. try_drop takes a count.
  Taking out (take_item, eating, throwing, banking, selling, the priest) takes
  one unit; a depot or shop takes a dragged stack unit by unit. World.units,
  count_of, slot_units, slot_count, slot_of_unit and take_units read and take
  by unit: the healer's "5 herbs" is paid from one slot. handed fires once per
  unit given to a resident, so npc's tally counts units. A barter's give is
  still a uid per unit; the barter message's pack entries carry the stack's
  uids and its count, and takes join a stack of their kind first. The cache's
  find and the healer's brew go onto a stack of their kind first.
- **Weight per unit.** _weigh adds each unit's weight, so carried weight (and
  so the loyalty pack-weight check and the "worked like a mule" draft that
  read it) stays honest: five antlers weigh fifteen kilograms in one slot as
  in five.
- **The ground.** zone.ground stays a uid list per cell. GROUND_PER_CELL
  counts heaps: a stackable kind's units are one heap up to its stack size.
  GroundPile replicates ids, repeats and all; the views group them. A stack
  laid down whole lies as its units.
- **The wire** (revision 33's line): slot_counts, replicated on Player,
  Companion, Chest and Cargo, empty while no slot holds more than one;
  "transfer" and "drop" carry an optional "count". Until ui draws the count,
  a stack's slot note begins "5 × ".
- Companions' turns_down sees a moved stack's first uid; a clean stack's
  first stands for the rest.

items_test _test_stacks (pick-up, split, join, a grave herb kept apart, a count
put down, one taken out, the book saved); return_test (five antlers in one
slot pay the healer); economy_test (a bought kit joins the stack it finds).
No new class_name.

## 623. The low-horizon camera, a trial toggle

Jeff (2026-10-22): "drop the camera angle so we can see the sky and the
land"; he picked persp22 (pitch 22, fov 50) from ui's sheet of four and
wants it in its own cut, sooner, to play. It is a toggle, off by default,
so the ortho view he has stays until he says: Options, Video, "Camera:
low horizon (trial)" Off/On; settings.cfg camera=low|high (Net.camera_low,
set_camera_low, camera_low_changed; read before the first frame beside the
colours). Applied at once and on a map change (Client3D._apply_camera_mode
from _build_camera, rebuild and the signal).
- Outdoors only (_terrain "outdoor"): under stone, dungeons and rooms, the
  ortho camera as it is, whatever the toggle. Off restores the ortho view
  exactly (projection, far, pitch, haze, shadow distance, distance).
- On, outdoors: a perspective camera (LOW_FOV 50; the sheet he picked from
  was 50), LOW_PITCH 22 above the ground, LOW_DISTANCE_SHARE half of
  CAMERA_DISTANCE off (20 units), LOW_FAR 300 (perf: the same read as 600,
  never under about 250). The wheel, a pitch peek and the mourning pull-back
  scale that distance (_camera_distance, _size_factor) as they scale the
  ortho size. The tilt's floor is LOW_PITCH_MIN 15 (pitch_floor), the rest
  LOW_PITCH (rest_pitch); the ridge rule (525) lifts the pitch as before.
- The sky is the day's (DayNight's look through _update_sky, as before);
  LOW_FOG 0.012 of haze is added over the look's fog density and the
  weather's, with LOW_AERIAL 0.6 of the sky in it (fog_aerial_perspective),
  so the far land fades into the horizon. Environment's note: a storm's
  haze is per unit of distance, tuned for a camera 40 off, so at 20 it
  reads thinner near the aim and, with the added haze, thicker far; the
  ground fog planes, the rain box and the cloud decal are sized for the
  ortho footprint and may show seams. Theirs with terrain once Jeff
  confirms the trial.
- The sun's shadows reach LOW_SHADOW_DISTANCE 150 in two PSSM splits
  (environment's advice), so the line where they stop is off the near
  ground; SHADOW_DISTANCE 70 orthogonal as before when off.
- What is on screen thinks every tick (238): the view's reach for shadows
  and puppets is held to World.NEAR_TILES; a body beyond it is not drawn
  (its puppet hidden, shown again within; all shown when the toggle goes
  off) and gets no bubble; a click past it lands NEAR_TILES out along its
  line (within_near, in mouse_grid). Dragging pans the frustum's height at
  the aim (_view_height), not the ortho size.
- Nothing on the wire, no new class_name. Perf measures after it lands
  (its trial: up to +2.4 ms GPU on the road at 22 degrees).

## 620. The cone of flight

Jeff, on v0.1.168: "I'm wondering if we can have an cone of flight that narrows the longer the
aim, extends out to each level the final level continues to narrow down the longer held?"
Combat's design, approved by the coordinator (C:/dev/review/combat/archery_cone/design.md);
pc-character built the sim, and items reviews the diff on try_loose and shoot.

- **The cone** (`Items.spread_at(verb, held)`, static and pure; `World.spread_of(entity)` wraps it,
  -1 when not drawing): the half-angle a drawn bow looses in narrows along one curve over the
  hold. It is the verb's `spread` first value (25°) until the first step, each step's value as it
  is reached ([25, 16, 10, 6]° at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 s), lerped straight between them, then down
  to `spread_floor` (2°) over `spread_settle` (40 ticks) past the last step, so the floor comes at
  6 s. A quick bow scales the ticks as it scales the steps. It reads only the hold, which
  replicates, so ui's cone on a client is the server's.
- **The roll** (`World.scatter(by, angle, spread)`): the arrow flies the aim plus the half-angle
  times half the sum of two rolls in -1..1 (triangular: most near the aim, the edge rare), seeded
  by `World.shot_salt`, the archer's name and the tick. The salt is drawn at the server's boot and
  never sent, so a client can't foresee the line; tests set it.
- **try_loose** reads the cone before it lowers the bow, then shoots the rolled line;
  `loosed` keeps the aim, and the archer faces the aim (`shoot`'s new `aimed`), so only the arrow
  strays. shot_aim and shot_ray are unchanged: the aim preview and a monster's clear-shot check
  read the centre line.
- **Every bow alike:** one model, the bow verb's fields in items.json; a verb without `spread`
  shoots straight as before. Monster archers loose through the same try_loose; enemy-ai sets each
  kind's wait (`aim_spread`, at least the floor, and `aim_hold_max`) in its own change.
- **Monsters' strays** (items, reviewing): until enemy-ai's wait lands, an archer looses as soon as
  its step covers the target, often at 25° or 16°. Its clear-shot check reads only the aimed line,
  and a monster's arrow spares no one (456), so a stray can hit a fellow monster beside the line.
  Kept (the coordinator): one cone for every bow, and 456's arrow spares no one. Enemy-ai's wait
  change makes it rarer and folds in a clear-shot check of the cone's two edges, so an archer holds
  while a friend is inside its cone.
- Damage by step is unchanged (damage_at). Walking drawn doesn't widen it in this step.

What a hold buys (combat's table, 40,000 rolls each; the miss is how far from the aimed line the
arrow lands at the step's range, a target one cell wide dead on the aim):

| hold | reach | half-angle | mean miss | hits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 s | 5 cells | 16° | 0.46 cells | 59% |
| 3 s | 9 cells | 5° | 0.26 cells | 87% |
| 6 s | 9 cells | 2° (the floor) | 0.11 cells | 100% |

The numbers are data in the bow's verb, for Jeff to tune by feel.

items_test: the cone at each hold (25, 21.4 between, 16, 10, 6, 4, 2, 2), 200 rolls inside it,
the same line for the same salt and none without a cone, and a loose flying the rolled line read
before the bow is lowered. monster_test's archer checks shoot straight (they test its standing off,
not its aim). Combat adds the mean-miss test. Wire: no new message; PROTOCOL_REVISION 34 (the
first wire change after v0.1.169) records that a client's and the server's bow fields go together. No new class_name.

Changed by 669: the cone's widths follow 669's steps, held at full draw's past it; the settle to the floor is gone.

## 620, enemy-ai's side: an archer's hold, and the cone's edges

The coordinator approved enemy-ai's design (2026-10-23): a monster archer looses through the
same cone as a player (620), and each kind says how long it holds first. A goblin snaps off a
wide shot, the patient dead wait for the cone to close.

- **The hold** (`Monster._aimed`): a kind's row in monsters.json may carry `aim_spread`
  (degrees) and `aim_hold_max` (ticks). An archer looses once its draw's step covers the target
  (as before) and either its cone (`World.spread_of`, radians, -1 when not drawing) is at or under
  `aim_spread`, or it has held `aim_hold_max` ticks. A row with neither looses as soon as the step
  covers it, as before 620.
- **The floor:** `Monster.read_kinds` keeps both keys and raises an `aim_spread` under the bow's
  `spread_floor` (items.json, 2°) to it with a warning; under it an archer would loose only on its
  cap. Every archer kind arms "bow" today, so the floor is read from that verb.
- **The edges** (`Monster._cone_clear`): an archer looses only when both edges of its cone
  (`World.shot_aim` at the aim plus and minus the spread, as far as the target) meet no body but
  the target, so it holds its draw while a friend is inside the cone, the cap not firing; the cone
  narrows and it looses once the friend is outside it. `_clear_shot` checks the edges at the floor
  as well as the aimed line: a friend inside even the narrowest cone is no clear shot, and it
  lowers the bow and moves for one as it does with a body on the line.
- **The numbers** (drafts for Jeff, at 10 ticks a second; the bow's cone is 25, 16, 10, 6° at 5,
  10, 15, 20 ticks of draw): brute 25° / 8 (a snap shot), imp 16° / 12 (about 1 s), sneak 10° / 20,
  robber 10° / 25, skeleton and skeleton_guard 6° / 30 (about 2 s). None for beasts or the draugr
  (he throws).

monster_test `_test_archer_hold`: the rows read, a spread under the floor raised; three off, no
hold looses at 5 ticks, 16° at 10, 6° at 20, the floor capped at 25 at the cap; a crate on the
cone's edge holds the draw past a cap of 12 and it looses at 14 as the cone clears it, the crate
unstruck. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 619, ui's side: a stack on the interface

Items' 619 (28573df8): a slot holds a stack of one kind; slot_counts
replicated, "transfer" and "drop" take a count, the barter's pack entries
carry the stack's uids and count, GroundPile.ids keeps repeats. The
interface's side, approved by the coordinator 2026-10-23:
- **The count on the slot.** A slot holding more than one shows the number
  small in brass in its bottom-right corner (PackPanel.count_words; the
  box's count label), nothing for one, so a lone thing looks as it did. It
  reads World.slot_count (slot_counts on a client), on the host and on a
  companion's, a chest's or a cart's row alike, and the panel's signature
  includes slot_counts so the badge follows a split. The slot's note no
  longer begins "5 × " (World._show_notes, the stop-gap items left for
  this): the tip reads the thing, the badge the count.
- **One unit by Shift.** A drag moves the whole slot (count 0, as before);
  Shift held when it begins (PackPanel.shift_down) drags one unit, the drag
  data's count 1, passed through PackPanel.drop and Main._transfer as the
  command's "count". Dropping onto an empty slot splits that one off, onto
  a stack of its kind joins it (items' try_transfer).
- **The barter.** A click on a stacked box gives the whole stack, unit by
  unit as far as the merchant takes (toggle_give's "won't buy" and "the
  town has enough of that" stop it, and the hover says), or unselects it
  all; a Shift-click gives one more unit, or takes one back when all are
  given (_select_mine's third argument from the box's click). The hover
  adds "3 of 5 to give" over a part-given stack (stack_words); pack_entry
  finds an entry by any of its units, so the frames and the sum's words
  hold. The care buttons for herbs and antlers already light on holding any
  (584 amended (2)).
- **The ground.** A pile's hint counts the first kind lying there: "5
  herbs", "2 herbs and 1 more", "12 gold and 2 herbs" (Main.pile_words).
  The heap is drawn with one model per kind (Client3D._on_pile_shown), so
  five herbs lie as one plant with the ring under it, not five.
- Client only, nothing on the wire, no new class_name.

25 degrees at the draw's start lerped down the steps to 6, then to a floor
of 2 over 40 ticks of the last step, no reset when the aim turns; the
server rolls the arrow's line inside it. ui draws it and never guesses an
angle:

## 622. Armour: one slot, one piece, four kinds (step 1)

Jeff: "just have an armor slot next to the weapon slot ... the armor is just one
piece that covers the chest, arms, legs ... leather, plate, robes and others
change appearances". Items' design (C:/dev/review/armour/design.md), approved by
the coordinator; built with the draft values as they stand (Jeff, 2026-10-23: "i
can't take decisions that i dont even have the base function in game yet"), to be
tuned from the cut checklist.

- **The slot.** A seventh carried slot: Items.ARMOUR = 6, CARRIED = 7 (the pack
  0-3, the right hand 4, the left 5, the armour worn 6), for players and
  companions alike. A record saved before it holds six slots and is padded with
  the armour slot empty (Items.tidy), so nothing moves and nothing is misread.
  Monsters armed by a level before it have six slots and keep them:
  Items.HANDED (6) is what having hands needs (has_hands, the monster's
  replicated hands).
- **The rule.** Only armour is worn there, and armour is worn or packed, never
  held (its catalog hands 0 says so too). World.worn_refusal says why a set of
  slots breaks it; hands_allow keeps to it, so every move (a drag, a pick-up, a
  barter's take) does. A drag refused for it emits World.slot_refused, and Main
  says the why to the player who moved it ("Only armour is worn there.",
  "Armour is worn, not held."). Putting it on or off is a drag between your
  own slots; it takes no time yet (don_ticks later, if wanted).
- **The kinds.** A catalog field "armour": {look, stats}, read as
  Items.armour_of(id) ({} for a thing not worn; an unknown look warned and not
  armour). Looks: Items.ARMOUR_LOOKS, leather, mail, plate, robes. The four
  kinds (draft numbers): leather_armour 6 kg, value 22; mail_armour 10 kg, 45;
  plate_armour 20 kg, 80; robes 2 kg, 12. Stats: deflect_shot (0, 0.25, 0.5,
  0), deflect_pierce (0, 0.2, 0.3, 0), range_steps (9, 7, 5, 9), draw (0.9,
  1.0, 1.1, 1.0), robes' aura 2. Their art slots are placeholders.
- **Its weight is its mass.** Worn armour weighs as any carried thing does
  (World._weigh): plate's 20 kg make its wearer heavier to push and pushing
  harder, by the same rule as a hammer in the hand; no separate mass stat.
- **worn.** Player.worn and Companion.worn hold the armour slot's id ("" for
  none), set by World as the slots change and replicated, so the views draw
  the covering (pc-character) from Items.armour_of(worn).
  World.worn_armour(entity) is what reads a stat (combat's deflections and
  regen, the bow's range_steps and draw at step 2).
- The pack panel marks the slot "A" beside R and L; ui places and styles it.
- **Later steps.** Step 2: the stats read (items: range_steps, draw; combat:
  deflect_shot, deflect_pierce, aura, stamina from the weight). Step 3: where
  they come from (economy's tanner, weaver and smith; dungeon's mail rows; the
  fence). Until then no armour comes into the world but by a test or the
  console.

items_test _test_armour (the slot, a six-slot record, pick-up into the pack, a
hand refused and said, worn and weighed, a knife refused, taken off); the
tests that counted six slots count seven. Wire: a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 34
(opened by 620), the seventh slot and worn. No new class_name.

repair lost points but can't raise past the current tier. No decay over time.
Tiers change her behaviour, not just a number: wary hesitates and refuses
risky orders; close follows; devoted takes the lead when asked and protects
you aggressively. Damage never costs loyalty." And (10:xx, 2026-10-23): "i
can't take decisions that i dont even have the base function in game yet",
so it is built on the draft numbers and tuned from the cut checklist. The
coordinator settled the two readings from his words: only devoted takes the
lead, and crossing into devoted needs a milestone (trust stops one short).

- companion_traits.json "bond" is now tables: "deeds" names each raise's tier,

  bandaging; trust 1 up to 5: tended (bandaged by her player under a third of

## 622, combat's side: armour turns arrows and thrusts, and weighs on the breath

Jeff's draft values from items' design (C:/dev/review/armour/design.md, section 4), the
coordinator's step 2. Combat reads the worn kind's stats through items' World.worn_armour.

- **Arrows.** World.shoot, after a raised shield's guard: World.armour_turns(target,
  amount, "deflect_shot") turns that share of the shot's damage, rounded, and lets at
  least 1 through. Mail 0.25, plate 0.5.
- **Thrusts.** A blow whose verb is a backstab (the dagger) or a reach (the spear) is
  marked pierce on its Hit. In _resolve_hits, after the guard, its damage goes through
  armour_turns with "deflect_pierce": mail 0.2, plate 0.3. A cut, a knockback or a
  knockdown is not turned.
- **Breath.** _regen_stamina gives a breath times World.armour_breath(entity), which is
  1 − the armour's kg / 100: leather 0.94, mail 0.9, plate 0.8, robes 0.98. The fraction
  is carried by the breath's count, with no new state: floor(rate × (n + 1)) −
  floor(rate × n) for the nth breath, so plate's 1.6 a tick gives 1, 2, 2, 1, 2 and so on.
  It is the server's alone (stamina replicates; no client predicts regen).
- **Not yet.** Robes' aura waits for the staff kit. range_steps and draw are items'.

Headless numbers (combat_test _test_armour):

| worn | 10-point shot | 10-point thrust | breath, 30 ticks from empty |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 10 | 10 | 60 |
| leather, robes | 10 | 10 | (0.94, 0.98 of bare) |
| mail | 7 | 8 | 54 |
| plate | 5 | 7 | 48 |

A 1-point shot still does 1 in plate. A spear's 10-point thrust does 7 in plate; a
sword's cut does 10. All numbers are drafts for Jeff to tune in levels/items.json.

## 644. A client-only release from a branch off the last tag (release_client -Hotfix)

Jeff, 2026-10-23: v0.1.169's low camera (623) shipped a wrong indent that snapped bodies under it
and froze far ones without it, while main already ran revision 34 (620) ahead of the box, so no
release cut from main could join the box. He chose a client-only hotfix built from the v0.1.169
tag with the fix cherry-picked, over a full cut with a deploy.

`tools/release_client.ps1 -Hotfix` releases a branch off the last release's tag: it skips the
check that the commit has origin/main in it, and pushes its commit to origin's
`hotfix/<tag>` branch, not to main; the tag and the GitHub release are as for any release (the
newest is the launcher's Latest). Main then takes the hotfix's `## v<tag>` CHANGELOG section,
moving the fix's bullet out of `## Unreleased`, and version.txt at the hotfix's version, so its
next cut is numbered past it (v0.1.170 hotfix/v0.1.170, main's next v0.1.171).

Only for a client-only fix whose protocol equals the box's: a hotfix tree's `--print-protocol`
must read the box's, its sound store must match the tag's takes.json (no take moves until it
is published), and it runs land.sh like any cut. Anything server-side waits for main's next
cut. Main stays the only line of development: the hotfix commit is a cherry-pick of one that
landed on main first.

## 573 amended (2): the Hall waits for the companion (enemy-ai's side)

Jeff on v0.1.169: "draugr door closes to quickly companion can't get in". The coordinator's
ruling: the Hall's door waits for the first player's companion while she comes along.

- `Draugr._tend_hall`: the first living player into his lair while he sits shuts the Hall, as
  before, unless their companion is coming (`_companion_coming`). Then it waits, at most
  `DOOR_WAIT_TICKS` (50, 5 s) from that player's coming in, and shuts once she is in, has stopped
  coming, or the time is up, whether she is in or not. Nobody left in the lair while it waits
  starts it over.
- Coming: a Companion whose keeper is that player, up and not downed, outside the lair and within
  `DOOR_WAIT_CELLS` (6) of it (`_cells_from_lair`, Chebyshev to its room), and no farther off than
  `COMING_TICKS` (10) ago. "No farther" rather than "nearer" (companions: she trails 2 to 5 cells
  and a doorway bump or a corner can hold her distance flat for a second). Never one told to wait
  (`stays_put()`), with an order ("wait", "rest", "watch"), on an errand, pulling back or fleeing
  (RETREAT): companions' fields, read as they stand, nothing new on her side.

monster_test `_test_hall_waits`: she comes along 4 off and the Hall shuts as she is in; she stands
4 off and it shuts at 50 ticks; told to wait, it shuts at once. Server only, protocol unchanged,
no new class_name.

## 580 amended: the dead at their graves sit up for a foe in sight (enemy-ai's side)

Jeff on v0.1.169: "not enough skeletons in the ossuary and the ones that are are lying down or
stuck in their niches". Dungeon's data: each skeleton walks to a grave (a dead-end cell) and lies
there (547), the barrow laying them deepest first, so he passed lying skeletons that never rose.
Dungeon raises the count (14, a draft) and spreads them by band; the coordinator approved
enemy-ai's rule for the lie.

- One lying at its grave gets up when a foe of its side (`_may_fight`: a player, a kept
  companion, a resident or monster its side fights) comes within its `sight_range` and it sees
  them (`Monster._waking_foe`: no cone, lying any way; a barrow layer's dead see in the dark).
  It rises as when the curse renews (`rise`: it keeps its grave, GUARD there), turned to that one,

- The draugr's rest holds (`_under_rest`, factored out of `_mind_the_rest`): while it lasts, one
  stilled, or lying at its grave in a zone under his rest, never wakes, whatever comes. The rest

## 645. A room keeper's leash is its room

Jeff on v0.1.169 and again on v0.1.170: "draugr no longer walks but has a long reach", "lair
didn't seem like it changed at all". Found by enemy-ai's repro on a freshly generated
barrow_lair, the draugr's real spec on his throne cell, and a player walking in and striking, or
keeping 2 to 4 cells off. He took plain steps after a moving player, so physics' chain did not
root him. But his leash (his row's 8, 12 for a bold one) is measured from where he took up the
fight (`Monster._post`), his throne at the back of a 32 x 22 hall. Past 12 cells he gave up and
turned home, the pact or the blow set him on again, and he hovered about 12 cells out. The hall's
door is about 18 cells from the throne, so a player near it was never walked to and was reached
only by his throw (6 to 8 cells) and his rush (603): "doesn't walk, long reach".

- `Monster._beyond_leash`: a room keeper (`keeps_room`, with a room: its level's anchor round
  its home, `room_of`) is beyond its leash only once out of its room, however far it came. A
  monster with no room keeps the distance from where it took up the chase, unchanged.
- Every room keeper: the draugr in his Hall and the barrow's altar guards alike. Its room already
  bounded whom it sees and threatens (`threatens`, `_nearest_visible_target`); now it bounds how
  far it chases too.

## 607 amended: a lunge and a rush read the ground

Combat's ask before its feel pass, approved by the coordinator (2026-10-22). Each cell of a
lunge (596) or a rush (604) takes its time (lunge_ticks_per_cell / its drive u) times
ground_drag for the cell it enters. Its speed in that cell, step_velocity, is that cell's speed,
the line over that cell's time. A braced spear and a body met in that cell feel the slowed speed:
a collision's given and kept terms use u / drag. The ground does not spend its drive: u is
unchanged past the cell, so a charge picks up again on open ground, unlike a slide, which spends
its speed on the ground for good. Hits on a rush still take from u (604). Open level ground is 1,
so every existing number stands; a draugr charging through a ford is easier to stop there, which
combat reads as right. Server sim only, no new rule, protocol unchanged.

tests/physics_test: a 120 kg rush over 7 cells, 2 of them ford, takes 9 ticks, its speed 0.5 in
the ford and 1 past it.

## 604 amended: a rush is tended only in its own zone

The draugr standing still in the live lair (Jeff, v0.1.170), approved by the coordinator. World.step
runs _step_zone for each awake zone, and each zone keeps its own tick, terrain and occupancy
(enter swaps them), but 604's _rushers is one dictionary for the world. Every awake zone's step
tended every rush, so a rush's cell could be taken under another zone's step: read against that
zone's walls (it ended "wall" there), with its next_move_tick set on that zone's clock (hours
ahead of a lair asleep since boot, so the monster could not step again). _tend_rushes now skips
a rusher whose zone is not zone.name, as the other zone-wide tenders do; combat's boss tenders
take the same skip (603 amended (2)). Server sim only, protocol unchanged.

tests/physics_test: two zones awake with a player each, the other 5000 ticks ahead; a 120 kg rush
in the lair runs its 5 cells on the lair's clock and arrives, its next step never on the other's
clock. Before the fix it ended "wall" after 1 cell, at the other zone's tick 5001.

## 602 amended: telegraphs drawn smooth, and the rule they keep

Jeff, on v0.1.169: "draugr abilities should be in a smooth pattern like a cone similar to
archery, not blocky tiles." The coordinator's ruling: the sim keeps deciding in cells, and
the drawn shape is honest about them. Combat's side; ui draws it (623's fight reads, (a)).

- **The rule every telegraph keeps:** a body is struck exactly when its cell's centre, where
  its feet stand, is inside the drawn shape. A later telegraph's shape must be one that
  Telegraph.outline draws to this rule.
- **Telegraph.outline(shape) -> PackedVector2Array:** the drawn shape as a polygon in cells
  about the origin cell's centre, its points in order round it. A cone is its sector at
  length + REACH_SLACK and its half-angle (+0.001 rad, as cells() reads it), back to the
  origin. A ring is whole, with its hole just outside the inner radius. A line is a band of
  half its width (less LINE_EDGE) out to length + REACH_SLACK. Arcs are cut so a chord falls
  at most ARC_SAG (0.001 cell) short of its arc, under the nearest a centre comes to a reach
  (0.0625 / (2 x reach)), so no centre sits between them. Ui meshes it from the source's cell
  centre and masks the fill to the sent cells, so walls, closed doors and their shadows
  (World.telegraph_cells) cut it along their own edges.
- **A line's cells change.** They had been the cells that half-cell steps along the line
  rounded to. They are now every centre strictly inside the band, nearest first, so the
  drawn band holds exactly them. Straight and diagonal lines take the same cells as before.
  A slanted line can now strike a body it used to miss, or miss one it used to catch. The
  draugr's 8-cell throw:

| aim | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 20 degrees | (1,0) (1,1) (2,1) (3,1) (4,1) (4,2) (5,2) (6,2) (7,2) (7,3) | (1,0) (2,1) (3,1) (4,1) (5,2) (6,2) (7,3) |
| 30 degrees | (1,1) (2,1) (3,1) (3,2) (4,2) (5,3) (6,3) (6,4) (7,4) | (1,1) (2,1) (3,2) (4,2) (5,3) (6,3) (6,4) (7,4) |
| 60 degrees | (1,1) (1,2) (2,3) (2,4) (3,4) (3,5) (3,6) (4,6) (4,7) | (1,1) (1,2) (2,3) (2,4) (3,5) (3,6) (4,6) (4,7) |

  The cells dropped are those whose centre lies more than half a cell off the line (the old
  rounding's stair steps). The line stays unbroken at every angle, one or two cells a column.
  Use an odd width for a wide line: an even one puts centres on its edge when straight.
- **Nothing on the wire.** The "telegraph" message already carried the shape beside the
  cells, so enemy-ai's moves need no new data.

combat_test _test_telegraph_outline: 2,543 cones, rings and lines at 72 angles and on the
axes, every centre about them inside the outline exactly when it is struck (a centre within
a hundredth of a cell of the drawn edge is let be); a line at 30 degrees in order, banded and
unbroken. Godot's Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon misreads some of these fine circles, so the
test counts crossings itself. Server and pure geometry; protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 603 amended (2), combat's side: a boss is tended on its own zone's tick

Jeff's top find on v0.1.170, "the draugr doesn't walk", traced by physics: each zone keeps its
own tick (World.enter swaps it in), but the draugr's moves (_boss_moves), his axe (_axes) and
every wind-up (_winders) are held world-wide. With a second zone awake, that zone's step could
land his spin or throw on its own clock, or arm him from its own ground. His next_move_tick then
stood on the other zone's clock, and he did not walk again.

- _tend_boss_moves (and _tend_charge, which it calls), _tend_disarmed and _tend_wind_ups now skip
  a body whose zone is not the zone stepping, as the other world-wide tenders already did
  (_tend_buffs, _tend_wounds, the downed). Its own zone's step tends it on its own tick.
- _tend_wind_ups (392) had the same gap for anyone's wind-up, a player's too; it takes the same
  skip.
- Physics' _tend_rushes takes the same skip under 604 amended.

combat_test _test_other_zone_waits: another zone 1000 ticks ahead steps; his spin and his
wind-up do not land and his axe is not handed back; in his own zone the spin lands as ever. It
fails three checks without the skip. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 625: a bandage refused says why; the patient's step breaks it off

Jeff, playing v0.1.169: "I can't bandage Pip, Pip seems lazy at bandaging.
Check play test dialogue. Just says "fine". ... If target moves it
interrupts." The finding: "Fine." is 616's stock word (ORDER_ACKS, picked by
her name's hash: Pip's and Nix's is "Fine."), said when her voice has not
answered within ORDER_ACK_TICKS of a plain order. The bandage then failed
(most often World.calm: a monster within BANDAGE_SAFE, or either hurt within
BANDAGE_CALM_TICKS) and the reason went only to her voice, which was slow or
silent; a player's own refused bandage showed nothing at all.

- World.bandage_refusal(by, patient): try_bandage's checks in its order as a
  reason, "" if none: gone, not_beside, no_wound, mending, busy, no_kit,
  hurt_now (calm's hurt half), not_safe (its monster half).
- Her words, at once, no model (companion_traits "bandage_says", drafts; a
  "_self" key for her own wound): Companion._say_bandage. 616's obey checks
  the reasons when it reads the order (no_kit, no_wound, mending, hurt_now,
  not_safe), so the line comes before the stock word could; at the patient
  (_errand_do) a try_bandage that fails, and a bandage broken off, say theirs
  too. Her voice is told as narration only (no second ask), so she does not
  speak twice. The stock word stays for every other order; a refused bandage
  is no longer covered by it.
- A player's own: "bandage" and "apply_item" (593) that fail send
  Main._tell_bandage_refused, the reason worded for them (BANDAGE_REFUSED,
  "You can't bandage Pip: a monster is too near."), to that player alone as a
  Server party line (the channel of 622's slot refusals); a bandaging of theirs
  broken off, "Your bandaging broke off: Pip moved." (_tell_bandage_broke).
- The patient's first step off their cell breaks it off (Jeff's rule):
  try_bandage keeps "patient_tile", _tend_wounds breaks on a change, for
  players and companions alike, through the same broken-off branch as every
  other break (so pc-character's tending clears there too).
  World.bandage_broke_why names the cause for both sayings: patient_moved,
  moved, hurt, not_safe, gone.
- Badly hurt with a foe at her (the reflex), a bandage errand she drops is
  said too ("low": "Not now. I have to get clear of it first.").
- The box's day (release's grep, counts and wording only): 3 plain bandage
  orders, all done; 11 bandage errands, 10 done, 1 dropped "you are badly hurt"
  (said nothing: now "low"); 7 bandages begun, all finished; one "Fine." all
  day, the stock word. A player's own refused bandage leaves no line at all,
  which is where "can't bandage Pip" went. Her voice answered in a median
  456 ms and said 72 of 97 lines: errand reports are not shortened to "fine",
  so the errand prompt is left as it is.

tests: companion_test _test_bandage_words (the reasons, no kit and not safe
said at once and no stock word after, the step breaking it off with "hold
still"). Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 646: a joined client paces a one-cell change by its arrival (the draugr's rush drawn at half pace)

The coordinator's check after enemy-ai's draugr leash fix (2026-10-23): does a rush or
an axe charge draw as a slide on a joined client? It did, never a jump, but at half pace:
a mirror is told only the tile, so _mirror_tile_changed queued every one-cell change as a
slide of the body's own step (World.step_ticks, 4.5 ticks for a draugr), a cell a tick
or not; the next cell could not start until that slide ended (350: a slide is never cut
short), and _catch_up shortens a late one to half at most (CATCH_UP_SPEED). A draugr's
8-cell rush (a cell a tick, 604) was drawn over 20 ticks and stood on its last cell 12
ticks after the server, its blow a second before its body.
- Now, when a one-cell change arrives and the slide before it would end more than a tick
  after this arrival (and is not a present push), the server is stepping the body faster
  than its walk: the slide before is paced to end at this arrival's tick (a queued one
  takes the gap since its own arrival; the one on screen goes on from where it was drawn
  at the display clock last drawn, _drawn_shown, never a jump), and this one takes the
  smaller of its step and that gap, a tick at least.
- A plain walk, whose steps arrive as the slide before ends, is untouched (the within-a-
  tick chaining rule keeps it); so is a push (present slides are left alone), and a step
  that arrives late.
mirror_test _test_a_rush_is_drawn_as_a_slide (8 cells a cell a tick: every sample moves,
none faster than a cell a tick, there within the display delay plus two ticks; a 6-tick
walker whose next step comes three ticks in is hurried to a cell in three, never faster,
and ends on its tile); the walk, fast-walker, corner, push, overtaken and stall checks
guard the rest. Client only, protocol unchanged.

## 591, terrain's side: the felled forest drawn

maps' Clearing (591, maps' side) fells a woodlot's edge trunks and grows
them back a stage a season. This is how the view draws them (the
coordinator's approval of the design).
- At a build the felled cells are land (maps lays them in terrain["floor"]
  before the view is built), so the forest grows round them as it does
  round any land: no tree on them, and the ring and 575's edge curve follow
  the new outline. Client3D._clearing holds each cell's stage as drawn
  (terrain["clearing"]), and _dress_clearing adds its props:
  - stump: tree.stump on its dirt;
  - grass: the grass's scatter;
  - scrub: thick, tall grass (SCATTER_SCRUB), with a plant.bush SCRUB_BUSH
    of the time;
  - saplings: two or three tree.small at CLEARING_SAPLING of a tree's
    height, which fade as trees do.
  Dead wood and the bush are drawn only once their slots have art
  (_deadwood_drawn).
- Live, through Client3D.clearing_changed(terrain, cells), which Main calls
  when a "clearing" message comes:
  - A stage changed on the land swaps the cell's props, sets its ground's
    kind texel (_set_ground_kind, the kinds texture kept) and draws its
    chunk's scatter again (_rescatter, each chunk's MultiMeshes kept). No
    rebuild.
  - A fell takes the cell's tree (or a sapling or dead wood on it) away at
    once and leaves its stage's props.
  - A regrowth takes the props away and puts a tree back.
  - A fell or a regrowth moves the outline (the forest's ring, the edge
    curve, the ground). That redraws only at a zone load, never mid-visit
    (the coordinator's ruling, amending its earlier rule of a redraw once
    no player sees the cell). The reason: the redraw is a whole rebuild,
    which freezes the view 1 s on the hills and 3.5 s on the wilds wherever
    the player stands, and the plants round them grow back in after it.
    Until then a felled edge cell shows its stump on the forest floor.
    Don't schedule a full rebuild to "fix" this. If the ring ever needs to
    move while people watch, that is an incremental rebuild (perf's), not
    a scheduled full one.
  - A grown forest's trees (467) follow at the redraw, not live: no town
    stands in the forest level.
view_test _test_clearing: four edge trunks inside the hills or the wilds, one stage each,
with no tree on any and each on the land's side of the edge; each stage's
props, and scrub's tall grass. Live, with no rebuild: grass from a stump;
a fell (its tree gone at once, the land's at the next build); a regrowth
(a tree at once). Client only, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.

## 580 step 3, terrain's side: a dais drawn as a dais

The coordinator approved dungeon's halls dressed (580 step 3); the Hall of
Fallen Souls has a dais 12 x 4 one level up, its whole front row stairs
climbing onto it. Indoors that step was drawn as a cliff's rock face.
- On an indoor level with no relief given, an edge between two floors
  exactly one level (0.5 m) apart is art-kit's dais.edge in place of a cliff
  face (Client3D._is_dais, _add_dais_edge from _add_cliffs; _cliff_edges
  still lists it). Where the low cell is a stair climbing onto the dais,
  the piece is dais.steps.
- Both pieces are in buildings' edge frame: along z, +x the low side, the
  origin on the low floor at the edge's middle. Each is turned so +x points
  down off the dais, and carries its slot as meta "slot".
- A stair onto a dais is not a ramp: _shape_ramps leaves it flat
  (_dais_stairs) so the ground doesn't poke through the steps piece.
  _height_in walks it up the steps, flat to their foot (DAIS_STEPS_REACH,
  0.624 m from the edge) and then up to the dais at the edge.
- What stays a cliff:
  - every step outdoors;
  - a drop of more than one level;
  - an edge down to void or water;
  - every step if either piece has no art yet (a placeholder);
  - every step on a level with a relief.png (the coordinator accepted this
    narrowing). The reason: the sample is indoor and its relief's one-level
    steps are rock ledges, not built daises. A built hall that is ever
    given a relief.png draws its dais as rock. dungeon keeps the Hall on
    height.png and knows the rule.
- The outer corners, where two edge pieces meet, are to be checked in the
  Hall's shots after the all-clear; a corner piece is art-kit's if needed.
view_test _test_dais: an in-memory stone hall with the dais and its stair
row. It checks 32 pieces, 12 of them steps on the front, each turned off the
dais and with no cliff face; the stairs flat and walked up; the same map
outdoors as cliffs; the sample with no dais. Client only, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.
## 580, terrain's side: the damp level's look

Jeff on the barrow's third layer: "damp and dark, human eyesight barely
lights it up, its too moist to light lamps". The coordinator's ruling: the
level key "damp" (level.json; dungeon sets it on barrow_lair), the sim
environment's (a286f09d: Fields.carried_reach halved, two cells; Level
quenches torches, lanterns and fire on it), the look terrain's.

- Under "damp" (_apply_sky, indoors): the zone's ambient DAMP_AMBIENT
  (0.4) of itself and lerped toward DAMP_COLD; a faint cold exponential
  haze (DAMP_FOG, DAMP_FOG_DENSITY 0.02) all but black, so it darkens with
  distance (a lighter fog lifted the dark to a flat blue-grey in the first
  shots), only what a lantern lights showing through it.
- Each carried lantern (player, companion) at the sim's reach:
  PLAYER_LIGHT_RANGE times Fields.carried_reach(damp) over CARRIED_REACH
  (6 m, 3 m when damp), at DAMP_LANTERN (0.75) of its energy; set as a
  puppet's lantern is made and again for every puppet when a level is
  built (_size_lantern), so walking down into the lair shrinks it.
- The floor darkens by the sim's light already (floor_brightness on
  Fields), so it follows environment's rule with nothing more. The soft
  scatter (tufts, flowers, reeds) did not: it kept full light, green
  against the near-black floor (the coordinator, on the first shots). Now
  indoors each cell's brightness as the floor draws it is an L8 image over
  the mask's cells (_publish_floor_shade, written by _shade_floor), the
  global shader uniform "floor_shade" with "floor_shade_rect"
  (project.godot's shader_globals), and scatter.gdshaderinc darkens by it
  as the ground does; outdoors (the sky lights the plants) and in glimpses
  none. Stones and roots (a plain material) are as before.
- No flames to hide: the level holds none once Level quenches them.
- No live plants indoors. Jeff, answering the damp-lair ask: "moss and
  spiderwebs for decor, no live plants". The coordinator: plants are gone
  from dungeons altogether, not just unlit. Terrain's scatter was the only
  thing growing there (grass tufts on stone, flowers and tall grass on an
  indoor grass cell). Indoors it now lays only SCATTER_INDOORS (stones)
  on every ground but grass, each kind's rolls unchanged so the stones
  stand where they did. The coordinator kept the stones: a barrow floor
  with a few reads better than bare. Grass indoors keeps its plants,
  because a level only has it when laid on purpose: every dungeon floor is
  stone, and the sample's yard is grass and tall grass. This covers every
  indoor level, damp or not. The barrow's decor is moss and
  spiderwebs: art-kit makes the pieces and dungeon places them.

view_test _test_damp_look: the barrow made damp: the ambient a share of
the zone's, a haze, its lanterns at 3 m; not damp, 6 m and no haze;
indoors the scatter's floor shade each cell's as drawn, outdoors none;
indoors no plant in the scatter, outdoors the tufts as before.

## 608 amended, environment's side: the hidden niche's draft

Jeff wanted the barrow's hidden door to leave clues: "you feel a cool draft coming from one of the niches". Dungeon leads 608 amended (the server's party line from the hidden entry, sound's whisper, art-kit's footprints); this is the draft you see. Approved by the coordinator as designed with dungeon.

- Client3D._add_hidden_niche gives the hidden niche's holder a "Draft" (_make_draft): one GPUParticles3D in the holder's own frame, +x into the room as the wall pieces are placed, so it moves with the niche each generation and nothing elsewhere can fake it. DRAFT_PUFFS (7) faint puffs DRAFT_SIZE (0.7) across rise from a thin box along the cracked wall's foot, no higher than DRAFT_LOW (0.45 m): a draft hugs the floor. They drift DRAFT_SPEED (0.22 to 0.34 m/s) into the room, sinking a little with a slow waver along the wall, swell and fade over DRAFT_SECONDS (4 s), about a cell and a half.
- Lit, not unshaded (the falls' mist's material, now Client3D._soft_puff for both): on a dark barrow layer it shows only where a lantern or torch lights it, so you find it by holding your light to the niches; it never glows across the room to give the door away. No shadows cast.
- _show_hidden_niche: while the niche's Door is shut the cracked wall and the draft; once open the open niche and the draft stops (its last puffs fade as they go); shut again, it comes back. _sync_doors calls it from the Door's replicated open state.

## 623, environment's side: the weather and the horizon under the low camera

Jeff on the low camera (623, ui's side): "amazing... well worth the change". Ui's entry left the seams it showed to environment with terrain: the storm's haze per unit, the fog planes' edges, the rain box and the cloud decal's edge, and the sky under the haze. Designed here and approved by the coordinator; under the ortho camera everything stays as it was.

- The haze: weathered_look now gives the weather's share of the fog density on its own (fog_weather). Client3D.hazed_density scales that share by CAMERA_DISTANCE / the camera's distance under the low camera, with LOW_FOG on top. The aim then reads as clear or as hazy as in ortho (the share was tuned for a camera 40 off; at 20 it read thinner near), and a storm hides the hills while clear air shows them. It is set every frame (_set_haze), since the wheel moves the camera.
- The sky: under the low camera, Client3D.hazed_horizon draws the sky's horizon toward the haze's colour as fog, rain or cloud thicken (cloud at 0.6), so the land fades into the sky with no band: grey under overcast, the fog's in fog. The sky's top is the day's as ever.
- WeatherView.set_view(low, the camera's place, the way it looks along the ground) sizes the weather for the view when the camera mode turns:
  - Rain and snow fall in a box LOW_BOX (34 across, 70 deep) from the camera out along the view, turned to it. Their drops are LOW_DROPS (1.5) times as many at most, not by the area (2 times). The roofs' heightfield covers that box (78 square at 512) instead of following the camera.
  - The fog's three layers are LOW_FOG_WIDE (3) times as wide (216 m), centred LOW_FOG_AHEAD of FOG_SIZE (54 m) ahead of the aim. Their shader fades them to the rim (rim 1), so no edge shows; in ortho rim is 0 and they are whole, as before.
  - The clouds' decal is LOW_CLOUD_TILES (9) periods wide (324 m) instead of 3, its texture built once a size from the one tile (_cloud_texture, blitted). Its edge is then at least 144 m from the aim, where the haze has the land. The design said a distance fade; Godot's decal fade dims the whole decal by its centre's distance, not by the pixel's, so it would have dimmed every cloud shadow near the view. The wider decal does the same work.
- The sun's shadows under the low camera (LOW_SHADOW_DISTANCE 150 in two splits, ui's) stay. Perf measured them (2026-10-23, CPU ms / GPU p95 ms): ortho's 70 in one 1.12 / 3.08, 120 in two 1.28 / 3.17, 150 in two 1.31 / 3.16-3.28, 150 in four 1.55 / 3.42. 150 in two costs about 0.2 ms of CPU over ortho and nothing that shows on the GPU, and four splits cost more for no gain the view needs; the coordinator agreed to keep it.

weather_test _test_low_view: ortho's haze is the look's; under the low camera the storm's haze to the aim matches ortho's; clear air gets only LOW_FOG; the horizon is the sky's in clear air and the haze's in a storm; the rain's box runs deep from the camera ahead with at most 1.5 times the drops; the fog's layers are 216 m wide, ahead of the aim, faded to their rims; the clouds' decal is 324 m; back in ortho everything is as it was. Client only: protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 647. Moss and webs in the barrow

Jeff on the dressed halls: "moss and spiderwebs for decor, no live plants".
The coordinator approved the shape; art-kit's four slots (678fe3a4:
prop.moss_patch with three variants, prop.moss_strip, prop.web_corner and
prop.web_niche with two each) came first; terrain draws them ("647,
terrain's side", with no scatter sown in a level that is not outdoor).

- Level data, the niches' shape: level.json `"decor"` lists `[x, y, dx, dy,
  kind, variant]` entries; `Level.decor_from` reads them into terrain
  `"decor"` as `{cell, out, edge, kind, variant}` and holds each kind to its
  place: a patch flat on a floor cell, a strip along a wall edge, a corner
  web where two wall edges meet, a niche web across an open niche of kind
  "a" or "c" only (variant 1: never the hidden door's mouth, whose draft is
  its tell and a web there would lie; never a sealed slab, which has no
  mouth). The misplaced are said and left out, as a bad niche is.
- The templates hold a few by hand (plan_sheet's BARROW_DECOR and
  LAIR_DECOR: the first hall's two entry corners and a strip of moss at its
  south wall; the damp hall's moss along its walls between the furniture,
  patches off the ways and its four corners webbed), and
  `Regen.generated_config` keeps them inside the anchors as it keeps the
  buildings, a niche web excepted (the niches are re-rolled each
  generation, so the roll hangs that generation's own).
- `Regen.decor_of` rolls the rest by the generation's seed (its own salt,
  the layout's rng untouched, as the niche rolls do) over the floor outside
  the anchors in a set order: moss strips on a share of the wall feet by
  the level's damp (`"damp": true` 0.35, the Ossuary 0.15, the first hall
  0.05; the deep band half as much again, the low rooms), patches on open
  floor at 0.4 of the moss share, webs in 0.3 of the corners and across
  0.25 of the open niches; never a link's, a marker's or a spawn point's
  cell, and never a cell the ways run through: `Labyrinth.generate` records
  its paths dict on the map it returns (`LevelMap.extras`, a generator's
  notes for Regen, never in the images, taken along by `copy()`), the one
  new thing on the editor's class.
- `Regen.depth_frame`, `band_at` and `entrance_of` are the graves' band
  measure factored out, shared with the roll; `graves_of` unchanged in
  what it writes.
- No plant is laid: the barrow grows moss on stone and webs in the dark, and
  nothing green.

## 624, economy's side: the town sheet's answer

ui's town status sheet (624) asks the server how a town is doing; economy answers.

- The "town_sheet" command {town} (Main.ask_town_sheet) is answered by a new
  "town_sheet" message to the asker alone. It answers only for a town in the
  player's zone or among their known places; any other town gets {town, why:
  "you don't know that town"}. ui asks while the sheet is open (every 10 s is
  fine); nothing is pushed.
- Main.town_sheet(town) holds:
  - town, name (the Holdings place's), population (residents), trades
    {trade: residents, by first trade}, treasury (the store's gold);
  - officials [{name, trade, paid}], paid false while the town owes them a
    wage (528 amended);
  - dole and hungry: residents not away whose last meal the town gave, or
    who went without (Production.note_meal); sick (Townsfolk.is_sick);
  - needs [{id, short, bring}]: each raw good in economy.json "comfort"
    but gold, below it. short is 1 − have / comfort, 0..1; bring is comfort − have,
    in the resource's own units. Worst first, then by id;
  - builds [{kind, progress}] (Towns.build_progress, 566), season
    (Season.name_at), day (Townsfolk.day_of), stage (591);
  - faction {name}: its holder's display name. mood is a word from its
    safety: "safe", "uneasy", "on guard". There is no player-town standing
    yet; that waits for a design of its own;
  - sought [{trade, where}] (613's wanted newcomers, where "" until placed),
    and next_stage {stage, needs [{what, have, need}]} ({} at the last
    stage).
- Towns.stage_short(town, need) lists what a stage lacks. Each entry's what
  is "residents", a standing kind, a trade, "gold" or "wood", in the rule's
  order. _meets is now stage_short empty, and Towns.next_stage reads the same
  list, so the sheet says what the stage turn checks.

## 622, economy's side: where armour comes from

The armour design, section 5 (C:/dev/review/armour/design.md; the
coordinator approved it; Jeff's draft values, which he tunes in play).

- Leather armour is made by the tanner from leather 2 (value 22). Robes are made
  by the weaver from cloth 3 (12). These are plain items.json "made" rows on
  items' 622 rows, made by the makers already there; each has stock 2 so a
  shelf doesn't drain the inn's leather or the loom's cloth.
- Plate is made by the smith from ore 8 (value 80, stock 1), and only once his
  town stands a forge and is a village or more. This is a new optional recipe field,
  made.needs {kind, stage}:
  - Items keeps it, and made_problem checks the kind is a building kind
    (Level.kinds) and the stage one of Level.STAGES.
  - Production's recipe filter skips a recipe with needs unless
    Production.town_has (town, needs) says yes; without it set, never.
  - Towns sets town_has to Towns.has_for_make: the kind standing (_stands)
    and the town's stage at or past the needed one, in rules' "stages" order.
  - The field is general, so the next gated make reuses it.
  - Before then plate comes only as loot (dungeon's rows).
- Mail is never made and nothing makes it appear. It has no recipe and no
  market sells it. A shirt reaches a shelf only fenced by Snagfin by night
  (586), and it is then sold by day at day_markup. It stays on the town's
  shelf, at every counter; "only at Snagfin's" waits for Jeff.

## 640, economy's side: the hill herders

Jeff: "herders exist as people". The coordinator approved this design; maps
lays the places and draws the folds (640, maps' side), art-kit makes the
fold, and lore names the herders (sought.md). The numbers are drafts,
built as drafted; the cut that ships them carries a tune line.

- Places: rules' herder.places names the hills' two refuge tags,
  herders_hut and hill_shieling, not a new place kind. Each Holdings place
  with one of those keys is a herder's holding of its own, as a healer's
  hut is (562).
  - Its store is keyed by the place id. It is no stockpile place, so a
    player can't bank there.
  - The herder never reads the place's holder, so the sought butcher and
    weaver sheltering there (613's "sought:<id>" holder) don't collide with
    him.
- The herder: a Production worker "herder:<place>" (trade herder), whose
  town is the place.
  - One comes to a place without one after herder.growth_days (3), with
    herder.start (4) sheep, named from herder.names (lore's Grim, Asa, Ketil,
    Thora, Ulf, Sigrun).
  - Never sought.
  - Production.outside counts herder.trade: no rent, no town needs.
- The drove: the place's "sheep" in the stockpile.
  - Each spring it lambs as the town's flock does (herder.lambs 0.6),
    toward herder.most (8).
  - Every herder.every (3) days, while the herder is home, they walk all but
    herder.keep (2) to Towns.drove_town: a town whose butchery stands and
    whose store holds under butcher.from sheep, in the place's own area
    first, then by id.
  - The fold's count drops at once, and the herder is away for
    herder.walk_steps (3000).
  - What the town doesn't buy comes home with them.
  - No such town: they stay home.
  - The town's autumn cull (590) stays; the drove is a second source.
- Economy.buy_drove(town, herder, count, food):
  - Buys as many as the treasury pays above gold_floor, at the store's buy
    price for sheep (raw_price x store.buy).
  - Never owes: the herder is not the town's.
  - The gold goes to the herder as a sale (taxed).
  - With it they buy herder.food (2) food from the store at raw_price for
    their keep. It is eaten, and the gold comes back to the treasury.
  - Main sets Towns.drove to it.
- The folds:
  - Towns.folds(area) returns place id -> sheep at home.
  - Towns.folds_changed (a herder comes, lambs, a drove leaves, the herder
    comes home) sends the new "folds" message {counts} to every peer.
  - _send_towns sends a zone's folds to a peer arriving.
  - Maps' client draws min(count, 6) sheep in the fold as scenery. The town
    pasture's flock may later join the same map as "<town>:pasture".
- Saved: Towns.herders_to_dict under the snapshot's "herders", beside
  "towns". to_dict stays the towns alone, since nine callers read its keys
  as towns.
- Not built: the design let a raid take a herder. Raids take a town's
  residents, and a herder is no town's, so none is taken yet. With no
  herder, a place gets a new one after growth_days.

Jeff: "medicine man doesnt get lost, but there would be more than one, there
could be multiple huts that offer different potions". The coordinator
approved it.

  to the hut whose care they hold.

What is new:
- Each hut makes its own list. economy.json return.places.healers_hut.makes
  is looked up by the place's key, else its area, else "_default". The area
  is there because a hut a building makes carries its cell in its key.

    hut is maps' forest/healers_hut@45,31 (641, maps' side); until 642
    lands, the draught has no recipe and the hut makes the remedy alone.

    _workshop_makes, gates the recipe filter through Production.makes:

### 622, step 2, items' side: the bow under armour

- **range_steps** caps the step a drawn bow reaches: the last of its verb's
  steps at or under the armour's range_steps, at least the first
  (World.step_cap). With the hunting bow's [3, 5, 7, 9]: mail (7) holds at 7,
  plate (5) at 5, leather and robes (9) reach them all. draw_step,
  range_of and longest_range keep to it, so a monster or a view reading
  them sees the same reach, and the pull's pose is full at that step
  (World.draw_full_ticks).
- **draw** scales the bow's draw ticks beside a quick bow's strength
  (_draw_quick, now public as World.draw_quick, which Client3D's pull reads):
  leather 0.9 draws quicker, plate 1.1 slower. The cone (620) narrows with
  the same hold.
- Both read World.worn_armour from the replicated slots, so a client's
  prediction and the server's roll agree; a v0.1.169 client would not, so a
  line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 35 (release; 34 shipped first). items_test _test_armour (leather:
  19 ticks reach 9 cells, bare 7; plate: 5 at most, however long the hold).

## 642. The steadying draught

The second healer's hut (economy's 641) wanted a potion of its own, with an effect the
player can feel. The coordinator floated three; one is built.

- **steadying_draught** ("steadying draught", short "Steady"): the medicine man makes it
  from 2 herbs and an antler in 600 steps, a shelf of 3, stacks of 3 (draft values, built
  as drafted; the cut's checklist carries a tune line). Drunk, it puts a new buff kind on
  the drinker, **steady** (Items.BUFF_KINDS, shown "Steady"): amount 0.4 for 18000 ticks
  (30 minutes), held and renewed like any buff (add_buff).
- **World.spread_of** multiplies the cone of flight (620) by (1 - steady): the same hold
  is 40% narrower. Reach, draw time and the steps are unchanged. The factor applies
  after spread_at's floor, on purpose (pc-character asked): a steadied archer's narrowest
  cone is the floor times 0.6 (1.2 degrees on the hunting bow), so the draught still helps
  the one who holds to the settle. Enemy-ai's aim_spread clamp reads the verb's floor. Buffs replicate, so the
  client's drawn cone and the server's roll agree; a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 35
  (release), since an older client would draw the wider cone.
- **Held**: a night-sight draught. The sim's darkness only steers senses (monsters'
  dark_sight, is_lit), and players carry a lantern, so what a drinker would see is the 3D
  view's lighting (environment's). A "sight" buff kind waits until Jeff asks and the
  lighting side is routed.
- **Dropped until the cold hurts**: a warming draught. Season.cold_at only turns rain to
  snow.

Economy lists steadying_draught in the new hut's makes (economy.json
return.places.healers_hut) once it is on main. items_test _test_steadying_draught. No new
class_name.

## 581. She leaves, and goes home to live

Jeff (2026-10-22): "companion keeps their blessings and abilities but goes
back to their home town to live and work their vocation ... companion
would never become an enemy". The coordinator approved the design
(C:/dev/review/companions/leaving_design.md), in steps: this one (she
leaves and goes home), then winning her favour back (581 amended) and
recruiting her again (581 amended (2)).

- When: her bond at the bottom step, apart (555's ladder, -7), or the
  last straw: companion_traits.json "leaving" "last_straw" (let_bleed, at
  sullen or colder). Main._bond's drops check it (_check_leaving) and set
  her record's "leaving" {deed, why, day}. Dead now (a let_bleed is her
  bleeding out), she leaves when she is next back.
- Main._leaving_tick, at a calm moment (World.calm: nothing hostile near
  her, neither she nor her player downed): her voice is asked past the
  rate limit ("You are leaving <player> for good, and going home to
  <town>: they <why>."), the party told ("Wren leaves you, and goes home
  to The Wilds."), a walk she was leading ended, and her player's things
  put down at their feet (_return_gear: a thing her player once carried
  that they did not name for her; her own things and named gifts stay
  hers, told "Wren leaves you the bundle of arrows.").
- She walks to the zone's nearest level link (Companion.leaving,
  leaving_to: she heeds no one meanwhile); there, or past walk_s (30 s,
  draft) and out of her player's sight, at most twice that, she is gone
  home: _rest_in_town to her home (her record's home place if still a
  town's store, else the first town), working her trade, with no party
  line of resting; her record "left" {day, deed, why, place}.
- Main._join_companion: one who left does not come: "Wren left you and
  lives in The Wilds now." She keeps her card, facts, marks (the blessing,
  her capabilities, 576), focus (577) and roads (551).
- Never hostile: a resident, as any companion resting in town. The legacy
  three the same. A town's faction switch is a later system.
