## 626. The bandage kneel

Jeff (playing v0.1.169): "Bandages should have a ruffling sound and a kneeling next to the target
animation. If target moves it interrupts." The coordinator approved pc-character's design; the
interruption is companions' (the patient's step), the ruffle sound's.

- **Who is bandaging, on every peer:** World's bandaging was the server's alone (bandage_changed
  never reaches a joined client; only the patient's mending replicated). `GridEntity.tending` is
  the name of the body it is bandaging (its own for itself), "" when not; a player's and a
  companion's replicate. try_bandage sets it; it is cleared when the bandaging is done, broken off
  (_tend_wounds), when either body goes (the removal path) and when the bandager is downed.
  Sound's ruffle reads it too.
- **The kneel** (Client3D): ACTIVITIES' "bandage" (Fixing_Kneeling, looped: the hands at work low
  in front), anyone's work while it tends (work_word), so the same _animate and _lay as a
  resident's work: it plays only while the body is still, any gait wins, so a shove or a step
  never fights it. Turned to the patient's cell (_tending_yaw) and leant 0.3 m toward it (the
  work's "toward", only while still), its hands at the patient's legs and middle; bandaging
  itself, the kneel as it faces. The patient stands as before.

it walks, not leant; cleared, it stands with its own facing. Wire: a line under revision 35
(open, unshipped), no bump. No new class_name. A shot of the pose follows the coordinator's
all-clear.

Amended (sound's find, reading tending for 627): a bandager downed (lay_downed, decision 544)
dropped its bandaging without breaking it off, so the patient kept mending 1 with no bandaging
behind it, and try_bandage refused it for good (live since 544). lay_downed now breaks it off as
_tend_wounds does: the patient's mending back to 0, bandage_broke_why "hurt" (the player's line and
the companion's words for being hurt), bandage_changed "interrupted". items_test: a bandager

## 591 amended (2): felled ground re-walls by the outline rule

A felled trunk's cell (591) turned floor, but the WALL edge the parse's outline rule had
put between floor and void stayed, in the walk and the view: a felled row couldn't be
stepped into and drew a brick strip along the old forest edge (terrain's find, live since
v0.1.168).

- **Level.parse** records which walls the outline rule alone made (terrain "outline",
  Dictionary[Vector3i, bool]); a wall with a wall pixel is authored and not in it.
- **Level.relay_outline(terrain, cells)** re-derives only outline walls and missing
  edges round the changed cells: WALL where floor meets non-floor (water aside), else
  OPEN. Authored walls are never touched. It updates terrain in place and returns the
  changed keys (OPEN meaning removed).
- **Clearing.apply** and **apply_cells** call it; apply_cells returns the changes.
  **World.set_edges(changes)** applies them to the walk (grid caches reset, fields
  told). Main applies them on the server inside the zone and on each client.
- The view takes them through **Client3D.clearing_walls(edges)** (terrain's half, to
  follow); until that method exists Main redraws the zone. rebuild_walls isn't used: it
  redraws whole lines without _add_walls' fence and rock skips.
- Economy's ruins (649) take the same path: change terrain["floor"], relay_outline,
  set_edges.

No wire change: the outline is parsed from the shipped level on both sides. level_test
_test_felled_walls (fell a row, step in, regrow, walled again). No new class_name.

## 591 amended (2), terrain's side: the felled ground's walls drawn again

Maps' half re-walls felled ground by the outline rule and hands the changed edges to the
view (Main calls Client3D.clearing_walls(edges) after clearing_changed, if the method is
there; till now it redrew the whole zone).

- **clearing_walls(edges)** draws the walls on those keys again through rebuild_walls,
  the rest of the room untouched. A felled row's walls against the land go; the forest's
  new edge round it is the outline, drawn as trees, never a wall.
- **rebuild_walls** now takes _add_walls' own skips (one rule, _edge_drawn: the outline
  outdoors, a fence's or a railing's edge, a rock's), so a redraw never puts back a wall
  the build left out. It stands the posts at the given keys' ends again too, even where
  the key is now open (a felled cell's), and puts a post only where a drawn edge meets it.
  Buildings' broken and rubble town walls, its other caller, keep their look: their
  keys are none of the skipped.
- **The outline as the forest stands now.** The build's land (_land) is fixed for the
  build, since the border's worker reads it, so _is_outline reads _on_land: a cell felled
  since the build (_clearing) is land, and one grown back to a trunk since (_grown_back,
  cleared each build) is the void, though _land still holds it.

view_test _test_clearing: no wall or post round the four felled cells at the build; a
live fell's changed edges drawn again with none round the cell; a live regrowth after a
build, its trunk's edges the outline again with no wall round it (the last two fail with
the build's land alone). Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 591 amended (step 2, maps): a town's plots

The growth loop (591; the coordinator's approval of maps' design
2026-10-23, with two amendments): a town's new building goes on a plot
laid on cleared ground, so a town grows as its forest is felled.
- Clearing.plot_for(zone, plot_class, toward) -> Rect2i: the class's
  footprint (Level.PLOT_CLASSES) with a ring of a cell round it for its
  path and footing (the ring's rect), nearest the town's store within
  PLOT_REACH (64), turned either way. Every cell is floor (the level's, or
  felled), not water, a building, a link or another plot's footprint, more
  than EDGE in from the map's edge, all of one height (Relief.LEVEL_M is
  above WALK_RISE: one height level); the footprint is off roads (a road
  may touch the ring) and PLOT_GAP (2) cells clear of any other footprint,
  standing building or wall (612, the coordinator: never a one-cell
  walkway between). Summed tables make each candidate a few reads. An
  empty Rect2i when nothing fits: the town fells more first; the woodcut is
  the only clearer.
- Clearing.facing_for(rect, plot_class, toward): the kind's +y toward the
  store, along the axis the footprint's turn allows.
- Clearing.lay_plot(zone, town, kind, rect, facing, use) keeps {town, kind,
  use (economy's record key, the kind), rect, facing, day} in the world
  snapshot's "plots", never the level overlay (the coordinator's rule for
  the clearing); its cells never grow back; plotted is told.
- A plot is staked ground, not a building (the coordinator): Clearing.apply
  lists a zone's plots in terrain["plots"] (plots_of's shape, kept out of
  level["buildings"]: buildings' 566 raises the kind on it from staked
  ground through its stages by the record, never finished from being laid),
  and lays each plot's kind building (Level.plot_building: its box at the
  footprint's front, across the middle, at the record's size, level 2
  large) in terrain["plot_buildings"] with its walls and door in the edges
  (Level.plot_edges); Fields counts it among the town's buildings, so its
  walls stay open until the record says they are up (566). A plot laid in a
  loaded zone does the same live (World.add_plot).
- Main: Towns.plot (town, kind) -> Rect2i and Towns.lay (town, kind, rect),
  set once economy's Towns has them (economy's side: asked before a kind is
  planned; empty, the kind waits for the next town tick). The "clearing"
  message gains "plots" ([{town, kind, use, rect: [x, y, w, h], facing:
  [dx, dy], size}]): the zone's all with "whole" (before "map"), else the
  one laid; a client lays them as the server does, at the told size.
- Known limit: a kind raised from small to large on a loaded zone keeps
  its small walls until the zone loads again.
tests: level_test _test_plots, an S plot on the field's grass, a second
two cells clear, none when the forest stands, one on felled forest, none
across a road, off a step in the ground, its cells never regrowing, the
snapshot round trip, applied as buildings with walls and a door.
PROTOCOL_REVISION 35 (a line under dungeon's, which opened it): the
"clearing" message's "plots".
No new class_name.

## 650. Far landmarks: the world plane

Jeff: "now we can have the castle show on the horizon, perhaps under a
mountain. the dark elven tower standing off in the distance". Terrain's
far layer draws what lies beyond a level's edge; the coordinator approved
terrain's answer on its data: world cells on one plane, not bearings, so
a landmark shifts against the land as you walk and lines up between
zones. This is the data (maps); terrain's drawing is "650, terrain's
side".
- levels/world_plane.json, read by Level.world_plane() (WORLD_PLANE):
  - zones: each outdoor level's origin, the world cell of its cell
    (0, 0), a cell a metre, and its height, the metres added to its own
    ground. The wilds at (0, 0); the castle (112, -24), its south row
    against the wilds' north edge, its link (16, 23) at world x 128 with
    the wilds' (128, 20); the hills (-96, 58), against the wilds' west
    edge, its link's row (70) the wilds' link row (128); the forest
    (256, 80), against the east edge, its link's row (48) the same 128.
    The levels' grounds were made apart (the hills 3.3 m above the wilds
    at their links, the forest 6.08 m and the castle 5.19 m below), so
    each zone's height puts its link's ground on the wilds' there.
    Indoor levels (barrows, lair, rooms) have none. Held joins when its
    level is laid.
  - landmarks: {id, slot (art-kit's far piece: far.castle, far.tower, later far.mountain, in art/kit/far/), at (a world cell), base
    (the world height it stands on, metres), facing}. The castle
    (far.castle at its yard's middle, (128, -12), facing south) and the
    tower over the mine (far.tower at (560, 600), facing west): no level
    holds the mine and lore says only that it lies far from the town, so
    it stands far to the south-east, away from the castle (north), the
    hills (west) and the forest's way on to the stronghold (east), across

## 633: the low-angle fight, 2: a click's slack beside a monster in screen terms

PICK_SLACK (0.45 ground units past a body's pick shape) shrank on screen with distance
under perspective. Client3D.pick_slack_at(at): under the low camera the slack is
PICK_SLACK_SHARE (0.025) of the screen's height at the body's depth from the camera, in
ground units (the frustum's height there is twice the depth by the tangent of half the
fov), never under PICK_SLACK; the ortho camera keeps PICK_SLACK. A fixed pixel count was
a hair on a 4K screen, hence the share. monster_near_ray picks the body nearest the ray as
a share of its own slack, so the ortho behaviour is exactly as before. view_test
_test_low_pick. Client only.

change eases over REACH_EASE (0.5 s) through every GeometryInstance3D's transparency
(_set_transparency: meshes, name, bar), the puppet hidden only once gone and drawn at once
from gone as it comes; a puppet just made beyond the edge is simply not drawn (no ghost on
a join); the camera off puts every puppet solid and forgets the easing. The sim's edge
(238) is untouched: the client eases only what it is sent. view_test _test_reach_ease.

## 635: the low-angle fight, 5: names under the low camera

Client3D._sync_name each frame under the low camera: a name's scale is max(1, its depth
over the camera's distance from the aim), so it is never smaller on screen than at the
aim; render priority 100 minus the depth, so the nearest draws over the farther; shown
past NAME_TILES (8) of the local player only for the party, the marked target, and a foe
(hunting, fighting or lately struck, as _fight_points counts one): name_shown. The ortho
camera's names untouched; the camera off restores scale, priority and visibility.
view_test _test_low_names.

## 649, maps' side: a plot dropped, so the forest takes it back

Jeff's "the forest overtakes": a ruin standing on a laid plot never grew
back, since a plot's cells never regrow (591 amended) and terrain's
unbuild (649, terrain's side) leaves a plot's cells alone. Maps owns the
plot, so maps drops it (the coordinator).

- **Clearing.unplot(zone, rect)**: the plot laid on rect (its ring's, as
  plot_for and lay_plot have it) dropped from Clearing.plots (and the
  snapshot's "plots"), its cells no longer kept from growing back, and
  **unplotted(zone, plot)** told; returns the plot, {} if none is laid
  there. A felled cell then grows back as any does; a level floor cell
  once terrain's unbuild hands it to the regrowth. **Clearing.plot_at(zone,
  cell)** finds the plot whose rect holds a cell, for unbuild.
- What a plot laid is kept so it can be taken off exactly:
  Clearing.lay_plots records the edges it added in its building's "laid";
  **Clearing.unlay_plot(terrain, rect)** takes the plot out of
  terrain["plots"], its building out of terrain["plot_buildings"] and those
  edges out (any changed since kept). World.add_plot records the same in
  its town building ("plot", "laid", "edges"), as Fields does for a plot
  building read at a zone's load; **World.unplot(level, rect)** drops the
  town building and its edges, standing or held down while its walls were
  not up (_walls_down), and resets the paths' step cache.
- Main._on_unplotted (the server): a loaded zone takes it off its walk and,
  if drawn, its terrain; the zone's peers get the "clearing" message with
  **"gone"** [plots, plot_wire's shape]. A client drops them from its told
  plots and, in that zone, off its terrain and walk; the view is drawn
  again as for a plot laid (buildings drops the plot's building on it).
- Who calls it: economy, when a ruin's record is dropped after its season;
  terrain's unbuild, for a plot whose rect its cells fall in, before it
  hands the cells to the regrowth.

Wire: a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 35 (the "clearing" message's "gone").
level_test _test_unplot (laid, dropped, off the terrain, grown back; live
off the walk and the town buildings; a client told it laid, then gone).
No new class_name.

## 649. Towns fall as well as rise (economy's side)

Jeff, answering draft-held-growth.md: "I would actually have towns be able
to "regress" not just make progress. say the population falls, the
resources can't keep up, the town is raided, the people captured..
buildings at the edge fall into disrepair and the forest overtakes, towns
start as a settlement with tents, everything needs to be built up to inn,
temple, smith, farms, livestock". The coordinator approved economy's design
with amendments. The other trees' parts land as "649, <tree>'s side":
buildings (the settlement's camp plot kind, disrepair and ruin looks),
terrain (Clearing.unbuild and build), maps (the settlement layout, a
fresh-world start), ui (the sheet's strain), lore (words).

Stages (Level.STAGES, economy.json stages):
- "settlement" comes first, below hamlet: tents and nothing standing. A
  town's first _stage_turn makes it one.
- Hamlet needs 4 residents, the field standing and wood 10.
- Village needs 8 residents, the temple, inn, forge and pasture (the
  town's livestock; its map piece is buildings' fold) standing, and a
  priest.
- _stage_turn still only raises. The fall is decline's.
- A town that seed_from gives the map's buildings and that has no stage
  yet starts at hamlet (the coordinator: not tents with a temple
  standing), and goes higher at once while it meets each next stage
  (Towns._seeded_stage). A saved stage is kept. Only a town with nothing
  seeded (a "start": "tents" world, or no map buildings) begins as a
  settlement.

Decline (economy.json "decline", Towns._decline, once a day per town):
- Strain: a town past the first stage gains a day of strain on a day it is
  - short of its stage's residents,
  - missing a needed standing kind because it is in disrepair or a ruin (a
    needed kind never built doesn't count, so a need added after a town
    reached its stage never drops it),
  - more than hungry_share (0.5) of its residents hungry while the hungry
    outnumber the food, meat and fish in the store.
  This is Jeff's list: the people fall, the resources can't keep up, raids
  and captives. The second soak showed why the store must be counted: the
  wilds town had food, but its treasury sat at the floor, so the dole
  couldn't feed people. Hunger with food in the store is a purse problem,
  not the town's. An unpaid official is gold, not one of Jeff's words, so
  it was dropped as a strain (coordinator's ruling).
  A resident carried off (Towns._take, _take_companion) adds captive_strain
  (3). A day with none of these takes a day off. At strain_days (10) the
  town falls one stage, never below the settlement, with a note naming
  why, and its strain starts again.
- Upkeep: every upkeep.every (14) days each building standing, damaged or in
  disrepair pays (the first time that many days after decline first sees
  the town, so a fresh world owes nothing before its first gathering) upkeep.cost (wood 1) times its level from the store. A
  building row's own "upkeep" overrides the cost, and {} wants none, so
  the settlement's camp keeps itself and no trade it can't have is needed.
  Upkeep is taken from the store by the town as a whole, not by a
  carpenter. Buildings pay nearest the store first (Towns.placed's
  distance), so when wood is short the edge goes owing first. Wood is
  gathered and paid for as ever; no gold is lost.
- The build reserve: a new build or raise starts only if the store keeps
  a round of upkeep after its cost (Production.keep_for, set to
  Towns.upkeep_due: each building's cost times its level). A repair or a
  roof may use the reserve. Without it, the first soak's wilds town
  (upkeep every 7 days, a hamlet's wood 20) put all its wood into
  building: it never became a hamlet, and the forge, kitchen, tannery and
  temple fell into disrepair by day 28. The woodcutter's 60 or so wood a
  month is the town's whole income (before 649 too), so the numbers were
  tuned (every 14, hamlet wood 10) and the reserve added, not the rule
  taken out.
- Disrepair: a building is neglected when its upkeep is owed, it is
  damaged, or none of its trade lives in town. After unkept_days (14)
  neglected days running it falls into disrepair (DISREPAIR). It is out of
  use: not standing, so no workshop and no stage credit. While in
  disrepair it loses a level each season (Season.season_days). At level 0
  it becomes a ruin (RUIN). _repair mends disrepair as it does damage,
  share 0.5 of the cost at its level.
- A ruin is kept for a season. Then its record goes, its kind is added to
  the town's "gone" list (seed_from never seeds the map's piece again; a
  new build takes it off), and Towns.ruined(town, kind, zone, cells) is
  told. Main gives the cells to terrain's Clearing.unbuild(zone, cells,
  day) once it exists, so they regrow from stumps to trunks.
- Towns.placed (Main._town_placed) gives a kind's world-map building of
  that use: its zone, its rect's cells, and its distance from the store.
  A building the map doesn't place counts as nearest and gives back no
  ground.
- Nothing falls on load: strain starts at 0, and saved states, owing,
  neglect, decay, ruin days, strain and "gone" are all kept.
- A fresh world: economy.json "start": "tents" makes seed_from seed no map
  buildings, so each is built up from the settlement. The flag is absent
  today, so worlds are seeded as the map has it, the box's wilds town too,
  until maps' settlement layout lands.

Walls: a building in disrepair keeps its walls up. A ruin (level 0) has
its walls down (Towns.walls_up), and so does a "gone" one (buildings_of
walls false), so 566's World._open_walls takes the level piece's outline
out of the edges on the server and, through the "town" message, on
clients: a ruin is walked over and blocks no one. Clearing.unbuild leaves
authored walls alone (terrain).

Views: buildings_of carries the new states ("disrepair", "ruin", and "gone"
for a ruin's map piece that is no more). The town sheet (624) gains strain
{days, of, why} (Towns.strain).

Soaks (the default world, 30 days, one player):
1. Upkeep every 7 days, hamlet wood 20, no reserve. The town stayed a
   settlement (it wasn't yet seeded at hamlet). From day 11 its buildings
   owed upkeep, and by day 28 the forge, kitchen, tannery and temple were
   in disrepair.
2. Upkeep every 14 days, hamlet wood 10, the reserve, seeded at hamlet.
   Nothing went unkept. But "hunger" (fed by nobody, with the treasury at
   its floor) gave strain from day 6, and the town fell on day 16. Food
   sat in the store, so the trigger was changed and "officials unpaid"
   was dropped.
3. With the trigger counting the store's food. Nothing went unkept. Strain
   came from hunger from day 7 to 15 (9 days); the town fell to a
   settlement on day 16, strain was 0 from day 17, it was a village again
   on day 26, and it had at most 1 day of strain after that.
A fresh world falls once before its first harvest. That is Jeff's rule
doing its job on a gap that predates 649: start_food is meant to reach the
first harvest and doesn't, and a caravan sells 10 food on day 0. That gap
goes to economy's gold and food note (with the treasury at its floor), not
into 649. The box's town is past founding: its stage and buildings are
kept, its strain starts at 0, and its upkeep is covered.

## 649, terrain's side: a ruin's ground back to the forest

Economy's rise and fall (649; Jeff: "buildings at the edge fall into disrepair and the
forest overtakes"; the coordinator's approval): a building that reaches RUIN stands as
rubble for a season, then its record drops and Main hands its footprint to Clearing.
Terrain's side is the two calls Main makes, as agreed with economy and maps.

- **Clearing.unbuild(zone, cells, day)** fells the cells at a stump from that day; they
  grow on as any felled cell (a season a stage, twice that with no trunk beside). It
  returns how many it took and tells changed, so Main's _on_clearing_changed carries them
  as it does a woodcut: World.set_floor, apply_cells with maps' outline relay,
  World.set_edges, the "clearing" message, the view's clearing_walls.
- **A kept trunk.** Until now a cell grown back was erased, so it was the level's own
  cell again: right for a felled trunk, wrong for a ruin's cell, which is the level's
  floor. A cell of the level's floor given back is kept as [stage, day, 1]; past
  saplings it becomes [4, day, 1], a trunk that stays: apply takes it out of the floor,
  cells_of names it "trunk", daily leaves it, _is_floor counts it void, and a woodcut
  fells it as any edge trunk (its entry keeps the 1, so it grows back kept again).
- **Built cells kept in the snapshot.** base["built"] (the level's buildings and roads)
  is read from the level every boot, so a change to it must be saved: the zone's entry
  gains "built" (cells build took) and "unbuilt" (the level's own built cells a ruin
  gave back), lists of "x,y". An older build reads the 2-entry cells and skips the rest.
- **Clearing.build(zone, cells)** takes cells for a building planned on them: built
  over (never growing), a kept trunk or a standing trunk grass again, a felled cell held
  at its stage; told changed for the cells that changed.
- **A plot under a ruin is dropped first.** A laid plot's cells never grow back (591
  step 2), so unbuild drops any plot whose rect (its ring's) holds one of the cells,
  the whole of it, through maps' Clearing.plot_at and unplot (649, maps' side: its
  building and edges off the walk, the terrain and the clients through unplotted),
  then fells the cells.
- **A client keeps "trunk".** _on_clearing used to forget a cell told "trunk"; over the
  level's floor that cell would come back as floor on the next load. It keeps "trunk"
  in _clearing_told now, and apply_cells makes the cell void. A changed meaning of an
  existing message: a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 35 (open, unshipped).

level_test _test_unbuild: three cells unbuilt (one the level's building's, given back),
a trunk not; grown back, three kept trunks, "trunk" in the zone's cells; applied, no

from the cells the same; a woodcut fells one, kept again; build takes them, grass, never
growing, kept; a ruin over a plot drops the plot, then its cells. Protocol changed (35's line), no new
class_name.

## 655. The shown walk bends through the cell centre

Jeff, on the tilted camera (v0.1.171): "moving along tiles is now more
unnatural ... diagonal movements stand out". Every body moved on a straight
line from cell centre to cell centre and changed heading at once at each
centre; the top-down view hid it because a sprite has no heading to see,
and a 3D body jerking its yaw every step, worst where straight and diagonal
steps alternate, does not read as walking. The coordinator approved ui's
design: the client's drawing changes, nothing in the sim or on the wire.

A step is drawn as a bend round each corner (GridEntity.bent_position): a
quadratic from the reach point on the step before, through the cell's
centre as its control point, to the reach point on the step after, with the
reach BEND_REACH (half a step: midpoint to midpoint; the corner cut by 0.18
cells at a right angle, 0.25 at a reversal, never more) or BEND_REACH_NARROW
(a quarter) round a cell with a wall on any side, so a body in a 1-cell door
edge keeps nearer its cell. The bend is timed on each step's own time, so
every reach point is crossed when the straight line would cross it: arrival
times, hearing, the moment a tile counts, stay the server's, and a straight
run is the straight line at the straight pace. The shown facing is the
bend's tangent (bent_tangent), so the yaw turns across the bend (the half
step before and after the corner) instead of at the centre; TURN_RATE stays
as the clamp for everything else (aim, a standing turn, a slide taken over).
The 3D puppet takes its yaw from the shown facing as before, the rig
untouched (pc-character's).

Where the next cell is known: a mirror's queued slides (_slides, usually
holding the next step by the time one starts, drawn display_delay_ticks
behind) and the own predicted body's planned steps (MovePrediction._steps).
The bend at a step's end is settled as its tail begins (the next slide
queued by then, joining straight on at the display clock, one cell, not a
push) and never changes under way; the step after starts on that bend, else
straight from the centre: the body never jumps onto or off a bend. A push, a
slide from off the centre (a catch-up), a jump of more than a cell, a
correction's ease and a walk from rest are drawn straight as before. The
host's own body (its next step unknown to the client code, a held key read
tick by tick) walks straight and turns at the centre as now: known, left.
DIAGONAL_TICK_SCALE 1.5 (a diagonal 6% slower than its length) is physics'
and the pathfinder's and stays; with the corner rounded the dip falls inside
the bend. view_test _test_bent_walk: the straight run, the midpoints at the
straight moments, the two steps meeting on the bend, within the cells and
moving on, the tangent between the ways, the narrow reach, the reach read
off the map, a mirror's slide bending toward the queued slide and not toward
a late or present one. Client only; no wire change; no new class_name.

## 613 amended: one place and story per trade, and wandering off (economy's side)

Jeff answered the sought's draft (2026-10-22, through the coordinator): "i
think every npc has their own place and story of how they got there...
for replayablity sake they may wander off (get re-captured) if they run
low on resources or funds". The coordinator approved the amended design.
Lore wrote the stories (docs/lore/sought.md, drafts pending Jeff's
wording check except the smith's). Maps lays each outdoor place under its
key, and dungeon lays the dwarven forge as a fixed anchor of the castle's
halls.

- **The data.** economy.json sought.trades replaces 613's where, default
  and guards. Each trade has one row: {place (maps' or dungeon's place
  key, or "camp"), where, holder (a faction, "" lost), band (enemy-ai's),
  story (lore's id), alt (a second variant)}.
  - smith: dwarven_forge, castle_dungeon, held by the goblins.
  - butcher: herders_hut, hills.
  - fisherman: far_bank, wilds.
  - woodcutter: woodcutters_lean_to, forest.
  - farmer: old_farmstead, wilds.
  - shepherd: hill_cave, hills.
  - weaver: hill_shieling, hills.
  - carpenter: ruined_barn, wilds.
  - cook: thick_wood, forest.
  - tanner: boar_path, forest.
  - fletcher: fletchers_tree, forest.
  - Each has the alt <trade>.camp, at a hostile camp.
  - The medicine man has no row until Jeff says whether he is Hob or
    another. A trade without a row walks in meanwhile, as an interim only
    (the coordinator), told to the coordinator as each trade turns on.
- **Placed by story.** Towns._story(trade). The first time out uses the
  row's own place; later times use the variants in turn (the town's
  sought_tries per trade), and a variant that can't be placed now gives
  way to the next (Towns._place_variant). place_sought is now (town,
  trade, variant, id) -> {place, where} for the variant's key, or ""
  while it isn't laid. "camp" stays 518's path. The entry carries story
  and tries.
- **Wandering off.** Towns._wander_turn, each tick, covers a resident of a
  trade with a row. Never a companion, and never one away (a captive or
  one being led home).
  - The resident is low (Towns._low) while hungry and not on the dole,
    while owed unpaid wages, or while seated with work queued at their
    workshop and none of it going (waiting on stock).
  - Past sought.leave_days (10) low, they go: out of the residents, away,
    sought again as themselves (the same worker, card and purse;
    _seek(..., wandered)), placed by their story's next variant.
  - The log says "<name> the <trade> has gone, low too long; they say back
    where they were found". The signal Towns.wandered(town, id) is npc's,
    for the officials' word.
  - At most one a town each sought.wander_every_days (7). Saved: low,
    wandered_at, sought_tries.
  - Tuned from 5 days and one a town a day after the 20-day soak (one
    player, the wilds on 649): 10 wanderings in 20 days, one a day from
    day 9, every core trade twice (woodcutter, farmer, cook, smith,
    tanner). The town's low was the same poverty as economy's gold and
    food note: the treasury at its floor, the founding food gone by day 8.
    A town shouldn't lose a trade a day even when poor (the coordinator's
    ruling). Draft numbers, Jeff's to tune; a re-soak follows 652 (the
    founding larder).
  - A wandered one whose trade the town fills another way comes back to
    the town out of work, not removed.
- **Soak.** town_soak --rescue-after stands in for the trade's place and
  brings wanderers home the same way, counting "wandered".

## 657. A despawn takes the body out of its own zone

Maps' find (zone_test, through the coordinator): a player who left while
World was in another zone, then came back and went through a link and back
in the same frame, left freed-instance errors in Fields.any_carried_heat
(through Main._nearest_free) and in World._step_zone. The cause was
World.despawn: it took the body out of the entities and occupancy of the
zone World was in, not of the body's own. Main._leave run with World in the
test room freed Bo's body while the sample still listed it and held its
cell, and erased the test room's occupancy at that cell in its place.

World.despawn now enters the entity's zone when that differs from the zone
World is in (and is loaded), despawns it there and comes back, so its
entity_despawned listeners also run in its zone. One fix at the source
rather than is_instance_valid guards in each reader. The box's disconnect
path, travel and the raids' despawn already entered the body's zone first,
so this mostly closes a path for any other despawn made from elsewhere (a
companion or resident sent away from another zone's tick).

zone_test _test_bounce_back runs right after _test_restart, not at the end:
Bo leaves with World in the test room, his body out of the sample's
entities and cell; back, through the link and back in one frame; no zone
holds a freed body in its entities or cells, and _nearest_free there reads
none. Before: 2 FAIL and 2 SCRIPT ERRORs ("sample", "sample (1, 4)").
Server sim only; protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 652. The founding larder, and the officials by stage

The coordinator's ruling on economy's gold and food note (649's soaks: a fresh world sold its first stores on day 0 and went hungry before its first harvest; a poor treasury owed its officials from the start).

Food (ruling (a)):
- A raw good's comfort is the most of rules' comfort and comfort_per_head x the town's workers (Production.comfort; food 2 a head), used wherever the store's comfort was (prices, buying, caravans, the "full" tier).
- A town's first stores (Towns._found) are the most of start_food and founding.per_head_day x its residents (at least founding.heads) x the days to the first autumn it can sow for (Towns.founding_food: this year's while spring has more than a day left, else next year's).
- Till its first harvest is in (Towns.before_harvest; a "harvests" count on the town's record, 1 for a town saved before 652 that was founded) a caravan keeps founding.keep_days x per_head_day food a head (Economy.before_harvest, set by Main).
- Old numbers: start_food 120 and comfort food 20 alone, so the caravan could sell everything over 20 on day 0. Now start_food 120 is the least; per_head_day 1, heads 4, keep_days 30, comfort_per_head food 2.

Officials (ruling (b)): they come with the stages. official.<trade>.stage: the guard from hamlet, the priest from village, the lawspeaker from town (a settlement pays none). Below its stage an official is neither paid nor owed (Production.official_paid = Towns.official_paid). The lawspeaker is appointed on reaching the town stage (official "appoint"), no longer at 6 residents of its own; the town stage no longer needs a lawspeaker among its residents, which would have deadlocked. The priest still comes when the temple stands (396). A lawspeaker already seated in a town below that stage stays, unpaid. The wage rule (a share of tax and rent) waits for the 3-player soak.

Tests: larder_test (first stores, the founding caravan), rescue_test (the lawspeaker at the town stage; a hamlet pays its guard, no priest or lawspeaker, nor owes them). Server only; protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 653: the low camera's scatter reach

Jeff: "clipping of ground details they should load in earlier." Under the low camera (623)
the scatter was built only within World.NEAR_TILES (22) of the aim, so its edge popped in
in plain sight, and built chunks were never freed and drawn to the far plane. Approved by
the coordinator with perf's points (a cap by distance, faster builds with a backlog,
benches with the scatter fully built).

- **A reach of its own.** Client3D._scatter_reach(): under the low camera
  scatter_reach_low (LOW_SCATTER_REACH, 90; map_bench --scatter-reach=N sets it), else the
  screen's reach as before. NEAR_TILES still bounds bodies, clicks, puppets and shadows
  (238); only the scatter looks further.
- **A fade at the edge.** The swaying kinds' shader (scatter.gdshaderinc) takes
  reach_fade (the aim, where the shrink starts and ends): past reach - SCATTER_FADE (16)
  each plant sinks toward its root, gone at the reach. A shrink, not a discard, so the
  early depth test is kept. The kinds that don't sway (stones, roots: a StandardMaterial3D)
  get a visibility range ending at the reach with SCATTER_FADE of fade margin (fade self).
  Ortho: no fade, no range.
- **Freed past the reach.** A chunk whose middle lies SCATTER_KEEP (16) past the reach
  and a chunk is freed (_unscatter, which _rescatter now shares) and made again when the
  view comes back, so what is drawn is held by distance, not by the walk so far.
- **Faster with a backlog.** With more than SCATTER_BACKLOG (8) steps due, steps go on
  within SCATTER_BUDGET_USEC (2 ms) a frame; else one a frame as before.
- **The bench.** map_bench --low=1 turns the low camera on, --scatter-reach=N sets the
  reach; before the frames the scatter round the view is built in full (its time, chunks,
  MultiMeshes and instances printed, and again after the frames).

**The reach: 90** (the coordinator, on perf's bench: windowed, off-screen, low camera,
noon, a 12-tile walk, three interleaved rounds). At the wilds square, reach 38 / 60 / 90 /
120 drew 33 / 53 / 85 / 119 chunks (18.7k / 30.2k / 48.4k / 69.7k instances), the render
GPU 1.4 / 1.6 / 1.9 / 2.3 ms a frame and the CPU 1.1 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.2 ms. A full build
from nothing took about 250 ms, about 2 s of fill at the 2 ms budget. On the hills every
reach was the same: the map is small enough that 38 covers it. 90 is the furthest within
the +0.5 ms line, and it answers "load in earlier" best. (60 was named the fallback
should a laptop play test show the cost; Jeff's ruling below settles it.)
SCATTER_KEEP 16 holds what stays drawn after a walk to about 1.3x the full build, and
that band past the reach is shrunk to nothing, so it costs vertex work but no pixels.
view_test _test_low_scatter. Protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

**Jeff's ruling, on v0.1.172** (2026-10-24, through the coordinator): "grass load in is
just about right - at that distance it just feels that the load in is natural visual
distance". The reach stays 90; the 60 fallback is dropped.

## 658. Decor kinds: the ways a piece sits

647 gave a level `"decor"`: `[[x, y, dx, dy, kind, variant], ...]`, four kinds of moss and web
each with its own fit in `Level.decor_from`, and a table of variant counts. The Dwarven Halls'
step 2 (613 amended) wants the smith's fallen guards lying with a facing, and maps wants
art-kit's `prop.grave_fence` (654) along the pauper's graves on Held, an edge piece on open grass.
The coordinator's rulings: no new level.json key, the decor list grows kinds that take a facing;
and an edge piece must work on an outdoor level too, as 647's strip does along a wall edge.

- **One table, how a kind sits.** `Level.DECOR_VARIANTS` becomes `Level.DECOR_KINDS`, kind ->
  `{sits, variants, faced}`. Five ways of sitting: `flat` on the cell (`(0, 0)`: the yaw rolled by
  the cell; a side: the way the piece's +z faces, for a kind marked `faced`); `wall` along a wall
  edge's foot with rock behind it; `edge` on any edge of the cell, wall, open or a fence's, indoors
  or out, seen from the cell; `corner` where two walls meet; `niche` across an open burial niche.
  The moss and webs keep their fits (`moss_patch` flat and not faced, `moss_strip` wall,
  `web_corner` corner, `web_niche` niche); `fallen_guard` is flat and faced with two variants,
  `grave_fence` edge with three. `decor_from` matches on the way of sitting, not the kind; the
  warnings are the same, and a flat piece on a diagonal or an edge piece with no step is said.
- **Edge, not wall loosened.** A strip needs rock behind it; a fence stands between two grass
  cells, or on a town wall's edge, or on the map's own edge, and must be allowed there. Outdoors
  the terrain's `"edges"` is sparse (open edges absent); `edge` reads that as fine. The entry
  carries the Terrain edge key as a strip's does.
- **Drawn, never solid.** Decor stays dressing: the server parses it into terrain `"decor"`, the
  client draws `prop.<kind>` when its kit has the slot and skips it when not, nothing on the wire
  changes its meaning. A thing that must stop walkers is a building (the rack, below).
- **The frame.** `Client3D._add_decor`: a flat piece sits on its cell, its yaw the cell's roll or,
  faced, `atan2(out.x, out.y)` so its +z turns the way its step names; every edge-borne piece
  (wall, edge, niche) sits at the edge's midpoint with +x toward the cell and z along the edge,
  the stone runs' frame the strip already used, its height read at the midpoint. Along a straight
  run laid from one side every section's +z end is the same end, so `prop.grave_fence`'s one post
  (at +z, art-kit's 654) is shared between neighbours; a run laid from both sides would double a
  post, so maps lays each run from one side (`docs/levels.md`).
- **Regeneration.** Unchanged: a template's entries inside the anchors are kept through every
  generation (`Regen.generated_config`), and `Regen.decor_of` keeps its moss and webs off the
  cells they hold.

Tests: level_test `_test_decor` (a faced guard and a rolled one, a fence on a wall edge and on an
open one, a guard on a diagonal and a fence without a step said; an outdoor level with a fence
along open grass edges and the map's edge and a body on the grass, nothing said); view_test
`_test_faced_decor` (the guard's +z turned east, the fence at its open edge's midpoint facing the
cell). Client and sim alike; nothing on the wire.

## 451 amended (2): the hand pass (Jeff: the sword's grip, the shield's side, the block)

Jeff (2026-10-24 02:10): "sword and shield also need graphical fix, sword hilt is at the end of
hand, not in palm. shield should be carried on the outside of arm, not inside. shield block
graphic should be raising shield in front of body, not sideways out." With the great axe's left
hand off its haft (art-kit's stills after 451 amended), the coordinator approved four client steps:
the grip, the shield, the block and two hands. Each lands on its own.

### Step 1: the grip in the palm

The bodies' hands are mittens: body_gen weights each hand's mesh to its hand bone, so the
fingers' curl (Idle's and Sword_Idle's alike, about 78 degrees) never bends it. Posed in Blender
(build/hand/measure.py, the Body's vertices weighted most to the right hand or its fingers), the
mitten runs 0.017 to 0.13 m out from the wrist along the hand's +Y. Its middle is at 0.069 (the
woman's 0.065), and it sits 0.005 to the palm's side of the bone and 5 cm thick. The socket was
at the knuckle line tools/grip_sockets.gd measured from the finger bones: 0.10 out and 0.03 to the
palm, so on a mitten a hilt sat three quarters of the way to its tip, at the palm's surface.

- **The socket:** HAND_GRIP 0.07 and HAND_PALM 0.005 put a held piece's grip (its origin) through
  the mitten's middle, for both hands and every body (each times its hand size). A finger-curl
  modifier was the first design, dropped: with mitten hands it changes nothing.
- **The chop:** Chop_Loop was authored with the old hold (humanoid_clips' HOLD_AT, kept with a
  note). The shipped clip keeps the left hand on the haft with the new socket, by anim_rig_test's
  measure. Authored again with the new hold, the left forearm went 6 cm into the chest at 0.55 s,
  so the clip stays as it is.
- **The unread "stance":** HUMANOID_MOVES' "stance" (Sword_Idle) is read by nothing, and the hand
  pass doesn't use it. A held weapon plays the same idle, walk and swings as before.

view_test _test_attach_points: a held sword's grip 0.055 to 0.085 m out from the wrist (reads
0.069), short of the knuckles, along the fist's axis. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new

### Step 2: the shield on the outside of the forearm

The shield was in the left hand's socket, turned a quarter, so it stood out of the back of the
fist, inside the arm's line. It is now strapped on the left forearm.

- **The arm_l socket:** on LeftLowerArm at its middle (half the hand's rest offset, set in

  -X on every body, from the hand's -Z at rest: build/hand/frames.gd), +y along the forearm toward

## 655 amended. The own held walk bends too, and the cut is capped

655 left the own body's held-key walk straight: Main._drive_wasd appends
the next step only as the one on screen ends (MovePrediction.ready_for_step),
so at a step's tail no step followed to bend toward, and the clip pair
(2026-10-24) showed companions and other players bending while the player's
own body turned at the centre. Jeff's complaint was about his own walk. The
coordinator approved: the hint, only where no planned step follows; the
cut capped at a quarter cell; a refused step sliding back, never snapping.

The hint: Main._drive_wasd tells the prediction the direction the keys hold
each frame (GridEntity.hint_step, MovePrediction.hint; ZERO for none). As a
step's tail begins (_bent, where the bend is settled) with no planned step
after it, no move order and a hint under HINT_FRESH_TICKS old that the
replicated world would not refuse (_blocked), the bend is toward the cell
the hint points at. When the step comes (step()), it starts on that bend
(bend_prev), as a planned step does; the key changed in the last half step,
it starts straight from the bend's end to its centre, as a mirror's
catch-up slide does, and the step after bends again. Main reads the keys
after the bodies are drawn, so the step comes later in the frame the one
before ends in: with the key held a frame ago the body is drawn on along
the hinted bend meanwhile (position, as the step to come would draw it,
COAST_MAX of it at most), and the step joins it without a jump; a fixed
rest at the apex showed a two-frame jump instead. No step by the next
frame, or the key let go, the body slides from where it is to the centre
over SETTLE_TICKS (a settle Step, eased; ready_for_step is true through it,
and a step or order under way starts from where the body is drawn). A walk
that ended within the tick is continued from the cell's centre, on the
line, rather than from the body's last drawn point a frame short of it,
and a rest point within the projection's rounding of a centre counts as
the centre (_drawn), so a held walk's steps are all between centres and
bend. A hint into a wall or into someone bends
nothing: the body reaches the centre and stops there. A step the server
refuses is corrected as before, rebase blending from the drawn point, now
on the bend, to the server's cell: a slide, not a snap. The host's own body
(no prediction) walks straight as before.

The cap (GridEntity.capped_reach, in bent_position and bent_tangent so the
timing matches): the apex is reach / 4 of the turn (the step out less the
step in) from the centre, 0.18 cells at a right angle and 0.25 at a
reversal at the half-step reach, but 0.35 at a diagonal reversal, where the
body left its cell; the reach is cut to 1 / |turn| so no corner is cut by
more than a quarter cell. Mirrors share it.

## 543 amended, ui's side. The held walk pauses while the server holds three steps

Found in 655 amended's clip pair (2026-10-24): the player's own body slid 3
to 5 tiles three times in each 35-second held walk. The recording starved
the loopback server to about 58% of real time (its log ends at tick 400
after 69 s of sim) while both clients' clocks ran real time, so each held
walk sent steps faster than the server took them. The server keeps at most
World.MAX_QUEUED_STEPS (3) queued WASD steps and World.order_step drops a
fourth unheard; once a client was four steps ahead its next directions
vanished, the server walked later directions from an earlier tile, its
path parted from the one shown, and the client saw "the server moved it
elsewhere" and slid there. The sim never repositions a walking player:
every server move was one cell along a sent direction. The setup made it
common; on the box a server stall of about a second under a held key (four
steps' worth) would do the same, rarely, and a player would see it. The
coordinator: pause the body at three unconfirmed steps; a short stall looks
like a stumble, not a teleport; a normal walk on a healthy server must
never pause.

MovePrediction keeps when each step in _sent was sent (_sent_at).
ready_for_step is false while MAX_QUEUED_STEPS steps are sent and not
seen taken and the oldest was sent more than a round trip plus
RECONCILE_GRACE_TICKS ago: the server has it and has not walked it, so a
step sent now could be the one dropped. The held walk then pauses at its
shown end (Main._drive_wasd sends nothing; the hinted bend's settle brings
the body to the centre) and goes on as the server takes them, every step
sent still walked. A server keeping up never has three unseen that long,
whatever the round trip, since each step is seen a round trip after it is
sent: three in flight at once (an 800 ms trip) pause nothing.
waiting_on_server says when it is paused. Decision 543's own rules stay:
a step overdue by CATCH_UP_WAIT_STEPS is still a correction (the stalled
server's one correction in the test, the body sliding back to its tile
before the queued steps are shown again), and the catch-up stretch still
drains a backlog of a step or two. No wire change; the server's cap and
silent drop are untouched (the client now never reaches them under a
stall, and a deliberate flood is still dropped).

prediction_test _test_paused_walk: a server at 60% of the pace (28 frames
paused, nothing dropped, every step walked, no correction off the path), a
server stalled 15 ticks (paused, nothing dropped, every step walked), the
server keeping up (never paused), an 800 ms round trip with the server
keeping up (never paused); the scripted server now queues three and drops
a fourth as the real one does. The held zigzag check also asserts no pause.
Client only; no wire change; no new class_name.

## 659. The tower style: floors in a footprint, a shaft that lines the stairs

Jeff: "The tower's inside shifts too." The dark elven tower over the mine (650's `far_tower`) is a
far landmark until he places it; its zone, link and lore come then. Dungeon builds the
infrastructure first (the coordinator's brief, 2026-10-24, the design in
C:/dev/review/dungeon/tower_style_design.md approved): a "tower" style for the labyrinth
generator, a sample in memory, tests, a plan sheet; no real level, link or zone.

- **One level a floor.** A tower of N floors is N regenerating levels (`<tower>_1` the foot to
  `<tower>_N` the top), as the barrow's layers are: the engine's zone, sleep and regenerate rules
  are per level and a link joins levels. Each floor is laid again on its own period while its zone
  sleeps, so a player on floor 3 never has floor 2 change under them, only behind them.
- **The footprint is the template's.** The block's `"footprint"` ("octagon": the map's rect with
  a cell of rim and each corner cut along a diagonal about 0.29 of the shorter side; "round": a
  disc of half the shorter side less a cell; else the whole map) names the cells the generator may
  carve (`Labyrinth.footprint(size, kind)`, kept in the map's extras as "footprint"); `Tools.rock`
  reads it, so carving, the path search (`path_through`, `path_around`) and room placement
  (`_in_footprint`) never leave it, and the floor's outline is the tower's wall. Nothing in the
  generator assumes a size: the test lays the sample at 22 and 30 across.
- **The style.** The dwarven rules with no great hall: rooms `[3, 3]` to `[7, 6]`, four to seven
  a floor, ways two wide, a door where a way meets a room, blind ways and alcoves, torches along
  the ways (the "torch" marker stands in for art-kit's cold lamp until step 2), `loops` 0.15.
- **The shaft lines the stairs.** A 7 x 6 anchor about the middle of every floor, open on all four
  sides so every floor's ways meet at it, holds the stair down west of the middle (a link to the
  floor below, spawn `from_above`, cue `down`, variant 3 for the dark stair) and the stair up east
  of it (to the floor above, spawn `from_below`, cue `up`), the arriving spawns on the row below
  them; the foot has no stair down and the top no stair up. Two clear cells round each stair cell
  and spawn on every floor whatever the floor rolled, checked explicitly in `_test_tower`.
- **The foot and the top.** Floor 1: the door anchor at the south edge (5 x 3, walled east and
  west, the link out with cue `arch`, spawn `from_outside`, the start) and the mine's way down
  against the north wall (3 x 3, walled north, east and west, a sealed link with cue `sealed`,
  `"sealed": "tower_mine"` a placeholder until lore names the mark). Floor N: the chamber (10 x 7,
  walled all round but its south over the shaft's span), bare but for two torches; what stands in
  it is lore's and art-kit's later. Floors between hold the shaft alone.
- **The sample and the sheet.** `tools/plan_sheet.sample_tower(floor, floors, prefix, across)`
  lays a floor's template; `write_tower_sheet(prefix, floors, generation, out, scale)` draws the
  floors in a row, the foot at the left (`write_sheet`'s drawing moved into `sheet_image`).
  labyrinth_test `_test_tower` (two generations a floor at 22 and 30 across: anchors kept and
  inside the octagon, every floor cell walked to from the shaft (the coordinator, on the sheet:
  "not only every anchor"), no one-wide way, nothing outside the footprint, doors, torches, a
  chest, the stairs at the same cells on every floor with their clear cells, the sealed link on
  the foot alone, the top chamber bare but lit) and `_test_sheet`'s row; level_test
  `_test_tower_levels` (each floor parses clean, the links both ways with cues up and down, the
  foot's arch and sealed hatch). docs/levels.md.
- **Deferred.** Windows in the ring (a level's walls take no window edges; the tower's outside is
  a landmark, not yet a piece with an inside). Step 2, on art-kit's "659, art-kit's side": the
  dark wall and floor set, the cold lamp marker and environment's light, `building.dark_pillar`
  (solid, doorless; a protocol line), `prop.rune_strip` as a "wall" decor kind, the hatch piece
  over the sealed link. Step 3 when Jeff places the tower: maps' zone and links, lore's names,
  enemy-ai's foes, a real `<tower>_1..N` written from the sample.

Generator and tools only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 667. The land lock: one landing at a time, stale after 25 minutes

The land lock (tools/land_lock.sh, from d005aaf9 on 2026-10-14, after items lost three
landing races, never written up here till now) is one atomic-mkdir lock folder,
`/c/dev/land.lock`, with tools/bench_lock.sh's mechanics: a tree takes it for its final
fetch, rebase, retest and push, so nobody lands between its retest and its push, and releases
it right after. The resource gate's suite take comes first and is never waited on while the
lock is held (394). A take that finds it held exits 1 and names the holder; the tree keeps
working and tries again.

A lock older than its stale limit may be taken over. That limit was 15 minutes (900 s), when a
landing took under 10. It is now 25 minutes (PSYKINETIC_LOCK_STALE=1500, release, 2026-10-24):
a lean landing (394 amended (10): memory short, the suite alone and then net_test, state_test
and server_boot_test) takes about 16.5 minutes of tests, and perf's held the lock about 17
with its rebase and import, so another tree could have taken over mid-landing. CLAUDE.md's
"older than 15" line is the coordinator's to change.

Tools only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 664. Every Godot the tooling starts writes its own log, in its checkout's build/logs

Godot writes `user://logs/godot.log` unless told otherwise, and that folder is shared by every
worktree and by Jeff's own client (all one `user://`). It keeps the last five logs. A suite
starts dozens of Godots, so within minutes of a landing the log of Jeff's client was rotated
out (the coordinator, 2026-10-24: a draugr fight he wanted read was gone).

- Every Godot launch in tests/ and tools/ passes `--log-file` into its checkout's
  `build/logs/<name>.log` (build/ is gitignored), each Godot running at the same time with a
  name of its own: a scene by its basename (`_again` for run.sh's retry), net_test's and
  state_test's by phase, server_boot's export and client, the benches' server, proxy and
  clients. Helpers: `tests/godot_log.sh` (`godot_log NAME`, sourced after the script's cd)
  and `tests/godot_log.ps1` (`Get-GodotLog NAME`). A GDScript tool that starts one
  (items_art_slots) passes it too.
- `tools/godot_log_check.py` fails any launch line in tests/ or tools/ (sh `"$GODOT" -...`,
  ps1 `& $godot` / `-FilePath $godot`, gd `OS.execute(OS.get_executable_path()`) with no
  `--log-file` within three lines, `--version` aside. land.sh and land.ps1 run it before
  the gate, beside the CHANGELOG check, so a new launch without one fails the landing at
  once. It reads the scripts, not the logs folder: other trees and Jeff's client write
  there too, so a check on the folder would fail for what others do.
- A server the box runs, and the game itself, keep the default log.

Tools only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 652 amended. The founding food lasts to the first crop it can reap

The 652 soak (25 days, one player, the default world) sold no food on day 0, but two gaps showed. The town was founded at step 0, before its people were counted, so it was stocked for the four-head floor (120 food for 12 residents). Its field stood only on day 8, after spring's sowing, so "the first autumn it can sow for" was next year's. Hunger strain began on day 9 and reached 7 of 10.

The coordinator's ruling ((1) plus (c), as a general rule):
- A town's first stores last to the first crop of any kind it can reap, counted from when its field can stand: now if it stands, else founding.field_days (8) on. That crop is the autumn harvest if the field stands with more than a day of spring left, else the winter's roots, whichever comes first (Towns.founding_food). In the soak that is the roots, about 35 days, 420 food for 12. A later season table that puts a sown harvest before the roots is picked up by the same rule.
- Topped up once, the first time the town has residents (Towns._larder, run from _spread; "larder" on the record till then, saved).
- Why not stock to next year's harvest (960 food): a hamlet's store becomes a granary and hides the strain that rise and fall exist to show. Why not keep this year's harvest: it leaves the day-9 hunger, against Jeff's ask that a fresh town not fall before its first crop.

The re-soak (38 days, per_head_day 1): 140 at founding and 245 topped up for 11 people (385). Strain stayed at 0 till day 22, then hunger, and one fall to a settlement on day 33 (back to a hamlet the next tick; a village on day 35). The roots dug on day 35 gave 60 food for 14. The town ate about 1.4 a head a day: newcomers (11 to 14), and the cook turning about 9 store food a day into rations that residents bought and carried out. The coordinator's call: founding.per_head_day 1.5, a draft on the checklist's tune line, and the cook's draw on the larder as a follow-up design (the cook takes from the store only above what the residents need till the next crop, as Production.keep_for does for builds), after which per_head_day can come back toward 1.

larder_test: the first-crop days from spring and summer, the top-up once. A tune line for the founding food goes on the next cut's checklist.

It is kept on the trip (Production._trip_catch, saved as "trip_catch"), shown as Production.trip(id)["catch"] ("" for none, or for another trade), and its drops land at BACK as before. ## 652 amended (2). The founding larder: the cook draws only above it

The 652 amended re-soak showed the leak behind the founding food: the cook turned about 9 of the store's food a day into rations and roasts, which residents bought and carried out, while the town went hungry before its first crop. The coordinator's approval:
- Production.larder_for, (town) -> int, set by Towns: a workshop make that takes food from the store (the cook's ration and roast, any recipe with food in made.from) starts only if the store keeps at least that much food after its cost (Production._spares_larder). It is the same check as keep_for for builds (649), for food alone. The residents' meals still come from the store as before.
- Towns.larder_for: founding_food from now while the town's first crop is still to come, else 0. The winter's roots now count as a crop ("harvests" on the record), for the caravan's keep too, since the first crop may be the roots.
- Limited to the founding stretch, where the soak showed it. After the first crop the cook's rations are the town's business, as before.

larder_test _test_larder_reserve: no ration from a store at its larder, rations again once nothing is kept; Towns' larder before and after the first crop.

Soaks (38 days, one player, the default world):
- At per_head_day 1 with the reserve, the cook made 25 rations in 38 days, against 192 without it. Strain held at 0 till day 24. Newcomers (11 at the founding count, 15 by day 37) still ate the larder by day 25, and the town fell for a tick on day 34.
- The coordinator's call: per_head_day stays 1.5 ("people come"), with the reserve. Stocked 210 + 368 = 578. No hunger day and no fall through day 38, a village on day 30. Roots dug on day 35 (60 food) with about 20 food left in the store by the ledger (579 banked, 559 meals). A thin margin. The coordinator's call: founding.margin_days 3 (a draft on the tune line), three days' more food for the founding heads, for a wetter year or a mouth more; checked to day 38 before landing.

## 661. Arrival shelter: no harm while a zone's view builds

Perf found that every zone crossing freezes the client while it builds the 3D view, about 4 s
into the wilds and 1.3 s into the hills, on the box too. The sim doesn't wait, so an arriving
player could be struck while they couldn't see. Perf's 660 turns the wait into a fade and
shortens it. This decision covers the server side, as the coordinator approved it.

- **Shelter on arrival.** Main.travel (a link, an edge, the hidden door from below) ends with
  Main._shelter_arrival. It calls World.shelter(player, ARRIVAL_SHELTER_TICKS 60), which is
  World.protect's spawn grace plus GridEntity.sheltered (server only).
  - Being protected means no monster targets the body, which is drawn faded to everyone: that
    fade is the tell.
  - While World.is_sheltered, nothing harms it, from monsters, players or the ground alike:
    World.damage skips every cause but bleeding, and _stun_for, knock_down and afflict (no
    ailment takes hold, so none ticks on after) pass it by. _push treats it as a body that won't
    give: pushed directly, nothing moves; met by a pushed body, it is a wall to that body (a
    wall's stop and hurt, nothing goes on, logged "<name> (sheltered)"). No guard is spent
    (_meet_guard), and a blow or shot on it neither wears its bundle, credits the striker, nor
    slows a rush. A telegraph still draws over it and strikes nobody there. (Physics checked
    this side.)
  - Respawns and first joins keep the plain spawn grace (Main.SPAWN_GRACE_TICKS).
- **How it ends:**
  - The client's new "view_ready" command {zone} (Main.tell_view_ready, sent by perf's view
    build). Main._view_ready ends the shelter with World.unshelter, and plain spawn grace runs
    from that moment, so the player gets a respawn's first seconds once they can see. A
    view_ready naming another zone (a stale one) does nothing.
  - The 60 ticks.
  - Any act that already ends spawn grace: a step, an attack, a shove, a bash, a wind-up or a
    lunge.
  - Any command except talk and looking (Main.SHELTER_KEEPS: say, party, face, greet,
    town_sheet, view_ready). So use, search, bandage, a stance and the rest end it at once:
    nobody hops a link to stand untouchable doing things.
- **Cooldown.** A player sheltered on arriving isn't sheltered again for
  SHELTER_COOLDOWN_MSEC (30 s). Main._sheltered_at is keyed by player id, not peer, and timed
  by the machine's clock because zones' ticks differ. A crossing inside the cooldown gets spawn
  grace alone, so crossing back and forth never chains shelters.
- **Companion.** A companion arriving with her player is sheltered with him
  (GridEntity.shelter_lead): hers lasts while his does, and her own steps (following him) don't
  end it. His view_ready moves hers into spawn grace with his. His act ends hers, and her own
  attack ends hers alone.
- **Chasers.** No monster crosses a zone after a player today: animals flee off an edge and
  raids enter on their own. So in practice this rule covers the arrival zone's own monsters:
  they can't target the sheltered body, and a wind-up begun before the arrival lands on nobody
  sheltered. If pursuit across a link is ever built (enemy-ai), its chasers arrive under the
  same rule and wait until the shelter ends.
- **Never saved.** sheltered, shelter_lead and the cooldown live only in memory. A world saved
  during a shelter loads without it: it is a 6-second state, and nobody logs back in sheltered.

Wire: PROTOCOL_REVISION 36 (35 shipped in v0.1.172), for the new "view_ready" command. An old
client never sends it, and its shelter runs the 6 s. zone_test _test_arrival_shelter:
- he and his companion arrive sheltered;
- a blow (a player's too), fire and a shot land on neither;
- no stun, no knock-down, no ailment, and a push moves him nowhere;
- a body knocked into him stops as at a wall, with a wall's hurt;
- her own step keeps hers, and talk keeps his;
- a stale view_ready does nothing, and the right one moves both into spawn grace, after which a
  blow lands;
- a second crossing inside the cooldown gets spawn grace alone;
- 60 ticks end it;
- use, search and a step each end his at once, and hers with it.
No new class_name.
## 660 step 2 A, terrain's side: the ground's fields apart from the members

Perf's phased zone arrival (660, the coordinator's approval): a crossing froze for the
whole view rebuild (the wilds about 4.3 s). Step 2 runs the ground's fields on worker
threads while frames go round (A, this) and builds the chunk meshes and cliffs nearest
first (B, perf's, on top). A changes no output: a throwaway digest of every ground
member, image and texture (grounds, kinds, corners, shore heights, floor bytes, the
shore, depth, road, forest-edge, water, floor and kinds masks, ground bytes, vertex
pairs, ledge splits, the edge memo) on hills, wilds, castle, barrow, held and forest is
the same byte for byte as main's (d0ff03f9), with one thread and with the pool.

- **_build_ground in four.** _ground_input(kinds) on the main thread (the waters,
  roads and ledges read as curves, the cells in order, the members the build remakes
  cleared; {} with no cells). _ground_fields(input), which writes no member and makes
  no node or texture: the corner pass (each cell's place, kind, corners and floor byte,
  the masks' bytes, the cells by chunk), then the shore field (shore_image,
  _water_depth, _curve_field), the road field and the forest edge's side by side, then
  the shore's finer cells (_shore_band). _apply_ground_fields(fields) on the main
  thread: the members assigned, every ImageTexture made there. _build_ground_meshes
  (fields): the material and a mesh a chunk, as before.
- **What it reads, unchanged while it runs**, listed in its doc comment: the relief,
  the waters' and roads' and the forest edge's curves and samples, _wet, _bed_levels,
  _fords, _ramp_heights, _rocks, _road_cells, _stream_cells, _built_water, the floor
  sets. Perf's arrival holds what writes them.
- **Its own memos.** The curve searches' memos (_curve_kept, _road_kept, _edge_kept:
  _near_segments' and _edge_segments' results by cell) were filled as they went, from
  whichever thread asked; a worker filling one while the main thread asks is a race.
  The chain passes its own (copies of the members', from the input) down through
  _ground_corners, _shore_bed, _curve_surface, _curve_near, _road_near, _curve_field,
  _road_field and _edge_field (each a parameter defaulting to the member, so every other
  caller is as before), and _apply_ground_fields puts them in place. _bed_kind,
  _floor_bytes_at, shore_at and _shore_corner take the fields under way the same way;
  _curve_fine and _shore_band take them as one dictionary.
- **Threads.** _run_fields runs the three fields with WorkerThreadPool.add_group_task
  and waits; Client3D.field_threads (static, 0 the pool's count, 1 each in turn on the
  calling thread) is perf's, for a small machine.

view_test _test_ground_fields (Held: its river's shore, roads and forest edge):
_ground_fields leaves the members as they were; one thread and the pool make the same
bytes. Protocol unchanged, no new class_name.


## 660 step 2 A2, terrain's side: the ground's fields in slices

Perf's first numbers on 660 step 2 A (the ground's fields apart from the members, run on
a worker as a crossing begins): the fields were 1.8 s of the wilds' 2.7-3.0 s to the card
lifting, with the corner pass and the shore's finer cells (_shore_band) run one after
the other round a three-way fan-out that gave little. The coordinator approved cutting
them into slices across threads (with perf's per-zone field cache beside it).

- **The corner pass in slices.** Each cell's place first (grounds, a quick pass: a
  water cell's bed takes its kind from the land round it, _bed_kind, whichever slice has
  it), then each cell's kind and corners in slices side by side (_run_slices), each with
  its own memo of the curve searches, then put in place in the cells' order.
- **_shore_band in its three phases**: the cells picked, their corners (_shore_corner,
  the corners listed in the order the one pass met them), their finer heights
  (_curve_fine with a slice's own memo, or the shore field), each in slices put together
  in order before the next; the four corners written back last, as before.
- **The water curves' and the forest edge's fields as texels**: _curve_texels and
  _edge_texels make a slice of cells' texels apart from the images (each texel is one
  cell's alone), and they run beside the shore and depth and the road's in one fan-out,
  put into the images in order after. _curve_field and _edge_field do the same on one
  thread for any other caller.
- **Four threads at most** (FIELD_THREADS_MOST; Client3D.field_threads still sets it,
  1 each in turn on the calling thread). Past four the threads lose: they contend for
  what they all read. On this machine the wilds' curve field took 317 ms on one thread,
  130 on four and 200 on 16; sixteen of the road's whole field at once took 2998 ms
  against 250 for one.

The same digest as A's (every ground member, image and texture on hills, wilds, castle,
barrow, held and forest) matches main's byte for byte, at one thread and at four. The
fields alone, headless beside economy's soak: the wilds 2.06 s on one thread, 0.78 s on
four; the hills 0.52 and 0.22; Held 0.89 and 0.34. view_test's _test_ground_fields (A's)
covers it. Protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

again (2026-10-24, the coordinator's (b)): "as long as you paid once you get
unlimited attempts". 548's rule was that a pact lost by the challenger's
death or leaving is lost with its gold, and nothing remembered the payment.
Now the payer's deal is kept on their record: PlayerRecord.paid_deals, the
draugr's zone -> {level, paid_step}, saved and loaded with the record
(an entry naming no deal's level is dropped), so it outlives a death, a
restart and a rejoin. The draugr reads and writes it through two World
hooks Main sets, as charges_in: World.paid_deal(player id, zone) ->
{level, paid_step} or {}, and World.deal_paid(player id, zone, level), ""
erasing (Main.paid_deal_of, set_deal_paid); enemy-ai's side writes it when
a pact is bought, keeps it when one is lost, erases it when he yields, and
offers a payer only his free "again" deal (kind "deal", cost 0, no steps)
at the paid level. The zone goes through Main.PAID_ZONE_MOVED
(barrow_lair -> barrow_deep, dungeon's barrow_two_depths.md), so a deal
bought before the redesign is the same deal after it. The talk side: a
free deal (Offers.free_deal) is taken with no gold whatever sum is said
(Main._monster_accepts), and a bare yes with nothing standing takes it at
