## 665. Room names mid-screen

Jeff: "when you enter the room, it says in the mid screen. same for
entering zones". The coordinator approved ui's design; it lands before
dungeon's barrow redesign, which writes the barrow's entries.

The data: a "rooms" section in level.json, key -> {name, rect [x, y, w, h]
or rects [[x, y, w, h], ...] or cells [[x, y], ...]} (Level.rooms_from,
beside "places"; an entry with no name or no extent is warned and left
out), read on the client as the level files are its own: nothing on the
wire and nothing for the server. Only a room a regeneration cannot move is
named (anchored, or fixed by the template), so a name never drifts off its
room; a corridor or a stair has no entry. Level.room_at says which room a
cell is in. The editor's properties panel does not offer the section yet
(EditorFields.NOT_OFFERED): its entries are written into level.json by
hand, by the tree that lays the room. Today the Hall of Fallen Souls and the Ossuary are each a whole
level, which the zone's name covers.

The showing: ArrivalCard.say(name) shows a name exactly as a zone's is
shown (660, ui's side: the title face, the outline, a third down, 0.2 s
in, held 1.5 s, 0.4 s out) with no dark and no rule: at once when nothing
shows, else after the name showing has left, never over it; a name already
showing is not said again, and a crossing (begin) drops a room name still
waiting. Main._update_room, each frame: the local player's shown cell
(GridEntity.shown_tile) entering a named room it has not just left says
the room's name; a room left and re-entered within ROOM_AGAIN_MSEC (10 s)
says nothing, so a doorway does not nag; a level load forgets the rooms
visited. Every crossing says the zone's name, with or without perf's
phased rebuild (660): Main._client_zone (a client's crossing: a link
inside a dungeon, a walk-over edge between outdoor zones, the join) and
_show_home_zone (the host's view moving zone) call say(zone_display_name())
after the repaint; when perf's begin() has already put the name up with
the dark, say() sees it showing and adds nothing. On a crossing whose
arrival cell is in a named room, the room's name follows the zone's.
ui_test _test_room_names: the section read with its warnings, room_at,
say's cases, the player walking in, out and back. Client only; no wire
change; no new class_name.

## 671. Eight camera views and the overhead lock

Jeff, after playing with the new camera: "now that we have this view it
doesn't make sense to lock into 90 degree diagonals on ad. it could be
broken into 45 degrees, W should go into nearly overhead view and lock
that way, S to move back to normal angle. going inside buildings should go
into top down view and make roofs invisible." The coordinator approved
ui's design; the indoor part follows with buildings' enclosure ("671,
buildings' side"). The bow's zoom-out with the reach is combat's (669),
not this.

Eight views. Client3D.ORBIT_STEP is 45, not 90: the yaw rests on the four
diamonds and the four square-on views between them. The free turn, the
TURN_COMMIT rule and the settles are as they were (A/D in the click
scheme, the sideways middle drag in WASD), so a tap goes one view on, 45
degrees. The saved yaw (camera_yaw=) keeps a multiple of 45 as it is, so
an old file's square-on yaw is no longer rounded to a diamond. The wall
cut, the see-through and the roofs read the camera's own direction
(_update_fade on the camera's basis, the sight shader on _camera_offset),
so they hold at any yaw; view_test's chunk-index check now runs over all
eight views and the overhead pitch. Main.wasd_direction already maps the
walk keys through the yaw, so on a square-on view W walks one straight
grid step, where on a diamond it walks a grid diagonal: W stays up the
screen, and the walk under it changes.

The overhead lock. Click scheme: W eases the pitch to OVERHEAD_PITCH (82)
over PITCH_EASE_SECONDS (0.3, eased in and out from wherever it is, so a
turn back mid-ease goes on from there with no snap) and the camera stays
there with no key held; S eases it back to the normal pitch (CAMERA_PITCH
50, or LOW_PITCH under the low camera) the same way. This replaces the
hold-to-tilt and spring-back (TILT_RATE, PITCH_MIN's floor, LOW_PITCH_MIN
gone with it). The state is saved as camera_overhead=on|off
(Net.camera_overhead, set_camera_overhead). WASD scheme, where W/S walk:
the vertical middle drag peeks toward the other pitch (up the screen from
the normal one, down it from overhead) as the peek did; let go past
PEEK_COMMIT (a third of PEEK_DRAG_PX), it goes on to that pitch and stays
(set_overhead), less and it springs back. Zoom stays on the wheel. The
ridge rule (525) still lifts the pitch where a hill would hide the player.
The overhead view shows less ground than 50 degrees does, so the view's
reach stays inside World.NEAR_TILES. The key help and the hint list say
"overhead / normal view".

controls_test: the eight-view settles and saved yaws, W overhead and S
back with the ease and its turn back, the peek's commit both ways, the
keys through Main. view_test: the low camera's overhead and back; the
chunk index at eight views. Client only; no wire change; no new
class_name.
## 660. A zone's room built over frames behind the arrival card

perf's arrival probe (2026-10-24): every crossing froze one frame for the whole 3D rebuild, about
4.2 s into the wilds and 1.3 s into the hills, the same at every visit, on a host
(Main._show_home_zone) and a box client (_client_zone) alike, both through Main._repaint. The
coordinator approved three steps: (1) the rebuild's builders a frame apart behind ui's arrival
card, (2) the near ring first by chunk and the builders cut, the goal the card lifting in under
1 s on the wilds on this card, (3) one zone's view kept, a later question of its own. Combat's
arrival shelter (661) keeps the player safe meanwhile; the client ends it with view_ready.

Step 1:

- **Client3D._room_phases** lists the room's builders in order, each whole as before:
  _phase_sets (the room node, the sets, _warm_art), _phase_land (land, rocks, solid cells,
  glimpse plans, grown trunks, forest distance, _read_edges, _read_field, _shape_ramps),
  _phase_ground (_build_ground, fires), _build_water, _add_cliffs, _phase_lights (_add_rocks,
  torches, lanterns, the fields), _add_walls, _add_decor, _phase_forest, _phase_grown,
  _phase_border, _phase_glimpses, _add_buildings, _phase_roofs (link cues, roofs, town walls),
  _phase_doors (doors due, piles). _build_room runs them in one go (setup, a rebuild by default:
  tests and benches unchanged).
- **rebuild(terrain, centre, over_frames)**: Main's _repaint passes true. _build_room_over_frames
  runs one phase, awaits the next frame, and goes on while its generation is still the latest:
  a rebuild started mid-build (a death mid-arrival, a link straight back, a zone message twice)
  bumps _build_generation, frees the room the first was building into, and the first stops at its
  next phase. _room_built (_classify_walls, the camera mode, the warm-ups) ends it,
  building_room false, the room_built signal.
- **While building_room**: Client3D._process waits (puppets, doors, fades, scatter, shadows all
  after); Main holds the player's input (_arriving: _unhandled_input, _drive_wasd).
- **Main._repaint(crossing)**: true from the crossings (_show_home_zone, _client_zone), which
  begin Main.arrival_card (ui's side of 660) with zone_display_name() and rebuild over frames; the
  zone's own terrain again (_on_terrain's same-zone refresh, _drop_zone_entities) rebuilds at once
  with no card, as before (ui: a refresh mid-play must not dim the screen); **Main._on_room_built** (room_built) shows the towns and folds on the whole room,
  finishes the card, and tells the server view_ready (combat's 661, Main.tell_view_ready with
  map_name, the level shown: a client's World.zone is a mirror with no name, which the server's
  zone check would have ignored, leaving the shelter its full 6 s). ui's card (42fc1927) landed
  just before this; ui's say() after a crossing's _repaint adds nothing over the name begin()
  already shows.

view_test _test_phased_build: over frames, then whole and told once; the same room as built at
once (scatter, which grows after, not counted); a second rebuild two frames in: the first's room
gone, told once, the same room, no orphan nodes. Client only; the view_ready command is combat's.

Step 2 B (perf's side, on terrain's A and A2 above):

- **The ground's fields on a worker.** _phase_ground_over_frames hands terrain's
  _ground_fields(input) to a WorkerThreadPool task and awaits frames until it is done (A2's slices
  start and wait inside that task); a newer rebuild, or the view leaving (_exit_tree), waits for
  it first (_end_fields_task), since it reads what the next build remakes. While it runs
  (fields_running) Main holds a clearing change to the zone shown and replays it on fields_done.
- **The ground's and cliffs' chunks in sight first.** _ground_meshes_start / _ground_mesh_chunk /
  _ground_meshes_finish and _cliffs_start / _cliff_chunk split the two builders by chunk, each
  chunk's mesh as the whole build made it. After the other phases, _fill_step builds the chunks the
  camera's frustum holds (_chunk_seen: a chunk's column CHUNK_LOW to CHUNK_HIGH) under the card at
  CARD_BUDGET_USEC (14 ms) a frame; then the card lifts (_room_built) and the rest come at
  FILL_BUDGET_USEC (4 ms) a frame, in sight and nearest first. ground_filling is true till the last
  (room_filled): the floor's shade (_shade_floor) waits for every chunk's pairs and is worked out
  once at the end, and Main holds a clearing redraw till then. So that no chunk shows at full
  light till then and darkens when the last comes (terrain's review: a pop at night or in a
  dungeon), _seed_shades works out every ground cell's shade once the fields and the indoor shade
  image are in, and each chunk is built with its corners' shade bytes already (and the soft
  scatter's shade image indoors); the shade at the end finds them right unless the light moved.
- **No pop-in.** A chunk built in sight after the lift dithers in over APPEAR_SECONDS (0.4 s): the
  ground through its SIGHT variant (the only one with a discard, so the plain ground keeps its
  early depth test), the cliffs' own shader, both reading an instance uniform `appear` against
  sight.gdshaderinc's sight_dither; the ground goes back to its own material when whole. The
  appearing material's relief_light follows the camera's yaw with the ground's (_aim_hillshade).
- **The old room hidden, freed a slice a frame** after the new one's chunks (0.2 s at once on the
  wilds).

Step 2 (a): a zone's fields kept. _kept_fields / _keep_fields hold the last FIELDS_KEPT (3)
zones' ground fields, by level, glimpse and the terrain's hash (7.8 ms on the wilds), most recent
first; any terrain change makes another key, so a changed zone is worked out afresh. A crossing
back into a kept zone skips the fields entirely (fields_hits counts it).

view_test _test_phased_build also checks every chunk job done and every old room freed, each
ground and cliff chunk's mesh (its arrays and the ground's shade bytes, by node path) the same as
built at once, and the chunks drawn when the card lifts already as shaded as at the end (it fails
without _seed_shades);
_test_kept_fields: a second arrival is a hit with the same fields (corners, shore heights, the
shore, depth, road and kinds images), a changed kind a miss whose room matches one built at once,
and at most three kept. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 671, buildings' side: inside is a space closed in by walls; the roof eases off

Jeff, after playing: "going inside buildings should go into top down view and
make roofs invisible", then, correcting the rule: "any space with enclosed
walls would count as inside, ruins, castle, etc." Ui's camera (671) tips to
top-down on it; this side tells it when.

- Client3D's signal inside_changed(inside, rect) and inside_building() ->
  Rect2i are for the local player only (the first focus point). They are
  told when the bounds of the space the player stands in change; rect is
  empty outside. Ui reads only the bool.
- A space is the floor cells (_find_enclosed) from which no way through edges
  that do not close (_closes) leads off the floor outdoors, nor reaches more
  than ENCLOSED_MOST (1500) cells outdoors, so a walled town or a fold is open
  ground.
  - An edge closes (_walled) when it is a wall or door the terrain has: drawn,
    not a plot's or a frame's (566). A ruin's stubs, rubble and gaps close
    too, since its stubs still enclose (649). A gone building's edges never
    close, and neither do edges off the floor outdoors (the land's outline,
    drawn none).
  - A lone missing edge between walls along one line (ENCLOSED_GAP 1) also
    closes. A two-cell way between buildings does not, and stays outside.
  - Underground, every room is a space.
- Outdoors only the cells beside a wall are tried. A way that opens marks
  everything it crossed as outside, so open ground is crossed about once.
- It is worked out on a layout's load. After a wall change (rebuild_walls's
  edges: a plot built, a wall felled, a decline), only the spaces beside the
  changed edges are dropped and the cells beside them tried again, never the
  whole map.
  - Full work-out on load, unlocked timings: wilds 11.5 to 18 ms, every other
    level under 5 ms.
  - A 30-edge change: wilds about 3 ms, elsewhere under 2 ms.
- The roofs off (unchanged: the buildings the player or companion stands in,
  for FADE_HOLD after) now ease over ROOF_FADE (0.2 s): their meshes'
  transparency rises, then they are shadow only; back on, it falls again.
  This replaces a cut under ui's 0.35 s camera tip.

view_test _test_inside:
- grass is outside; the house is inside, with its room's bounds;
- the roof is half eased at half ROOF_FADE, then shadow only;
- a ruin is inside; a gone plot is not; built again, it is inside;
- a local refill equals one worked out afresh;
- out again, the roof comes back whole after FADE_HOLD.

The roof tests in _test_buildings and the damage test advance ROOF_FADE. Client
only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 672. The admin panel

Jeff: "i need a admin command list in game that i can reset quests, spawn
in different zones, etc." and "i need to reset individual quest givers
because hob is the one i wanted to test again." The coordinator approved
ui's design; release keeps the box side.

One dispatcher. The panel runs the server console's own commands
(Main.admin_command, which stdin and the admin port use), never a second
list. The client sends the "admin" command {line}; the server's
Main._admin_from runs it with the sender as the caller and answers
"admin_reply" {line, text}. "help" is now one line a command, "name args:
what it does" (Main.CONSOLE_HELP), which the panel lists. The replies
release's scripts read keep their shapes: "version" with "protocol <hex>"
(stage.sh, deploy_box.ps1), "stop"/"restart" starting "restarting"
(server/deploy.sh), "players" with its count line first (ship.ps1);
ui_test pins them.

The gate. The server decides: Net.admins, from --admins or
PSYKINETIC_ADMIN_IDS (comma-separated player ids, in the box's own
/etc/psykinetic/env beside the builder ids, set by Jeff with sudo, never
in the repo), plus a host's own player. Every "admin" command is checked
(Main.admin_peer_allowed); anyone else is answered only "not allowed". The
journal says counts and kinds only: "[admin] N admins configured" at
start, "[admin] refused N", "[admin] <verb> ran"; never an id, a name or
the line. Right after an admin joins, the server sends them "admin"
{admin: true} (the join's is_admin); only then, or on the host, does F10
open the panel (Main.admin_allowed). A client that lies gains nothing.

The panel (render/admin_panel.gd, AdminPanel): F10, Esc closes; the help
lines with a filter (a line picked fills the typed line), the typed line
with its history (Up/Down, the last 30, this session), the replies; buttons
for go to a zone (every map, by its shown name), reset quests (all, or one
of the zone's quest givers by name), reset this room (zone reset), regenerate
this level (regenerate now), the hour (dawn, noon, dusk, night) and the
weather. Reset and regenerate ask once: pressed again within 3 s they run.
While its line has the keys the player does not walk (Main.is_typing).

New commands, on the console too. "go <zone> [player]": zone move, the
panel's own player without one. "quests reset [all|<giver>] [player]": the
player's quests undone (npc's and companions' lists): a giver's (a resident
by name in the player's zone) are his card's asks they took (and the
record's mirror, PlayerRecord.commissions), his once-only care done for them
(the medicine man's walk and brew, with the brew's herb and antler tally;
Hob is one), the priest's told secrets, the standing offer if it is his;
then the givers near them send their offers again. "all" is every giver's,
plus the sought they lead (Towns.sought_lost, a led body taken away as one
taken on the way is), the draugr's paid deals (the record only: a pact on
ends by its own rules), and a companion held by raiders let go, to come at
the next join (Jeff's pick open, decisions/quest-reset-captive.md; let go
till he says). Their trust and the residents' memory of them, the healer's
bought care, the barrow's blessing and the companion's story stay.

Wire: under PROTOCOL_REVISION 36 (open, unshipped): the "admin" command and
the "admin" and "admin_reply" messages, listed in net.gd. ui_test
_test_admin_panel: the kept shapes, help's lines, the console's go and
quests asking for a player, the gate, a giver's card reset, the panel's
open, help, filter, history and confirm. New class_name AdminPanel.
## 671, the indoor view

The third part of 671, after buildings' side (inside_changed). Jeff:
"going inside buildings should go into top down view and make roofs
invisible", then "any space with enclosed walls would count as inside,
ruins, castle, etc." Buildings works out the walled spaces and hides the
roof; this is the camera's half. While the local player is in a walled
space (Client3D.inside_changed true: a house's room, a castle's, a ruin
inside its stubs, every room underground) the pitch eases to INSIDE_PITCH
(88, not 90, where look_at has no up) over INSIDE_EASE_SECONDS (0.35) from
wherever it is (rest_pitch). Out, the leave counts only after
INSIDE_LEAVE_HOLD (0.5 s) outside (_update_indoors), so a doorway cell that
reads open for a step, or a step out and back, never bobs the camera, and a
room to the next room keeps it still (inside stays true, only the bounds
change); then it eases back to the view it had. Yaw and zoom are untouched;
W/S and the peek still set the view to come back to (overhead or not),
which shows on leaving. The low camera keeps its own pitch indoors (the
coordinator, until Jeff says otherwise). Underground, the whole level is
walled spaces, so a barrow or the halls are seen top-down throughout.
Client3D.indoor_view (true in the game) lets a test of the other pitches,
in a walled test room, turn it off. view_test _test_indoor_camera (in,
room to room, a doorway within the hold, out past it, S indoors, the low
camera's own); controls_test's rig and view_test's turn it off. Client
only; no wire change; no new class_name.
## 649 amended (3), economy's side: a fallen town settles before it rises

In 652's re-soak a town fell to a settlement for hunger and was a hamlet again on the very next tick. Players would see "falls back to a settlement" and "is a hamlet now" minutes apart. The coordinator's approval:
- On a fall the town's record gets "settling": 0. Each day of _strain_turn counts a calm day (nothing strains it at its stage; at a settlement, nothing at all) and a strained day sets it back to 0.
- _stage_turn won't raise a town that is settling until settling reaches decline.rise_after_days (draft 7, on the next checklist's tune line). The rise clears it. A town that has never fallen rises as before. Saved with the decline's keys.
- The town sheet's strain carries settling {days, of} while it waits, so ui's strain line can say "settling, 3 of 7 days calm" (649 amended (3), ui's side).

Wire: "settling" in the town_sheet message's strain changes what an existing message carries, so it needs revision 36 (release: 35 shipped in v0.1.172; 36 was already open on main, from 661), with its line under ## 36.

farm_test _test_settle: fallen, settling 0 of 7; the hamlet's needs met but 3 calm days still a settlement; a hungry day restarts the count; 6 calm days still settling and saved; the 7th a hamlet with settling gone. No new class_name.
## 649 amended (3), ui's side. The town sheet says a fallen town is settling

Beside economy's 649 amended (3) (the coordinator: the strain line to say
"settling, 3 of 7 days calm"). After a fall, economy's "town_sheet"
message's strain dict carries "settling": {"days": calm days in a row,
"of": the days of calm the town needs to rise again (decline's
rise_after_days, 7)} while the town is waiting to rise, and no key
otherwise; a strained day puts days back to 0. TownSheet.strain_words
adds the sentence "Settling, 3 of 7 days calm." to the strain line: alone
while the town is calm (the strain days are 0 then), after the strain
sentence on a strained day ("Strained 1 day of 10: hunger, the store
short of food. Settling, 0 of 7 days calm."), so the one line tells both
what the town is waiting out and what set it back. Nothing without the
key, as before. ui_test (the strain checks). Client only: the wire change
is economy's (PROTOCOL_REVISION 36, its push); no new class_name.

Jeff on v0.1.172, in the Ossuary: "skeletons still spawning in niches and lying down on ground,
clipping through walls." The generator's half (the coordinator's brief, 2026-10-24; the lying
and the clipping are enemy-ai's half, "631 amended, enemy-ai's side"; the two land together):

- **Open floor only.** In the barrow style every generated monster marker (the Ossuary's
  skeletons, the lair's oldest dead, layer 1's robbers) is laid on open floor: a cell with floor on
  all eight sides and no wall or door edge of its own (`Labyrinth._open_floor`; `_markers` filters
  the rooms' and ways' cells through it before 631's band spread and "near" sorting). That takes
  out by construction every alcove and niche cell (one open neighbour), every grave (a dead end),
  every cell along a room's wall or a passage's side, and any way under three wide; the Ossuary's
  passages are three wide, so their centre lines and the tombs' interiors remain, and the lair's
  caverns their middles. A band short of open cells lays fewer and the rest go deepest first, as
  631 does. Chests and crates keep their corners and niches. Other styles are unchanged (the
  halls' imps stand in two-wide ways as before).

  laid it on"): the home of a dead one is the cell it was laid on (its spawn marker, the same after
  a respawn); it rests there standing and walks back there after a chase; the level's "graves"
  list is no longer read for it. The cell is dungeon's to lay (open floor, eight floor neighbours,
  no wall or door edge), the rest on it enemy-ai's. The generated "graves" list (542 amended) is
  still written: a map of the dead ends for the tests and any later reader, no monster's.
- **Tests.** labyrinth_test `_dead_at_walls`: on every layer of the sample barrow, generations 1

guards. they must be cleared to enter the hall. the hall becomes locked on a challenge. if you fail
you forfeit gold and everything resets in the room but not the enemies you can still walk back
down again to rechallenge as long as you paid once you get unlimited attempts." Dungeon led the
design (C:/dev/review/dungeon/barrow_two_depths.md), the coordinator approved it with its answers;

the restart), npc (the payer's record, paid_deals), ui (665, the name cards), maps (654 follows),
lore (the lines and names). This is dungeon's side, step 1. Amends 580 (two layers, not three),
573 amended (the seal beside the lock), 631 (the Ossuary's count).

- **Two levels, the ids kept.** `barrow` ("The Barrow", layer 1, robbers) unchanged but for its
  named rooms; `barrow_deep` ("The Ossuary", layer 2): its far anchor is now the Hall of Fallen
  Souls, 580's hall moved whole (32 x 22 at (34, 56), against the south rim), still named `lair`
  so Main._hall_doors and the draugr's room reading move nothing; its door at (49, 56) in the north

  (GridEntity.holds_cell false): anyone may stand on the dais. Nothing

  prop's: rotation.y = atan2(f.x, f.y)) is the first of his own way and

## 397 amended (2): herds' leaked bodies counted back, a missed arrow lands with a thud

Jeff: "after removing wolf packs from the wilds there were 0 animals now". The box's journal
showed the wilds seeded once (34 groups) and the cull taking only two wolf groups, so the rest
had not gone: a group's "out" (bodies made and not yet back) only came down through retire,
a kill or a flight, and a body that left any other way (a room reset, a regeneration, a saved
body not made again at a restart, any despawn) kept its out for ever. Once an area's out
reached out_per_zone (24), recall_near made nothing there again. The coordinator approved (a)
and (d) of enemy-ai's four; numbers and placement unchanged, economy (on hold) reviews after.

- **Herds.reconcile(area)**: counts the spawned animals of each group among the bodies in the
  zone World is in (`bodies`, a Callable; unset, World.entities()) and puts any out beyond
  them back into the group's count. recall_near calls it once a day an area, at its first
  recall, so a body made today and wandering is never taken for a leak twice. It prints
  `[herds] <area>: <n> leaked bodies back`, and the end of each day prints
  `[herds] <area>: <groups> groups, kept <n>, out <n>` for every area, for release's grep
  after a deploy. Economy's review: fold_records, folding a record that names a group still
  held, lowers that group's out by one, as retire does, so reconcile never counts it back a
  second time.
- **A missed arrow lands with a thud** (World.shoot): a shot that hits nothing makes
  Senses.NOISE_THUD_LIGHT (2) at the cell it fell on, by the archer, beside the bow's own
  NOISE_BOW (3) at the archer. An Animal flees any noise that is not a step and not its herd's,
  so game beside a miss bolts, as it would from a stone; a hit already made its own sound.
- Sight, for the coordinator (unchanged): rabbit 7, boar 6, wolf 8, deer and stag 9; the bow
  reaches 3, 5, 7, 9 cells by draw. A deer or stag sees a hunter at the bow's full reach, so
  only a full draw from the edge of its sight lands before it runs.

herds_test _test_leaks (24 made, the zone reset: stalled the same day, all 24 back the next,
then 3 back after a second reset, then none, and a body folded back from a record not counted twice); monster_test _test_wild_shot_near (an ears-only
rabbit nine cells from the archer grazes, a shot along the row past it falls beside it, it
bolts). Narrow by request: herds.gd and World.shoot only. Protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

Finished (economy's note (2), the coordinator's approval: the same fix, no label of its own): an
area nobody came near kept its leaked out, and economy's spare() gives hunters and camps nothing
from a group with out, so its hunting stayed shut till the next recall there. Zones never close
once open (boot opens every zone the snapshot holds), so a herd body is only ever in an open
zone's entities. reconcile moves from recall_near's first call of a day to the start of
Herds._daily, before the day's budget (economy's ask: the animals back are hunted that day), for
every area with out: an open zone's out beyond its spawned bodies goes back, as before, and an
area whose zone is not open gives all its out back. Herds.bodies_in (area) -> its bodies or null
(a test's); unset, World's own list for the zone World is in (a zone's entities are kept only
while World is elsewhere), the zone's entities for another open one, null for none. A reset is
caught at the next day's turn, as before. herds_test _test_leaks turns the day instead of
recalling, and checks a zone not open (all out back, spare again) and the unset bodies;
_test_taken's two bodies out are in the room.
## 603 amended (3), combat's side: a move under way is dropped when he yields or rests

In Jeff's fight, and in enemy-ai's monster_test, the draugr began a spin, yielded, and the spin
still swept a few ticks later and knocked the player down while he rested. Draugr._yield and
_end_pact dropped his own wind-up and recalled his axe, but World had no way to drop a boss's
move under way. The coordinator approved enemy-ai's ask.

- **World.drop_boss_move(by):** the move he has under way is given up at once, and nothing of
  it lands.
  - A spin or a throw: its telegraph ends unlanded and his wind-up is shown over. A throw
    dropped before it lands leaves the axe in his hands.
  - A charge, still roaring or already running (physics' rush): it stops as a body in its way
    stops it (_end_rush, then _charge_over "stopped"). He stands where he is, and the axe stays
    where it lies until his recall.
  - Any other telegraph of his ends unlanded too.
  - Nothing happens when no move is under way.
- **Who calls it:** enemy-ai's Draugr._yield and _end_pact, beside _drop_windup and
  _recall_axe (573 amended (3), enemy-ai's side). Any other boss mind that ends a fight calls
  it too.

combat_test _test_dropped_moves: a spin dropped sweeps nobody; a throw dropped strikes nobody,
the axe kept; a charge dropped in its roar never runs, and dropped under way stops where it
was. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 669. The bow's draw: damage, reach and stamina over the hold

Jeff on the bow: "it takes full pull back to get damage maxed", "holding at max nock narrowest
accuracy starts draining stamina", and "full damage at current max range, but held longer goes
out further at the expense of diminishing damage, maybe only if the target is in the range does
it take 4 dmg, but if its beyond that it gets slightly less damage". The coordinator approved
combat's design; the numbers are drafts for Jeff. This changes 583 (shorter shots had hit
harder: 1.5/1.2/1.0/0.8 at 3/5/7/9 cells) and 620 (the cone settled to 2° over 4 s).

- **Drawing up**, three steps (the bow's verb: steps, damage_at, full, draw_min, draw_steps):

  | Step | Reached at | Strength | damage_at | Reach | Cone |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0.3 s | 2 | 0.8 | 5 cells | 20° |
  | 2 | 0.7 s | 3 | 1.2 | 7 cells | 10° |
  | 3, full draw | 1.2 s | 4 | 1.6 | 9 cells | 4° |

  Each step takes longer than the last. The cone is lerped between steps over each step's ticks.
  A quick bow and armour's draw multiple scale the times as before.
- **Held past full draw**, the reach grows in bands of +2 cells: 11 at 1.8 s, 13 at 2.5 s, 15
  at 3.3 s. The damage goes by the struck body's distance (World.distance), not the hold:
  - within 9 cells, 1.6;
  - 9 to 11 cells, 1.2;
  - 11 to 13 cells, 0.8;
  - 13 to 15 cells, 0.4.

  That is Items.damage_for: before full draw, the step's; at or past it, the band the body
  stands in, out to the step drawn. An arrow flies no farther than its step's reach. The cone
  stays at full draw's 4° (no shaking), so the longer lob strays farther in cells only because
  it flies farther.
- **Stamina** (World._tend_draws): at or past full draw, the bow's drain, 2 a tick, comes off
  the holder's stamina as an exertion, so none comes back while held. A full bar of 100 lasts
  5 s past full draw. At 0 the arms give out: the bow is let down with the arrow kept and
  nothing loosed (World.draw_given_up; the archer is told "Your arms give out."), and the 0
  winds them (597). Lowering resets the draw as ever. A body that pays no stamina never drains.
- ~~**Armour caps the reach, not the strength**~~ (622 step 2's range_steps). Withdrawn by
  "622 amended, bending 669": armour no longer caps the reach, World.reach_cap is gone, and
  step_cap is the bow's last step.
- **The aim** (ui's marker, read on the client from the replicated raised_tick, so it is the
  server's):
  - the arc at range_of;
  - the cone from spread_of;
  - the pips beside the marker are now the shot's strength at the aim's reach (Main.aim_pips:
    2, 3, 4 drawing up, 3, 2, 1 in the bands);
  - past full draw, a ring on the aim at full_range_of, where full strength ends
    (Client3D._aim_full_mark).
- **The camera pulls back with the reach** (Jeff: "for hunting.. you want to have distance, the
  camera should start to zoom out as the bow range goes up"):
  - Client3D.aim_reach, which Main calls beside 617's aim_lead each frame while drawn, eases a
    pull-back factor in _size_factor over the player's zoom.
  - The factor is the least that keeps the point DRAW_PULL_MARGIN (1.5 cells) past the reach,
    the aim lead counted, on screen. It's found by halves through the camera itself
    (reach_fits: the ortho size under the high camera, the eye's distance under the low).
  - It's never under 1, so the view never zooms nearer than the player's own setting.
  - It's at most DRAW_PULL_MOST, 1.8, and under the high camera within World.NEAR_TILES as the
    wheel's ZOOM_MAX is.
  - It eases at DRAW_PULL_RATE (7.5 a second: most of the way in about 0.4 s), out as the reach
    grows and back when the bow is let go. Client only.
  - view_test _test_draw_pull: from the high camera and the low, 15 cells out is kept on screen
    every way, a reach of 5 leaves the zoom, and let go it is back.
- **The mean miss** (combat_test _test_cone_spread, 400 rolls each), in cells at the step's
  range: 0.43 at 0.5 s (5 cells), 0.21 at full draw (9), 0.35 at the last band (15).

The arrow's landing and hit sounds (art/audio/slots.json: arrow_hit_flesh, _wood, _stone,
arrow_land, arrow_water) now carry 18 cells, past the bow's new 15, keeping the +3 margin they
had over its old 9 (sound_kit_test checks they carry past the reach).

Monster archers loose on their kind's aim_spread and hold cap, as 620 enemy-ai's side has it.
They now loose the first step at 0.8, where they had loosed at 1.5; enemy-ai tunes them later.
Wire: a line under 36, since the client reads the steps, reaches and cone from the verb and
raised_tick. Tests:
- items_test: range by the hold, the edge, the cone, damage_for by band, strengths by step,
  plate full at 5;
- combat_test _test_draw_held: full strength within 9 at the last band, the least at 14, short
  of it at 13's band; no drain below full draw, 2 a tick at it, none back; at 0 let down,
  nothing loosed, winded;
- monster_test, ui_test and view_test: the new numbers.
No new class_name.

## 673. Feel tuning: live fields, slow time and a practice hall, in a local host

Jeff: "i need way to tune combat and animation feel that has a quicker feedback loop." A number
changed used to mean land, cut, deploy and play: hours. Combat leads; pc-character has the clips,
ui the panel, enemy-ai the monsters' fight values. The coordinator approved the design
(C:/dev/review/combat/tuning/design.md) as steps 1 to 3. This is step 1.

- **Where:** only in a local host (Net Mode.HOST: the sim and the view in one process), by
  Tuning.allowed. A joined client's keys do nothing (its numbers would be the server's), and a
  server (the box) never runs any of it. Nothing reads a save at start-up: only the panel loads
  one, on a click. No message, command or replicated field, so no wire change.
- **Fields (Tuning):** a path whose first part is the source that reads and sets it:
  - `combat.<key>` and `combat.moves.<move>.<key>` go through World.load_combat_rules and moves;
  - `physics.<key>` goes through World.load_physics_rules, using physics.json's names;
  - `items.<id>.<key>` is an item's verb, through the new Items.set_verb, which puts the row
    through verb_from again, so a bow's ticks to full draw are worked out anew;
  - a tree's own come through Tuning.register_source(prefix, get, set, list). Main registers
    `camera.draw_pull_margin`, `_most` and `_rate` (Client3D's draw pull, now vars with the
    constants as defaults). Step 2 adds pc-character's feel.json, ui's camera and enemy-ai's
    `monsters.fight`.
  - Tuning.fields() lists each one for the panel: group, kind (int, float, bool, ints, floats),
    range, owner, and takes (now, or spawn for a value read when a body is made).
  - apply() fits the value to the field's kind and refuses a word, a number under 0 or a wrong
    shape. It keeps the repo's value the first time, for reset, reset_all and the save. Setting
    a field to its repo value drops the change.
- **Save:** save() writes only what changed, path to {value, repo}, with the build's version, to
  user://tuning/<date_time>.json. copy_to_review() puts the file in C:/dev/review/tuning, and the
  coordinator routes Jeff's sets to the owner trees, which commit his numbers in their data
  files. The game never writes levels/ or art/. load_file() reads a save back in. Tests write
  only under test_ports.gd's scratch().
- **Time:** fixed keys, not the Options' (Main.tuning_key):
  - F8 steps the time scale through 1, 0.5 and 0.25 (Engine.time_scale). World's tick runs off
    _process's delta, so the sim, the clips and the eases slow together.
  - F9 pauses: time_scale 0.
  - "." while paused plays exactly one sim tick at the scale. World.pause_at_tick stops the
    tick loop after it, sets time_scale 0 again and clears the accumulator, so no catch-up
    burst follows.
  - F7 emits Main.tuning_panel_toggled for ui's panel. F10 is ui's admin panel (672) and F11 is
    fullscreen.
- **The practice hall:** levels/practice, a 24 by 24 stone hall (written through the editor's LevelMap, its layout an image import as every level's) with a pillar to shoot past and
  a walled side room behind a door.
  - It's a dev level (Level.DEV_LEVELS): no link, border or world map reaches it, and WorldMap's
    reach check leaves it out. It's content Jeff asked for, not part of the world.
  - `--practice` (Net.practice) makes the process a host of its own there: 127.0.0.1, port
    PRACTICE_PORT (DEFAULT_PORT + 73), no snapshot. The main menu's Practice button
    (MainMenu.practice_pressed, Main.start_practice) starts one beside the game and closes the
    game, so practice never mixes with the box.
  - Main.place_dummies puts a dummy at each of the hall's `dummy...` spawn points, each time the
    room is laid.
- **The arena:**
  - Tuning.spawn_dummy: a brute's body, Monster.practice_still (it never moves or strikes) and
    never_dies (World.damage holds its hp at 1; full again after DUMMY_REFILL_TICKS, 3 s,
    without a blow).
  - spawn_kind(kind, at, fights): any monsters.json kind, standing passive or fighting.
  - clear() removes only what the arena made.
  - give(who, id): armour worn, a shield or arrows in the left hand, else the right; two hands
    or a bow empty the left, and a bow comes with its arrows.
  - full(who) restores hp and stamina.
  - ui's panel calls these.
- **Tests:** tuning_test covers:
  - the fields and their kinds;
  - apply, refusal and reset for each source, plus a registered one;
  - a client and a server refused (no change, time left alone, no save written or read, Main
    taking none of F7, F8, F9 or "."), and no script but Tuning's own calling load_file;
  - a save holding only the changes beside the repo values, copied for review and read back;
  - the scales, the pause, and a step of exactly one tick with nothing after it;
  - the dummy held at 1 and full again, never moved, a passive kind and a fighting one, clear;
  - give and full;
  - the hall reached by no level, map or plane.
  world_map_test counts the dev levels out of "every level is reachable".

New class_name: Tuning.
## 668. A level's own music: barrows-moody in the barrow

Jeff (2026-10-24, by way of the coordinator): "barrows-moody.wav is in for barrows 1st
level music".

- **A level key**: a level's level.json may name a music slot, `"music": "music.barrow"`
  (levels/barrow only: not barrow_deep or barrow_lair). Music.level_music(level) reads it
  from the registered config (a generated or edited level, Level.register) or else the
  file, once per level; a name that is no slot reads as none. Regen's generated config is
  the template's, so a regenerated barrow keeps it.
- **Played by Music**: in a level with its own music, Music.weights puts that slot at the
  ground's weight (1, less half the tension) in place of the zone's ground and melody,
  always, not in phrases; the tension layers still rise over it. It starts from its
  beginning, and eases in on arrival and out on leaving over LEVEL_FADE 1 s (95% of the
  way), as the title's music does (656); the beds keep FADE_SECONDS. A level left keeps
  its slot in the weights at 0 so it eases out. The view and its Music last across zones,
  so the fade is heard.
- **The slot, music.barrow**: music, a bed on the Music bus, flat, 0 dB. Its take is
  Jeff's own work, in the repo at art/audio/music/music.barrow/music.barrow.ogg (963 KB),
  named in the slot's "source" (by Jeff, Ableton Live, licence "own", 2026-10-24): not
  third-party, so takes.json has no entry and THIRD_PARTY.md's generated block no line
  (it lists own takes only when someone other than Jeff made them); docs/sound_status.md
  lists it under own takes. No Sonniss file and nothing from any library went into it.
- **The take**: his master, the second export (Jeff: "its loop should avoid the click";
  48 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV, 42.67 s: 16 bars at 90 bpm, peak -7.3 dBFS) as Ogg Vorbis
  quality 7 at its own level (no headroom needed), the same 2048000 frames, imported
  looping at the file's end. The master stays in his folder, copied, never moved or
  edited.
- **The seam, by measure**: the first export (21.33 s) cut its last bar while sounding (a
  step of 0.102 against at most 0.029 at its bar lines, a high-frequency burst 4 to 5 dB
  above theirs, -20.5 to -28.5 dB rms across the wrap). The second wraps as its own bar
  lines cross: the high-frequency burst at the wrap -42.1 dB against -42.8 to -43.1 at
  theirs, the level -21.2 to -26.1 dB rms across it as at theirs (a drop of 3 to 6 dB at
  half of them), the step 0.042 against 0.007 to 0.029 (the largest, but within the
  track's own sample-to-sample motion: its second difference 0.037 against the track's
  most, 0.056). So no click by measure; a listening file for Jeff in
  C:/dev/review/sound/barrow.

sound_kit_test: the barrow names music.barrow, the levels below none; Jeff's take; the
weights in place of the dungeon's and under tension. view_test _test_level_music: in the
barrow it is wanted, eased in within 1 s and playing; gone below, eased out and stopped.
Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.


## 668 amended. A room's own music: umbrage-theme in Umbrage

Jeff (2026-10-25, by way of the coordinator): "umbrage-theme wav has been done", the town
of Umbrage's music; the name goes wherever the town stands.

- **A room key**: a named room's entry in level.json "rooms" (665) may name a music slot
  as a level may, `"music": "music.umbrage"` (the wilds' umbrage room only, for now).
  Music.room_music(level, cell) reads it from the same config as level_music (the
  registered one, else the file, read once), the room found by Level.rooms_from and
  room_at as the room cards find it; ui's rooms_from is unchanged and does not carry the
  key. While the listener is in such a room its slot is the own music, played and eased
  as a level's (in place of the zone's ground and melody, from its start, LEVEL_FADE in
  on entering and out on leaving), over the level's own music if that has one too.
- **It goes with the town**: when Held step 2 (654) moves the town, maps carries the key
  to the town's room or to its level (levels/held, "music" at the top) and drops it here;
  Music needs no change for either. Regen keeps an anchored room's entry whole, key and
  all.
- **The slot, music.umbrage**: music, a bed on the Music bus, flat, 0 dB, Jeff's own take
  in the repo at art/audio/music/music.umbrage/music.umbrage.ogg (565 KB, since 2.57 MB: 668 amended (2), below; source by Jeff,
  Ableton Live, licence "own", 2026-10-25): no takes.json entry, no THIRD_PARTY line.
- **The take**: his master (48 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV, 22.59 s: 8 bars at 85 bpm, peak
  -6.7 dBFS, rms -26.9, 7 dB under the barrow's) as Ogg Vorbis quality 7 at its own
  level, the same 1084236 frames, imported looping. The master stays in his folder,
  copied, never moved or edited.
- **The seam, by measure**: clean, the wrap as its own bar lines. Each bar ends decayed
  and opens on a hit; at the wrap the step is 0.0004 against 0.0002 to 0.0013 at the seven

  against 17.3 to 21.4). A listening file for Jeff in C:/dev/review/sound/umbrage.

## 583 amended: Shift stands firm and draws

Jeff, on v0.1.172: "holding down shift while running allows you to move while aiming - the
point of shift is to stand firm and start nocking". The coordinator approved this binding.
It replaces 583's walk while drawn (at half pace, World.DRAWN_TICK_SCALE, now gone) and amends
ui's 2026-10-22 Shift+LMB binding (draw on Shift with the left press, loose on the release,
letting go of Shift changing nothing).

- **The keys (Main):** with a bow and arrows in hand:
  - Shift held (the stand key; not while typing, nothing on the cursor) draws at once, each
    frame through Main.drive_stand_draw. A Shift+left press before the draw is up draws too.
  - A left press while drawn looses the aim's way (or lets down before draw_min). The left
    release no longer looses.
  - Letting go of Shift while drawn lowers the bow ("stance" ""), the arrow kept, nothing
    loosed. With Shift still down after a shot, the next draw starts.
  - While drawn, a walk key only turns the body (Main.face_toward, a "face" command at the
    cursor's turn rate) and the aim follows the mouse. No step is predicted or sent, in either
    scheme: the click scheme's keys stay the camera's (671), and its clicks are the bow's as above.
- **The server (World):** a drawn body stands firm.
  - try_move refuses a step while raised is "draw", and order_move refuses a walk ordered
    while drawn.
  - As a draw begins, try_stance calls World.stand_firm: the walk ordered, its via tiles and an
    attack walked to dropped, and a player's queued steps cleared. If the client was already
    showing one, the step is refused to it (report_move_refused, its refusal count), so its
    view comes back to the cell it stands in. A client can't walk while drawing.
- **Wire:** a line under PROTOCOL_REVISION 36. raised "draw" means standing now, so an old
  client would predict drawn steps the server refuses. No new message or command.
- **ui's side follows:** the controls help, the hints and the key list say the new binding.
- **Tests:** controls_test _test_bow_click_walks: a plain click walks; Shift with the press
  draws; the button let go stays drawn; a press looses; Shift held while walking drops the walk
  and draws; drawn, no walk order and no step; let go of Shift, let down with the arrow kept,
  and walking again; queued shown steps refused as the draw begins. items_test: a step while
  drawn refused, the draw kept.
No new class_name.
## 662. Held weapons rest out of a fight, and fidget clear of the body

Jeff: "while we're working on weapons, hold weapons should have different resting animations, such
for example, sheathing sword, definitely not scratching head or anything that sword goes near
body." The coordinator approved pc-character's design in three steps under this number: (a) the
fidgets filtered by what is in hand, with a test; (b) rest clips for what stays in hand; (c) the
blades sheathed at the hip (art-kit's gear.scabbard and gear.sheath, "662, art-kit's side"), the
shield on the back, the lantern moved to belt_r, with sound's draw and stow cues ("662, sound's
side"). Stowing is a look only: no blow waits on a draw (the coordinator: if Jeff wants a cost to
striking from the sheath, he'll say so).

**The survey** (each held piece through each idle and fidget clip, a man, every 0.2 s): with a
sword in hand the head scratch (Idle_LookAround, 0.06 m from the face), Drink (the hand to the
mouth), Fidget_Sleeve, Fidget_ArmsCrossed and Fidget_Shoulders put the blade into the body
(hundreds of its vertices inside), and Idle_Talking brings it to 0.13 m of the head; the dagger,
knife, hammer and spear alike. Clean for every kind: Idle, Idle_Tired, Fidget_Shift,
Fidget_LookBack, Fixing_Kneeling, PickUp_Kneeling, Crouch_Idle, but for the hammer crouching (its
head 0.06 m from the face) and the shield kneeling (0.02 m); the test's five builds found more
(below). A two-hander stands ready (Axe_Ready)
and never fidgets; the bow's Bow_Idle holds the arms over a fidget.

**Step (a).** `Client3D.fidget_with(clip, held)`: both hands empty, any of the model's fidgets;
anything in either hand, only ARMED_FIDGETS (Fidget_Shift, Fidget_LookBack, Fixing_Kneeling,
PickUp_Kneeling, Crouch_Idle) less ARMED_NOT for a held kind, as the test found them: the
hammer's crouch and both kneels (its head 0.10 m from the face), the shield's Fixing_Kneeling,
and the bow's (into the leg, the heavier builds). `_pick_fidget` draws only from those. Addressing someone with a thing
in hand plays no Idle_Talking: it stands (the coordinator: calm, it stows first once (c) is in;
mid-fight, no gesture at all). `AnimRig.base_at(clip, seconds)` holds the base layer on a pose to
measure, as upper_at does the upper. anim_rig_test `_test_armed_fidgets`: none of the six with a
sword in hand, all of them empty-handed; knife, dagger, sword, hammer, spear, bow (Bow_Idle over
it) and shield as Client3D holds them, standing (Idle, Idle_Tired) and through each fidget
fidget_with allows them, five builds, every quarter second: no vertex inside the trunk, the head
or the left leg, none within ARMED_HEAD_CLEAR (0.12 m) of the head.

**Step (b).** Client3D.RESTS: a piece that stays in hand rests after REST_STAND_SECONDS (2)
standing and REST_SECONDS (8) with nothing rousing it, its upper clip (tools/humanoid_clips.py),
the piece slid "grip" up in the hand (`_slide_held`) so its end meets the ground: the giant axe
head down on the ground ahead at 60°, the right hand on its butt before the belly, the left hand
over it (Haft_Rest; HandReach let go); the battle axe, 1.6 m, the same with the hands at the upper
chest (Haft_Rest_High; slid up its haft instead, its butt came up into the chest); the spear
grounded upright beside the right foot, the hand at the chest (Spear_Rest, slid 0.55); the hammer
and the pick hanging at the side, the head down and out from the leg (Hang_Rest; the pick slid
0.16 so a shorter body's doesn't touch). Each loop looks slowly about, the head alone (no
Fidget_LookRound or Fidget_Grip: under a rest the upper layer holds the spine and head, so a
fidget beneath only shifts the legs). Rousing (`_rest_of`, `_roused`): its own swing, raised
guard or draw; a blow seen near it (`_combat_at`); a monster's own alert hunting or fighting;
anyone else's, a monster so within REST_ROUSED_CELLS (6), looked for twice a second; and taking a
piece up (a held change). Roused, the rest goes at once, the piece back as held, the left hand to
grip_2 (the ready stance as before). A resting kind kneels or crouches in no fidget (KNEELS in
ARMED_NOT: the piece is on the ground). Set down and taken up are heard (SoundKit.stow_slot,
"662, sound's side": gear_stow, gear_draw), once sound's side is in: sound held (Jeff low on
credits), this landed first, so Client3D looks stow_slot up on SoundKit's script and is silent

**Step (c), after art-kit's pieces.** The sword (gear.scabbard), dagger and knife (gear.sheath)

so that the bow curve faces the body, it lies under the quiver in the same direction". The

draw, a blow seen near or a monster hunting near puts it back in the hand at once (no draw delay, as

its upper limb clears the neck through the jog. The one he doesn't pick is dropped. anim_rig_test

## 663. She steps clear of a boss's telegraph

Jeff's draugr fight on v0.1.172: "Pip didn't attempt to dodge the swing
and died." A companion never read World.telegraphs() (decision 602), so she
stood in a spin or a charge till it landed. The coordinator's approval;
the numbers are drafts for Jeff.

- Each choice (Companion._act, _read_telegraphs): the telegraphs showing in
  her zone whose source (a Monster) she has a line to within SIGHT_RANGE.
  Their cells are her danger. One covering her cell that lands within
  DODGE_LOOK (12) ticks, once she has seen it DODGE_REACT (2) ticks
  (DODGE_WARY 2 more when wary or worse: hangs_back), and she dodges:
  Intent.DODGE (server only) to the nearest free floor cell within
  DODGE_REACH (3) outside every telegraph showing; of those as near, one
  still beside whom she fought, else one farther from the source. Her
  voice is told "You leap clear of <source>'s <kind>."
- While any telegraph she sees shows she steps into none of it: whatever
  her intent (but a dodge or a retreat) she strikes from where she stands
  if she can reach, else waits it out.
- Devoted and standing over her downed player (_stands_over) she does not
  dodge: she takes the blow for them (approved).
- A telegraph she cannot see (no line to its source) she does not dodge;
  a dodge too far for the ticks left still tries, and the blow lands.

companion_test _test_dodge: a ring telegraphed over her; not before it
nears and her reaction; clear of it before it lands; into none of it while
it shows; nothing once it lands. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

  writes it through World.deal_paid(player_id, zone, level or "" to erase),

  spawn index (npc's).

## 673 step 2, enemy-ai's side: the monsters' fight feel as data

Combat's feel tuning (673, the coordinator's approval of
C:/dev/review/combat/tuning/design.md; Jeff: "i need way to tune combat and
animation feel that has a quicker feedback loop"). Monster's fight constants
move to levels/monsters.json, so the tuning panel can set them live. Release:
"the move must not change any fight".

- **The block**: a top-level "fight" block in levels/monsters.json holds
  windup_ticks 6, charge_range 4, charge_pace 0.5, dart_after_ticks 3,
  backstab_damage 1, pace_spread 0.15, cooldown_spread 2,
  flank_patience_ticks 20, flee_ticks 60, flee_tiles 6, flee_near_tiles 4,
  rout_hurt 0.7, dread_flee_below 0.5, and flee_below {bold 0.15, cautious
  0.35, cowardly 0.6}.
- **Overrides**: a kind's row may carry its own "fight" over the block.
  read_kinds skips the block (it is no kind) and keeps a row's "fight".
- **The reading**: Monster.fight_for(kind) gives FIGHT_DEFAULTS (the old
  constants, kept as the defaults), under the block, under the row.
  _temper sets the instance vars of the same names (windup_ticks and the
  rest) at spawn, and the fight reads those.
- **The panel's loader**: Monster.set_fight_block(dict) sets the block in
  place; new spawns take it. null reads the file again.
- **Unknown keys**: an unknown key is warned of and left out. Ints are kept
  ints.
- **The panel's source**: Tuning.register_source("monsters",
  Monster.tuning_value, Monster.set_tuning_value, Monster.tuning_fields),
  registered by Main beside the camera's when Tuning.allowed().
  - Paths: "monsters.fight.<name>" (flee_below as
    "monsters.fight.flee_below.<temper>"), and "monsters.<kind>.fight.<name>"
    for a kind's own (null where it has none).
  - The setter merges one key into the block and sets it (or into the kind's
    row); unknown paths and non-numbers are refused.
  - The lister gives the block's 16 rows, group "Monsters", owner enemy-ai,
    takes "spawn", each with its range (FIGHT_SPANS).
- **Left for later**: the draugr's own (spin, throw, closing, back-off,
  fists) wait for combat's word after 573 amended (4).
- **Tests**: monster_test _test_fight_data: every kind's fight from the file
  equals the old constants, value and type, overrides included; "fight" is
  no kind; a spawned brute carries them; the panel's block reaches new
  spawns with the rest as before; null reads the file again.
  _test_fight_panel: through Tuning on a host, the source's 16 rows listed
  (windup_ticks an int taken at spawn), windup_ticks and flee_below.bold
  applied reach the next spawn, and reset gives the file's values again.
- **Wire**: none (server sim; a client's monsters carry the defaults). No
  new class_name.
## 673, ui's side. The tuning panel

Combat's 673 holds the fields (Tuning); ui builds the window to it, as the
coordinator's design (C:/dev/review/combat/tuning/design.md) splits it.

- **Where:** render/tuning_panel.gd (TuningPanel), on Main's HUD. F7 in a
  local host (Main.tuning_key emits tuning_panel_toggled) toggles it; open()
  does nothing unless Tuning.allowed(), so a joined client never shows it.
  Esc lets an arena pick go first, then closes it (after the admin panel).
  While a typed field has the keys the player does not walk (Main.is_typing).
- **Fields tab:** a row for each of Tuning.fields(), under its group's
  heading (a group with a field that takes at a spawn says "new spawns
  only"), read afresh at each open so a tree's later source shows. The
  control follows the kind: an int or float a slider over its min to max
  (an int's step 1, a float's a 200th) with a typed number beside it, a bool
  a checkbox, ints or floats a typed list ("4, 6, 8", commas or spaces).
  A change goes through Tuning.apply at once; a refused one (a word, a
  wrong length) changes nothing and says so. A changed row (Tuning.changes)
  is marked "* " in rust with its Reset; Reset all, a filter by path, Save
  (Tuning.save), Copy to review (the newest save, saved first if there are
  changes, Tuning.copy_to_review) and Load (a pick of the saves in
  Tuning.save_dir, newest first, Tuning.load_file).
- **Arena tab:** a monsters.json kind (Monster.kinds) with Fights on or off,
  "Spawn at a click" and "Dummy at a click": the next left click in the
  world (Main._unhandled_input, before any other click) places it at the
  cell under the cursor (Tuning.spawn_kind / spawn_dummy); Clear
  (Tuning.clear); an item (Items.ids) given to the local player
  (Tuning.give); Full hp and stamina (Tuning.full); Reset the hall (the
  console's "zone reset" for this zone, the tuning kept, its dummies laid
  again by place_dummies); the time keys' buttons and the scale shown.
- **Wire:** none. A local host is the world, so the panel calls Tuning
  directly; no message, command or replicated field.
- **Tests:** ui_test _test_tuning_panel: a client's F7 opens nothing; a row
  a field with its kind's control; typed numbers and lists; a change taken
  and marked, a word refused, a row's reset and reset all; the filter; save,
  then load in a scratch folder; the arena's pick waiting and Esc letting it
  go.

New class_name: TuningPanel.

## 666, enemy-ai's side: the draugr says whether his zone's dead stand (ossuary_sealed)

666 (dungeon's two depths) has Main connect the draugr's `ossuary_sealed(sealed)` to
`_seal_hall`, which holds the Hall's door with DEAD_LOCK while the Ossuary's dead stand ("they
must be cleared to enter the hall"). Until now the draugr had no such signal, so the Hall never
sealed. Now he has it:

- **The rule**: `sealed` is true while any of his zone's OSSUARY_KINDS (skeleton,
  skeleton_guard) stands: hp left, not laid at rest, and not one of his own risen (his retinue
  fights beside him in the Hall, not in the Ossuary). It is false once every one is dead or laid.
- **When**: Draugr._tell_ossuary runs each sim tick, before anything else he does, gone or not.
  It emits at his first tick and again only when the answer changes. Main hooks him at spawn
  (_hook_talker), before that first tick.
- **His rest** stills the zone's dead (_still_the_dead, laid), so while he rests the seal lets go
  on its own. When his rest ends they rise and the seal holds again.

monster_test _test_ossuary_sealed drives the real signal: true at the first tick and said once;
a skeleton killed with the grave guard still standing stays true; the guard laid gives false; the
guard risen gives true again. level_test's _seal_hall checks stay dungeon's. Server sim, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.

## 673 step 2, pc-character's side: the animation feel in art/kit/feel.json

Combat's feel tuning (673; Jeff: "i need way to tune combat and animation feel that has a quicker
feedback loop"), step 2: each tree moves its own constants to data, so the F11 panel can set them
live. pc-character's are how a swing, a step or a hit reads. art/kit/feel.json holds them as
{"feel": {"<script>.<constant>": value}}: client3d's clip_blend, clip_heavy_contact,
backpedal_clip_speed, roll_speed, down_tilt_speed, shot_speed and a new gait_rate (every gait's
clip played that much faster than its pace says, 1 as before: steps read quicker or slower);
anim_rig's strike_speed_min and _max; art_kit's clip_contact; creature_view's speed_min,
speed_max, charge_speed and blend. `ArtKit.feel(key, CONSTANT)` reads one where it is used (the
file read once, a key it lacks the constant); `ArtKit.set_feel(key, value)` sets one for the run
(null puts the file's back), so the next clip, step or blow takes it: one store, not a setter per
script. The constants stay in the code as the values a key the file lacks falls back to, and
anim_rig_test `_test_feel_moved` holds every value in the file to the constant it names (release:
nothing seen changes by the move); a set Jeff saves comes back through the coordinator into the
file and the constants with it. clip_blend (but a fidget's) and creature_view.blend are a rig's
when it is made: they take on bodies made after a change. On combat's panel (673 step 1, F7) the
feel is a registered source, not rows in a table: Main registers "feel" beside the camera's
(`Tuning.register_source("feel", ArtKit.feel_value, ArtKit.set_feel_value, ArtKit.feel_fields)`), each
key of the file a row "feel.<key>" in the Animation group with its range (ArtKit.FEEL_RANGES),
owner pc-character, the two blends marked "spawn". anim_rig_test also sets strike_speed_max for a
run and puts it back, and `_test_feel_source` lists, applies and resets through Tuning. Client
only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 674. The Character Lab: the player's body alone, its clips under a game camera

Jeff: "i also need to work on the player model and run animations separately." Approved by the
coordinator as three steps; this is step 1. A scene of its own, client3d/character_lab.tscn
(class_name CharacterLab), run as `godot --path <checkout> --scene res://client3d/character_lab.tscn`
(C:/dev/review/character_lab/lab.cmd starts it from the main checkout). It shows one person on a
grid floor under the game's three views (keys 1, 2, 3: CAMERA_PITCH orthographic, the low
camera's LOW_PITCH and LOW_FOV, the overhead OVERHEAD_PITCH), orbited by a drag and zoomed by the
wheel. The body is made as Client3D makes a person's: `Client3D._make_model` (now static; it
used nothing of the instance) on a puppet carrying a PersonLook from one of five builds (the
man, heavy, broad and lean, the woman: anim_rig_test's) and the look's words typed in; what each
hand holds by `Client3D._hold`, the loop that was inside `_sync_held` split out unchanged, and the
second grip by `_sync_reach`; an armour by `PersonLook.wear`. So what the lab shows is what the
game draws, and nothing in the game is copied into it. Any clip of the body's library loops on
the base layer (the gaits and idles listed first), any on the upper layer over it, at a speed;
Space pauses, "." steps a frame of 1/30 s, a bar scrubs (AnimRig.base_at). The treadmill runs
the floor's grid under the body at the clip's gait pace as Client3D plays a gait: HUMAN_GAITS'
(HUMAN_F_GAITS') pace times the look's stature and the speed, over feel.json's gait rate; a foot
that slides on it says the pace is wrong.

It is local only: it starts no World zone, opens no connection (Net and World load as autoloads
and do nothing more) and writes no file, in the project (art/, levels/) or in user://. It opens a
window, so it is under the windowed rule while Jeff is on the machine; lab_test runs it headless
(each build made, keyed and holding; held, worn and emptied; the clip list; pause, scrub, step
and resume; the treadmill's pace and floor).

Steps 2 and 3 follow, each its own landing. Step 2: a drop folder, C:/dev/review/character_lab/drop
(human_m.glb, human_f.glb, clips/*.glb), outside the repository and outside user://; a new or
changed export goes through Godot's own import as `heavy_job run <tree> godot_import` (never a bare
import, never from a script already holding a gate take) into the gitignored build/lab, and the
lab loads it from there, a status line saying what it is doing; a dropped clip named as a game
clip takes its place in the lab only. Step 3: two bodies side by side, the foot-slide readout,
and the gait paces into feel.json for the tuning panel. Nothing the lab shows reaches the game
but through pc-character's usual pipeline ("Copy to review" routed by the coordinator). Client
only, protocol unchanged, new class_name CharacterLab.

## 674 step 2: the Character Lab's drop folder

Jeff's Blender exports go into the running lab (the coordinator approved the design; release: under
674). client3d/lab_drop.gd (no class_name; CharacterLab preloads it as LabDrop) watches
C:/dev/review/character_lab/drop once a second: human_m.glb and human_f.glb are bodies, clips/*.glb
are clips (any name, one or more actions, "_Loop" looping as the game's import does). A .gltf, .fbx,
.blend or .obj there is named in the status line ("export as .glb") and left alone. A file is taken
once its size and time have held still 2 s, and R takes the folder again. It is copied into the
checkout's build/lab (gitignored: no export is ever committed) with a .glb.import written from
tools/lab/glb.import.template (human_m.glb.import's settings: the UAL bone map onto
SkeletonProfileHumanoid; animations on for clips), and the checkout's import runs as a process of
its own through the resource gate: `python -B tools/heavy_job.py run <checkout folder> godot_import
--expect 10 -- <godot> --headless --path <checkout> --import`, its output in build/lab/import.log.
It is never a bare import and never nested (the lab holds no take), and the gate's own limit stops
it. The lab polls it and never blocks. A gate stop is said ("the machine is busy") and tried once
more.

Each file is then loaded fresh (CACHE_MODE_IGNORE_DEEP) and checked: an armature with the humanoid
bones after the retarget (else "bones ... not found: keep the UAL bone names and the armature named
Armature"); for a body, a mesh named Body, 1.3 to 2.2 m tall (else "apply the scale"); for clips,
an animation with tracks on the skeleton. Only a good one is kept in the cache (CACHE_MODE_REPLACE,
so a second export at the same path is the new one): a bad one keeps the last good, says why in red,
and its copy is removed. A good body becomes the lab's for its sex (the model's "scene"), and good
clips are laid over the game's library in build/lab/lab_clips.res (the model's "clips"), shown in
the pickers marked "(yours)". A clip named as a game clip takes its place in the lab only. Nothing
is written to art/, levels/, user:// or the drop folder. lab_test `_test_drop` drives it with a
stand-in import and load in a scratch drop folder and build/lab_test: the 2 s settle, the copy with
its import settings, a body loaded and the lab's made again, unchanged not imported again, the four
bad cases (no Body, the wrong bones, the scale, not a glTF) each said with the last good kept and
the copy gone, an .fbx named, a gate stop tried again, a clip laid over the game's and marked in
the picker. Checked once by hand through the real gate (human_m.glb and a UAL clip export: imported
in about 10 s, the body and two clips loaded). Client and tool only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

## 674 step 3: the Character Lab compares, measures the feet, and the gait paces in feel.json

The coordinator approved the design (two guards: the paces' defaults exactly today's, a test that
an untouched feel.json gives them; "Use measured" live only). Three parts.

**Compare.** CharacterLab.compare puts a second body, B (puppet_b, rig_b, look_b; body_b, words_b,
own_b), SPACING (1.2 m) across the way from A, each made by `_made` as A was (Client3D._make_model,
_hold, wear); A is Jeff's export when the drop folder has one, B the game's or his ("B is"). The
clip, upper clip, speed, pause, scrub, step and held things are both's (`rigs()`), so both play
from the same moment; a Label3D over each head says "A: yours, man" or "B: game, woman". The floor
runs at A's pace.

**The feet, measured live.** client3d/lab_feet.gd (preloaded as CharacterLab.LabFeet, no
class_name) takes tools/gait_pace.gd's measure (decision 160) on the body as the lab plays it, so it
reads his exports too: each frame both toe bones' places; the lower toe within PLANTED_M (0.02 m)
of its lowest over the window planted; its ground speed backwards along the body's front (the toes
ahead of the feet at rest). Over the clip's last loop: the measured pace (the median planted ground
speed, the floor's speed that keeps the foot still) and the slide at the table's pace (|ground
speed - pace| over the planted samples: the median, its share of the pace, and the 90th, mostly a
plant or lift). Red over SLIDE_RED (5%) of the pace, or STILL_RED (0.05 m/s) for a clip that
stands. A mark (a flat yellow disc) at the planted toe every MARK_SECONDS (0.05), riding the
treadmill, gone after MARK_LIFE (1.5 s): a slide smears them, a good pace stacks them. On the man's
Jog_Short at speed 1 it reads 3.35 m/s against the table's 3.34 at his stature, slide 3%, so the
live measure agrees with gait_pace's tables.

**The gait paces in feel.json.** feel.json's "feel" gains client3d.gait.<clip> (the man's,
HUMAN_GAITS, which the barrow's skeletons and ghost share) and client3d.gait_f.<clip> (the
woman's, HUMAN_F_GAITS) for Walk, Jog_Short and Sprint_Short, each today's constant exactly, with
ArtKit.FEEL_RANGES rows (Animation, "now"). `Client3D.paced(gaits)` gives those two tables with
feel's paces (the constants' when feel lacks one), any other table as it is (the orc's, the
kobold's, the draugr's own), worked out again only when ArtKit.feel_serial (counting set_feel's
changes) moves; the gait choice and clip rate read through it, as does the lab's pace(). "Use
measured" sets the gait's key, for this run, to the table value that gives the measured pace at
this speed and stature (ArtKit.set_feel_value: Tuning.apply is a local host's, the lab is not
one); the lab writes no file, keeping a value is the panel's save or feel.json's edit.

lab_test `_test_compare` (B made, tagged, both playing and scrubbed together, gone with Compare
off) and `_test_feet` (the jog stepped by hand two loops: the measured pace within 5% of the
table's, the slide under the red line, the readout line, marks made, Use measured set and read by
the treadmill, put back, nothing for an idle, the marks aged out); tuning_test
`_test_gait_paces` (untouched, both tables exactly; a row each; his jog set, hers not; reset; the

## 397 amended (3): a zone asleep holds its herds as counts only

After v0.1.173, the box's daily herd lines (release's grep) showed hills and forest with bodies
out (21 and 20) and nobody online. Those bodies were real: the ones left standing when the last
player walked out. They were never retired, because Main._retire_and_recall only runs in an awake
zone (World.step steps a zone only while a player is in it), and nothing retired a zone's bodies
as it fell asleep. A group with bodies out spares nothing to economy's hunters and camps
(Herds.spare), so the hunting in an empty zone stayed shut by bodies nobody could see. The
coordinator approved retiring them when the zone falls asleep.

- **Main._retire_sleeping(zone)**, from World.zone_slept: every body in that zone that a keeper
  takes (the herds' animals of a group) goes back through keeper.retire and _despawn_kept, the
  same path the far tier uses: out down by one, count up by one, not a death, its slot neither
  alive nor dead. Not one owned by a peer, kept by one, or in a raid (as _retirable). A level's
  own animal (no group) is no keeper's and stays. It prints `[herds] <zone> asleep: <n> bodies back
  into their counts`.
- **Wounded or fleeing**: an animal goes back as a whole count, its hurt forgotten (the
  coordinator: that is fine). Wolves too, their pack's count whole.
- **The next visit** makes bodies again near the player (recall_near), as from any counts.
- **Economy's side**: an empty zone's groups have out 0, so spare() gives them their surplus over
  the reserve again, and the day's budget (taken after the day's reconcile, before the bodies
  could come back) counts them.

monster_test _test_herd_sleeps calls Main's own _retire_sleeping on a bare Main: 4 bodies out, one
wounded; asleep, none left, out 0, kept 4; a level's own deer stays. Server only, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.

## 238 amended: a fleeing monster keeps the full rate

Jeff on v0.1.173, hunting: "for hunting stag, the stag started to run and phase glitch while at a
distance". It bends 193's tiers. World._tier kept a monster on NEAR (it thinks every tick) only
while it had a target or stood within NEAR_TILES (22, 238) of a player. Past that it went to MID,
thinking every MID_EVERY_TICKS (4). A fleeing animal has no target, and a step lands only on a
think, so on MID its pace p became ceil(p / 4) x 4 ticks a cell. The stag's run of about 4.4
became 8. The client tweens each cell at its replicated move_ticks, so it ran a cell, stood, and
ran again. There was also a stall of up to 15 ticks where the tier changed. The view reaches 24
to 28 cells since the camera changes, so the 22 to 30 band is seen. With the bow's 9 to 15 cell
shots (669), a stag sees the hunter at 9 and runs straight into that band.

- **The rule**: a monster whose alert is FLEEING is NEAR, as one with a target is, wherever it
  is. Its flee is short (flee_ticks, 60) and few flee at once, so it costs little.
- **Ruled out**: network interest (about 36 cells, net/interest.gd), the client's puppet freeze
  (Client3D._sync_puppets' reach, at least 30), herd retire and recall (FAR past 60, calm only),
  and doubling back (after its flee it walks home, toward the hunter, at its idle pace).
- **Next, after a bench**: a monster walking in the 22 to 30 band shows the same run and stop on
  MID (an idle walk of 4.2 ticks a cell becomes 8, a brute's 5.6 becomes 8, a grazing stag's 6.9
  becomes 8). Keeping walkers within VIEW_TILES on NEAR is built but waits for map_bench numbers
  against 238's budget.

monster_test _test_far_pace: a stag kept fleeing, its pace 4.4, steps every 4 or 5 ticks at 23 to
30 cells; main gave 8 every step. Steps after a flee runs out and it stands a moment are not
counted. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 677. The bow's lob: the right-button arced shot

Jeff: "for the right click ability of the bow, im thinking arced shot, where the bow is aimed up to
the sky and you see an brass color arc drawn from the end of the arrow to the landing circle. it
would be right click hold and release to fire. a hit would cause a knock down impact." Combat's
design, approved by the coordinator. The unbuilt "backstep to come" on the right button with a bow
is dropped.

- **Input** (Main): with a bow and arrows in hand, holding the right button sends "stance"
  {kind: "draw", lob: true}. The server raises "draw" with GridEntity.lobbing (replicated), and the
  body stands firm as with Shift (World.stand_firm). Letting go sends "lob" {at: the cursor cell}.
  One draw at a time: while lobbing, the left button and Shift do nothing, and a flat draw or
  try_loose is refused; while flat-drawn, the right button does nothing.
- **The draw** (World.draw_step): the same steps as the flat shot, its first lob_draw_min ticks in
  (5, the flat's 3), the steps after as the flat draw's. Reach comes from reach_at/range_of, so a
  later "bow from energy" step moves both shots together.
- **The circle** (World.lob_radius): lob_circle cells by step, 2.5 at the first step, 1.75, 1.0
  at full draw, then 0.5. World.lob_aim draws the cursor cell in along the line to the reach drawn
  so far. try_lob rolls the landing cell in the circle (seeded like the flat shot's scatter), and
  falls back to the aimed cell when the rolled one cannot take it.
- **Over cover**: only the landing cell counts. Walls, cover and bodies between are flown over.
  It comes down only on ground under open sky (World.lob_open: walkable and Fields.under_sky).
  Never onto a wall's cell or a roof's, and nowhere indoors. There the loose does nothing and the
  arrow is kept. The client draws the aim red over such a cell.
- **Cost and harm**: the loose takes lob_cost stamina (8), on top of the flat draw's drain while
  held. The damage is attack_damage x the bow's damage x lob_damage (1.2) at any reach, no bands.
  No guard meets it; armour's deflect_shot does. A hit knocks down lob_down ticks (15) through
  World.knock_down, so a draugr (never_lies) staggers. A friend is spared, as by a flat shot.
- **Flight** (World.lob_ticks): lob_flight + lob_per_cell x cells seconds (0.6 + 0.05; 1.0 s at 8
  cells, 1.35 s at 15). World._tend_lobs strikes whoever stands on the cell when it is due, in its
  own zone, so a target that steps out is missed and one that steps in is struck. lob_landed
  either way; nobody there, a thud.
- **The arc**: World.lob_point(from, to, t, apex), static: the line between, lifted on a parabola
  lob_apex (0.25) x the ground covered. Client3D flies the arrow on it (_on_lobbed, from
  GridEntity._net_lobbed {to, ticks}), nosed into the ground at the end. Client3D.lob_aim draws the
  brass arc (lob_arc_mesh, two crossed ribbons) from the nocked arrow to the cell and the ring of
  its circle there. Physics reads lob_point. The spent flat arrow's dip (583 amended (3)) stays
  its own client curve.
- **Tuning**: every lob_* is a ranged-verb default (Items.VERBS), so it shows on F7 under
  items.bow.
- **Wire**: PROTOCOL_REVISION 37: the stance's "lob", the "lob" command, GridEntity.lobbing in
  SUBCLASS_REPLICATED, and the _net_lobbed RPC. Needs the server deployed.
- **Not yet**: the puppet's bow is drawn as for a flat shot, not aimed at the sky. The pose is
  pc-character's to add (read raised "draw" and lobbing).

Tests: combat_test `_test_lob` (stance, steps, circle, aim drawn in, cost, the landing tick, the
knockdown, one stepped out missed, a draugr staggered, roof and indoors refused, lob_point);
controls_test (RMB held lobs, the left button and Shift leave it, RMB let go looses, the controls
