## 676. Items as mass, step 1: load_arms and load_body

Jeff, testing the bow in plate: "items shouldnt have direct impacts, they
should just form stats like weight/mass. and the impact falls out of the
physics"; then "armor should add a clank sound that scares prey and mass
that drains stamina from archery a little faster". The plan (physics'
C:/dev/review/physics/items_as_mass.md, the coordinator's approval) takes
the direct effects out step by step; this is the first: where the mass sits.

World.load_of(entity) is {arms, body} in kg, to 0.1: what the hands hold and
the armour's arm share on the arms, the rest of the armour and the pack on
the body. An armour row says where its mass sits, "on": {arms, body} (676,
items' side: leather 0.2/0.8, mail 0.25/0.75, plate 0.2/0.8, robes 0.1/0.9;
none given, all on the body). _weigh sets GridEntity.load_arms and load_body
as the slots change; a Player's and a Companion's replicate (revision 37),
so a client's walk and draw read what the server's do and no held weight
goes on the wire.

One rule reads them, load_scale(kg, capacity) = 1 + load_k x max(0, kg /
capacity - load_free), the capacity the body's own mass (load_capacity: its
base mass; a client's spawned mass, the same) and the arms' ARMS_SHARE 0.2 of
it (16 kg for an 80 kg body):
- the walk: step_ticks x load_scale(load_body, the body's);
- the draw: _draw_quick x load_scale(load_arms, the arms'), in place of the
  armour's "draw" (gone from the rows: leather no longer draws quicker);
- a held draw's drain (669): x 1 + load_k x (the arms' share past free +
  DRAIN_BODY_SHARE 0.25 x the body's), carried as whole units a tick;
- the breath: x 1 / load_scale(the whole load, the body's), in place of
  622's 1 - armour kg / 100.
The pack sheet's bands (ui's side) are the whole load's share: light under
load_free, burdened under load_heavy, heavy under load_overloaded,
overloaded past (World.load_band). load_k 0.5, load_free 0.15, load_heavy
0.3 and load_overloaded 0.5 are in levels/physics.json and on F7
(physics.load_*, group "Load"), so the slowdown and the bands move together.

Numbers (physics_test _test_load): an 80 kg player with a bow and arrows
(1.6 kg on the arms) walks 2.5 ticks a cell, draws to full in 10, drains 1 a
tick and breathes as before. In plate (4 kg on the arms, 16 on the body):
the walk 2.5625 (x 1.025), full draw 11 (x 1.1, today's plate draw kept),
160 ticks held at full draw 177 stamina, the breath 1 / 1.06. 622's breath
was harsher: mail's 10 kg is now under the free share (30 ticks from empty:
60, was 54) and plate 58 (was 48); combat_test follows, and load_k and
load_free are Jeff's to tune. Robes' "aura", which nothing read, is gone. A
monster's load slows it as anyone's (a draugr's 7 kg axe sits under his
arms' free share). Next, before the bow from energy: noise from a worn
material as it moves.

### 676, step 1b: the armour clank

Jeff: "armor should add a clank sound that scares prey ... creatures run
from noise." A worn piece's noise falls out of its material and its mass,
not a per-item number: World.armour_noise(worn_id, pace) is {radius, kind},
the material's cells a kg (clank_plate 0.25, clank_mail 0.2; leather and
robes none) times its kg times the pace (a player's walk, CLANK_WALK_TICKS
2.5 over the step's own ticks, 0 to 2), rounded, under CLANK_MAX 19 (below
a shout: a monster goes to look, it does not hunt); kind "plate", "mail" or
"none". try_move's step noise is unchanged, and a player's or a companion's
step adds its own &"clank" noise at that radius (none at 0), once a step:
plate 5 cells at a walk, mail 2. A stranger's &"step" only turns prey (a
hunter can creep up); any other noise in reach makes them bolt (enemy-ai's
side, its own commit), so plate scares game from 5 cells where leather
reaches nobody. Weather and walls shorten it as every noise. clank_plate and
clank_mail are in levels/physics.json and on F7 (group "Load"). Noises stay
on the server: protocol unchanged. Sound's side plays it later from the same
function on the client (Player.worn, the pace), so what the player hears
grows as what the game hears. physics_test _test_clank: plate 5, mail 2,
leather 0; twice the pace 10, half 3; a dummy 4 cells off hears plate's
"step 4" and "clank 5", leather's nothing.

## 676, ui's side: the pack sheet's load line

Physics' items-as-mass step 1 (C:/dev/review/physics/items_as_mass.md,
part 4): the pack sheet shows what the load is and what it does, from

- **The line:** "carrying 21.6 of 80 kg: burdened": the whole load against

## 679. A step into your own companion swaps places

Ui's trace (net_smooth, a held walk beside her): 7 of 8 held-key corrections
a minute were "no confirmation", a step the server took late because a step
into or through the player's own companion waited on her moving (the bump's
step_aside, a click's make_way) on the server's tick, where the client had
shown it at once. The coordinator's ruling: a sim rule. World.try_move, for
a player, tries _swap_with_own before _shift: a step into their own
companion's cell (Companion.keeper the player) swaps them on that tick
through swap_places, which now takes the walk's start (a step's clock kept
within a tick, as a plain step's), so the step lands when the prediction
showed it and she takes his old cell, his heel (companions: her follow does
not fight it). Not for another's companion, nor one downed, lying, stunned,
leaping clear of a telegraph (Intent.DODGE) or fighting (Intent.ATTACK: a
swap would pull her off her foe; companions' thought); he bumps then as
before. Never across a wall, a closed door or a cut corner (swap_places'
own checks). MovePrediction._blocked treats her cell as open to her own
player (keeper_peer replicates; not downed or lying); her dodge and fight
are the server's alone, a swap it refuses corrected as any refused step.
The bump and step_aside stay for the refused cases and the click's make_way.

prediction_test _test_through_her: a held walk of 6 steps east through her,
the real try_move the server: he at (16, 24), she at (11, 24), none
corrected, refused or late (before: the walk stopped at her); another's, one
downed, one fighting and one round the wall's corner not swapped.
companion_test: walking into her swaps them on the tick, no mind asked; the
dead end's swap no longer goes through YIELD. Wire: no new field; an old
client predicts her cell blocked and is corrected, so it rides revision 37
(676's, unshipped) with a line there.


### 676, step 1b, sound's side: worn armour heard

The clank the game hears is heard too: each step of a player or a companion
in plate or mail plays its slot beside the footstep, never in its place.
Client3D._step_sound calls World.armour_noise(worn, pace) on the client, the
function the server's &"clank" noise comes from, so the two grow together
and follow physics' F7 knobs: worn is the replicated Player.worn or
Companion.worn, and pace is SoundKit.step_pace of the seconds since that
body's last step as the client saw it (CLANK_WALK_TICKS over the step's
ticks, 0 to 2; a first step, or one a second or more after the last, a
walk). No new wire. (Once a cell, as first landed; now on the body's
footfalls, the footstep with it: 676 step 1b, sound's side, amended, below.)

- **The slots**: SoundKit.armour_slot(kind), sfx.armour_plate (a clank,
  -14 dB) and sfx.armour_mail (a jingle, -16 dB); "none" (leather, robes,
  nothing worn) plays nothing. Both are movement one-shots on the sfx bus,
  positional, heard as far as the noise's radius carries (their "range", 5
  and 2, is the walk's).
- **Loudness by reach**: SoundKit.armour_db(kind, radius) is 0 dB at the
  kind's walk radius with physics' first knobs (ARMOUR_WALK_RADIUS: plate 5,
  mail 2) and 6 dB a doubling, within -12 to +6. So a run is 6 dB louder and
  carries twice as far, and a knob turned up is heard louder; a knob at 0
  silences it, as it silences the noise. Plate at a walk sits a little under
  the footstep, mail lighter.
- **The takes**: Freesound, each one's licence in takes.json and
  THIRD_PARTY.md. Plate: sgossner's plate armour rustles 209400, 209404 and
  209405 (CC BY 4.0) and one clank of Vrymaa's knight footsteps 770065 (CC0).
  Mail: sgossner's chain rustle 192612 and BeezleFM's chainmail rustle 512134
  (CC BY 4.0) and Ali_6868's chainmail footstep 384898 (CC0). The two
  footstep recordings were high-passed (770065 at 400 Hz, 384898 at 1 kHz,
  two passes each), so the boot is gone and only the metal is left; OGsoundFX's
  chainmail walk loop (423147) was left out, half its energy the footfall.
  Listening mixes for Jeff in C:/dev/review/sound/armour.

sound_kit_test: the slots by kind, armour_db at a walk and by doubling and
its range, step_pace, physics' radii giving plate 0 dB at a walk and louder
at a run. view_test _test_sounds_follow_events: a player's step in plate clanks, in mail
jingles, in leather nothing more. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

## 678. Straight lines over the tiles

Jeff: "with the original tile system, walking still wants to be on a
diagonal and it doesn't fit with the new camera"; the coordinator's option
1, approved as ui designed it: the server stays on cells, but a walk goes
and looks straight. Folded in, Jeff's "movement with the mouse and left
click seems slightly jumpy ... it highlights a tile which is unneeded" and
his repro ("placing the cursor to move on a diagonal 1 square in front of
me and if i keep that there the run camera stutter is reproducible").

- **Held keys (client):** the keys' way is the exact camera-relative angle
  (Main.wasd_vector), not rounded to the eight. Each step is one of the two
  of the eight either side of it, the one that leaves the body nearer the
  line through where the walk was anchored (Main.line_steps, a DDA), so over
  a few steps the walk goes where it is pushed. A walled pick takes the
  other; the line is anchored again where the walk is when the way changes
  (a key, the yaw) or the body is off it by LINE_OFF (a push, a walled pick
  taken round). The steps are plain order_steps: nothing new on the wire or
  in the server's prediction. The 655 hint is the line's next pick.
- **Clicked routes (sim, players' own):** World.walk_path is find_path with
  the string pulled: each run of the way that a straight line (line_cells,
  the nearest cell to the true line at each of max(|dx|, |dy|) steps) can
  take is replaced by it, a run growing while every step of its line is one
  the way could take (_line_clear: no wall or corner refusal, nobody but the
  walker or the goal's holder, no fire). Never longer: the same steps and
  diagonals, so the same time. The prediction's plan and its shorter-way
  check, Player's re-path and its via check use it; monsters and companions
  keep find_path. A server change (the host's and a walk past the via
  tiles), no wire change.
- **The glide (client, own body):** the prediction draws the body on its
  walk's line (MovePrediction._glide): the held line (hint_line, fresh), or
  the run of the planned route round the step that keeps to two
  neighbouring ways, both taken. The 655-bent point is pulled onto the line,
  GLIDE_MAX half a cell at most; a change of line (a new way, the route's
  next run, none) is eased out at GLIDE_EASE rather than jumped. A step
  drawn from where the body was (a correction, a walk from rest, a settle)
  is not pulled. The facing is the line's way. Others are drawn as 655 has
  them; the cell stays the server's for everything.
- **The held button near the body steers:** with the cursor within
  STEER_CELLS of the body, the held left button walks the cursor's way on
  the same line as a held key, one steady run, never a cell reached and
  set off from again. Held farther, a new walk only when the cell changes
  and a straight step's time apart at most, with no ripple.
- **The jitter's cause:** every new cell under a held button was a new
  order, and MovePrediction.order dropped the planned step after the one
  under way; in its second half 655 had already bent the body toward that
  step, so the body ended half a step on toward a cell no longer planned and
  the new route set off from the centre: a jump at every re-order in a
  step's tail. Now an order keeps the step the one under way bends into
  (_cancel_unbent) and plans on from it; the server walks it as a via tile.
  Jeff's repro was the worst case: the cell under a still cursor moving
  with the camera, one step away, re-ordered every step.
- **The hover square** shows only while building (Main._building) and where
  a cell is the answer (the drawn bow's landing cell); in play the cursor is
  enough. The lob's ring is its own.
- **Tests:** mirror_test (where the prediction is driven by hand):
  _test_a_route_is_drawn_straight (a 12 x 4 route, each cell within half a
  cell of the line, drawn within 0.1), _test_a_held_line_is_drawn_straight
  (a 20 degree line, ten steps, drawn within 0.1). controls_test
  _test_straight_lines: W at a 20 degree yaw within half a cell of its line
  over ten steps; the button held a diagonal cell ahead sends a step that
  way, no walk to a cell; held far, one walk a step's time apart.
- **Not here:** the companion stutter (net_smooth, clean, 60 s: a WASD
  walker's corrections 8/min with companions, 0 without, 7 of them "no
  confirmation", the server taking the step late beside her; every body
  near drawn going back 82 and 157 frames/min against 18 and 31, not split
  by body, so not yet hers): a step swapping with your own companion at
  once to physics; which bodies go back, measured per body, next.

No wire change, protocol unchanged; walk_path needs the server deployed.
No new class_name.
### 676 step 1b, sound's side, amended: the clank on the footfall

Jeff on the first mixes: "the running ones go a little too fast, the walking
ones are approximately running speed". The game had it too: the clank and
the footstep came once a cell, and a person covers 4 cells a second at a
walk, quicker than its feet fall. Now both fall on the drawn body's own
footfalls, together (the coordinator: "so step and clank land together").

- **Footfalls from the clips**: GAIT_FOOTFALLS, each gait clip's footfalls
  as a share of the clip, measured by tools/gait_pace.gd (which now prints
  them: each moment a toe comes down to within PLANTED_M of its low): Walk
  0.081 and 0.581, Jog_Short 0.027 and 0.532, Sprint_Short 0.044 and 0.587,
  the two human bodies alike within 0.005. Played at HUMAN_GAITS' paces as
  _animate plays the clip.

  clip's place (AnimRig.base_position, the base layer's under a strike)

## 680. A late start is drawn from now: the mirror re-anchors (bending 350)

The coordinator's ask, after perf's trace on v0.1.177: a companion (Hollis)
standing since the join set off a cell a tick just after the client's worst
hitches (515, 144 and 180 ms), and was drawn in six leaps of 0.47 tiles.
Her first slides were due ticks before the display clock reached them, and
350's _catch_up drew them at CATCH_UP_SPEED (twice the pace), on a display
clock that was itself catching up after the hitch.

- **Re-anchored, not hurried:** when the slide the mirror takes up is late
  (its tick before the display clock's now) and the body stood since the
  last slide ended (not a present push, nor a slide with its own
  from_pos), the slide starts at now and every slide queued behind it moves
  as much later. _catch_up then finds nothing late, so a start from
  standing is drawn at the body's own pace. A body already walking still
  catches up as 350 has it: there the lag is the display's, and the queue
  has to stay near the server.
- **The cost:** a body that set off during a hitch is drawn up to the
  hitch's length further behind the server until it next stands. This is
  the same delay a present push takes back (its "back to the display
  clock" re-anchor, which this mirrors).
- **The coordinator's other option,** capping the catch-up at 1.3x, was
  not taken: it would slow every catch-up, including a walking body's.
- mirror_test _test_a_standing_body_starts_without_leaps: a body standing
  10 ticks, then a 3-tick hitch with a step a tick arriving and no frame
  drawn, then 14 ticks at 60 frames a second. No drawn frame goes over a
  quarter tile, and it arrives. Without this change the worst frame is
  0.333.
- With it, the smooth meter's per-body labels (net/smooth_meter.gd,
  bodies_report; net_smooth.sh's third argument turns the server's
  companions off): which body went back, whether its tile did (A, B, A: the
  server's own), and how many went back just after a swap (679). These
  feed the trace of the remaining held-key corrections beside a companion.

Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 678 again, amended: a held walk turns at once and faces the way it goes

Jeff on v0.1.177: "movement got worse, its too delayed, i can move cursor
behind me and character keeps going, now I run in a diagnonal line the body
doesn't face the direction of travel." 678 was taken out of v0.1.178
("678 reverted" above); this puts all of it back, with the fixes below,
for v0.1.179. A
headless probe (--test-hold-near, given an angle, a cursor distance and a
swing behind: `--test-hold-near=6,angle=20,far=6,flip=3`) measured it on
the wilds, a server and a click client: steering near the body was right
(the step under way finished, 0.67 cells on, back in 0.33 s; facing 0.3
degrees off the way travelled), but held farther, the routes went 1.4 to
1.6 cells on after the swing, back only after 0.4 to 0.6 s, and the body
faced 8 to 9 degrees off the way it went on average, 24 at worst.

- **A turn goes at once:** held far, a new cell more than TURN_KEEP (45
  degrees) off the way to the last one, seen from the body
  (Main.held_turns), is sent at once, not a step's time later. And
  MovePrediction.order keeps the step the one under way bends into (the
  jitter's fix) only when the new target lies within TURN_KEEP of that
  step's way; otherwise it drops that step too and bends the one under way
  again toward the new plan. Whatever a new order changes on screen is
  carried in the glide's carry and eased out, never jumped. A swing behind
  in a step's tail now goes on 0.01 cells; no frame moves more than a
  step's pace.
- **Held far steers on the line where it can:** with the straight way to
  the cursor's cell open (World._line_clear from the walk's end), the held
  button steers along the line as it does near the body (STEER_CELLS), so
  an open-ground run is one line, at the cursor's angle. Routes only where
  that way is shut (walls, others, fire), walking round.
- **A route held far is planned again less often:** each plan is a
  straight line from where it starts; planned again every step, only each
  line's first step was ever taken, the straight one, so the walk went
  straighter than the cursor and the drawn body weaved between the plans'
  lines. Now a new plan only when the cursor's way drifts HELD_DRIFT (12
  degrees) off the last one's or fewer than HELD_PLAN_LEFT (3) of its
  steps are left (Main.held_replans), a step's time apart at most, and at
  once on a turn.
- **A small change of the held way keeps the line's place:** the line was
  anchored again on the walk's end cell at any change of way, and from a
  cell the line's first pick is the straight step: a way shifting a degree
  a frame (a hand on the mouse, the camera following) walked straight.
  Under LINE_TURN (20 degrees) the line now goes on from the walk's point
  on the old one (Main.line_anchor); a bigger turn, or the walk LINE_OFF
  off the line, anchors a new one on the cell as before.
- **The facing:** a step drawn from where the body was (each new order, a
  key's turn) faced its own way of the eight, and the run of a route's line
  was taken back through earlier plans' cells. Such a step now faces along
  the line it is on too (MovePrediction._line_of, loose), and a route's line
  is its own plan's (Step.plan), not one through cells the walk has left.
- Tests: mirror_test _test_a_far_held_walk_faces_its_line (routes, 20
  degrees, planned again as Main does: 4.4 degrees off the way travelled on
  average, 17.6 at worst where a plan hands over; it was 11.9 and 24.4),
  _test_a_held_line_keeps_its_slope_under_a_shaking_hand (the way shaking 4
  degrees: 18.4 degrees walked, facing 2.7 off at worst),
  _test_a_far_held_walk_turns_at_once (0.01 cells on, it was 0.95), and the
  held line's facing; controls_test: held_turns, held_replans, line_anchor.

Server and client: World.walk_path is back (the server's re-path and its
via check), so the server is redeployed with the cut. No wire change,
protocol unchanged. No new class_name.
## 675, npc's side: townsfolk hold their tongue near a fight

The coordinator, 2026-10-25, after 675: "Give residents the same rule: no
hails and no resident voice lines while a hostile is within a few cells of
them or of the listener, with a short calm tail after." The coordinator
approved the design as written; release named it a side, not an amendment.

- What counts as hostile: a spawned Monster (an Animal too) in the
  resident's zone whose threatens() (enemy-ai's 551) is true for the
  resident or for its listener. That covers a raider, a predator, a
  charging boar, and a draugr only while he would fight. The reach is
  Companion.COMBAT_RANGE (4 cells) from either. Main._fight_near.
- Main._resident_quiet(body, listener) marks the tick a fight is near, in
  _resident_fight_at by worker id. The resident is quiet for
  Companion.QUIET_AFTER (30 ticks, 3 s) after the last such tick. Off
  with Companion.hold_tongue, as 675's is.
- Quiet, nothing is said:
  - No hail (_hails_tick).
  - On a click there is no greeting word, no "Not now.", no rumour or
    shelter line, and they don't turn to face the player (_greeted).
  - The player's words ask no mind, so there is no ollama call
    (_ask_resident). What speaking does still happens: an errand done by
    speaking, a strayed one's escort, the sick walked to the healer.
  - A mind answer that comes back mid-fight is dropped
    (_resident_answered). A hail's marks go back as for an unsaid line, so
    it can be told later.
  - An offer's spoken words are dropped (_speak_offer), and so are
    _say_plain and _resident_says lines. The offer stands, the trade goes
    through, and the panel is still sent.
  - The bard's bubble is dropped. The inn's listeners still get the song.
- A fight begun lets the resident's waiting ask go. Nothing is queued for
  after.
- Each held line is counted in the mind log: kind "voice", mind
  "resident", trigger "greet", "heard", "voice", "say", "offer", "song" or
  "ask", outcome "held tongue". No words, no names.
- Hearing (claims asks) is unchanged. A body hiding from raiders was
  already silent.

resident_test _test_quiet_near_hostile covers: a monster that would fight
nobody leaves her talking; one that would fight the player lets her ask
go; the click, words, plain lines, hails and a late answer are all held;
one that would fight her, the player away, also quiets her; once it is
gone she stays quiet a breath, and after QUIET_AFTER her word comes on a
click. It runs late, since its steps move the hail tick's phase that the
voice sections count on. tests/foe_stub.gd is a Monster that would fight
only the ones it is given.

Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 682. The remedy heals over time: the "heal" buff

No item healed hp, so Pip had nothing to drink mid-fight (economy's ask). Under the rule
that items are physical, a herbal remedy healing over time is what the thing is, a body
state like the steadying draught (642), not a stat multiple. Physics' rules, the
coordinator's ruling.

- **The remedy's row** (levels/items.json): effects [{"kind": "heal", "amount": 1.0,
  "ticks": 200}], value 6 (was 4), the medicine man's shelf of 3 ("stock"); the recipe is
  unchanged (2 herbs, 600 steps). It is still the sickness cure given to a resident (501).
  The numbers are drafts.
- **A new buff kind, heal** (Items.BUFF_KINDS, "Healing"): its amount is hp a second.
  World._heal_tick, in the buff pass, gives it whole at TICK_RATE (_carried), so 1 a second
  is 20 hp over the 200 ticks. add_buff keeps a heal's start as a third element
  ([amount, end, start]), and it heals the ticks after its start through its end, so a
  drink heals exactly amount x ticks whether the command ran before the tick's buff pass or
  after (physics' review: counted from the start's own tick, a 201st tick gave 21). It never heals past max_hp, nor a downed body, and ends at
  death. A hit does not stop it, and a bleed or a burn runs beside it. A second one keeps
  add_buff's rule, the larger amount and the later end, so it refreshes the time and does
  not add up.
- **Not the bandage's mending.** That track (World._mending, the replicated mending) is
  broken by any hurt and means "bandaged": try_bandage refuses a patient already mending,
  and Pip's words read it. A remedy and a bandage run side by side, and the bandage stays
  the calm-only one.
- **F7 tunes it**: Items.effect_fields, effect_value and set_effect_value give
  effects.<id>.<kind>.amount and .ticks for each thing with effects, registered in Main
  beside the other sources.
- Pip gets no special path. Her player gives her remedies the normal way and she drinks her
  own (try_use); companions adds when she does (retreating under 0.35) after this lands.

Wire: PROTOCOL_REVISION 38 (37 had shipped in v0.1.177). Buffs may hold "heal", a new key
in a replicated value (release, after 642's precedent). items_test _test_remedy_heal (20

## 677, sound's side. The lob heard: up, coming down, and a heavier blow

The coordinator (2026-10-25, Jeff play-testing the bow most): a sound pass on
677's arced shot, filling the gaps from the existing stores at the footfalls'
loudness. Already there and kept: the draw's creak rising with the draw (475),
the twang on any loose (sfx.bow_loose), the arrow landing (sfx.arrow_land, or
sfx.arrow_water in water), the fly-by whistle past the listener and the body's
fall on a knockdown (sfx.knockdown).

- **Up**: sfx.arrow_lob_rise, a whoosh with the loose, at the bow
  (Client3D._on_lobbed). Three CC0 takes (freesound 427823, 384908, 384909),
  -14 dB, range 4.
- **Coming down**: sfx.arrow_lob_fall, a falling whistle from the cell it will
  land in, starting Client3D.LOB_WARN_SECONDS (0.5 s) before it lands, so a body
  there can hear it and step out (677's miss). A lob flies at least 0.65 s
  (lob_flight 0.6 plus 0.05 a cell), so the warning always fits. Three cuts of
  one CC0 whistle (freesound 268914), each 0.55 s, swelling 24 dB over 0.45 s,
  -18 dB, range 6: heard round where it lands, not across the field. Neither
  slot is a noise for monsters; the loose's bow noise stands.
- **A heavier blow**: a shot that knocks its body down plays sfx.hit_blunt_flesh
  once over the arrow's hit, when the hit (Client3D._on_struck, cause shot) and
  the body's fall (_sync_down) come within Client3D.KNOCKDOWN_BLOW_MS (500 ms)
  of each other while it lies, whichever news comes first. A shot that leaves it
  standing, or a fall with no shot near it, sounds as before.

Loudness: slot level plus take rms comes to about -30 dB for both, beside the
footsteps' -31. sound_kit_test (the slots placed, silent to monsters, three
takes each) and view_test (the lob's rise at the loose, its whistle once before
it lands, then its thud; the knockdown's one blow, none standing, none for a
late fall). Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.
## 498 amended (2): a hut works on its own account

The box's two healers' huts logged "waits for remedy: its maker can't pay for the materials" every production step, and they never made a remedy. Their medicine men bank the herbs they gather into the hut's own store as a plain deposit (main.gd _take_herbs, 502 amended), unpaid, since a hut has no treasury. To make a remedy, Production._start then had him buy those herbs back (Economy.buy_materials, 498) from a purse of 0, with a loan that would come from the hut store's gold, which is also 0. Neither 652 nor 649 caused it; it has stood since the huts got workshops (641).

The coordinator's approval: a workshop whose place is no town's store (holdings kind isn't Stockpile.KIND: a healer's hut, Main's place workshops) works on its own account, like a town's meals. It takes its materials from its own store without buying them. He gathered them, he uses them, and nobody is owed. A medicine man in a town's workshop still buys the town's herbs.

## 679 amended: the prediction knows when she won't swap

Jeff on v0.1.179: "sometimes she catches up into the same tile and bounces
off, causing visual effect that seems like the screen is jerking". Two
causes, read against swap_places and MovePrediction._swaps_with. The first,
her catch-up step taking the cell he is walking into on the tick of his
step (the swap then sends her straight back, the client drawing her into
his cell and out), is companions' to fix: her follow keeps clear of his
next cells. The second is this one: the server refused a swap the client
could not foresee, and his predicted body snapped back.

- **Stunned**: MovePrediction._swaps_with now reads her stun as the server
  does, through _reel_until (her _net_stunned sets it on a client, World's
  stun on the server). A stunned companion's cell is blocked on both sides.
- **Dodging or fighting** (the coordinator's ruling, companions'
  recommendation): no longer excluded. Her intent (Companion.current_intent)
  is the server's alone and does not replicate, and a refused step of his
  own body is worse than her being pulled a cell off her foe or out of her
  dodge. A wind-up she began is given up, as any wind-up whose winder is
  moved off its cell (_tend_wind_ups); a blow she queued lands from where
  she now stands or misses. Her blows only ever aim at her foe, so none
  falls on him.

The rest of 679 stands: not another's companion, nor one downed or lying;
never across a wall, a closed door or a cut corner.

prediction_test _test_through_her: she reels from a stun: no swap, and the
prediction shows him stopped; the stun over, her cell open again; she fights
(ATTACK), she dodges (DODGE): swapped all the same. Wire: no new field
(holds_ground not needed), protocol unchanged; no new class_name.


## 678, companions' side: she follows on the pulled line

Jeff on v0.1.179: "Pip now does zig zag run behind me in the wilds", and
"sometimes she catches up into the same tile and bounces off, causing visual
effect that seems like the screen is jerking" (the coordinator's ruling: her
moves never take her player's cell or the one he steps into, her goal is
kept rather than picked again each tick, and she runs the line he walks).
678 string-pulled the player's own route; her follow (Heel, decision 485)
still stepped find_path's eight-way first cell toward a heel cell picked
afresh each tick behind his facing, so on a slant she stair-stepped a cell
off his line, the heel flipped sides when he turned, and her catch-up could
take the cell he was walking into on the tick of his step, which the swap
(679) then sent straight back.

- **His way kept clear** (Heel.keep_clear): his cell, the next two of his
  way (WASD steps queued, the via cells, else the line to his move order;
  Heel.next_cells) and, while he walks on (WALK_ON_TICKS 3 after a step's
  end), two cells along his last step. No heel goal is one of them, and a
  step into one waits: she stops short rather than bump. Heel.step takes
  the leader; Companion._step_toward passes her player for every move but a
  dodge (663), so errands keep clear too.
- **His footsteps** (_footstep): walking on, she makes for the cells he
  left (the trail, TRAIL_KEPT 4), a cell back from him (so a turn straight
  back does not walk into her), only one nearer him than she is. His step
  due this tick and not yet taken counts as taken, so she sets off with it.
- **Beside him and out of his way she stays put** while he walks by (a turn
  back toward her), and standing in his way she steps aside to the nearest
  clear cell (_aside), not round to his new back.
- **The goal kept** (_serves): a heel cell is picked again only when it
  stops serving (more than STOP from him, taken, in his way, or ahead of
  where he goes: Heel.travel, his last step's way while walking on, else
  his facing). Stopped, she waits on his footstep SETTLE_TICKS 6, then closes
  to his heel as before.
- **The pulled line** (Heel.step): a way of 3 cells or more, its goal one
  she may stand on, is World.walk_path's, so off his footsteps she goes
  straight too.

companion_test _test_heel_keeps_clear: twenty runs east, a stop of 0 to 4
ticks, then back west, north-west, south-west, north, or a turn and on
again, his steps queued ahead as a client sends them. Before, after: swaps
4, 0; swaps into a cell she had just taken (the bounce) 1, 0; steps straight
back within 6 ticks 24, 0; refusals of his steps 0, 0. Her step gaps follow
his pace (his 2.5 ticks a step on that ground: 2, 3, 3), no stop-go.
_test_heel_on_the_line: a slant at 20 degrees and back; her widest drift off
his line 1.40 cells before, 0.59 after (a 20 degree line still alternates
straight and diagonal steps; the mirror draws them as softly bent slides,
and a line glide for mirrors is ui's if that still shows). Two older
sections moved with her: the attack's imp spawns on the nearest free cell,
and the retreat waits 16 ticks, not 8, for her to close in.

Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.


## 681: She tends wounds unasked

Jeff's direction (companions are the centerpiece; the core verbs plain and
reliable), from the box: after fights her player went on hurt while she
carried a bandaging kit, since only her voice ever chose the bandage errand
(and 675 now keeps it quiet through a fight's tail), and once her kit went
to her player through a slot move she offered nothing against. The
coordinator approved (a), (c), (d) and (e) of the design, and (b), the
remedy, once items' 682 gave remedies a "heal" buff.

- **Her hands tend unasked** (Companion._tend_unasked, every TEND_EVERY 10
  ticks): calm (World.calm, nothing within COMBAT_RANGE), her kit to hand,
  no errand, order or hesitation running, her player not downed. Her
  player first, then herself: one wants it when hurt and not mending, and
  under TEND_BELOW 0.75 of their hp or bleeding (_wants_tending); her player
  only in her zone, within PERCEPTION_RANGE and seen. The bandage errand
  does it (walk there, World.try_bandage, wait it out), marked unasked: a
  refusal she can wait out (hurt just now, not safe, busy) waits, a patient
  not to be bandaged is passed over.
- **Narrated, not said**: nobody asked, so nothing is answered. _say_bandage
  says no refusal or break-off line for an unasked errand, _report_errand
  asks no voice, and the mind log's errand note is left empty. An unasked
  errand that comes to nothing is not tried again for TEND_BACKOFF 100
  ticks. The words logged name no player ("tend your player's wounds").
- **Her kit and her remedies stay off her give offers** (can_do): handed
  over, she could tend no one. An order ("give me your bandages") still
  works.
- **The remedy** (_drink_if_low, the coordinator's ruling): under
  REMEDY_BELOW 0.35 of her hp she drinks one she carries (World.try_use on
  its slot; Companion.is_remedy: an item with a "heal" effect), not while
  one heals her (World.buff "heal"), not with a blow wound up, not downed,
  and bleeding with a bandage she could begin now, the bandage first.
  Narrated only: it is mostly in a fight (675). Her player gives her
  remedies with the ordinary give.
- **Companion.tends_unasked** (static, on): companion_test's older sections
  hurt bodies she would tend, so they run with it off, as hold_tongue (675).

companion_test _test_tends_unasked (both hurt, no kit: nothing; the kit not
among her give offers; a monster near: nothing; calm: her player bandaged
first, then herself; nothing said) and _test_drinks_a_remedy (remedies off
the give offers; at half her hp she keeps them; under 0.35 she drinks one;

## 683: Stops, turns and let-go land on the step under way

The coordinator, on Jeff's "movement isn't right yet" after v0.1.179: stop
guessing and measure the lag, from input to what is on screen. A headless
client (--test-latency=N[,hold], Main._run_test_latency) times each input
to the first frame that shows it and to the response done: full pace for
a start, settled on the new way for a turn, standing for a stop. It covers
a held button, a click and the keys, against v0.1.176 too. The box's
round trip is 0 to 5 ms (Tailscale); a proxy at 1±1 ms each way matched
direct to the frame, and every own-body response is predicted from the
input's frame, so the 10 Hz tick wait never shows on the own body.

On v0.1.180 (medians): a start 17 ms to the first frame, ~85 ms to full
pace; a click's turn ~120 to 150 ms; a key's turn 283 ms, waiting for the
step under way. A stop was the step's rest plus about 150 ms of creep:
held 250, keys 283. The step's tail had bent toward a step that was never
sent, then slid back over SETTLE_TICKS (1.5 ticks), and the walk's line
offset (678's glide carry) eased out at 12/s after it. Held with Pip in the
straight line, the steer fell to a route and letting go did not stop it:
it went on 5.7 cells, standing after 1550 ms.

- **A bend let go** (MovePrediction._let_go_bend): the hint dropping to
  none while the step under way bends toward the step it hinted at blends
  that bend back onto the straight line over the step's rest (Step.unbend_at,
  _bent), so the body stands on the centre as the step ends, no settle after.
- **The settle at the walking pace**: a settle that still happens (let go
  after the step ended, coasting on the bend) takes its distance at the
  pace (SETTLE_MIN_TICKS 0.3 at least, SETTLE_TICKS at most), not 1.5 ticks.
- **The carry at the pace as the walk ends** (_ending: no fresh hint and
  no step planned past the one under way): the glide carry eases at 12/s or
  at the walking pace, whichever is quicker.
- **A held walk let go ends at the step under way** (Main._let_go_held): if
  the hold steered since its click (Main._held_steered: a step or a new cell
  sent), button up clears the hint and the line and, when the walk shown
  goes on past the step under way (GridEntity.shown_step_tile) or the
  authority holds a move order, sends a move to that step's tile (an
  existing order; no protocol change). A click let go without steering
  walks on to its cell.

A key's turn was not made quicker. Sending it mid-step and drawing it
round the committed cell reached the new way only ~30 ms sooner: a body
moving along the old way can curve off it only as fast as a bend's corner
cut allows (655: a quarter cell), and the tail bend already starts as
early as that rule lets it. The facing already turns at once. Quicker
needs a deeper corner cut or the server letting a committed step go; the
coordinator keeps the second off the table for now.

Measured after (6 rounds a case, with companions): held stop 250 -> 67 ms
(worst 1550 -> 167), keys stop 283 -> 167; 0 corrections, 0 swaps.
prediction_test _test_let_go: let go at 80% of the last step, no settle,
standing as the step ends; let go after it, standing 0.33 ticks after (the
settle alone was 1.5). controls_test: let go after steering ends the walk
at the step under way; a click let go walks on. The harness stays as a test
option (Net.test_latency; Main._lat_*).

Client only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 684. Regeneration made off the main thread

The coordinator asked perf for the server's ~290 ms join stall. That
turned out to be local: a windowed client starting on the same machine
starved the server for a frame. With a headless client the whole join took
8 ms, and on the box the minute after a real join peaks at about 110 ms
once. The box's real freezes, from its journal (timings and level names
only), were all zone regenerations. Every 3 game days (4.5 h) barrow,
barrow_deep and castle_halls (barrow_lair until its retirement in 666) were
re-laid in one tick: 0.4 to 1.35 s, and 1.2 to 2.2 s at boot. It held
every player in the world.

Measured on the wilds' world with a private overlay, the zones open and
asleep as on the box: Regen.generate is 85 to 95% of it (barrow 132 to
168 ms, barrow_deep 360 to 1091 ms from one try, castle_halls 131 to
139 ms). Rebuilding the zone takes 19 to 36 ms, WorldMap.build 26 to 33,
the write 3 to 7, holdings and richness about 1. Spreading the levels over
ticks alone would still leave barrow_deep's tick at up to 1.1 s.
- Regen.generate is split: Regen.prepare (the main thread's part: the
  template from Level's caches, its "regenerate" block, the generator
  script loaded, the dictionaries copied for the worker) and
  Regen.generate_prepared (the tries). The generators touch no node,
  autoload or cache, only the template, LevelMap and Images.
- Main._regenerate_due, on the slow world tick (every 30 s): a level due,
  its zone not awake, is started on Main._maker (_start_making_if_due),
  one at a time. The slow tick after it finishes applies it on the main
  thread (_apply_made, then _apply_generation: the write, the open zone
  rebuilt, WorldMap, holdings, raids, trade and richness, as before) and
  starts the next. A result whose zone has woken meanwhile waits for it to
  sleep. One that is no longer the next generation is dropped, because the
  console's "regenerate now" laid one meanwhile.
- _regenerate_if_due (travel, joining or opening a due level): a level
  being made is waited for and laid then, made once. Any other due level is
  made on the spot, as before; the travel card covers it.
- Boot opens the saved zones as they were (_open_zone's regenerate false).
  The levels that came due while the server was down are laid on the slow
  ticks after, the same way.
- A quit joins the worker and drops its result (_drop_making in
  _exit_tree). Nothing is written to the overlay until the main thread
  applies it, and a save meanwhile keeps the old generation, so the level
  is laid again when next due.
- Dungeon confirmed that the levels may be laid in any order and at any
  spacing. Every cross-layer link (stairs, the sealed shortcut) sits in an
  anchor that generations never move, the niche door is within the barrow
  alone, and each level is seeded on its own.

Locally (wilds, the three levels open and asleep): all three in one tick
1166 to 1449 ms before. After, they are laid over 4 slow ticks, the worst
tick 65 to 69 ms, and no frame over 20 ms while a worker runs.
regen_test covers the rest:
- the same seed gives byte-identical generations on a worker and on the
  main thread (the test's halls, barrow, barrow_deep and castle_halls);
- nothing is written while a generation is made, and a save meanwhile says
  the old generation;
- a result made while Bo comes back waits until the halls sleep, then is
  laid;
- a quit mid-generation writes nothing;
- a travel in mid-generation waits for the worker and stands in the new
  generation, made once.
Godot's thread guards are on in this debug build (a probe touching a node
from a worker printed their errors, which fail the suite), and regen_test
runs clean under them.

Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 685. Companions' short searches bounded

A companion asked for short answers through World.find_path with no
max_tiles. A search like that is unbounded A*, and a cell behind a wall or
with no way to it walked the search round the whole zone. Over 400 yields
from cells beside walls in the wilds, one yield's searches took 2.7 ms on
average and 332 ms at worst. Bounded at 81 cells they take 0.28 ms on
average and 1.9 ms at worst, and none of 6,852 short ways differ.

- Her yield (_find_yield_tile: every cell within YIELD_REACH, kept only
  for a way of YIELD_REACH steps or fewer) closes at most
  YIELD_SEARCH_TILES, (2·(YIELD_REACH+2)+1)² = 81.
- Her step aside out of her player's way (Heel._aside, wanting a one-step
  way) closes at most ASIDE_SEARCH_TILES, 49.
- Her dodge (_read_telegraphs, including the bow cone of 663 amended)
  chose its cell by distance alone and then walked there by Heel.step's
  unbounded search every tick. A cell behind a wall had her search round
  the walls, and an unreachable one flooded the zone. The candidates are
  now scored as before and taken best first, the first she has a way to
  within DODGE_SEARCH_TILES, (2·(DODGE_REACH+2)+1)² = 121. A cell with no
  short way is no dodge, since DODGE_LOOK's 12 ticks can't cover a detour,
  so she takes the next-best one (the coordinator's (b)). Where today's
  cell has a way of up to 6 steps the choice is the same.
- Her door errand looked for a way to each of the door's sides every step,
  near side first. A side with no way flooded the zone each step while she
  walked to the far one. A side found with no way is skipped for
  ERRAND_RETRY_TICKS (20) and asked again only when no other side has a
  way, so the errand still ends "no way there" exactly when today's does.
  The one change: she keeps to the far side for up to 2 s after the near
  one opens up.

The other per-tick callers were audited and left alone:
- monsters' flee (bounded by IDLE_SEARCH_TILES);
- leash and the swap (no search);
- herd grazing and regrouping (Monster's idle, _about_search);
- the heel and catch-up walks, players' and residents' routes, the guide's
  leg fallback and main's shop and store checks (long answers, not short
  ones).
The step memo stays as it is: a cold memo makes the farthest walk 85 ms
against 11 ms warm.

path_bound_test checks every short way, bounded against unbounded, on the
wilds and the castle from about 250 to 400 cells beside walls and doors:
- yields: 0 of 12,374 ways of up to 2 steps differ;
- steps aside: 0 of 4,295 one-step ways differ;
- dodges: 0 of 24,349 ways of up to 6 steps differ;
- nothing the bounded search finds differs from the unbounded way.
With a yield bound of 6 it fails, so it catches a bound that is too small.

Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 581 amended, npc's side: what she left over, and the town's word

Companions' 581 step 2 (winning back a companion who left; the coordinator
approved it once the keys were agreed between the two trees) needs three
things from npc's side. Two are built here; the third is companions' alone.

- **Production.set_left(worker_id, why, back):** stores "left_why" and
  "left_back" on her worker ("" clears; nothing for an unknown id).
  Companions' side writes both when she leaves and each day she is away,
  on the worker its set_mood uses: "companion:<her name>", whose origin is
  "companion:<her player's id>" (Towns.note_companion_in).
- **Her resident prompt (Resident.facts_now):** appends both sentences,
  exactly as written, only when the one speaking to her body is her own
  player (the body's player_id, the asked_by). It finds her worker by
  origin == "companion:" + that id, since her body is keyed
  "companion:<player id>" and her worker by name. They are facts, never
  lines.
- **Townsfolk.reputation(production, town, player_id) -> float:** the
  mean Standing.score toward the player over the town's workers. It skips
  "companion:" workers and anyone whose stored card has no entry for them
  (never met). It reads stored cards only, rolling none, and returns 0.0
  when nobody counts. Companions compares it daily with "fond".
- **Her bond while away:** stays in record.companion["standing"].
  Companions decays it; npc's daily decay of worker cards is untouched,
  and companions doesn't read it for her bond.

resident_test checks: her two sentences reach the prompt for her own
player only, and are gone once cleared or when another player asks;
set_left on an unknown id does nothing; reputation is 0.0 with nobody met,
3.5 for scores 2 and 5 with the rest not counted, and 0.0 for another town
or no player.

## 686, economy's side: who a town can spare, and one away pays nothing

Companions' 686 (the coordinator's approval) lets a player recruit a town resident as a companion. Economy gives it two parts.

- Towns.sole_needed(town, worker_id) -> String: "the only <trade>" when the resident is the town's only one, not away, of a trade it needs; otherwise "". A trade is needed when a standing or building kind uses it (rules' buildings[kind].trade: forge's smith, field's farmer), when the town's current stage counts it (its "trades"), or when an open build job uses it. Companions puts the reason in their voice.
- While recruited, companions sets the worker away (Production.set_away), and back when they're home. Away already kept their job waiting and skipped their needs and bank turn. Now it also skips rent (Production._rent moves rent_due on and takes nothing) and the wage floor (Economy._floor_turn), since they neither sleep in town nor work for it. Both run again from the next turn after their return. One side effect: the town's alms runner away at the floor's turn misses that day's floor, which is rare and small.

farm_test _test_recruit: the only smith and the only farmer can't go, a hauler can, a second smith frees either, the other smith away holds this one; away 3 days takes no rent and owes no floor, and back they run again. Server only: no wire change, no new class_name.
## 687. A companion's saved keys survive a load

PlayerRecord.from_dict rebuilds a player's companion key by key, and six keys
the game writes were never read back: "left" and "leaving" (581), "focus" and
"focus_day" (577), "mood" (555) and "warned_area" (581 amended). A save and a
load dropped them, so on the box every restart (each deploy is one) brought a
companion who had left back to her player, and threw away her focus's growth
(re-rolled from her traits on the join). A companion's numeric trait (her
justice, 581 amended) also came back as text; no effect yet, since a rolled
one falls back to the same seeded roll and the legacy three are fixed.

- from_dict reads them: focus as numbers, focus_day {day, grown}, mood and
  warned_area as words, left whole (JSON's whole floats made ints all the
  way down: days, ticks, the grave goods' uids), and a leaving in progress as
  only what she leaves over (deed, why, day): her walk (from, until, place)
  starts again on the next calm moment. A trait that is a number stays one.
- **The guard** (the coordinator's ask): tests/record_keys_test. It scans the
  source for every key written onto a companion (companion["key"] = ...) and
  fails, naming it, on one with no sample in the test, so a new key must be
  loaded and added; it fills a record with every sample, round-trips it
  through to_dict, JSON and from_dict, and fails naming each key dropped or
  changed; and the same for the player's own fields (every script variable
  of PlayerRecord). Against the old from_dict it names all six and the trait.
- Keys already lost in earlier restarts can't be brought back: a companion
  who left and came back after a restart stays with her player until she
  leaves again; a focus re-rolled grows again from there.

(left, focus, mood, the road she was warned off); one about to leave keeps

## 688. The free body: a player's centre of its own, the world on cells

Jeff on v0.1.182: "you can now tell that the pc character is running on a
grid, the mouse move directions is very unreponsive"; his pick 3 of
free-movement.md, ui's study (C:/dev/review/ui/free-movement-study.md) and
the coordinator's rulings. This is the server's body, behind a flag
(World.free_walk, Net's --free-walk); the grid's steps stay the default until
Jeff signs off, and the wire is ui's 689.

- **The body**: GridEntity.free_pos, the centre in cell units (Vector2(tile)
  a cell's centre), and free_way, its velocity in cells a tick. Every body
  has a free_pos (its cell's centre) so shots and lobs may read one origin;
  only a player's moves on its own (World.free_body: a Player, the flag on).
- **Input**: World.free_input(entity, intent, seconds) queues a command, an
  intent of length up to 1 (shorter walks slower) held for its dt. The
  player's act (Player._sim_tick, World.tend_free_body) applies them in order
  against a bank of real time, a tick more each tick and FREE_BANK_TICKS (3)
  at most, so more commands than time never walk faster. Queued steps and
  move orders are the grid's and are dropped; an action order is pursued as
  before.
- **Speed**: 1 / step_ticks the way the intent mostly points, from its cell:
  load (676), winded, the speed buff and the ground (607) all count. A
  diagonal costs what a straight does (the coordinator's ruling; the grid's
  3.75 ticks a diagonal step is gone for a free body).
- **Collision**: a circle of FREE_RADIUS 0.3 moved a substep (at most 0.2
  cell) at a time and pushed out of what is solid: an edge a step from the
  side its centre is on could not cross (_terrain_blocks_step: a wall, a
  closed door, a step up, the walkable's edge; one-way where a height is),
  and the cells others hold (a monster, another player, a crate). It slides
  along what it meets; at two walls' corner it stops a radius off it, so it
  never cuts a corner. A closed door pressed into is opened if it may; a
  crate pressed into is shifted a cell (_shift) at the walk's pace; a body
  on a link's cell is bumped as a refused step was (link_bumped, 571).
- **One cell held**: the body holds the cell its centre is in once the
  centre is FREE_HYSTERESIS (0.1) past its own cell's edge, so a body on a
  border does not flicker. The claim is a step: _relocate (entity_moved:
  interest, links, the log), a slide for the views, and _stepped_off (the
  grass, spawn grace, the footstep and the clank, its pace from the speed),
  taken out of try_move for both.
- **Its own companion never blocks him** (the coordinator's ruling): her
  cell is not solid to him and he passes through; while his centre is in
  her cell his claim waits, bumping her (entity_bumped, every
  FREE_BUMP_TICKS) so her yield hears it. swap_places refuses a free body,
  so 679's swap is retired for it.
- **Halt**: World.halt(entity, until_tick) drops the velocity and the
  waiting commands and takes no intent before that tick (combat's attacks
  and wind-ups; stand_firm halts at once). No intent is taken with a bow
  drawn (583 amended), stunned, lying or downed (free_held).
- **A step is any move**: last_step_tick is set on any tick the body moved
  over 0.01 cell, so a spear is braced only standing still; step_velocity
  and step_until carry the velocity as a step's momentum (592).
- **Pushes snap**: any change of tile but the body's own claim
  (_world_set_tile: a push, a lunge, a rush, a relocate, a spawn) puts its
  centre on the cell's centre. Impulses on a free body come later (688
  amended (2)).

tests/walk.gd, the walk-to helper: Walk.to(entity, cell) walks a body there
either way, a grid step at a time along walk_path or a free body's command a
tick toward the path's next cell. tests/free_walk_test: the flag off as
before; 10 ticks east 4 cells, south-east 4 too, half an intent half; the
claim at 0.65 past, not at 0.55, and not back at 0.55; 30 commands of a

wall's slide at y 1.2; a corner never cut; a door opened and walked
through; halted, drawn, stand_firm; inching counts as a step; a relocate and
a knock snap it; the helper round a wall either way. Wire: none with the
flag off (free_pos and free_way are not replicated; ui's 689 packs them),
protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 688, combat's side: blows and shots from a free body

ui's design, physics' free body (688): while World.free_walk is on, a player's body has a float
centre, GridEntity.free_pos. Combat's side, agreed with ui:

- **A blow stops the body; it is no longer refused mid-step.** A free body never sets
  next_move_tick, so the grid's mid-step refusals pass it. In their place,
  World._halt_for_blow(entity, until) calls physics' World.halt.
  - A swing (try_swing), a blow or a shove (_try_hit) and a door's bash (try_bash_door) hold the
    body until next_attack_tick.
  - A wind-up (try_wind_up) holds it until it lands.
  - A shield bash (try_bash) holds it until bash_moment_until.
  - While held, the walk keys do nothing (World.free_held). A body on the grid is unchanged.
- **Shots and lobs start from the body's own centre.** World.shot_origin(entity) is free_pos for
  a free body, else the cell's centre.
  - shot_ray takes it as an optional origin and starts its walk across cell sides from there.
    shot_aim passes it, so the server's shot and the client's aim read the same line.
  - lob_aim draws the aim in to the reach from it.
  - Main._point_direction (swing, shove and shield toward the cursor) aims from it.
  - The cells counted for reach are still World.distance's.
- **Melee keeps cell adjacency**, with no change to any number: can_melee, in_reach and
  is_behind read player.tile, the one cell a free body claims.
- **Physics' side.** A brace reads last_step_tick, which physics sets on any movement over
  0.01 cell. A lunge, a rush, a push or a relocate snaps free_pos to the cell's centre first.
  stand_firm halts a free body.
- **Diagonals cost the same as straights** under free walk. A flank to is_behind and
  kite-and-shoot get easier; this is to be re-checked in play.

combat_test `_test_free_blows`:
- a swing mid-walk is taken and stops the body;
- the walk keys do nothing until the attack is ready, then it walks on;
- an arrow from the bottom edge of its cell strikes a body in the row below that a centre shot
  misses;
- the lob drawn in from the body's centre.

Protocol unchanged, no new class_name. It changes nothing in play until free_walk is turned on.

## 688 amended: a pure glide, the server's ack, no stall at a corner

What ui's 689 (the wire, the client's replay) needs of 688's body, and what
its prototype found.

- **free_glide(entity, from, intent, ticks) -> [centre, velocity]**: the
  body's move, touching nothing: no free_pos written, no door opened, no
  crate shifted, no cell held, nothing told, whoever calls it (a host's
  replay runs on the same Player as the server). The server's own turn runs
  the same routine (_free_glide) with its effects on, so the two cannot
  drift. Its cell is the tile as it stands; on a client a closed door and a
  crate stay solid till the server opens or shifts them.
- **free_cell(entity, at) -> Vector2i**: the cell a centre at `at` would
  hold (the tile, till FREE_HYSTERESIS past its edge on either axis), pure;
  _free_claim reads it.
- **The ack**: free_input takes the client's seq. Player.free_acked is the
  seq of the last command done with and Player.free_used the ticks the head
  one has had. Every command the server drops counts as done (ui: else a
  halted body runs on in the view): halt's drop, the FREE_INPUTS_MAX
  overflow, a held body's command (its time spent standing), and a spawn
  (World.spawn drops what was sent before: free_drop).
- **No stall at a corner**: a substep that keeps under a quarter of its move
  (head on at a wall's outside corner, where the push-out sent it straight
  back) is tried along the way the intent mostly points alone, then the
  other, x first on a tie: it slides off. An inside pocket, both ways
  blocked, still stops it.
- **Pushes as impulses** are now 688 amended (2).

free_walk_test: through its own companion 0.4 a tick every tick (no slowing
on her, only the claim waits); head on at the corner it slides off east to
(3, 3), never (2, 2) through it, never nearer than a radius; a pocket stops

a drawn bow (acked 5), 65 at once (the first, 10, acked). Server only,
protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 689: free movement's wire

Step 2 of free movement (Jeff's pick 3; the coordinator's step list), on
physics' free body (688, 688 amended) and combat's side. Nothing changes in
play while the server's free_walk is off. Protocol revision 39.

- **The flag, live.** The admin's `free_walk on|off` (Main.admin_command)
  calls World.set_free_walk: no release, no restart, and it is kept in the
  --state file ("free_walk"; --free-walk turns it on at start). Off puts
  each body on the cell it holds (a free body always holds its own; its
  companion's cell it only waits on), on starts each at its cell's centre;
  the seqs and acks start over (as on any placing: a spawn, a respawn, a
  join). The box stays off until Jeff says.
- **No message for the flag.** It rides on each player's own replicated
  Player.free_state: empty, the body walks the grid; not, it is free. A client
  switches per body as its state arrives, and its own World.free_walk
  follows its own body.
- **Commands up.** The owning client closes a command every 1/30 s (the
  intent quantised to int8s, how long in ms) and sends the newest four by
  World.request_free, unreliable and ordered (FreeNet.pack_commands, 5 bytes
  each), so a lost packet costs nothing; standing still sends nothing (the
  last command goes as it stops and twice more). A host's own go straight to
  World.take_free.
- **What the server takes** (the game port is public): the sender must own
  the body (else dropped, logged once a peer); a packet of the wrong size or
  more than four is dropped; each seq once (wrapping at 65536); at most 40
  commands a second by the clock (World.FREE_COMMANDS_PER_SECOND), the rest
  dropped; each intent at most a unit long. The speed stays the bank's
  (688): more commands never move it faster.
- **State down.** Player.free_state (FreeNet.pack_state, 17 bytes): the centre in
  1/1024 cells, the last command done with (Player.free_acked), the ticks
  had of the next (free_used), the server tick's low bits and the cell it
  holds (where the replay's ground speed starts, for physics' 688 amended
  (3), in the same packet as the centre, never a tile from another). Packed after
  the body's turn (Player.pack_free) only when the centre or the ack
  changed, so a body standing still sends nothing.
- **The own body by replay** (FreeNet.Own): the commands not yet done with
  are replayed from the server's centre through World.free_glide, the code
  the server moves it by, and the open command too, each frame: an input
  shows the frame it is pressed. A correction under 0.75 cells is blended
  out over 0.1 s; a bigger one (a push, a link) shows at once. A host's and
  an offline player's own body take the same path. MovePrediction is not
  used for a free body.
- **Mirrors** (FreeNet.Mirror): another free player is drawn from the
  states as they came, World.display_delay_ticks in the past, between the
  two around it; one that stood still sets off from where it stood a tick
  before its next state, not gliding all the while.
- **Steering on the client.** A click plans World.walk_path from the cell
  the body is shown on and steers along the pulled line, slowing onto the
  last cell's centre. One click and let go walks the whole route (Jeff on
  the prototype: "wasn't one click enough before?"); the button still held
  past 0.25 s steers at the cursor instead, straight in the open and along a
  route when something stands between (a tree, a wall), planned again as the
  cursor moves. The keys' way is the intent as it is. Server routes and
  steps are not sent for a free body.
- **Her on a client.** A companion's keeper is the server's alone, so a
  client's replay took its own companion for solid and the server passed
  through her: corrections up to a cell over the box's link. The free body
  knows her by World._own_companion_of: her keeper, or her keeper's peer.
- **Drawing.** GridEntity._free_shown gives a free body's centre and way;
  the body is drawn there, its cell slides dropped (Client3D reads the
  position as ever).

Tests: free_net_test (the wire both ways; the five hostile cases; the bank
the only speed; the own view a frame after its input, no corrections on a
walk, a turn and a stop; under 150 ms lag each way with every third packet
lost the view ends on the server's centre; the switch). controls_test
_test_free_click (one click and let go walks to its cell; a new click on the
way redirects). The latency harness offline and over the box's link: see
the landing message.
## 688 amended (3): ground speed from the cell held, a substep at a time

ui's 689 prototype showed its own body corrected by about 0.25 cells, two
times in six, in the wilds (mixed ground). Two causes, both in the free
glide:

- **The cell a command starts from**: free_glide took each command's cell
  as the body's tile, or the cell its centre rounds to when it is far off.
  The server's body keeps the cell it holds from one command to the next
  (FREE_HYSTERESIS past an edge before it changes), so a replay near an
  edge read the speed of the wrong cell's ford, grass or slope.
  free_glide(entity, from, intent, ticks, held) now takes the cell held at
  [from] (the tile if not given) and returns it third: [centre, velocity,
  held]. A replay passes each command the last one's.
- **Where the speed changes**: the speed was read once per call, and then
  once per substep, so it changed at whichever substep's end followed the
  change of cell, and the server's bank splits a command elsewhere than a
  client's replay of it whole. Now a substep is cut where the cell held
  would change (_free_cell_exit), and the next one reads the new cell's
  speed: the same place however the command is split.

free_walk_test's replay used to compare only when the server had no
command waiting, which, three commands to a tick's bank, it almost never
did. It now steps till they are all applied and compares 13 times a room.
On the old glide: 0.26 cells off across fords. Now: open ground and fords
exactly, the cell held the server's each time; by walls under 0.01 (a
circle rounding a convex corner goes a little otherwise as its substeps
fall; allowed 0.02). Server and sim only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name; ui's FreeNet.Own passes held through.

## 689 amended: the own replay carries the server's held cell

688 amended (3) gave World.free_glide the cell held at its start and back
the cell held at its end, since ground speed is read from the held cell
(hysteresis keeps it 0.1 past an edge). FreeNet.Own now keeps `held`
beside `base`: the server's held cell from each state (Player.free_state
already carries it, 689), passed into each replayed command's glide and
taken back from it, and into the open command's. Without it a replay read
speed from the cell its centre rounded to, and a step from a ford onto open
ground came out a little off: free_net_test's new case (150 ms each way,
a third of packets lost, across fords on every other column) counted 11
corrections before, none now. Client only, protocol unchanged, no new

whose body moves freely (688) as well as one on the grid, before free_walk is
on for the box. 689 sends the server intents only, no route (ui), so his

  cells his centre crosses within FREE_AHEAD (2) cells along free_way, as

## 688 amended (2): a push on a free body, decided at once, shown over the ticks after

Till now a push on a free body (688) slid its cell a cell at a time, as any
body's (592), and its centre snapped onto the cell it ended in. Now it
slides from its centre, at any angle. The coordinator's ruling on the
design: decide at once, show over the ticks, consistent with the grid's
push and keeping its same-call results (apply_blow's, launch's, a lunge's
and a ram's struck lists read them in the call).

- **The trace** (World._free_slide, from _push for a free body not lofted):
  its centre from its free_pos along the push's way, a substep at a time
  through the free collision (_free_resolve; its own companion, whom it
  walks through, a push meets), each cell's length costing its
  ground_drag, as far as u x slide_per_speed cells (max_travel at most):
  _push's reach, but not in whole cells. The cells its centre comes to hold
  (_free_cell_from, the hysteresis) are taken on the way, so its tile, the
  occupancy and what the call returns are all decided then.
- **A wall** (a closed door, a step up, the edge of the walkable) met within
  30 degrees of head on (FREE_GLANCE_COS 0.87) stops it, a radius short;
  what speed it has left hurts as _push's does (impact_per_energy x 1/2 m
  u^2). At more of a slant it slides along it, its speed scaled by the
  sine, and the speed it lost into the wall (the glance) hurts the same way.
- **A body met**: the hand-off as now (restitution; the one met goes on
  from its cell along the way the slider was going). **Water** at the edge
  stops it unhurt; **a drop** it goes off into the cell below and falls (the
  fall hurts); **fire** stops a creature in it.
- **Shown**: its free_pos does not move in the call. The path is kept
  (GridEntity.free_kick_path, free_kick_at, free_kick_ticks:
  push_slide_ticks of its cells) and shown a tick at a time, slowing
  (1 - (1 - t)^2 along the path) by World._tend_free_kicks before anyone
  acts, so a stunned body (which skips its turn) slides too; its own
  zone's clock only (604 amended). Its state is packed each tick for its
  client (ui's 689). While shown it is free_held, and what it sends is
  dropped and acknowledged (free_drop), as a halt's is: the commands the
  push overrode drop out of its client's replay. Any other move of its
  tile (a relocate, a toss over the head) ends the showing there.

Distances: on open ground from a cell's centre the cells are the grid's
(east at 2: three). Into a wall it travels a radius less than to the cell's
edge, so it meets it a little faster than a grid body does (head on at 2
from a cell's length away: 1.2 left, 4 hurt, where the grid's 1.33 would
be 5).

free_walk_test: a speed of 2 from off a centre takes its cell at once and
shows the slide over 6 ticks, each shorter, a command sent meanwhile
acknowledged and not walked, steering after; the grid's and the free
body's cells the same from a centre; head on into a wall, stopped a radius
short, hurt by what was left; at a slant along a wall, never past it, the
glance hurting; nearly head on, stopped; into a dummy, which goes on at the
restitution share; into its own companion, met; off a ledge, a fall.
free_net_test (with ui, its lag-and-loss proxy): pushed while walking east,
the view ends on the server's centre with nothing left to replay, and the
walk taken up after. Server and sim only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

## 690: the server's token from the environment, /opt root-owned, a builder cost cap

Jeff, 2026-10-26, from the host security review of the box (its handoff note on
the box, ~/psykinetic-hardening-handoff.md): the server is internet-facing (a
friend joins by IP and token), and the box now runs a systemd sandbox drop-in
(/etc/systemd/system/psykinetic.service.d/hardening.conf, host-side, not in the
repo, never removed or worked round: a feature it blocks changes it deliberately).
Three changes:

1. server/deploy.sh installs /opt/psykinetic as root:root, not the service user:
   the service must not be able to replace its own binary. Each deploy until now
   handed it back.
2. The token leaves the command line. The unit ran --token=${PSYKINETIC_TOKEN},
   which systemd expands into argv, readable by every local process (ps,
   /proc/<pid>/cmdline). Net._token_from_env reads PSYKINETIC_TOKEN before
   _parse_args, so an explicit --token still wins (stage.sh, tests); the unit's
   ExecStart drops --token. EnvironmentFile is read by systemd before the sandbox
   applies, so /etc/psykinetic being inaccessible to the process doesn't matter
   (the old ${PSYKINETIC_TOKEN} expansion already proved the variable reaches the
   environment). The refusal to run a server with no token stays. protocol_test
   _test_token_from_env: the environment's token used with no flag, the flag
   overriding it, nothing set leaving it alone. Afterwards Jeff rotates the token.
3. ExecStart gains --builder-max-cost=1.00 (Jeff's amount; the code's default, now
   explicit): a builder request stops at $1.00 of the API key.

Server only (a unit change: release installs the unit, daemon-reload, deploy),
protocol unchanged, no new class_name. docs/server.md and server/env.example
updated.
## 691. No player's id in what a client is sent of a resting companion; no remote dev-host

The coordinator, for Jeff's box hardening (690): the server is reachable
from the internet, and a player's id is the key to their record and to
builder and admin rights. Two holes.

- **A resting companion's body** (decision 333 amended) was named from her
  worker key, "Resident_" + "companion:<player id>", so her player's whole
  id went to every client who saw her: in the spawn spec's name, in the
  "death" message (the entity's name) and in every "speech" (its path).
  She is now named by her player's index, as their own body is
  ("Resident_companion_<index>"; Godot makes it unique while a despawned
  body's name is held). Resident.worker_id and player_id keep the real key,
  server side only (neither is replicated). A town's own residents keep
  their worker ids in their names: none is a player's id.
- **The dev host's fixed id**: a host or server run from the project plays
  as Net.DEV_PLAYER_ID ("dev-host"). On a dedicated server nobody plays it,
  and a remote hello claiming it would have got its record. Now
  Net.reserved_id refuses it on a dedicated server ("reserved player id");
  a host's own id, and every other, are as before.

resident_test _test_no_id_in_names: a resting companion whose player has an
id of the usual length (a made-up one): no body's name or path holds any
player's id, her name is Resident_companion_..., her key kept on the
server; the death and speech sent of her hold none; reserved_id refuses
dev-host on a server only. Protocol unchanged (the names are not a
replicated value's meaning; --print-protocol the same), no new class_name.
Server only, protocol unchanged, no new class_name.

## 692. A player with no record is "a traveller", never their id

The coordinator, 2026-10-26: the box is internet-facing and a player's id
is the key to their record. Offers ctx "name_of" fell back to the raw id
for a player with no record, and that id flowed into what the town
repeats: gossip (Townsfolk's hearsay of a standing, whose own fallback
was the id too), learned facts (brought home, cleared the camp), the
chronicle's names, the bard's listeners, and the lawspeaker's party_log
line, which wrote the raw "player:" said_by when players' words are on.
From there it went out to other players as hearsay and rumour offers.

- **Main's ctx name_of:** returns the record's name, or "a traveller"
  (Offers.TRAVELLER) for no record or a blank name. This is the word
  TownMemory._name and Lawspeaker._who already used.
- **Offers.name_of(given, player_id):** every reader goes through it,
  not the raw ctx call. It gives TRAVELLER for no ctx, an empty id, a
  blank name, or a name equal to the id. The readers are offers' facts,
  chronicle and gift lines, Townsfolk's song, gossip and grievance, and
  Main's escort words.
- **Kept behaviour:** a grievance against an unnamed player is still not
  written, as before. A song still doesn't treat "a traveller" in a
  memory's text as a listener's own deed.
- **The lawspeaker's "left as talk" line:** names its teller through
  Lawspeaker._who, so a player is "a traveller".

resident_test _test_names_never_ids covers no record, an empty id, no
ctx, a name_of that echoes the id, a record with no name, and a named
record, using a placeholder id.
## 686, npc's side: a refusal, a bond written back, a companion settled

Companions' 686 lets a player recruit a trusted resident as a companion.
The coordinator approved it; these keys were agreed between companions
and npc, and economy's side (Towns.sole_needed, no rent or wage floor
while away) was checked for overlap. npc's side:

- **Production.set_asked(worker_id, player_id, why):** a refusal sentence
  per player, in worker["asked"][player_id] ("" erases that player's).
  Companions writes it when a resident turns them down. The resident
  prompt (Resident.facts_now) appends it, as written, only when that
  player is the one speaking.
- **Standing.set_score(card, player_id, score, why, step):** sets the
  score, clamped as bump clamps, and remembers why. It makes the entry if
  the player is a stranger, and marks it their own so hearsay leaves it
  be. Companions uses it to write a recruit's bond back to their card
  when they come home (card_of, set_score, Production.set_card).
- **Townsfolk.settle(production, towns, worker_id) -> String:** a
  companion's worker ("companion:<name>") becomes a resident of her town
  for good. Through Towns.settle_companion (new; economy's file, told) it
  makes a new worker "settled:<name>" (":2" and on when that is taken),
  origin "settled" (room-exempt, no old-age death, as Snagfin's). The new
  worker takes her trade and her place among the residents, and the
  companion worker is removed. Her mind and what she has heard are
  copied, and a resident card is rolled. Her purse (paid as "what the
  town owed", so not earned anew), what the town owes her and any loan
  go with her (economy and companions pointed out that remove_worker
  would lose them). It returns the new id, or "".
  Companions calls it at every hand-over (a recruited one parts or
  leaves, or her player recruits another while she is away) instead of
  clearing her origin. Almost everything in town keys on the
  "companion:" id prefix: cards, gossip, sickness, kin, bodies (only from
  player records). So a cleared origin would have left her a bodiless
  worker.
- **Kept across a restart:** Production.from_dict keeps "left_why",
  "left_back" (581 amended) and "asked" on a worker.
- **Away while recruited:** companions' production.set_away is enough on
  npc's side (no body, no hail, no gossip, no runs). Companions refuses
  residents who are strayed, sought, escorting, on a drive or caravan, or
  on a run, since those paths clear "away" on their own. Pip's runner is
  unchanged: only record.companion counts as out with a player.

resident_test checks the refusal (only to the one who asked, kept across
a save, erased), set_score (a stranger met then, clamped, own, the reason;
set again; hearsay refused), and settle (settled:Sel with her trade, mind,
hearing and card, in her place; settled:Sel:2 for another; "" for none).

- **The word** (Main.asks_to_part, the rules' part_words: "go home", "go home
