## 689 amended (2): a click on its own cell stops a free body where it stands

The latency table's click stop on the box's link took 166-186 ms in half
its rounds against 33 ms in the rest, offline as well, and the slow rounds
had gone on 0.36-0.40 cells. A click on the cell the body is drawn in,
which mid-walk is often the one ahead of the cell held (rounded past half
way, held till 0.1 past the edge), routed the body on into it, to its
centre. Main._free_route now takes a click on the cell held or the cell
drawn in as a stop where it stands: a free body has no centre to finish.
Grid walking is unchanged. controls_test: a click on the cell drawn in
mid-walk stops it (0.54 cells on without this, none with).

With it, two test-only flags for the kick-replay check (688 amended (2)
through the proxy, before free_walk goes on): a server's
--test-kicks=S,v,... pushes each player walking free back across its way
every S seconds at the speeds given in turn (Main._run_test_kicks); a
client's --test-latency=N,kick holds a walk key, turning at each push,
and reports for N pushes the cells slid, the biggest move drawn in a
frame, the own body's corrections, and the times the view went back with
the key and then with the slide again (a rubber band;
Main._run_lat_kicks).

That check, through the proxy at the box's round trip (pushes at 1.23, a
draugr's thrown axe, and 2.94, his spin on an exhausted player, while
walking), found the own view rubber-banding: 15 bands in 6 pushes, jumps
to 4.9 cells. Each frame's closed command was glided on the server's
centre and replayed on each state while the server slid the body and
dropped them. FreeNet.Own now holds while the server moves the body
itself (physics' signals, no threshold, so a wall or a body stepping in
front cannot set it off): from its body's `pushed` (Player connects it;
Own.pushed drops what is pending and the open command and holds for
World.push_slide_ticks(tiles), at least a tick: the server's playback,
falls included), and while the replicated _reel_until, down_until or
downed_until run (Own.held_by_server). Held, nothing is replayed or
glided, and the server's centre is blended in up to 3 cells
(HELD_BLEND_MAX). The hold, timed from the client's tick, ends about half
a round trip after the server's playback: on the safe side. After: 0
bands in 6 pushes; a blow's first tick can still show at once (up to 3
cells in a frame), as the hit landing. free_net_test's push under lag now
hears `pushed` at the lag and counts turns drawn. Client only, protocol
unchanged, no new class_name.
## 603 amended (4), combat's side: the spin throws whoever it strikes

Physics found that on a rested, unarmoured 80 kg player the spin pushed at
1.47, under knockback_min_force (1.5): it struck and knocked down but never
moved them, so 603's sweep into a wall never happened in play. Two causes.
603 tuned impulse_scale 0.84 as "about 150 of physics' 178", but the
draugr's swing_impulse is 140 (strength 0, his 7 kg battle axe x
swing_speed 20); the old spin test reached the sliver only because its
boss had strength 6 and a giant axe. And the floor, meant for light taps,
held back a blow that 603 says always throws.

- apply_blow takes blow["no_floor"] (bool, default false): true skips
  knockback_min_force, any push above zero slides (agreed with physics;
  below one cell's reach it still moves nothing). Only the spin passes it;
  launch, the axe throw and every other blow are as before.
- impulse_scale 0.84 -> 1.0 (the coordinator's pick; 1.07, 603's 150,
  left 1 of 20 at the wall): his swing whole, 140. A full-health 80 kg
  player swept into a wall is left at a sliver (3 of 20, as Jeff's list
  has it), the kill only on one already hurt. One ahead is thrown 2 cells
  (1.75); in plate (100 kg) 1.40 and still thrown (under the floor, so
  no_floor is what moves him). Exhausted (stamina 0, pushed_mass halved)
  the same player is thrown 5 cells (3.50) and the wall kills from full:
  printed by the test for Jeff's checklist, not asserted. F7 Tuning holds
  the knob (Telegraphs and boss moves, combat.moves.spin.impulse_scale).

combat_test _test_spin_throws: the real draugr's numbers (strength 0,
battle axe) on 80 kg rested, unarmoured players, on plate, and exhausted
(printed); _test_spin
moved to the same numbers. Server only, protocol unchanged, no new
class_name.

## 689 amended (3): a standing free body's state written again every second

Jeff's free body froze in the barrow (2026-10-26 16:18): the room was reset,
he respawned on the start cell and joined again on the same peer, and
nothing he did moved it; the server's body stood on its cell, no command
refused. A client drives the free body only once its body's free_state has
made it an own view (Player._free_heard, while the body is known as its
own); till then it walks the grid, whose steps and orders the server's
free body clears every tick. Player.pack_free wrote only on a change, so a
body placed again whose first state that client missed (or took before it
knew the body its own) never sent another while it stood, and the client
never left the grid.

Now pack_free writes a standing body's state again once every
FreeNet.STATE_RESEND_TICKS (20 ticks, about a second): the same centre and
ack, its tick new, so it replicates as a change. About 17 bytes a second a
standing player; a mirror takes it as a repeat where it was, the own
replay as a state with nothing new. ui's client half makes the own view as
soon as the body is known as its own, so it heals at once rather than
within the second.

free_net_test _test_resend: a first state heard before the body was its
own makes no own view; 21 ticks standing write it again once, after 20, and
the own view is made from it; the same centre and ack. Server only,
protocol unchanged (the same state, more often), no new class_name.
